title: Seafood Allergy and Iodinated Contrast
body: Seafood allergy does not confer any increased risk of anaphylaxis from iodinated contrast media and does not necessitate pretreatment with glucocorticoids and antihistamines.

title: IgG4-Related Disease
body: IgG4-related disorders can present with autoimmune pancreatitis, lymphadenopathy, and bilateral salivary and/or lacrimal gland enlargement. Diagnosis is confirmed by peripheral eosinophilia, elevated serum IgG4 levels, and tissue biopsy showing IgG4-positive plasma cells. Treatment involves glucocorticoids and possibly azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, or rituximab for refractory disease.

title: Blood Product Selection in IgA Deficiency
body: Patients with IgA deficiency should receive washed RBCs to remove as much plasma (containing IgA) as possible. Patients at risk for transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease require irradiated RBCs. To reduce CMV transmission, patients should receive leukoreduced RBCs.

title: Hymenoptera Sting Anaphylaxis
body: Venom immunotherapy reduces the risk of anaphylaxis recurrence from approximately 60% to 5%. It is indicated for patients with a history of systemic reaction to an insect sting and evidence of venom-specific IgE.

title: Allergic Rhinitis
body: Nasal corticosteroids are the most effective and best-tolerated treatment for typical allergic rhinitis.

title: Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID)
body: Common variable immunodeficiency is the most common immunodeficiency disorder affecting children and young adults and is caused by impaired B-cell differentiation and immunoglobulin production (IgG, IgA, and/or IgM). Patients typically present with respiratory infections, chronic lung disease, and increased risk of malignancies. Management includes immunoglobulin replacement therapy and vigilant cancer screening.

title: Specificity Specificity is the proportion of true negatives among all those who do not have the disease
body: Specificity Specificity is the proportion of true negatives among all those who do not have the disease. The formula is TN / (TN + FP). Specificity and sensitivity are intrinsic characteristics of a test and are not affected by disease prevalence.

title: Becker and Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) and Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) are X-linked recessive
body: Becker and Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) and Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) are X-linked recessive disorders. Diagnosis is made with genetic analysis or muscle biopsy showing reduced (BMD) or absent (DMD) dystrophin. Respiratory failure and heart failure are common causes of death.

title: Number Needed to Harm (NNH) The number needed to harm is the reciprocal of the difference between the absolute event rate in treated and
body: Number Needed to Harm (NNH) The number needed to harm is the reciprocal of the difference between the absolute event rate in treated and control patients and provides a measure of potential harm from treatment.

title: Sex Disparities in Cardiovascular Disease Although cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women
body: Sex Disparities in Cardiovascular Disease Although cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, evidence suggests women are treated less aggressively than men when presenting with symptoms and signs of coronary heart disease.

title: Test Indication Curves Test indication curves identify three groups: no-test/no-treat, test/treat-if-positive, and no-test/treat
body: Test Indication Curves Test indication curves identify three groups: no-test/no-treat, test/treat-if-positive, and no-test/treat. Testing is most useful in patients with intermediate pretest probabilities.

title: Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values Screening tests should have high sensitivity (SnOUT), while confirmatory tests should have
body: Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values Screening tests should have high sensitivity (SnOUT), while confirmatory tests should have high specificity (SpIN). Increasing sensitivity increases NPV; increasing specificity increases PPV.

title: Relative Risk and Confidence Intervals Relative risk compares risk in exposed versus unexposed groups. A confidence interval crossing the null value is not statistically significant.
Randomization Randomization distributes known and unknown variables equally among study groups.
Likelihood Ratios Positive likelihood ratio = sensitivity / (1 - specificity). Negative likelihood ratio = (1 - sensitivity) / specificity. Likelihood ratios are independent of disease prevalence.
Odds Ratios and Confounding The odds ratio represents the odds of an outcome occurring with an exposure compared with without exposure
body: Odds Ratios and Confounding The odds ratio represents the odds of an outcome occurring with an exposure compared with without exposure. Adjustment for confounders allows estimation of the true association between exposure and outcome.

title: Number Needed to Treat (NNT) The number needed to treat is the reciprocal of the absolute risk reduction and is used to estimate the effectiveness of an intervention.
Confidence Intervals A 95% confidence interval means that if the study were repeated many times, the true effect estimate would fall within the calculated interval approximately 95% of the time.
Management of chronic venous insufficiency (with or without ulceration) consists of lower-extremity elevation, leg exercise, weight loss
body: Management of chronic venous insufficiency (with or without ulceration) consists of lower-extremity elevation, leg exercise, weight loss, and continuous compressive therapy. Aspirin accelerates ulcer healing. Topical antibiotics, zinc sulfate, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy are not effective.

title: Patients with STEMI should undergo prompt and emergent evaluation with cardiac catheterization (preferably with angioplasty and stent) and
body: Patients with STEMI should undergo prompt and emergent evaluation with cardiac catheterization (preferably with angioplasty and stent) and receive concurrent medical therapy with aspirin, heparin, and a beta blocker (if no contraindications exist).

title: Ranolazine decreases myocardial oxygen consumption and provides effective treatment for chronic stable angina without significantly
body: Ranolazine decreases myocardial oxygen consumption and provides effective treatment for chronic stable angina without significantly affecting heart rate or blood pressure. It may be used as a substitute for or in combination with beta blockers and other antianginal therapies when initial treatment is unsuccessful in relieving chronic stable angina.

title: Warfarin or target-specific oral anticoagulants have been shown to significantly reduce the risk of embolization in patients with atrial
body: Warfarin or target-specific oral anticoagulants have been shown to significantly reduce the risk of embolization in patients with atrial fibrillation and moderate to high risk for thromboembolic events. The CHA2DS2-VASc score is recommended for assessment of stroke risk in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. I

title: Risk factor modification and graded exercise are effective in improving exercise capacity in patients with claudication and peripheral
body: Risk factor modification and graded exercise are effective in improving exercise capacity in patients with claudication and peripheral arterial disease (PAD). If Iifestyle-Iimiting claudication persists, medical therapy with antiplatelet agents (aspirin or Clopidogrel) is recommended to improve pain-free walking distance and prevent PAD progression. Patients who fail antiplatelet therapy and do not meet criteria for revascularization can be prescribed Cilostazol to improve pain-free walking distances.

title: Serial echocardiogram is recommended every 3-5 years in patients with mild aortic stenosis (AS), every 1- 2 years in those with moderate
body: Serial echocardiogram is recommended every 3-5 years in patients with mild aortic stenosis (AS), every 1- 2 years in those with moderate AS, and every 6-12 months in those with asymptomatic, severe AS. Pharmacologic therapy has no role in the management of patients with mild AS in the absence of concurrent hypertension, coronary artery disease, or heart failure.

title: Maneuvers that decrease left ventricular cavity size (i.e., Valsalva, standing) cause the hypertrophied septum in hypertrophic
body: Maneuvers that decrease left ventricular cavity size (i.e., Valsalva, standing) cause the hypertrophied septum in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy to obstruct further and make the murmur louder. Fixed obstructions, such as aortic stenosis, get slightly quieter as the decreased venous return results in less flow across the fixed obstruction.

title: Sacubitril inhibits neprilysin, resulting in elevated levels Ofatrial natriuretic peptide, brain natriuretic peptide, bradykinin, and
body: Sacubitril inhibits neprilysin, resulting in elevated levels Ofatrial natriuretic peptide, brain natriuretic peptide, bradykinin, and angiotensin II. Sacubitril-valsartan improves cardiovascular mortality but causes a nonproductive cough, similar to that seen with ACE inhibitors, in approximately 10% of patients.

title: The presence of high-risk features on exercise stress testing and normal radionuclide myocardial perfusion imaging should raise suspicion
body: The presence of high-risk features on exercise stress testing and normal radionuclide myocardial perfusion imaging should raise suspicion for the presence of balanced ischemia. Such patients should be further evaluated with coronary angiography for the presence of multivessel coronary artery disease.

title: Aortic regurgitation murmurs are best heard when the patient is sitting up, leaning forward, and holding their breath in full expiration
body: Aortic regurgitation murmurs are best heard when the patient is sitting up, leaning forward, and holding their breath in full expiration while the diaphragm of the stethoscope is placed along the left sternal border at the 3rd or 4th intercostal space.

title: Patients with chronic mitral regurgitation (MR) require mitral valve repair if they become symptomatic, show echocardiographic (ECHO)
body: Patients with chronic mitral regurgitation (MR) require mitral valve repair if they become symptomatic, show echocardiographic (ECHO) evidence of cardiac dysfunction, develop pulmonary hypertension, or new- onset atrial fibrillation. Asymptomatic patients need serial monitoring with clinical exam and ECHO depending on the severity of the MR.

title: Hemolytic anemia is a complication of prosthetic heart valves. Treatment involves oral iron or blood transfusion. Patients with paravalvular leak or valve failure may need valve replacement.
Ventricular septal defects cause a loud holosystolic murmur which is best heard over the third or fourth intercostal space along the left
body: Ventricular septal defects cause a loud holosystolic murmur which is best heard over the third or fourth intercostal space along the left sternal border. It can be distinguished from other systolic murmurs by its characteristic location and presence of a palpable thrill.

title: Patients with a history of peripartum cardiomyopathy and persistent LV dysfunction have a high risk of further decline in LV function
body: Patients with a history of peripartum cardiomyopathy and persistent LV dysfunction have a high risk of further decline in LV function, recurrent heart failure, and death with subsequent pregnancies. Such patients should be advised to avoid future pregnancy.

title: Physical examination findings in patients with mitral stenosis include a loud first heart sound, opening snap after S2 (best heard at the
body: Physical examination findings in patients with mitral stenosis include a loud first heart sound, opening snap after S2 (best heard at the apex), and a low-pitched diastolic rumble best heard at the cardiac apex. Patients with tricuspid regurgitation from long-standing pulmonary hypertension also have a holosystolic murmur that increases in intensity with inspiration.

title: Management of perioperative anticoagulation with warfarin involves balancing the bleeding risk Ofsurgery with the thrombotic risk of
body: Management of perioperative anticoagulation with warfarin involves balancing the bleeding risk Ofsurgery with the thrombotic risk of stopping anticoagulation. Low-bleeding-risk surgeries or procedures (eg, cataract surgery) typically require no adjustment or interruption in the warfarin regimen. High-bleeding-risk surgeries (eg, joint replacement) require a temporary interruption in anticoagulation; the interruption should be accompanied by bridging (eg, low-molecular-weight heparin, unfractionated heparin) in patients at very high thrombotic risk.

title: Statins are associated with an increased risk of diabetes and worsening glycemic control in patients with established diabetes mellitus
body: Statins are associated with an increased risk of diabetes and worsening glycemic control in patients with established diabetes mellitus. However, this excess risk is significantly less than the reduction in risk for cardiovascular events. The benefits of statin therapy outweigh the adverse effects on blood glucose, and new-onset or worsening diabetes does not warrant discontinuation of statin therapy.

title: Superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome is most commonly due to tumor compression
body: Superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome is most commonly due to tumor compression. However, implantation of a transvenous automatic implantable cardioverter defibrillator can induce thrombosis and occlusion around the leads, resulting in SVC syndrome. Bilateral upper-extremity venography is the gold standard for diagnosing SVC syndrome. However, contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography is usually the initial test of choice.

title: A falsely elevated ankle-brachial index (ABI) >1.3 can be present due to calcified and non-compressible arteries in patients with advanced
body: A falsely elevated ankle-brachial index (ABI) >1.3 can be present due to calcified and non-compressible arteries in patients with advanced peripheral arterial disease in the setting Ofdiabetes and/or chronic renal failure. High ABI (similar to low ABI) is associated with an increased risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.

title: Patients with clinical or Subclinical hyperthyroidism have a higher risk Ofdeveloping atrial fibrillation (AF)
body: Patients with clinical or Subclinical hyperthyroidism have a higher risk Ofdeveloping atrial fibrillation (AF). Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone levels should be measured during the initial evaluation of all patients with new-onset AF.

title: In the evaluation of syncope, it is critical to first rule out structural heart disease
body: In the evaluation of syncope, it is critical to first rule out structural heart disease. If none is found, then ambulatory monitoring can be very helpful. Syncope due to high degree AV block is a class I indication for permanent pacemaker placement.

title: Beta blockers are recommended for patients with congenital long QT syndrome to reduce the risk of symptomatic arrhythmias and sudden
body: Beta blockers are recommended for patients with congenital long QT syndrome to reduce the risk of symptomatic arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. An implantable cardioverter-defibrillator is recommended for patients with syncope (especially if recurrent) or ventricular tachycardia (eg, torsade de pointes) on beta blocker therapy or for those with aborted cardiac arrest.

title: Valve replacement in patients with chronic severe aortic regurgitation should be considered based upon the development of symptoms or left
body: Valve replacement in patients with chronic severe aortic regurgitation should be considered based upon the development of symptoms or left ventricular dilatation/dysfunction. In the absence of those findings, close clinical follow up and echocardiograms every 6-12 months are warranted.

title: The major high-risk features that increase risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy include family
body: The major high-risk features that increase risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy include family history of sudden death, recurrent or exertional syncope, nonsustained ventricular tachycardia on Holter monitoring, hypotensive response during exercise, and massive left ventricular hypertrophy >3 cm. Patients with >1 high-risk features should have an implantable cardioverter­ defibrillator for the primary prevention of SCD.

title: ICD therapy for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death is recommended in patients with persistent LVEF < 30% (or <35% along with NYHA
body: ICD therapy for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death is recommended in patients with persistent LVEF < 30% (or <35% along with NYHA class Il or III symptoms) due to prior Ml, who are at least 40 days post myocardial infarction and 3 months status-post percutaneous coronary intervention or CABG (if performed).

title: ICD therapy for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death is recommended in patients with persistent LVEF < 30% (or <35% along with NYHA
body: ICD therapy for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death is recommended in patients with persistent LVEF < 30% (or <35% along with NYHA class Il or III symptoms) due to prior Ml, who are at least 40 days post myocardial infarction and 3 months status-post percutaneous coronary intervention or CABG (if performed).

title: Optimal medical therapy in patients with heart failure due to left ventricular systolic dysfunction includes diuretics, a beta blocker, an
body: Optimal medical therapy in patients with heart failure due to left ventricular systolic dysfunction includes diuretics, a beta blocker, an ACE inhibitor, and an aldosterone antagonist. Digoxin and a combination of hydralazine and oral nitrates can be used in symptomatic patients despite optimal medical therapy. Cardiac resynchronization therapy with biventricular pacing is recommended in patients in sinus rhythm who have persistent symptoms despite optimal medical therapy, a left ventricular ejection fraction <35%, a QRS duration >150 msec, and a left bundle branch block.

title: Patients with rheumatic fever should receive continuous antibiotic prophylaxis to prevent recurrent GAS pharyngitis and limit the risk of
body: Patients with rheumatic fever should receive continuous antibiotic prophylaxis to prevent recurrent GAS pharyngitis and limit the risk of progression of rheumatic heart disease. Intramuscular penicillin G benzathine every 3-4 weeks is preferred, and the duration of therapy is determined by the severity of underlying rheumatic heart disease (presence or absence of carditis and valvular disease).

title: Symptomatic patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) characteristically presents with left ventricular failure accompanied by a continuous murmur
body: Symptomatic patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) characteristically presents with left ventricular failure accompanied by a continuous murmur, wide pulse pressure, and bounding pulses. Pulmonary hypertension, and in severe cases Eisenmenger syndrome, can also occur. Unrepaired PDA increases the risk of infective endarteritis that typically affects the pulmonary end of the PDA.

title: Warfarin can cross the placental barrier and is associated with fetal bleeding and risk of teratogenicity when used during pregnancy
body: Warfarin can cross the placental barrier and is associated with fetal bleeding and risk of teratogenicity when used during pregnancy. With the possible exception of patients on low-dose warfarin for a mechanical heart valve, all others who require anticoagulation during pregnancy should be switched to low-molecular- weight or unfractionated heparin.

title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an autosomal dominant genetic disorder characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) of variable
body: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is an autosomal dominant genetic disorder characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) of variable morphology. In HCM1 LVH is frequently asymmetric and wall thickness is >15 mm; in individuals with athlete’s heart, it is generally symmetric and wall thickness is ≤12 mm.

title: Early surgical intervention is sometimes required in the management of infective endocarditis
body: Early surgical intervention is sometimes required in the management of infective endocarditis. Valvular regurgitation complicated by acute heart failure is a strong indication for early valvular repair or replacement. Other surgical indications include uncontrollable infection and embolic complications while on appropriate antibiotics.

title: Statin therapy can sometimes worsen an underlying metabolic muscle disorder that mimics statin myopathy
body: Statin therapy can sometimes worsen an underlying metabolic muscle disorder that mimics statin myopathy. Patients with suspected statin myopathy should first be tested for serum CK, vitamin D, and thyroid function studies. Further testing is guided by clinical and laboratory findings.

title: Myxomas are the most common benign primary cardiac tumors, with approximately 80% located in the left atrium
body: Myxomas are the most common benign primary cardiac tumors, with approximately 80% located in the left atrium. Patients typically develop constitutional symptoms (eg, fatigue, low-grade fever, weight loss), systemic embolization (eg, transient ischemic attacks, ischemic stroke, acute embolic arterial occlusion), and cardiovascular symptoms simulating mitral valve disease (eg, dyspnea, orthopnea, cough, pulmonary edema, hemoptysis).

title: The first step in evaluating a patient with suspected peripheral artery disease (PAD) is to obtain an ankle- brachial index (ABI) to
body: The first step in evaluating a patient with suspected peripheral artery disease (PAD) is to obtain an ankle- brachial index (ABI) to confirm the diagnosis. Patients with typical claudication symptoms and normal ABI should undergo exercise testing with repeat ABI to confirm the diagnosis of occlusive PAD. Vascular imaging studies are most useful in patients being considered for specific interventional procedures.

title: Men age <35 and women age <44 have low prevalence of dyslipidemia and low 10-year risk for coronary heart disease (CHD) events
body: Men age <35 and women age <44 have low prevalence of dyslipidemia and low 10-year risk for coronary heart disease (CHD) events. However, patients in these age groups with diabetes, hypertension, obesity, or CHD; tobacco use; or family history of CHD are at increased risk and are more likely to benefit from lipid screening and intervention.

title: ECG findings in Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) pattern include short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complexes
body: ECG findings in Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) pattern include short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complexes. Asymptomatic patients have WPW pattern, and symptomatic patients have WPW syndrome. The most commonly associated supraventricular arrhythmia is atrioventricular reentrant (or reciprocating) tachycardia, a regular and narrow complex reentrant tachycardia.

title: Combining rigorous sodium restriction with the standard Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet can yield significant blood
body: Combining rigorous sodium restriction with the standard Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet can yield significant blood pressure lowering, approaching that of antihypertensive medication. Older individuals, women, black patients, and individuals with metabolic syndrome may be especially responsive.

title: There is typically a positive net clinical benefit of chronic anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation and high thromboembolic
body: There is typically a positive net clinical benefit of chronic anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation and high thromboembolic risk. Compared to warfarin, direct oral anticoagulants (eg, dabigatran, apixaban, rivaroxaban) are associated with similar or reduced rates of ischemic stroke and a reduced risk of major bleeding in patients with atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease with estimated glomerular filtration rate >30 mL∕min.

title: The third heart sound can be a normal finding in healthy young adults and does not signify an underlying abnormality in asymptomatic
body: The third heart sound can be a normal finding in healthy young adults and does not signify an underlying abnormality in asymptomatic patients. In contrast, the fourth heart sound can be heard in healthy older adults and its presence in young adults usually signifies an underlying abnormality. ■ ÷0 End © Resources

title: Risk stratification of asymptomatic patients with WPW pattern on ECG can be performed with noninvasive tests (eg, exercise testing or
body: Risk stratification of asymptomatic patients with WPW pattern on ECG can be performed with noninvasive tests (eg, exercise testing or procainamide challenge) and/or electrophysiologic study (EPS) to identify those at greatest risk of sudden cardiac death. Low-risk patients with intermittent loss of preexcitation during faster heart rates can be managed conservatively without further evaluation or treatment.

title: Noninvasive cardiac evaluation (eg, stress testing, echocardiography) is not indicated in most asymptomatic patients undergoing noncardiac
body: Noninvasive cardiac evaluation (eg, stress testing, echocardiography) is not indicated in most asymptomatic patients undergoing noncardiac surgery. It is reserved mainly for patients undergoing intermediate- or high-risk noncardiac surgery who have >1% estimated perioperative cardiac risk and poor functional capacity (<4 METS).

title: Obese patients with difficult-to-treat hypertension, nocturnal arrhythmias, or nocturnal angina should undergo evaluation for obstructive
body: Obese patients with difficult-to-treat hypertension, nocturnal arrhythmias, or nocturnal angina should undergo evaluation for obstructive sleep apnea using overnight polysomnography with electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring.

title: Beta blockers are indicated for patients with angina, myocardial infarction, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, or atrial
body: Beta blockers are indicated for patients with angina, myocardial infarction, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, or atrial fibrillation. In the absence of specific indications, beta blockers are not recommended in routine perioperative management.

title: Many antihypertensive medications are associated with an increased risk of gout, including diuretics, beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, and
body: Many antihypertensive medications are associated with an increased risk of gout, including diuretics, beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, and most angiotensin Il receptor blockers. In contrast, Iosartan and calcium channel blockers are safe to use in patients with gout and may be used together in patients who require combination therapy.

title: Thiazide diuretics can cause volume depletion and other metabolic effects, leading to orthostasis and increased risk of falls
body: Thiazide diuretics can cause volume depletion and other metabolic effects, leading to orthostasis and increased risk of falls. Thiazides should be discontinued in elderly patients with orthostatic hypotension and recurrent falls. Other interventions to reduce the risk of falls include a home safety assessment and directed exercise program. ■ I■a End © Resources

title: Statin myopathy commonly occurs due to drug-drug interactions and usually resolves after discontinuing the statin
body: Statin myopathy commonly occurs due to drug-drug interactions and usually resolves after discontinuing the statin. After resolution of myopathy, patients requiring aggressive cholesterol lowering should be restarted on an alternate statin with a lower myopathic potential (eg, rosuvastatin, pravastatin, fluvastatin).

title: An implantable loop recorder is a subcutaneous monitoring device for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias
body: An implantable loop recorder is a subcutaneous monitoring device for the detection of cardiac arrhythmias. It has a significantly higher diagnostic yield than 24-hour Holter monitoring in patients with infrequent (<1 event/month) symptoms of palpitations or syncope of undetermined etiology.

title: Tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy can develop in patients with persistent tachyarrhythmias and prolonged periods of rapid ventricular rate
body: Tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy can develop in patients with persistent tachyarrhythmias and prolonged periods of rapid ventricular rate. Treatment in such patients is aimed at restoration of sinus rhythm or aggressive control of ventricular rate, which often leads to significant or complete recovery of left ventricular function.

title: Antithrombotic therapy with aspirin and warfarin is recommended for all patients with mechanical aortic or mitral valve replacement to
body: Antithrombotic therapy with aspirin and warfarin is recommended for all patients with mechanical aortic or mitral valve replacement to reduce the rate of systemic thromboembolism. Target International Normalized Ratio (INR) for aortic valves without risk factors is 2.0-3.0. Target INR for mechanical aortic valves with high-risk features (eg, atrial fibrillation, left ventricular dysfunction [ejection fraction <30%], prior thromboembolism, presence of hypercoagulable state) and mechanical mitral valves is 2.5-3.5.

title: Mitral valve prolapse is associated with single or multiple non-ejection clicks and/or mid to late systolic murmur of mitral regurgitation
body: Mitral valve prolapse is associated with single or multiple non-ejection clicks and/or mid to late systolic murmur of mitral regurgitation. Standing or the Valsalva maneuver causes an earlier systolic click and longer murmur (due to decreased venous return and left ventricular volume). Squatting or leg elevation causes a delayed systolic click and shorter murmur (due to increased left ventricular volume).

title: ACEIs and ARBs are effective agents that can lower blood pressure and slow progression of proteinuric chronic kidney disease, even in
body: ACEIs and ARBs are effective agents that can lower blood pressure and slow progression of proteinuric chronic kidney disease, even in patients with serum creatinine concentrations up to 3 mg/dL. With careful dietary instruction and monitoring, ACEI therapy is appropriate for many of these patients.

title: Patients with phenotypic features of Turner syndrome should be evaluated for associated cardiovascular anomalies, including bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation of the aorta, and aortic root dilatation.
In the absence of a reversible cause (eg, myocardial ischemia), patients with complete (third-degree) atrioventricular block require
body: In the absence of a reversible cause (eg, myocardial ischemia), patients with complete (third-degree) atrioventricular block require permanent pacemaker placement regardless of whether the block is symptomatic or asymptomatic, is persistent or transient, or occurs at rest or with exercise.

title: A combination of hydralazine and nitrate therapy, in addition to the standard optimal therapy, has been shown to provide additional
body: A combination of hydralazine and nitrate therapy, in addition to the standard optimal therapy, has been shown to provide additional symptomatic and mortality benefit in African American patients with NYHA class III or IV heart failure due to LV systolic dysfunction (LV ejection fraction < 40%).

title: The addition of an aldosterone antagonist (eg, spironolactone, eplerenone) is indicated in patients who are post-ST elevation myocardial
body: The addition of an aldosterone antagonist (eg, spironolactone, eplerenone) is indicated in patients who are post-ST elevation myocardial infarction with left ventricular ejection fraction <40% and symptomatic heart failure or diabetes mellitus, and those with New York Heart Association functional class Il to IV heart failure and left ventricular ejection fraction <35%.

title: Postprandial hypotension is characterized by orthostatic symptoms within 2 hours after eating and is common in the elderly
body: Postprandial hypotension is characterized by orthostatic symptoms within 2 hours after eating and is common in the elderly. Decreased portion sizes, increased salt/water intake, low-carbohydrate meals, and avoidance of alcohol can improve symptoms. Octreotide can be considered for severely symptomatic or refractory cases.

title: Management of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction includes diuretics to reduce volume overload; maintenance of adequate blood
body: Management of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction includes diuretics to reduce volume overload; maintenance of adequate blood pressure and heart rate control; and coronary revascularization in patients with significant ischemia. In addition, exercise training has been shown to improve functional capacity and quality of life.

title: Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) with a biventricular pacing device is recommended in patients with severe LV systolic dysfunction
body: Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) with a biventricular pacing device is recommended in patients with severe LV systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction < 35%), NYHA class III-IV heart failure symptoms, and intraventricular conduction delay with QRS duration > 150 msec. CRT is optional with QRS >120 msec but < 150 msec. No clinical benefit with CRT has been noted in patients with systolic dysfunction and normal QRS duration (< 120 msec).

title: Secundum type atrial septal defects (ASD) present as pulmonic outflow murmurs in the young along with a fixed split second heart sound
body: Secundum type atrial septal defects (ASD) present as pulmonic outflow murmurs in the young along with a fixed split second heart sound. Uncorrected large ASDs can result in chronic right-sided volume overload leading to pulmonary hypertension.

title: Antibiotic prophylaxis for infective endocarditis is indicated in patients with high-risk cardiac conditions undergoing certain invasive
body: Antibiotic prophylaxis for infective endocarditis is indicated in patients with high-risk cardiac conditions undergoing certain invasive procedures. Previous infective endocarditis is considered a high-risk cardiac condition, and such patients should be counseled on the need for antibiotic prophylaxis when undergoing certain invasive procedures (eg, dental cleaning) in the future.

title: Thiazide diuretics are associated with the highest risk of new-onset diabetes in patients treated with antihypertensive drugs
body: Thiazide diuretics are associated with the highest risk of new-onset diabetes in patients treated with antihypertensive drugs. Beta blockers (not carvedilol) are also associated with increased diabetes risk. Calcium channel blockers, angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitors, and angiotensin-receptor blockers have no significant effect on glucose metabolism.

title: Pseudoaneurysm formation and/or rupture is a potentially catastrophic vascular complication of cardiac catheterization
body: Pseudoaneurysm formation and/or rupture is a potentially catastrophic vascular complication of cardiac catheterization. Patients with a tender or pulsatile mass at the catheter insertion site should be evaluated by duplex ultrasonography to assess for pseudoaneurysm. ■ >3 End © Resources

title: Infiltrative cardiomyopathies (most commonly amyloid and sarcoid) are suggested by a mass/voltage discrepancy on echocardiogram and
body: Infiltrative cardiomyopathies (most commonly amyloid and sarcoid) are suggested by a mass/voltage discrepancy on echocardiogram and electrocardiogram. Amyloid cardiomyopathy is usually seen in AL amyloidosis and is associated with other systemic manifestations such as heavy proteinuria. Diagnosis is confirmed by tissue biopsy and treatment is largely supportive.

title: Nocturnal cardiac arrhythmias, including bradycardia, sinus pauses, asystole, and tachyarrhythmias (eg, nonsustained
body: Nocturnal cardiac arrhythmias, including bradycardia, sinus pauses, asystole, and tachyarrhythmias (eg, nonsustained Ventriculartachycardia, atrial fibrillation), are common in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The diagnosis is made by a full-night polysomnography with ECG monitoring, and continuous positive airway pressure is used to treat OSA and suppress the arrhythmias.

title: Catheter ablation is recommended in patients with symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation who have failed treatment or become intolerant to one or more antiarrhythmic drugs.
Orthostatic hypotension is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality.
Percutaneous mitral balloon valvotomy is preferred in patients with symptomatic moderate or severe mitral stenosis with favorable valvular
body: Percutaneous mitral balloon valvotomy is preferred in patients with symptomatic moderate or severe mitral stenosis with favorable valvular morphology. It is contraindicated in patients with a moderate or severe degree of mitral regurgitation and/or left atrial thrombus.

title: Cardiac auscultation findings in patients with mitral stenosis include an accentuated first heart sound (S1), an opening snap after the
body: Cardiac auscultation findings in patients with mitral stenosis include an accentuated first heart sound (S1), an opening snap after the second heart sound (S2), and a mid-diastolic murmur or rumble with presystolic accentuation. The diastolic murmur of mitral stenosis is best heard at the cardiac apex using the bell of stethoscope while the patient lies in the left lateral decubitus position with their breath held at end expiration.

title: Prolonged QTc interval can be congenital or acquired, and increases risk Oftorsades de pointes, a form of polymorphic ventricular
body: Prolonged QTc interval can be congenital or acquired, and increases risk Oftorsades de pointes, a form of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Electrolyte abnormalities (eg, hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia) and certain drugs (eg, fluoroquinolones, antipsychotics) are the most common causes Ofacquired long QT syndrome.

title: Development of tolerance to the effects of nitrate with chronic exposure is a major limitation to its use as an effective antianginal
body: Development of tolerance to the effects of nitrate with chronic exposure is a major limitation to its use as an effective antianginal therapy. It can be prevented by adjusting the dosing schedule to provide an adequate number of drug-free intervals.

title: In the case of known or suspected infection of a cardiovascular implantable electronic device, removal of the device (generator and leads)
body: In the case of known or suspected infection of a cardiovascular implantable electronic device, removal of the device (generator and leads) is indicated if there is echocardiographic evidence of valve or lead vegetation, blood cultures positive for a common infective endocarditis-causing organism, or evidence of pocket infection. Removal of the device should be accompanied by an appropriate course of antibiotic therapy.

title: Antibiotic prophylaxis is not recommended for patients with mechanical heart valves or prior endocarditis undergoing low-risk procedures
body: Antibiotic prophylaxis is not recommended for patients with mechanical heart valves or prior endocarditis undergoing low-risk procedures such as endoscopy or vaginal/cesarean delivery. Patients undergoing high- risk procedures should receive amoxicillin or clindamycin 30-60 minutes prior to the procedure.

title: Pharmacologic radionuclide perfusion imaging should be performed to evaluate suspected coronary heart disease in patients with paced ventricular rhythm or left bundle branch block.
Lifestyle interventions that can reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease include regular physical exercise, a Mediterranean-style diet
body: Lifestyle interventions that can reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease include regular physical exercise, a Mediterranean-style diet, the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet, smoking cessation, and moderate but not excessive alcohol intake.

title: Patients with probable or definite hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in young athletes
body: Patients with probable or definite hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in young athletes, should be instructed to avoid competitive sports or high-intensity physical activity. In addition, symptomatic patients should be treated with beta blockers or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers; those refractory to medical therapy may require surgical septal myectomy or alcohol septal ablation. Patients at high risk for SCD should receive an implantable cardioverter­ defibrillator.

title: Coarctation of the aorta is a congenital narrowing of the descending aorta that causes upper body hypertension and may lead to lower body
body: Coarctation of the aorta is a congenital narrowing of the descending aorta that causes upper body hypertension and may lead to lower body claudication. The condition may remain undiagnosed until adulthood. It is associated with several other congenital cardiac defects, with bicuspid aortic valve being the most common.

title: Current guidelines recommend uninterrupted dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor (eg, Clopidogrel, prasugrel
body: Current guidelines recommend uninterrupted dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor (eg, Clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor) for at least 6-12 months after intracoronary stent placement. Whenever possible, elective noncardiac surgery should be postponed until the minimum recommended duration of dual antiplatelet therapy is completed.

title: "White coat" hypertension refers to elevated blood pressure in the physician's office with normal blood pressure readings elsewhere
body: "White coat" hypertension refers to elevated blood pressure in the physician's office with normal blood pressure readings elsewhere. In such patients, 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring can more fully characterize the blood pressure pattern and is a better predictor Offuture cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality than are office or home blood pressure measurements.

title: Aortic root disease, leading to aneurysmal dilation and dissection, is a common complication of Marfan syndrome, and is the main cause of
body: Aortic root disease, leading to aneurysmal dilation and dissection, is a common complication of Marfan syndrome, and is the main cause of morbidity and mortality in these patients. Transthoracic echocardiogram is recommended at initial diagnosis and at regular follow-up intervals.

title: ECG abnormalities commonly seen in patients with an atrial septal defect include first degree AV block, right axis deviation, and incomplete or complete right bundle branch block.
Atrial septal defect with moderate-to-large left-to-right shunt causes a mid-systolic ejection murmur due to increased flow through the pulmonic valve. ■ I■a End © Resources
In patients undergoing low risk surgical procedures (e.g., dental extraction, excisional skin biopsy, cataract surgery), warfarin
body: In patients undergoing low risk surgical procedures (e.g., dental extraction, excisional skin biopsy, cataract surgery), warfarin anticoagulation is associated with a minimal risk of serious bleeding and should be continued through the procedure.

title: Dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin system with both ACE inhibitors and ARBs does not provide any significant benefit to cardiovascular
body: Dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin system with both ACE inhibitors and ARBs does not provide any significant benefit to cardiovascular or all-cause mortality over ACE inhibitors alone. Dual therapy is associated with an increased risk for hyperkalemia, hypotension, and worsening renal function.

title: A number of drugs can depress the sinoatrial node and cause symptomatic sinus bradycardia
body: A number of drugs can depress the sinoatrial node and cause symptomatic sinus bradycardia. All medications with this potential should be withdrawn or discontinued in symptomatic patients before further evaluation or treatment. These common medications include digoxin, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, Clonidine, amiodarone, and donepezil.

title: In patients with a high-risk condition for perioperative thrombosis (eg, mechanical bileaflet aortic valve) managed with warfarin, it is
body: In patients with a high-risk condition for perioperative thrombosis (eg, mechanical bileaflet aortic valve) managed with warfarin, it is recommended that warfarin be held until the INR is <1.5 and then the procedure may be performed; bridging therapy is not indicated. However, patients with a very-high-risk thrombotic condition (eg, mechanical mitral valve) should undergo perioperative bridging with low- molecular-weight or unfractionated heparin.

title: Management of atrial fibrillation with a rhythm-control strategy is associated with higher potential risks of adverse drug effects compared
body: Management of atrial fibrillation with a rhythm-control strategy is associated with higher potential risks of adverse drug effects compared to a rate-control strategy. Anticoagulation should be continued in all high- risk patients, regardless of which strategy is implemented.

title: The United States Preventive Services Task Force recommends screening male active or former smokers age 65-75 with a one-time abdominal ultrasound to evaluate for abdominal aortic aneurysm.
In patients with asymptomatic LV systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction < 40%), ACE inhibitors (or angiotensin Il receptor blockers) and
body: In patients with asymptomatic LV systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction < 40%), ACE inhibitors (or angiotensin Il receptor blockers) and beta blockers delay the onset of symptoms and improve cardiac morbidity and mortality.

title: Renovascular hypertension due to renal artery stenosis should be suspected in patients with recurrent flash pulmonary edema, severe
body: Renovascular hypertension due to renal artery stenosis should be suspected in patients with recurrent flash pulmonary edema, severe hypertension, and atherosclerotic risk factors. These patients should be evaluated with renal Doppler ultrasound or CT or MR angiography.

title: Dual therapy with an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor and a calcium channel blocker is an effective treatment for hypertension in
body: Dual therapy with an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor and a calcium channel blocker is an effective treatment for hypertension in patients who require 2 drugs. Thiazide diuretics are useful as monotherapy for patients with mild hypertension or as add-on therapy for patients with uncontrolled blood pressure following initial treatment.

title: Intravenous milrinone (inotrope) can provide symptomatic relief in patients with severe decompensated heart failure with evidence of low
body: Intravenous milrinone (inotrope) can provide symptomatic relief in patients with severe decompensated heart failure with evidence of low output state, marginal systolic blood pressure, or inadequate response to vasodilator and diuretic therapy. Its use is associated with a significant increase in hypotensive episodes and atrial or ventricular arrhythmias, and a non-statistically significant increase in in-hospital and 60-day mortality.

title: Brugada syndrome can cause syncope and sudden cardiac death in patients with apparently structurally normal hearts
body: Brugada syndrome can cause syncope and sudden cardiac death in patients with apparently structurally normal hearts. EKG findings include > 2 mm of coved ST elevation in the right precordial leads with associated T wave inversion and right bundle branch block appearance. Implantable cardioverter defibrillator placement is indicated in patients with syncope.

title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is mostly commonly due to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction
body: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is mostly commonly due to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction. Optimal therapy for HFpEF involves blood pressure control, ventricular rate control, and fluid volume management with diuretics.

title: Antihypertensive therapy is recommended for patients age >60 with blood pressure >150/90 mm Hg
body: Antihypertensive therapy is recommended for patients age >60 with blood pressure >150/90 mm Hg. Long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are efficacious and well tolerated, and can be combined with an ACE inhibitor if a second agent is required. Other first-line medications include thiazide diuretics and angiotensin Il receptor blockers.

title: Cor pulmonale is right ventricular failure due to pulmonary or chest wall disease and usually presents with lower extremity edema
body: Cor pulmonale is right ventricular failure due to pulmonary or chest wall disease and usually presents with lower extremity edema, progressive dyspnea, and findings of right-sided heart disease (e.g., elevated jugular venous pressure, severe tricuspid regurgitation, RV heave, and loud S2). An ECG typically shows right axis deviation, RBBB, RVH, and right atrial enlargement. Echocardiography usually shows pulmonary hypertension and RVH, with paradoxical bulging of the septum into the left ventricle during systole.

title: ACE inhibitors can reduce the peripheral edema induced by calcium channel blockers (CCBs). CCB- associated peripheral edema responds poorly to diuretics as it is not due to salt and water retention.
Cardiogenic shock is the primary cause of death in patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction
body: Cardiogenic shock is the primary cause of death in patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction. Emergency revascularization with primary percutaneous coronary intervention or emergency coronary artery bypass grafting is the only therapy that has been shown to improve mortality in these patients.

title: Carotid sinus massage testing is recommended in patients age >40 with syncope of uncertain etiology to diagnose carotid sinus
body: Carotid sinus massage testing is recommended in patients age >40 with syncope of uncertain etiology to diagnose carotid sinus hypersensitivity. Carotid sinus massage is considered diagnostic if the patient develops syncope along with asystole for >3 seconds and/or there is a fall in systolic blood pressure of >50 mm Hg. It should be avoided in patients with ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis or carotid bruits and/or history of transient ischemic attack or stroke within the past 3 months. Treatment requires permanent pacing.

title: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is recommended for a minimum of 6-12 months following placement of either a bare-metal or drug-eluting
body: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is recommended for a minimum of 6-12 months following placement of either a bare-metal or drug-eluting stent. Elective surgeries should be delayed until the minimum duration of DAPT is completed. At that point, P2Y12 receptor blockers (eg, Clopidogrel, prasugrel) should be stopped prior to surgery and aspirin should be continued perioperatively unless there is a high risk of severe bleeding complications (eg, neurosurgery).

title: Cardiac catheterization is recommended prior to valve surgery to define the coronary anatomy, since approximately 40% of patients require
body: Cardiac catheterization is recommended prior to valve surgery to define the coronary anatomy, since approximately 40% of patients require concurrent coronary artery bypass grafting. Cardiac catheterization should be done with extreme caution in patients with severe calcific aortic stenosis (due to increased risk of embolic stroke), and only when noninvasive techniques do not provide the desired information.

title: Patients with mitral stenosis frequently develop atrial fibrillation as the disease progresses
body: Patients with mitral stenosis frequently develop atrial fibrillation as the disease progresses. The loss of atrial contraction with atrial fibrillation can lead to a rapid increase in left atrial pressure, and can cause rapid decompensation with symptomatic heart failure in otherwise asymptomatic patients.

title: An EKG showing a new-onset prolonged PR interval in patients with aortic valve endocarditis suggests a perivalvular abscess causing heart
body: An EKG showing a new-onset prolonged PR interval in patients with aortic valve endocarditis suggests a perivalvular abscess causing heart block. Transesophageal echocardiography can confirm the diagnosis, and surgery is the definitive therapy.

title: Moderate to severe mitral regurgitation and a reduced ejection fraction <50% are associated with increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events in patients with mitral valve prolapse.
Hypertension in pregnancy is defined as systolic blood pressure >140 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure >90 mm Hg
body: Hypertension in pregnancy is defined as systolic blood pressure >140 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure >90 mm Hg. Antihypertensive medications are indicated for patients with severe hypertension (>160∕110 mm Hg) or evidence of end-organ damage. Treatment of mild to moderate hypertension (140-159/90-109 mm Hg) does not improve fetal or maternal outcomes and is not recommended.

title: High-risk cardiac conditions that necessitate further evaluation and management prior to noncardiac surgery include unstable coronary
body: High-risk cardiac conditions that necessitate further evaluation and management prior to noncardiac surgery include unstable coronary syndrome, decompensated heart failure, significant arrhythmia, and severe valvular disease. Patients with known or suspected severe aortic stenosis should undergo transthoracic echocardiogram prior to any noncardiac surgery.

title: USPSTF recommends one-time screening for AAA with ultrasonography in men ages 65 to 75 with a smoking history
body: USPSTF recommends one-time screening for AAA with ultrasonography in men ages 65 to 75 with a smoking history. Surgical repair is indicated for AAA > 5.5 cm in diameter or an increase in diameter > 0.5 cm in a 6-month period and in all symptomatic patients.

title: Cardiac rehabilitation has been shown to significantly improve outcomes after myocardial infarction (Ml), with an improvement in functional
body: Cardiac rehabilitation has been shown to significantly improve outcomes after myocardial infarction (Ml), with an improvement in functional status and reduction in repeat hospitalization, recurrent Ml, and all-cause mortality. It is recommended for all patients as a part of a secondary prevention program after recent Ml. Routine pre-discharge stress testing of asymptomatic patients after successful revascularization is not recommended.

title: Occlusive peripheral artery disease typically presents with intermittent lower-extremity claudication increased with walking and relieved
body: Occlusive peripheral artery disease typically presents with intermittent lower-extremity claudication increased with walking and relieved promptly with rest. Physical examination may show diminished or absent femoral pulses, bruits over femoral or iliac arteries, cool extremities, prolonged venous filling time, skin or muscle atrophy, prolonged wound healing, and foot pallor with elevation of the affected leg.

title: A dry, hacking cough occurs in about 5%-20% of patients taking an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI)
body: A dry, hacking cough occurs in about 5%-20% of patients taking an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI). Discontinuing the ACEI usually stops the cough, which can take 1-4 weeks to resolve completely. Angiotensin receptor blocking agents have a lower frequency of cough (2%-4%) and are an alternate agent for blood pressure control.

title: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor-induced angioedema can occur at any time during treatment and is not dependent on the dosage
body: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor-induced angioedema can occur at any time during treatment and is not dependent on the dosage or type of ACE inhibitor used. Treatment includes discontinuation of the drug and supportive care. Patients who require the cardioprotective effect of ACE inhibitors can be switched safely to angiotensin Il receptor blockers with close monitoring.

title: Prior upper gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB), peptic ulcer disease, active Helicobacter pylori infection, and age >65 increase the risk of
body: Prior upper gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB), peptic ulcer disease, active Helicobacter pylori infection, and age >65 increase the risk of upper GIB in patients taking dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). Proton pump inhibitor therapy has been shown to decrease the risk of upper GIB in high-risk patients taking DAPT

title: Coxiella burnetii causes Q fever and is one of the most common causes of culture-negative endocarditis
body: Coxiella burnetii causes Q fever and is one of the most common causes of culture-negative endocarditis. The initial evaluation of patients with suspected Q-fever endocarditis should include transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography to identify valvular vegetations.

title: For patients in whom the etiology of syncope is unclear, an assessment for high-risk features (eg, new ECG changes) is important to guide
body: For patients in whom the etiology of syncope is unclear, an assessment for high-risk features (eg, new ECG changes) is important to guide the need for further investigation. Patients with a clear presentation of neurocardiogenic syncope (classic trigger and autonomic prodrome) can be reassured and discharged with outpatient follow-up.

title: Immediate synchronized cardioversion is the initial treatment of choice in patients with wide complex tachycardia associated with clinical and/or hemodynamic instability.
Stent thrombosis typically presents as an ST elevation myocardial infarction, usually within the first month after stent placement
body: Stent thrombosis typically presents as an ST elevation myocardial infarction, usually within the first month after stent placement. Premature discontinuation of antiplatelet therapy is the most important factor associated with stent thrombosis.

title: Flecainide and propafenone are class 1C antiarrhythmic agents with good efficacy and a favorable adverse effect profile
body: Flecainide and propafenone are class 1C antiarrhythmic agents with good efficacy and a favorable adverse effect profile. In the absence of ischemic or structural heart disease, they are the preferred agents to reduce the frequency and duration of episodes in patients with symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

title: Pulmonary artery catheterization provides hemodynamic data that is useful in differentiating between various causes of clinical
body: Pulmonary artery catheterization provides hemodynamic data that is useful in differentiating between various causes of clinical decompensation and shock in critically ill patients. Patients with hypovolemic shock will have low right atrial and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure, along with increased systemic vascular resistance. ■ I■a End © Resources

title: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention is recommended emergently for acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
body: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention is recommended emergently for acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. All such patients referred for emergency PCI should be pretreated with antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy as soon as possible.

title: Stress cardiomyopathy (Takotsubo cardiomyopathy) presents with chest pain, ischemic appearing EKG changes, mild elevations of cardiac
body: Stress cardiomyopathy (Takotsubo cardiomyopathy) presents with chest pain, ischemic appearing EKG changes, mild elevations of cardiac markers, transient cardiac dysfunction (usually at the apex with basilar compensation), and absence of obstructive coronary disease. Treatment is largely supportive with recovery of left ventricular function in 8-12 weeks in most cases.

title: An echocardiogram should be obtained early in patients with suspected infective endocarditis to identify the size and location of valvular
body: An echocardiogram should be obtained early in patients with suspected infective endocarditis to identify the size and location of valvular vegetations, the degree of valvular regurgitation, and associated complications (perivalvularabscess, leaflet perforation, and/or fistula formation).

title: Patients with cardiogenic shock will have a low cardiac index, increased systemic vascular resistance, and elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure. ■ I■a End © Resources
Radiofrequency ablation has an excellent success rate in restoring and maintaining sinus rhythm in patients with typical atrial flutter
body: Radiofrequency ablation has an excellent success rate in restoring and maintaining sinus rhythm in patients with typical atrial flutter. It is generally preferred over long-term antiarrhythmic agents as a safe and effective first-line treatment in such patients.

title: Treatment of patients with acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) includes supplemental oxygen and ventilation, diuresis with intravenous
body: Treatment of patients with acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) includes supplemental oxygen and ventilation, diuresis with intravenous diuretics, and vasodilators in patients with poor response to diuresis. Beta blockers and ACE inhibitors are useful for chronic heart failure due to left ventricular systolic dysfunction, but may worsen ADHF by exacerbating heart failure symptoms or by causing hemodynamic deterioration.

title: Chest pain associated with hypertension and a widened mediastinum is suggestive Ofthoracic aortic dissection which has high mortality
body: Chest pain associated with hypertension and a widened mediastinum is suggestive Ofthoracic aortic dissection which has high mortality. Timely diagnosis with chest computed tomography angiogram is essential before treating other causes of chest pain. TEE is preferred in patients with renal insufficiency.

title: Patients with left ventricular (LV) dysfunction due to myocardial infarction may experience recovery of LV function following coronary
body: Patients with left ventricular (LV) dysfunction due to myocardial infarction may experience recovery of LV function following coronary revascularization and treatment with optimal medical therapy. Therefore, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement should be reserved for patients with significant LV dysfunction that persists for 3 months following revascularization or 40 days following myocardial infarction without revascularization.

title: Patients with unstable angina/non-ST elevation myocardial infarction and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) should be managed with
body: Patients with unstable angina/non-ST elevation myocardial infarction and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) should be managed with pharmacologic therapy similar to that for patients without renal failure. However, enoxaparin and the glycoprotein llb/llla inhibitor eptifibatide are contraindicated in patients with ESRD.

title: The timing and quality of chest compressions is the most important predictor of survival in cardiac arrest patients and should be the first
body: The timing and quality of chest compressions is the most important predictor of survival in cardiac arrest patients and should be the first action. Compressions are continued until the shock is ready to be delivered for patients with Ventricularfibrillation. Subsequent important maneuvers (e.g., intubation, IV access, etc.) should be done either during chest compressions, after a full cycle, or during the briefest possible interruption.

title: Dissection involving the ascending aorta can result in acute aortic regurgitation (evidenced by a decrescendo diastolic murmur)
body: Dissection involving the ascending aorta can result in acute aortic regurgitation (evidenced by a decrescendo diastolic murmur). Intravenous beta blockers are preferred in patients with suspected aortic dissection to lower blood pressure and decrease left ventricular contractility to reduce aortic wall shear stress. Nitroprusside should be given only following adequate beta blockade.

title: Papillary muscle rupture may occur acutely or within 3-5 days of acute myocardial infarction, most commonly one that affects the inferior
body: Papillary muscle rupture may occur acutely or within 3-5 days of acute myocardial infarction, most commonly one that affects the inferior wall. Patients have rapid-onset pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock due to acute mitral regurgitation. A new holosystolic murmur is often, but not always, present.

title: Digoxin toxicity can be precipitated by recent illness that causes volume depletion or by drugs that impair renal clearance of digoxin
body: Digoxin toxicity can be precipitated by recent illness that causes volume depletion or by drugs that impair renal clearance of digoxin. Patients usually present with gastrointestinal disturbances, neurologic dysfunction, vision changes, electrolyte imbalances, and cardiac arrhythmias.

title: Stress cardiomyopathy (Takotsubo cardiomyopathy) presents with chest pain, ischemic appearing EKG changes, mild elevations of cardiac
body: Stress cardiomyopathy (Takotsubo cardiomyopathy) presents with chest pain, ischemic appearing EKG changes, mild elevations of cardiac markers, transient cardiac dysfunction (usually apical with basilar compensation), and absence of obstructive coronary disease. It is most commonly seen in post­ menopausal women after an intense emotional or physical stressor. Treatment is largely supportive with recovery of left ventricular function in 1-4 weeks in most cases.

title: Pericardial tamponade is due to fluid accumulation in the pericardium and causes hypotension by preventing filling of both the left and
body: Pericardial tamponade is due to fluid accumulation in the pericardium and causes hypotension by preventing filling of both the left and right ventricles. Classic physical findings of tamponade include pulsus paradoxus, rapid "x" descent in the neck veins, hypotension, and tachycardia. Treatment involves prompt removal of the pericardial fluid, usually with pericardiocentesis.

title: Post-cardiac injury syndrome (PCIS) is commonly seen after cardiac surgery and is likely an autoimmune reaction, causing inflammation and
body: Post-cardiac injury syndrome (PCIS) is commonly seen after cardiac surgery and is likely an autoimmune reaction, causing inflammation and presenting with the typical symptoms of pericarditis. Treatment includes NSAIDs or steroids. Prophylactic colchicine after cardiac surgery significantly decreases the incidence of PCIS.

title: Although aortic dissections are classically associated with tearing chest pain and blood pressure variation, a minority of patients can
body: Although aortic dissections are classically associated with tearing chest pain and blood pressure variation, a minority of patients can present with subtle clinical findings, including faint diastolic murmur of aortic regurgitation, waxing and waning neurologic deficits, Horner syndrome, or vocal cord paralysis. Transesophageal echocardiogram, MR angiography, or CT angiography may be used to establish diagnosis.

title: Ischemic stroke is an absolute contraindication to fibrinolytic therapy if the stroke occurred within the last 3 months and a relative
body: Ischemic stroke is an absolute contraindication to fibrinolytic therapy if the stroke occurred within the last 3 months and a relative contraindication if it occurred more than 3 months ago. Prior history of intracranial hemorrhage (time unlimited) is also an absolute contraindication.

title: Right atrial collapse during end diastole is the earliest and most sensitive echocardiographic sign of cardiac tamponade
body: Right atrial collapse during end diastole is the earliest and most sensitive echocardiographic sign of cardiac tamponade. Right ventricular diastolic collapse is less sensitive than right atrial diastolic collapse but is highly specific for cardiac tamponade.

title: Complete heart block may present with syncope, especially in older patients or those with structural heart disease
body: Complete heart block may present with syncope, especially in older patients or those with structural heart disease. Patients should be evaluated for reversible causes but usually require a permanent pacemaker. Acutely symptomatic patients may require atropine or temporary pacing depending on QRS width.

title: The ECG in patients with acute pericarditis evolves serially over time
body: The ECG in patients with acute pericarditis evolves serially over time. In the early stages, there is diffuse ST segment elevation present along with PR segment elevation in aVR. This is followed by diffuse T wave inversion over the next several days, with eventual normalization of the ECG over several weeks or persistent T wave inversion.

title: Hypertensive urgency is defined as severe hypertension (systolic blood pressure >180 mm Hg and/or diastolic blood pressure >120 mm Hg)
body: Hypertensive urgency is defined as severe hypertension (systolic blood pressure >180 mm Hg and/or diastolic blood pressure >120 mm Hg) without signs or symptoms of acute end-organ damage. Patients with hypertensive urgency should receive oral antihypertensive medications in a monitored setting to gradually lower blood pressure over several hours to days.

title: Cocaine can cause chest pain through multiple mechanisms that simultaneously increase oxygen demand, decrease oxygen supply, and increase
body: Cocaine can cause chest pain through multiple mechanisms that simultaneously increase oxygen demand, decrease oxygen supply, and increase thrombogenicity. Beta blockers are contraindicated in acute cocaine-induced chest pain. Benzodiazepines, aspirin, and nitrates are first line therapy. Patients should also receive immediate cardiac catheterization with reperfusion therapy when presenting with acute ST elevation Ml.

title: Noninvasive cardiac evaluation (eg, stress testing, echocardiography) is not indicated in most asymptomatic patients undergoing noncardiac
body: Noninvasive cardiac evaluation (eg, stress testing, echocardiography) is not indicated in most asymptomatic patients undergoing noncardiac surgery. It is reserved mainly for patients undergoing intermediate- or high-risk noncardiac surgery who have >1% estimated perioperative cardiac risk and poor functional capacity (<4 METS).

title: Tall, peaked T waves with shortened QT interval are the earliest ECG manifestations of hyperkalemia
body: Tall, peaked T waves with shortened QT interval are the earliest ECG manifestations of hyperkalemia. PR interval prolongation, atrial asystole, and QRS widening with progression to sine wave pattern occur with worsening hyperkalemia. Treatment involves acute drug therapy (eg, calcium, insulin, glucose) or hemodialysis in more severe cases.

title: Pericarditis and myopericarditis share etiologies and are typically viral or idiopathic in nature
body: Pericarditis and myopericarditis share etiologies and are typically viral or idiopathic in nature. Treatment is directed at the underlying cause, but initial treatment of pericarditis with a combination of nonsteroidal anti­ inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and colchicine is recommended. Glucocorticoids are associated with higher rates of recurrent pericarditis and should be used only in refractory disease, in patients in whom NSAIDs are contraindicated, or for specific underlying causes.

title: Multifocal atrial tachycardia most commonly occurs in elderly patients with an exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease (eg, chronic
body: Multifocal atrial tachycardia most commonly occurs in elderly patients with an exacerbation of underlying pulmonary disease (eg, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), and is characterized by ECG showing an atrial rate >100∕min, irregular R-R intervals, and >3 distinct P wave morphologies. Treatment is aimed at correcting the underlying inciting disturbance.

title: BNP < 100 pg/mL and NT-proBNP < 300 pg/mL are highly predictive for excluding heart failure, and BNP > 400 pg/mL and NT-proBNP > 900 pg/mL
body: BNP < 100 pg/mL and NT-proBNP < 300 pg/mL are highly predictive for excluding heart failure, and BNP > 400 pg/mL and NT-proBNP > 900 pg/mL are accurate for diagnosing heart failure. Higher hormone levels are found in older individuals and those with chronic kidney disease. Lower hormone levels are seen in obese patients and should be interpreted with caution.

title: Observational studies have shown that the strongest predictors of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) expansion and rupture are large aneurysm
body: Observational studies have shown that the strongest predictors of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) expansion and rupture are large aneurysm diameter, rapid rate of expansion, and active cigarette smoking. Active cigarette smoking is associated with the highest rate of aneurysmal expansion and rupture. Referral for AAA repair is recommended for asymptomatic patients with aneurysmal diameter > 5.5 cm.

title: Patients with rheumatic mitral stenosis (MS) and atrial fibrillation (AF) have a very high risk of systemic thromboembolism
body: Patients with rheumatic mitral stenosis (MS) and atrial fibrillation (AF) have a very high risk of systemic thromboembolism. CHADS2 risk stratification criteria should not be used to assess the risk of systemic thromboembolism in such patients. Oral anticoagulation with warfarin with goal International Normalized Ratio of 2.5 (range 2.0-3.0) is recommended for patients with MS who develop AF or have a prior embolic event or left atrial thrombus.

title: Patients with hyperkalemia and significant abnormalities on ECG should receive intravenous calcium gluconate to rapidly antagonize the cell
body: Patients with hyperkalemia and significant abnormalities on ECG should receive intravenous calcium gluconate to rapidly antagonize the cell membrane effects of potassium. The hyperkalemia can then be corrected with β-2 agonists and/or insulin plus glucose.

title: Acute type A aortic dissections can extend into the pericardial space and cause hemopericardium, cardiac tamponade, and shock
body: Acute type A aortic dissections can extend into the pericardial space and cause hemopericardium, cardiac tamponade, and shock. Such patients should be evaluated by urgent bedside transthoracic echocardiography and immediately sent for definitive surgical management. Pericardiocentesis is likely to be harmful in patients with cardiac tamponade complicating type A aortic dissection.

title: In patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, anticoagulation with target-specific oral anticoagulants is associated with a lower risk of intracranial hemorrhage when compared to warfarin.
Patients with atrial fibrillation for >48 hours who require nonemergent cardioversion should undergo transesophageal echocardiogram to
body: Patients with atrial fibrillation for >48 hours who require nonemergent cardioversion should undergo transesophageal echocardiogram to assess for left atrial appendage thrombus. Patients in whom thrombus is ruled out can immediately proceed with cardioversion accompanied by periprocedural anticoagulation; otherwise, patients should receive ≥3 weeks of anticoagulation prior to cardioversion.

title: Constrictive pericarditis is an important cause of right heart failure following viral pericarditis, cardiac surgery, or radiation therapy
body: Constrictive pericarditis is an important cause of right heart failure following viral pericarditis, cardiac surgery, or radiation therapy. Diagnosis is made with chest radiograph (pericardial calcification), ECG (low- voltage QRS), echocardiogram (pericardial thickening, abnormal septal motion, biatrial enlargement) and sometimes right heart catheterization.

title: Severe aortic stenosis is a major clinical predictor of adverse perioperative outcomes in patients undergoing noncardiac surgery
body: Severe aortic stenosis is a major clinical predictor of adverse perioperative outcomes in patients undergoing noncardiac surgery. Patients with severe aortic stenosis who require emergency surgery should proceed with surgery, with the addition of invasive hemodynamic monitoring to ensure adequate intravascular volume, preload, and systemic vascular resistance.

title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFPEF) accounts for nearly 50% of hospitalized patients with heart failure
body: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFPEF) accounts for nearly 50% of hospitalized patients with heart failure. Diastolic heart failure is a common cause and therapeutic goals include optimizing volume control with salt restriction and diuretics, adequate blood pressure control, rate control in patients with atrial fibrillation, and coronary revascularization in patients with symptomatic or asymptomatic myocardial ischemia.

title: Cardioselective beta blockers (eg, metoprolol) have been found to be well tolerated in patients with underlying obstructive lung disease
body: Cardioselective beta blockers (eg, metoprolol) have been found to be well tolerated in patients with underlying obstructive lung disease. Combined beta and alpha receptor beta blockers (eg, carvedilol) have also been generally well tolerated in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients but less so in those with asthma. Use of nonselective beta blockers (eg, propranolol, nadolol, sotalol, timolol) should be avoided due to the higher likelihood of increased airway resistance.

title: Acute coronary syndrome patients with high-risk features, ST-segment depression, and/or positive cardiac biomarkers should be managed with
body: Acute coronary syndrome patients with high-risk features, ST-segment depression, and/or positive cardiac biomarkers should be managed with an early invasive approach using coronary angiography and primary percutaneous coronary intervention to reduce the rate of recurrent myocardial infarction and all-cause mortality.

title: Patients with mitral stenosis and atrial fibrillation (paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent) are at high risk of thromboembolic stroke and
body: Patients with mitral stenosis and atrial fibrillation (paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent) are at high risk of thromboembolic stroke and should receive long-term anticoagulation with warfarin. More recently developed oral anticoagulants (factor Xa inhibitors and direct thrombin inhibitors) are not approved for use in patients with valvular atrial fibrillation.

title: Pheochromocytoma may be clinically silent in many patients until symptoms are unmasked by a precipitating factor (eg, anesthesia induction)
body: Pheochromocytoma may be clinically silent in many patients until symptoms are unmasked by a precipitating factor (eg, anesthesia induction). For initial diagnostic testing, plasma and urine metanephrines should be measured. Ifthese are elevated, CT scan or MRI should be performed to check for an adrenal mass.
