title: Patients with new-onset atrial fibrillation (especially with rapid ventricular response) should always be evaluated for an underlying cause
body: Patients with new-onset atrial fibrillation (especially with rapid ventricular response) should always be evaluated for an underlying cause or trigger (eg, sepsis, hypoxia, congestive heart failure, poorly controlled hypertension, hyperthyroidism, valvular heart disease). Treating the underlying cause may restore sinus rhythm and avert the need for cardioversion.

title: Reocclusion can develop in about 20%-30% of patients with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction after initial successful reperfusion
body: Reocclusion can develop in about 20%-30% of patients with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction after initial successful reperfusion with fibrinolytic therapy. All patients who have received fibrinolytic therapy in a hospital or ambulance without capabilities for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) should be transferred immediately to a PCI-capable hospital.

title: Digoxin has a small therapeutic window, and decreased renal function is a common precipitant of toxicity
body: Digoxin has a small therapeutic window, and decreased renal function is a common precipitant of toxicity. Clinical manifestations of digoxin toxicity include gastrointestinal disturbance, neurologic and visual dysfunction, electrolyte imbalance, and cardiac arrhythmia. Treatment involves intravenous hydration; in addition, patients with life-threatening arrhythmia, end-organ dysfunction, or hyperkalemia should be given digoxin-specific antibody (Fab) fragments.

title: Peri-infarction pericarditis refers to onset of acute pericarditis within days after an acute myocardial infarction
body: Peri-infarction pericarditis refers to onset of acute pericarditis within days after an acute myocardial infarction. It is usually transient, and symptomatic patients should be managed with higher doses of aspirin. The use of anticoagulants, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and corticosteroids should be avoided in this setting.

title: Papillary muscle rupture (with acute mitral regurgitation) is a life-threatening complication of acute myocardial infarction
body: Papillary muscle rupture (with acute mitral regurgitation) is a life-threatening complication of acute myocardial infarction. It presents with sudden onset of hypotension and pulmonary edema with a hyperdynamic precordium and a systolic murmur. The murmur can be soft or inaudible (silent mitral regurgitation) in up to 50% of patients.

title: Retroperitoneal hemorrhage is the most common cause of unexpected mortality in patients undergoing cardiac catheterization
body: Retroperitoneal hemorrhage is the most common cause of unexpected mortality in patients undergoing cardiac catheterization. Bleeding results from an arterial puncture above the inguinal ligament. It often presents with sudden onset hypotension and a drop in hemoglobin, and does not usually cease with manual compression.

title: Central sleep apnea with Cheyne-Stokes breathing is a potential complication in patients with heart failure. Treatment includes positive airway pressure therapy and supplemental oxygen.
In preparation for coronary artery bypass graft, P2Y12 inhibitors (eg, Clopidogrel, ticagrelor, prasugrel) should be discontinued at least
body: In preparation for coronary artery bypass graft, P2Y12 inhibitors (eg, Clopidogrel, ticagrelor, prasugrel) should be discontinued at least 5-7 days before surgery to reduce the risk of bleeding complications. Aspirin reduces the rate of early graft occlusion and overall cardiovascular morbidity and mortality and should be continued.

title: Patients with RVMI present with hypotension, elevated jugular venous pressure, and clear lung fields in the setting of inferior wall ML
body: Patients with RVMI present with hypotension, elevated jugular venous pressure, and clear lung fields in the setting of inferior wall ML Patients with evidence of low cardiac output and hypotension should be treated initially with a bolus of intravenous fluid to improve right ventricular preload and forward flow of blood to the left ventricle.

title: Mobitz type I and Mobitz type Il second-degree atrioventricular (AV) block cannot be differentiated when 2:1 atrioventricular block is
body: Mobitz type I and Mobitz type Il second-degree atrioventricular (AV) block cannot be differentiated when 2:1 atrioventricular block is present on ECG. Symptomatic second-degree AV block in the absence of a reversible cause necessitates placement of a permanent pacemaker regardless of whether Mobitz type I or Mobitz type Il AV block is present.

title: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is a rare autosomal dominant disorder that usually presents with frequent spontaneous epistaxis (most
body: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is a rare autosomal dominant disorder that usually presents with frequent spontaneous epistaxis (most common), mucocutaneous telangiectasias, gastrointestinal bleeding, and iron deficiency anemia. Patients can also develop arteriovenous malformations in many organs, including the lung, brain, and liver.

title: Guttate psoriasis is a variant of psoriasis characterized by numerous small erythematous papules and plaques with a fine scale
body: Guttate psoriasis is a variant of psoriasis characterized by numerous small erythematous papules and plaques with a fine scale. It typically occurs 2-3 weeks after streptococcal infection (eg, pharyngitis, cellulitis) and is commonly seen in children and young adults. Diagnosis is made primarily by clinical examination.

title: Salicylic acid or liquid nitrogen application is effective for the treatment for many warts
body: Salicylic acid or liquid nitrogen application is effective for the treatment for many warts. However, liquid nitrogen use is contraindicated in patients with periungual warts due to the risk of nail bed dystrophy.

title: Hyperhidrosis is excessive sweating beyond that needed for normal thermoregulation
body: Hyperhidrosis is excessive sweating beyond that needed for normal thermoregulation. It most commonly affects the axillae, face, and palms/soles. Most cases are bilateral and idiopathic (primary hyperhidrosis). The majority of patients can be managed with topical aluminum chloride solution.

title: Telogen effluvium causes diffuse, noninflammatory hair loss
body: Telogen effluvium causes diffuse, noninflammatory hair loss. It is often triggered by a stressful event, such as severe weight loss, pregnancy, major illness or surgery, or psychiatric trauma. Patients have thinning of the hair across the scalp and a positive hair pull test. Telogen effluvium is self-limited but may take up to a year to resolve completely.

title: Pityriasis rosea is characterized by mildly pruritic, salmon-colored plaques involving the trunk, neck, and proximal limbs
body: Pityriasis rosea is characterized by mildly pruritic, salmon-colored plaques involving the trunk, neck, and proximal limbs. It typically begins with a single large lesion (herald patch). The diagnosis is usually made based on clinical features. The condition is self-limited, and most patients require only reassurance and symptomatic treatment.

title: Initial treatment of chronic urticaria includes second-generation antihistamines (eg, loratadine)
body: Initial treatment of chronic urticaria includes second-generation antihistamines (eg, loratadine). Treatment for refractory patients includes first-generation antihistamines, leukotriene receptor antagonists, H2 blockers, or a brief course of oral steroids.

title: Pyoderma gangrenosum is a rapidly progressing, painful Ulcerwith a purulent base and violaceous borders
body: Pyoderma gangrenosum is a rapidly progressing, painful Ulcerwith a purulent base and violaceous borders. More than 50% of patients have associated systemic disease (eg, inflammatory bowel disease). Treatment usually requires local or systemic corticosteroids.

title: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a chronic relapsing disorder that is most common in Intertriginous areas
body: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a chronic relapsing disorder that is most common in Intertriginous areas. It begins as a solitary, painful nodule that can progress to an abscess with subsequent drainage. The symptoms typically improve after drainage, but recurrent nodules can lead to sinus tracts, comedones, and scarring.

title: Mild to moderate plaque psoriasis is treated with high-potency topical steroids and emollients
body: Mild to moderate plaque psoriasis is treated with high-potency topical steroids and emollients. Moderate to severe disease (involvement of 5%-10% of body surface area or disabling lesions of face, palm, or sole) usually requires systemic therapy (methotrexate, biologic immunomodulator such as etanercept) or phototherapy.

title: Miliaria ("heat rash") is due to blockage of the eccrine sweat ducts in the setting of excess heat or humidity
body: Miliaria ("heat rash") is due to blockage of the eccrine sweat ducts in the setting of excess heat or humidity. It most often occurs in children but can also occur in bedridden adults with fever, increased sweating, or tight-fitting clothing. Typical lesions can range from small, thin-walled vesicles to erythematous papules and pustules.

title: Patients with suspected Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis should be immediately evaluated and managed in a hospital
body: Patients with suspected Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis should be immediately evaluated and managed in a hospital setting. In addition, immediate discontinuation of the suspected causative medication(s) and all other unnecessary medications is mandatory.

title: Melanocytic nevi are benign pigmented lesions that are usually tan to jet black in color, tend to be < 6 mm in diameter, and present with a
body: Melanocytic nevi are benign pigmented lesions that are usually tan to jet black in color, tend to be < 6 mm in diameter, and present with a symmetric and homogeneous surface with sharp borders. Melanoma should be ruled out in all pigmented lesions. Melanocytic nevi usually require no treatment other than periodic observation as most remain benign.

title: Intertrigo is most commonly due to Candida infection and presents as erythematous plaques and erosions in skinfolds of intertriginous
body: Intertrigo is most commonly due to Candida infection and presents as erythematous plaques and erosions in skinfolds of intertriginous regions. Topical antifungals (eg, miconazole, nystatin, terbinafine) are the preferred initial therapy.

title: Erythrasma is a superficial skin infection caused by Corynebacterium minutissimum
body: Erythrasma is a superficial skin infection caused by Corynebacterium minutissimum. The lesions are well- demarcated, red-brown, pruritic, and most common in moist interdigital or Intertriginous areas. Diagnosis is clinical and can be confirmed by the lesions' red fluorescence under a Wood's lamp. Limited infection is treated with topical antibiotics, while multisite disease may require oral macrolides.

title: Senile (solar) purpura should be suspected when an older patient has easy bruising limited to the forearms and hands
body: Senile (solar) purpura should be suspected when an older patient has easy bruising limited to the forearms and hands. Lesions arise due to blood vessel fragility after years of sun-related dermal damage. Laboratory studies are generally normal; the condition is benign and requires no treatment. He says it has been there for "a while" but his daughter insisted on having it examined. The patient has a history of colon cancer treated with left hemicolectomy 7 years ago. He takes daily vitamin D and calcium supplements. Physical examination findings are shown in the photograph below. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? K. Actinic keratosis [54%] B. Psoriasis [0%] C. Seborrheic dermatitis [21 %] D. Seborrheic keratosis [9%] E. Solar lentigo [13%] Omitted Correct answer A Illl 54% Answered correctly 10 SecondS Time Spent 02/02/2019 Last Updated Explanation This patient has a number of actinic keratoses (AKs), also known as solar keratoses. AKs often present as rough, scaly, erythematous macules or papules that are most commonly found on fair-skinned individuals. Sun-damaged skin and chronic sun exposure are major risk factors for development of these lesions, accounting for their usual detection on the balding scalp, face, lateral neck, and distal upper or lower extremities. AKs are often easier to feel than to see, making palpation a key element of the physical examination. AKs may progress to squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Although the likelihood of progression of an individual AK to SCC is low, approximately 60% of cutaneous SCCs arise from preexisting AKs. Biopsy is indicated if the diagnosis is unclear or for lesions > 1 cm in diameter, indurated, ulcerated, tender, or rapidly growing or for lesions that fail to respond to appropriate therapy. Treatment options for AKs include destructive therapies (cryosurgery, curettage, shave removal), topical medications (topical 5-fluorouracil, imiquimod), and photodynamic therapy. Prevention (eg, sunblock, avoidance of sun exposure, protective clothing) and continuous monitoring for cutaneous malignancies are important in all patients with a history of AKs. (Choice B) Psoriasis is a common chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by sharply demarcated papules and rounded plaques covered with a silvery scale. The most common areas of eruption include the elbows, knees, gluteal cleft, and scalp. (Choice C) Seborrheic dermatitis affects areas of the body rich with sebaceous glands such as the face (especially the eyebrows, nasolabial folds, and external ear canal/posterior ear), scalp, and chest. Affected areas are pruritic and develop erythematous plaques with fine, loose, greasy scales. Dandruff is a mild form of seborrheic dermatitis. More severe, atypical, and diffuse forms of seborrheic dermatitis can be seen in HIV patients with low CD4 counts. (Choice D) Seborrheic keratoses (SKs) are very common benign growths that have a warty or Cerebriform, stuck-on appearance. (Choice E) Solar Ientigines, also known as age spots or liver spots, are benign, asymptomatic, pigmented macules that appear in fair-skinned individuals on sun-exposed areas of the skin, including the face, upper chest, shoulders, forearms, and dorsal hands. They may coalesce to form irregular patches. In contrast to lentigo maligna, a malignant lesion of melanocytic origin, solar Ientigines usually show a more even distribution of pigment, a lighter color, and smoother borders and are relatively stable in size and shape.

title: Actinic keratosis is a pre-malignant lesion characterized by rough, scaly, erythematous macules or papules seen typically on chronically
body: Actinic keratosis is a pre-malignant lesion characterized by rough, scaly, erythematous macules or papules seen typically on chronically sun-exposed skin. Treatment options include destructive therapies (cryosurgery, curettage, shave removal), topical medications (topical 5-fluorouracil, imiquimod), and photodynamic therapy. Prevention and regular monitoring for cutaneous malignancies (eg, squamous cell carcinoma) are also important in patients with a history of actinic keratosis.

title: Discrete, circular patches of non-inflamed and non-scarring hair loss are usually due to alopecia areata
body: Discrete, circular patches of non-inflamed and non-scarring hair loss are usually due to alopecia areata. Characteristic exclamation point hairs are seen at the margins. First-line therapy is intralesional corticosteroids.

title: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea is characterized by erythema in the nose and medial cheeks, flushing, telangiectasias, and burning
body: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea is characterized by erythema in the nose and medial cheeks, flushing, telangiectasias, and burning sensations. Initial management includes mild cleansers, sunscreen, and avoidance of triggers that cause flushing (eg, hot or spicy foods, alcohol, temperature extremes, emotional distress).

title: Seborrheic dermatitis that is severe and extensive should prompt testing for HIV
body: Seborrheic dermatitis that is severe and extensive should prompt testing for HIV. In this patient population, it can involve unusual sites (eg, extremities) and is often resistant to commonly prescribed therapy. Treatment includes antifungals and corticosteroids, often for a prolonged period.

title: Mild superficial wound infections in immunocompetent patients may be treated with topical mupirocin
body: Mild superficial wound infections in immunocompetent patients may be treated with topical mupirocin. More extensive cellulitis (>2 cm from the wound margin) or infection of deep tissues should be treated with systemic antibiotics.

title: Seborrheic keratoses (SKs) are very common benign growths with a warty or cerebriform, "stuck-on" appearance
body: Seborrheic keratoses (SKs) are very common benign growths with a warty or cerebriform, "stuck-on" appearance. The explosive onset of numerous SKs has been associated with a variety of malignancies, particularly gastrointestinal cancers. No therapy is required unless the SKs become irritated or the patient desires them removed for cosmetic reasons.

title: Onychomycosis can be difficult to distinguish from other nail dystrophies (eg, psoriasis, eczema, lichen planus)
body: Onychomycosis can be difficult to distinguish from other nail dystrophies (eg, psoriasis, eczema, lichen planus). Potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation of nail scrapings can confirm the diagnosis prior to initiation of oral antifungal therapy.

title: Keratoacanthoma presents as a solitary, dome-shaped nodule with a central hyperkeratotic, keratinous plug
body: Keratoacanthoma presents as a solitary, dome-shaped nodule with a central hyperkeratotic, keratinous plug. These lesions grow rapidly over a 4- to 9-month period, stabilize, and spontaneously regress. Due to the difficulty of distinguishing KA clinically from squamous cell carcinoma, all lesions should be biopsied.

title: Molluscum contagiosum is due to a poxvirus and can present as a firm, dome-shaped papule with a shiny surface and central indentation or
body: Molluscum contagiosum is due to a poxvirus and can present as a firm, dome-shaped papule with a shiny surface and central indentation or umbilication. Patients with multiple lesions, widespread disease, or facial involvement should undergo HIV testing.

title: Rosacea should be suspected in patients age 30-60 with erythema and telangiectasias over the cheeks, nose, and chin
body: Rosacea should be suspected in patients age 30-60 with erythema and telangiectasias over the cheeks, nose, and chin. Papules and pustules may also be present. A topical antibiotic such as metronidazole is the most frequently prescribed initial therapy for mild-to-moderate rosacea. Oral antibiotics may be needed for more severe disease (especially if it is papulopustular).

title: Because nail dystrophies caused by other diseases (eg, psoriasis, lichen planus) can mimic the appearance of onychomycosis, confirmation
body: Because nail dystrophies caused by other diseases (eg, psoriasis, lichen planus) can mimic the appearance of onychomycosis, confirmation with potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation or culture of nail scrapings is recommended. Iftherapy is undertaken for toenail fungal disease, optimal results are obtained with 3 months of oral terbinafine.

title: Vitiligo is an autoimmune skin disease causing partial or complete loss of melanocytes in affected skin
body: Vitiligo is an autoimmune skin disease causing partial or complete loss of melanocytes in affected skin. It presents as depigmented patches and is associated most frequently with thyroid disorders and type I diabetes.

title: Abrupt onset of severe psoriasis is often seen in patients with HIV infection and may be the initial manifestation of the disease
body: Abrupt onset of severe psoriasis is often seen in patients with HIV infection and may be the initial manifestation of the disease. Psoriasis in HIV commonly affects intertriginous, rather than extensor, skin and can be associated with systemic symptoms. Rapid onset of severe psoriasis warrants screening for HIV.

title: Necrobiosis lipoidica diabeticorum is a skin condition seen frequently in patients with diabetes
body: Necrobiosis lipoidica diabeticorum is a skin condition seen frequently in patients with diabetes. The lesions typically occur in the pretibial areas and manifest as annular lesions with a yellowish-brown hue, dilated blood vessels, and central epidermal atrophy.

title: Tinea versicolor is a superficial yeast infection that can present as hypopigmented, hyperpigmented, or erythematous macules and patches
body: Tinea versicolor is a superficial yeast infection that can present as hypopigmented, hyperpigmented, or erythematous macules and patches. Lesions are frequently seen on oily areas of the skin such as the chest, back, upper arms, neck, and Intertriginous areas. Diagnosis is established by KOH preparation of a skin scraping. Treatment for limited disease is a topical antifungal agent. Systemic therapy is indicated for patients with widespread disease, recurrent tinea versicolor, or those who have failed topical therapy.

title: Toxicodendron dermatitis (poison ivy/poison oak) is the most common cause of contact dermatitis
body: Toxicodendron dermatitis (poison ivy/poison oak) is the most common cause of contact dermatitis. Treatment includes topical mid- to high-potency corticosteroids for limited disease or oral corticosteroids for severe or widespread disease. Treatment should be continued for 2-3 weeks.

title: Pitting and onycholysis of the nail are typical manifestations of psoriasis
body: Pitting and onycholysis of the nail are typical manifestations of psoriasis. Nail involvement in psoriasis increases the risk of psoriatic arthritis. Mild nail psoriasis involving 1 or 2 digits can be treated with topical corticosteroids and/or vitamin D analogs, but widespread nail involvement generally warrants systemic therapy.

title: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus is characterized by a photosensitive rash with small, erythematous, and slightly scaly papules that
body: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus is characterized by a photosensitive rash with small, erythematous, and slightly scaly papules that can coalesce into annular patterns with crusted margins. Patients usually have positive anti-Ro/SSA antibodies, normal complement levels, and no significant hematologic abnormalities.

title: Seborrheic dermatitis typically presents as erythematous plaques with fine, loose, yellow, greasy scales on areas of body rich in sebaceous
body: Seborrheic dermatitis typically presents as erythematous plaques with fine, loose, yellow, greasy scales on areas of body rich in sebaceous glands. All age groups are affected, but it is seen with increased frequency in patients with Parkinson disease and HIV. Treatment consists of low-potency corticosteroids, antifungal creams, or a combination of these.

title: Erythema multiforme is an acute, often recurrent, mucocutaneous eruption that usually follows a bacterial or viral infection, especially
body: Erythema multiforme is an acute, often recurrent, mucocutaneous eruption that usually follows a bacterial or viral infection, especially herpes simplex virus. Target-shaped lesions are the characteristic finding, and treatment is primarily symptomatic.

title: Venous lakes are benign lesions commonly seen on the lips and ears of elderly patients
body: Venous lakes are benign lesions commonly seen on the lips and ears of elderly patients. They appear as gray-blue to purple papulonodules that disappear when compressed. They are frequently brought to physicians' attention because of cosmetic concerns or a history of periodic bleeding.

title: Dermatitis herpetiformis is characterized by pruritic papules, vesicles, and bullae on the extensor surfaces of the elbows, knees, back
body: Dermatitis herpetiformis is characterized by pruritic papules, vesicles, and bullae on the extensor surfaces of the elbows, knees, back, and buttocks. It is commonly associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy (celiac disease), but the gastrointestinal manifestations may go undetected in patients with mild, nonspecific signs and symptoms.

title: Patients with mild-to-moderate plaque psoriasis should be treated initially with topical corticosteroids and emollients
body: Patients with mild-to-moderate plaque psoriasis should be treated initially with topical corticosteroids and emollients. Combination therapy with topical corticosteroids and vitamin D is more effective than either therapy alone. For facial or Intertriginous involvement, topical tacrolimus or pimecrolimus may be used as corticosteroid-sparing agents. Phototherapy and systemic therapies (eg, methotrexate, biologic agents) should be used for moderate-to-severe disease in consultation with a dermatologist.

title: Lichen planus causes pruritic, purple, polygonal papules or plaques involving the ankles and wrists, nails, oral mucous membranes, or
body: Lichen planus causes pruritic, purple, polygonal papules or plaques involving the ankles and wrists, nails, oral mucous membranes, or external genitalia. It has been associated with hepatitis C. Topical corticosteroids are first-line treatment.

title: Discoid lupus erythematosus typically presents with photosensitive patches of various sizes that are erythematous and well-defined
body: Discoid lupus erythematosus typically presents with photosensitive patches of various sizes that are erythematous and well-defined. The lesions tend to heal with hair loss, skin atrophy, deep scarring, and peripheral hyperpigmentation. Treatment includes sunscreen, protective clothing, and topical corticosteroids or Calcineurin inhibitor (eg, tacrolimus).

title: Pilonidal disease is a skin and/or subcutaneous infection near the natal cleft of the buttocks
body: Pilonidal disease is a skin and/or subcutaneous infection near the natal cleft of the buttocks. Patients can be asymptomatic or develop sudden onset of mild intergluteal pain with sitting or bending. Chronic disease can present with a tender mass or sinus with purulent, mucoid, or bloody drainage.

title: Sweet syndrome is an inflammatory disorder with abrupt onset of painful cutaneous papules, fever, neutrophilic leukocytosis, and dense
body: Sweet syndrome is an inflammatory disorder with abrupt onset of painful cutaneous papules, fever, neutrophilic leukocytosis, and dense neutrophilic infiltration on skin biopsy without signs of vasculitis. It may be associated with infections, inflammatory bowel disease, pregnancy, malignancy, ordrugs. Treatment involves topical corticosteroids for mild disease and systemic glucocorticoids for more extensive disease.

title: Calciphylaxis is due to systemic arteriolar calcification leading to soft-tissue calcium deposition, ischemia, and necrosis
body: Calciphylaxis is due to systemic arteriolar calcification leading to soft-tissue calcium deposition, ischemia, and necrosis. It occurs more commonly in end-stage renal disease patients on long-term hemodialysis with elevated calcium-phosphorus product.

title: Porphyria cutanea tarda usually presents with skin lesions (e.g., blisters, bullae, scarring) in sun exposed areas and is associated with
body: Porphyria cutanea tarda usually presents with skin lesions (e.g., blisters, bullae, scarring) in sun exposed areas and is associated with hepatitis C infection. Diagnosis is confirmed by elevated serum/urine uroporphyrin level. Treatment involves phlebotomy and treatment for HCV in patients diagnosed with the virus.

title: Psoriasis is characterized by erythematous, well-defined plaques covered by thick, silvery scales
body: Psoriasis is characterized by erythematous, well-defined plaques covered by thick, silvery scales. The lesions are typically seen over the scalp, knees, elbows, back, gluteal cleft, and nail plates, and may be associated with mild itching. Topical corticosteroids are the mainstay of therapy for localized mild-to- moderate plaque psoriasis.

title: Allergic contact dermatitis is frequently caused by latex, soaps/cleaning agents, cosmetic products, and topical medications
body: Allergic contact dermatitis is frequently caused by latex, soaps/cleaning agents, cosmetic products, and topical medications. It is characterized by local erythema, pruritus, vesiculation, and swelling.

title: Xerosis is dry skin due to depleted moisture that results in intensely pruritic areas
body: Xerosis is dry skin due to depleted moisture that results in intensely pruritic areas. Recurrent excoriation of the area can expand the lesion and lead to Iichenification. Most cases can be managed with daily skin moisturizers and topical emollients.

title: Oral leukoplakia is characterized by white patches or plaques over the oral mucosa that usually cannot be scraped off
body: Oral leukoplakia is characterized by white patches or plaques over the oral mucosa that usually cannot be scraped off. Risk factors for development of leukoplakia are similar to those for squamous cell carcinoma (tobacco and alcohol use). Development of areas with induration and/or ulceration should prompt biopsy to rule out malignant transformation of the lesion.

title: Skin tags are benign outgrowths of normal skin found in regions of the body subjected to friction, such as the neck, axillae, and inner
body: Skin tags are benign outgrowths of normal skin found in regions of the body subjected to friction, such as the neck, axillae, and inner thighs. Multiple skin tags may represent underlying insulin resistance.

title: Scabies is due to a burrowing mite that produces an intensely pruritic rash that is often worse at night
body: Scabies is due to a burrowing mite that produces an intensely pruritic rash that is often worse at night. Physical examination findings show excoriations with small, crusted, red papules scattered around the affected regions. Topical permethrin 5% cream or oral ivermectin is usually the treatment of choice.

title: Nonhealing pressure ulcers without signs of infection can be treated with topical antibiotics
body: Nonhealing pressure ulcers without signs of infection can be treated with topical antibiotics. Ulcers with signs of local infection can be treated with topical antibiotics and debridement. Ulcers complicated by cellulitis or sepsis/bacteremia require systemic antibiotics and debridement.

title: Pemphigus vulgaris is an autoimmune Vesiculobullous disease characterized by flaccid bullae that rupture easily
body: Pemphigus vulgaris is an autoimmune Vesiculobullous disease characterized by flaccid bullae that rupture easily. Lesions typically begin in the oropharynx and then may spread to involve the skin. Autoantibodies are formed against desmoglein, an adhesion molecule between epidermal cells. Diagnosis requires a skin biopsy and can be aided by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Systemic glucocorticoids are the mainstay of treatment.

title: Heel pressure ulcers are usually managed conservatively as removing tissue around the heel can increase the risk of osteomyelitis
body: Heel pressure ulcers are usually managed conservatively as removing tissue around the heel can increase the risk of osteomyelitis. Proper positioning to redistribute the pressure is the most important intervention to improve healing.

title: Tender, bleeding, or ulcerated papules, plaques, or nodules in sun-exposed areas or areas of chronic inflammation or scarring merit prompt evaluation for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
Pressure ulcer management requires pressure relief and attention to nutrition
body: Pressure ulcer management requires pressure relief and attention to nutrition. Dressings should be chosen to maintain a moist wound environment. Occlusive dressings should not be applied to full-thickness wounds.

title: Allergic contact dermatitis is a delayed hypersensitivity response to an exogenous agent
body: Allergic contact dermatitis is a delayed hypersensitivity response to an exogenous agent. Clinical findings in contact dermatitis due to artificial nails can include periungual edema or eczema, nail dystrophy, periungual hyperkeratosis, fingertip dermatitis, and paresthesias.

title: Androgenetic alopecia causes chronic thinning of hair
body: Androgenetic alopecia causes chronic thinning of hair. In men, it primarily affects the temples, anterior hairline, and vertex; in women, it primarily affects the vertex and center of the scalp with sparing of the hairline. Treatment options include topical minoxidil for men and women and finasteride for men.

title: Periungual warts are characterized by thick cauliflower-like skin around the nail plate and can lead to loss of the cuticle, paronychia
body: Periungual warts are characterized by thick cauliflower-like skin around the nail plate and can lead to loss of the cuticle, paronychia, and pain. They usually do not regress spontaneously. Topical salicylic acid is the preferred treatment for most patients.

title: Poorly differentiated cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma may appear as fleshy, soft, and granulomatous papules and nodules with less hyperkeratosis than seen in well-differentiated lesions.
Epidermal inclusion cyst is a benign nodule containing normal epidermis that produces keratin
body: Epidermal inclusion cyst is a benign nodule containing normal epidermis that produces keratin. Patients usually develop a dome-shaped, firm, and freely movable cyst or nodule with a small central punctum. The lesion can remain stable or gradually increase in size but usually resolves spontaneously.

title: Crusted scabies is an overwhelming infestation with thousands (compared to <50 in simple scabies) of scabies mites
body: Crusted scabies is an overwhelming infestation with thousands (compared to <50 in simple scabies) of scabies mites. It is more common in the elderly and immunocompromised (eg, HIV) and presents with erythematous patches that progress to prominent scales, crusting, and malodorous fissures. Itching is mild or absent. Treatment requires oral ivermectin with a topical keratolytic agent (eg, 20% urea ointment) and permethrin.

title: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome occurs 2-8 weeks after exposure to a new drug (eg, anticonvulsants
body: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome occurs 2-8 weeks after exposure to a new drug (eg, anticonvulsants, allopurinol, antibiotics). It is characterized by fever, Iymphadenopathy, facial edema, diffuse morbilliform skin rash, eosinophilia, and elevated hepatic transaminases.

title: Pustular psoriasis is characterized by erythematous patches followed by the appearance of sterile pustules, which may become confluent
body: Pustular psoriasis is characterized by erythematous patches followed by the appearance of sterile pustules, which may become confluent. It is typically seen in patients with a history of plaque psoriasis who become pregnant, develop an infection, or are withdrawn from glucocorticoid therapy. Patients with widespread lesions can develop systemic symptoms, desquamation, and sepsis.

title: Acute bacterial sinusitis usually presents with symptoms > 10 days; severe symptoms with fever > 39 C (102 F), purulent nasal discharge or
body: Acute bacterial sinusitis usually presents with symptoms > 10 days; severe symptoms with fever > 39 C (102 F), purulent nasal discharge or facial pain > 3 days; or worsening symptoms > 5 days after an initially improving viral upper respiratory infection. Amoxicillin-clavulanate for 5-7 days is preferred in non- penicillin-allergic patients. Doxycycline and respiratory quinolones (e.g., Ievofloxacin, moxifloxacin) are alternatives in penicillin-allergic patients.

title: Tinnitus is a perception of sound inside the ear that can be pulsatile (usually vascular etiology) or non- pulsatile (usually non-vascular
body: Tinnitus is a perception of sound inside the ear that can be pulsatile (usually vascular etiology) or non- pulsatile (usually non-vascular etiology). Non-pulsatile tinnitus usually originates in the auditory pathways and is frequently a sign of sensorineural hearing loss (although many patients do not complain about hearing loss) and requires initial audiometry testing.

title: Hoarseness is characterized by coarsening of vocal quality and is typically due to abnormalities in the larynx (eg, edema, hemorrhage
body: Hoarseness is characterized by coarsening of vocal quality and is typically due to abnormalities in the larynx (eg, edema, hemorrhage, laceration, mass lesions). Most causes of acute hoarseness are benign. However, patients with symptoms lasting >2 weeks or with a history of tobacco or heavy alcohol use, systemic symptoms, stridor, dysphagia, or referred ear pain require referral for consideration of laryngoscopy.

title: Unilateral painful parotid swelling is usually due to infection or parotid stone obstruction
body: Unilateral painful parotid swelling is usually due to infection or parotid stone obstruction. Risk factors for stones include dehydration, smoking, diuretics, trauma, gout, and anticholinergic medicines. Lack of erythema and fever suggests stone obstruction. Therapy is supportive in nature, but high-resolution CT is the preferred diagnostic test for persistent disease or suspected complete obstruction.

title: Most patients with acute unilateral sensorineural hearing loss have a benign etiology and recover spontaneously within 3-4 months
body: Most patients with acute unilateral sensorineural hearing loss have a benign etiology and recover spontaneously within 3-4 months. However, it can be difficult to determine the cause based on clinical findings alone, and patients should be evaluated with audiometry and MRI to exclude more significant disease (eg, vestibular schwannoma).

title: Otitis externa is most commonly due to Pseudomonas and Staphylococcus infections
body: Otitis externa is most commonly due to Pseudomonas and Staphylococcus infections. Treatment involves cleaning the ear canal and treating the inflammation and infection with a combination of ototopical steroid and antibiotic. Patients not responding to initial therapy after 3 days require culture of the ear canal or otolaryngology referral.

title: Rupture of the tympanic membrane in adults with acute otitis media is characterized by purulent otorrhea and relief of the initial ear pain
body: Rupture of the tympanic membrane in adults with acute otitis media is characterized by purulent otorrhea and relief of the initial ear pain. It usually resolves completely with a combination of oral and topical antibiotics.

title: Rhinitis medicamentosa usually occurs in patients with chronic use of vasoconstrictor nasal sprays
body: Rhinitis medicamentosa usually occurs in patients with chronic use of vasoconstrictor nasal sprays. Symptoms are due to a cycle of rebound exacerbation with worsening nasal congestion and discharge. Treatment involves stopping the decongestant spray and initiating a trial of intranasal steroids (e.g., fluticasone).

title: Ear fullness, popping sounds, and decreased hearing sometimes can be due to obstruction of the eustachian tube during or following an upper
body: Ear fullness, popping sounds, and decreased hearing sometimes can be due to obstruction of the eustachian tube during or following an upper respiratory infection. A short-term trial of decongestants is often effective.

title: Malignant otitis externa presents in older patients with diabetes with severe pain, ear discharge, erosion of the surrounding bones, and a
body: Malignant otitis externa presents in older patients with diabetes with severe pain, ear discharge, erosion of the surrounding bones, and a very high erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Patients with squamous cell cancer of the external ear generally have milder symptoms, a subacute presentation, and a lower ESR. A tissue biopsy is often required to differentiate between these 2 conditions.

title: Presbycusis is the most common cause of progressive, bilateral, high-frequency hearing loss in elderly patients
body: Presbycusis is the most common cause of progressive, bilateral, high-frequency hearing loss in elderly patients. Early recognition and treatment are essential to prevent social isolation, depression, and functional disability (falls). The whispered voice test and audiogram can be used for diagnosis. Treatment involves hearing aids and cochlear implants for refractory hearing loss.

title: Vasomotor rhinitis occurs commonly in women after age 20, with perennial symptoms and lack of atopic symptoms (eg, no nasal or eye itching)
body: Vasomotor rhinitis occurs commonly in women after age 20, with perennial symptoms and lack of atopic symptoms (eg, no nasal or eye itching). Intranasal corticosteroids are the preferred treatment. In severe cases, combined nasal corticosteroids and nasal antihistamines are effective in providing symptom relief.

title: Acute rhinosinusitis is usually viral and is routinely treated with supportive care
body: Acute rhinosinusitis is usually viral and is routinely treated with supportive care. Acute bacterial rhinosinusitis is more likely in patients with symptoms for > 10 days, severe symptoms (eg, fever plus sinus tenderness or facial pain) for > 3 days, or worsening symptoms > 5 days after an initially improving viral upper respiratory infection.

title: Hearing loss is a significant and sometimes treatable factor that can contribute to social isolation in the elderly population.
Minor variant recurrent aphthous stomatitis presents with a few ulcers that are small, occur on the non­ keratinized portions of the
body: Minor variant recurrent aphthous stomatitis presents with a few ulcers that are small, occur on the non­ keratinized portions of the tongue, cheeks, and lips, and heal in 7-10 days without scarring. They typically recur every 1-4 months. Topical glucocorticoids are the treatment of choice.

title: Epiglottitis should be suspected in patients when the severity of sore throat is out of proportion to the findings on oropharyngeal
body: Epiglottitis should be suspected in patients when the severity of sore throat is out of proportion to the findings on oropharyngeal examination. Drooling and stridor are seen in less than 40% of the patients. Odynophagia and dysphagia are much more common (>90%).

title: Meniere disease is characterized by episodic vertigo, sensorineural hearing loss, and tinnitus and/or a feeling of fullness in the ear
body: Meniere disease is characterized by episodic vertigo, sensorineural hearing loss, and tinnitus and/or a feeling of fullness in the ear. The diagnosis is based primarily on clinical findings. Initial management includes restriction of sodium, caffeine, nicotine, and alcohol. Diuretics can also be useful.

title: The therapeutic goal in primary hypothyroidism is to maintain TSH levels within the normal reference range by replacement with
body: The therapeutic goal in primary hypothyroidism is to maintain TSH levels within the normal reference range by replacement with levothyroxine. Levothyroxine dose adjustment should be based on TSH levels alone rather than direct measurement of thyroid hormone levels.

title: Glucagon-Iike peptide-1 receptor agonists are very effective antidiabetic agents with additional benefits of weight loss and low risk of hypoglycemia.
The initial evaluation of thyroid nodules includes a serum TSH assay and thyroid ultrasound
body: The initial evaluation of thyroid nodules includes a serum TSH assay and thyroid ultrasound. Most patients with normal or elevated TSH should undergo fine-needle aspiration of the nodule for cytologic assessment. Patients with a suppressed TSH should undergo thyroid scintigraphy. Hyperfunctioning nodules are rarely malignant and do not usually require fine-needle aspiration.

title: Patients with osteoporosis warrant laboratory testing for reversible secondary causes
body: Patients with osteoporosis warrant laboratory testing for reversible secondary causes. The evaluation should include serum chemistries (eg, calcium, phosphorus, albumin, total protein, and renal and hepatic function markers) and complete blood count. In addition, vitamin D stores should be assessed with a 25- hydroxyvitamin D level.

title: Suppressed serum thyroglobulin differentiates factitious thyrotoxicosis from other causes of thyrotoxicosis associated with low radioactive iodine uptake.
Patients with adrenal incidentaloma usually require evaluation for malignancy risk and biochemical testing (eg, overnight dexamethasone
body: Patients with adrenal incidentaloma usually require evaluation for malignancy risk and biochemical testing (eg, overnight dexamethasone test, urinary fractionated catecholamines, and metanephrines) to document excess adrenal hormone production. Hypertensive patients also require renin and aldosterone measurements to evaluate for primary hyperaldosteronism, which can present with low or normal serum potassium. Patients with adrenal mass characteristics suggestive of malignancy or positive biochemical testing should be considered for surgery.

title: Subclinical hypothyroidism is defined as a serum TSH above the upper limit of normal with a serum free T4 level in the normal range
body: Subclinical hypothyroidism is defined as a serum TSH above the upper limit of normal with a serum free T4 level in the normal range. Patients age ≥70 with Subclinical hypothyroidism should generally not be treated but should have periodic monitoring for progression to overt hypothyroidism.

title: Central hypothyroidism can be due to mass lesions, intracranial radiation therapy, or infiltrative disorders of the pituitary/hypothalamus
body: Central hypothyroidism can be due to mass lesions, intracranial radiation therapy, or infiltrative disorders of the pituitary/hypothalamus. It often coexists with other pituitary deficiencies. Initiating treatment of hypothyroidism prior to diagnosing and treating coexisting adrenal insufficiency may induce adrenal crisis.

title: Laboratory testing in patients with anabolic-androgenic steroid abuse shows increased hematocrit and decreased levels Ofendogenous testosterone, luteinizing hormone, and follicle-stimulating hormone.
Chronic opioid use leads to decreased gonadotropin-releasing hormone secretion, and is a common cause of hypogonadism
body: Chronic opioid use leads to decreased gonadotropin-releasing hormone secretion, and is a common cause of hypogonadism. Patients can develop decreased libido and other manifestations of hypogonadism. Management options include discontinuation, dose reduction, or rotation of opioid types, or androgen replacement therapy.

title: Klinefelter’s syndrome is the most common genetic cause of primary hypogonadism
body: Klinefelter’s syndrome is the most common genetic cause of primary hypogonadism. Patients typically present with gynecomastia and hypogonadism. Karyotype of peripheral leukocytes confirms the diagnosis. Patients with Klinefelter’s syndrome are at increased risk of breast cancer.

title: Patients age 40-75 with diabetes should receive statin therapy, with the dose intensity determined by the overall risk for atherosclerotic
body: Patients age 40-75 with diabetes should receive statin therapy, with the dose intensity determined by the overall risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Targeting low HDL with nonstatin medications has not been shown to improve cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Indications for parathyroidectomy in primary hyperparathyroidism include age <50, symptomatic hypercalcemia, complications of
body: Indications for parathyroidectomy in primary hyperparathyroidism include age <50, symptomatic hypercalcemia, complications of hyperparathyroidism (osteoporosis, nephrolithiasis/calcinosis, chronic kidney disease), or elevated risk of complications (calcium >1 mg/dL above normal, urinary calcium excretion >400 mg∕day).

title: Metabolic bone disease (decreased bone mineral density and osteoporosis) can occur in celiac disease without significant gastrointestinal
body: Metabolic bone disease (decreased bone mineral density and osteoporosis) can occur in celiac disease without significant gastrointestinal symptoms. Vitamin D deficiency due to malabsorption leads to secondary hyperparathyroidism and increased bone turnover. Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry scan is recommended for all patients with celiac disease for evaluation and treatment of bone loss.

title: Clinical features that suggest obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) include obesity, fatigue, excessive daytime sleepiness, morning headaches
body: Clinical features that suggest obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) include obesity, fatigue, excessive daytime sleepiness, morning headaches, hypertension, and polycythemia. The diagnosis is established with polysomnography. The prevalence of OSA is increased in patients with hypothyroidism.

title: Patients age 40-75 with diabetes and a 10-year risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) ≥7.5% should receive high-intensity statin therapy
body: Patients age 40-75 with diabetes and a 10-year risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) ≥7.5% should receive high-intensity statin therapy; those with CVD risk <7.5% should have moderate-intensity statin therapy. Intensive glycemic control in diabetes mellitus does not appear to reduce cardiovascular risk.

title: Severely obese patients with type 2 diabetes have a higher likelihood of achieving diabetic remission with bariatric surgery compared to conventional medical therapy.
Pregabalin is an effective first-line agent in elderly patients for diabetic neuropathy
body: Pregabalin is an effective first-line agent in elderly patients for diabetic neuropathy. In older patients, opiates and agents with strong anticholinergic effects should be avoided as initial therapy due to potential adverse effects.

title: Hereditary hemochromatosis is an important cause of secondary hypogonadism and is usually due to iron deposition in the pituitary
body: Hereditary hemochromatosis is an important cause of secondary hypogonadism and is usually due to iron deposition in the pituitary gonadotrophs. Restoration of gonadal function is more likely if phlebotomy is initiated before age 40.

title: Levothyroxine therapy in central hypothyroidism should be based on serum free T4 levels, with the dose adjusted to maintain T4 in the
body: Levothyroxine therapy in central hypothyroidism should be based on serum free T4 levels, with the dose adjusted to maintain T4 in the high-normal range. TSH in central hypothyroidism demonstrates minimal responsiveness to levothyroxine and may not rise in patients with inadequate replacement.

title: The evaluation of hypercalcemia depends on parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels
body: The evaluation of hypercalcemia depends on parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels. Hypercalcemia with an elevated or inappropriately normal PTH (PTH-dependent) is caused by very few disorders, mainly primary hyperparathyroidism.

title: The initial evaluation of a thyroid nodule includes a serum TSH and thyroid ultrasound
body: The initial evaluation of a thyroid nodule includes a serum TSH and thyroid ultrasound. Patients with benign ultrasound findings and suppressed TSH should undergo radioactive iodine scintigraphy. Toxic thyroid adenoma or multinodular goiter with hyperthyroidism is treated with radioactive iodine ablation or surgical thyroidectomy.

title: Overtreatment of hypothyroidism with levothyroxine is associated with an increased risk of excessive bone loss and atrial fibrillation.
Hypothyroidism is a common cause of dyslipidemia
body: Hypothyroidism is a common cause of dyslipidemia. Patients with dyslipidemia should be screened for hypothyroidism with serum TSH. Dyslipidemia due to hypothyroidism improves with levothyroxine therapy.

title: Germline RET gene mutation testing is recommended in all patients with medullary thyroid cancer
body: Germline RET gene mutation testing is recommended in all patients with medullary thyroid cancer. Preoperative imaging of the neck, chest, and upper abdomen is performed when the local lymph nodes are present or serum calcitonin is > 400.

title: Aldosterone receptor blockers - spironolactone and eplerenone - have been shown to improve survival in systolic heart failure with low left
body: Aldosterone receptor blockers - spironolactone and eplerenone - have been shown to improve survival in systolic heart failure with low left ventricular ejection fraction. Both may cause hyperkalemia. Spironolactone has significant anti-androgenic effects. Eplerenone is more specific than spironolactone for the mineralocorticoid receptor and has fewer endocrine side effects.

title: Insulin-Iike growth factor I (IGF-I) is the preferred screening test for acromegaly. Measuring random GH is not as sensitive because of wide fluctuations in circulating levels.
Subclinical hypothyroidism is relatively common in women age >60
body: Subclinical hypothyroidism is relatively common in women age >60. Severe overt hypothyroidism is associated with an increased risk Ofsurgical complications, but asymptomatic Subclinical hypothyroidism does not warrant delay of urgent surgical procedures.

title: Patients whose type 2 diabetes is not controlled on metformin should receive dual therapy with metformin plus a second agent
body: Patients whose type 2 diabetes is not controlled on metformin should receive dual therapy with metformin plus a second agent. However, patients with hemoglobin A1c >10%, glucose >300 mg/dL, or osmotic or catabolic symptoms should be considered for the addition of insulin. Patients who do not reach targets on 2 or 3 oral agents should also be considered for insulin.

title: Primary hyperaldosteronism (PH) is characterized by hypertension, hypokalemia, and an elevated plasma aldosterone to plasma renin activity
body: Primary hyperaldosteronism (PH) is characterized by hypertension, hypokalemia, and an elevated plasma aldosterone to plasma renin activity ratio. The diagnosis is confirmed with an aldosterone suppression test. CT of the adrenals can differentiate adrenal adenoma from bilateral adrenal hyperplasia, but if no adenoma is seen adrenal venous sampling is recommended. Surgery is preferred for an adrenal adenoma; medical therapy (eg, spironolactone, eplerenone) is preferred for bilateral adrenal hyperplasia.

title: Mild hypertriglyceridemia (<500 mg/dL) with no cardiovascular disease risk is generally treated with lifestyle modifications
body: Mild hypertriglyceridemia (<500 mg/dL) with no cardiovascular disease risk is generally treated with lifestyle modifications. Patients with higher triglyceride levels (especially >1000 mg/dL) benefit from fibrate therapy to reduce the risk of pancreatitis.

title: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases the risk of hypoglycemia in patients with diabetes
body: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases the risk of hypoglycemia in patients with diabetes. Short-acting sulfonylureas are usually safe to use in patients with CKD but can cause hypoglycemia. Linagliptin is a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor that can be used in patients with CKD and has a low risk of hypoglycemia when used in monotherapy.

title: Hypothyroidism can cause myopathy with pain, weakness, and elevated creatine kinase. Statins can worsen hypothyroid myopathy, and hypothyroidism can exacerbate statin myopathy.
Acromegaly is associated with an increased risk of esophageal cancer, gastric cancer, colon cancer, and melanoma
body: Acromegaly is associated with an increased risk of esophageal cancer, gastric cancer, colon cancer, and melanoma. Screening colonoscopy is recommended at the time of diagnosis and every 3-4 years after age 50. The mortality of untreated acromegaly is higher than the general population, usually due to cardiovascular disease and cancer.

title: Pituitary Incidentalomas measuring <10 mm usually do not cause visual defects or pituitary hypofunction
body: Pituitary Incidentalomas measuring <10 mm usually do not cause visual defects or pituitary hypofunction. Patients with small (< 10 mm) pituitary lesions only require monitoring with prolactin levels if there is no clinical evidence of pituitary hormonal hypersecretion.

title: Hypercalcemia normally suppresses parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion to very low levels
body: Hypercalcemia normally suppresses parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion to very low levels. In the setting of hypercalcemia, a high-normal PTH level suggests primary hyperparathyroidism. Although PTH is elevated in most patients with primary hyperparathyroidism, it is only borderline or high-normal in 10%-20% of these patients.

title: Major risk factors for thyroid cancer in patients with thyroid nodules include a history of radiation exposure or a family history of
body: Major risk factors for thyroid cancer in patients with thyroid nodules include a history of radiation exposure or a family history of thyroid cancer. A higher serum TSH level is associated with increased risk of malignancy in a thyroid nodule.

title: TSH and thyroid ultrasound should be performed in all patients with thyroid nodules
body: TSH and thyroid ultrasound should be performed in all patients with thyroid nodules. The risk of malignancy can be assessed based on historical risk factors, TSH, nodule size, and ultrasound characteristics. High-risk nodules should be further evaluated with fine-needle aspiration.

title: Hypoglycemic episodes may occur in patients on insulin therapy (or insulin Secretagogues) during and after exercise
body: Hypoglycemic episodes may occur in patients on insulin therapy (or insulin Secretagogues) during and after exercise. These can be avoided by adequate hydration, frequent monitoring of blood glucose, consumption of rapid-acting carbohydrates before and during exercise, and, if necessary, insulin dose adjustment prior to exercise.

title: Patients with hypercalcemia and elevated 1,25-hydroxy vitamin D require a chest x-ray to evaluate for granulomatous diseases (sarcoidosis) and lymphoma.
Patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity commonly have hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with borderline low testosterone levels (200-300
body: Patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity commonly have hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with borderline low testosterone levels (200-300 ng/dL) and do not routinely need pituitary imaging. However, patients with markedly low serum testosterone levels or abnormalities of additional pituitary hormones are more likely to have a pituitary mass and warrant pituitary MRL

title: Antithyroid drugs (eg, methimazole) can induce remission in patients with mild Graves disease
body: Antithyroid drugs (eg, methimazole) can induce remission in patients with mild Graves disease. They are also used to attain a euthyroid state in preparation for definitive treatment with radioactive iodine or thyroidectomy in patients with moderate to severe disease. Radioactive iodine can worsen Graves ophthalmopathy and should be avoided in patients with significant ocular symptoms.

title: Hyperprolactinemia suppresses gonadotropin secretion and leads to hypogonadism, which leads to low estrogen levels with bone loss and
body: Hyperprolactinemia suppresses gonadotropin secretion and leads to hypogonadism, which leads to low estrogen levels with bone loss and osteoporosis in women. Microprolactinomas are generally slow growing with low risk of rapid enlargement.

title: Insulin therapy should be titrated to maintain fasting glucose of 80-130 rng∕dL, postprandial glucose <180 mg∕dL, and hemoglobin A1c <7%
body: Insulin therapy should be titrated to maintain fasting glucose of 80-130 rng∕dL, postprandial glucose <180 mg∕dL, and hemoglobin A1c <7% while avoiding hypoglycemia. In patients receiving basal-bolus insulin therapy, the dose of basal insulin is reduced for preprandial and early-morning hypoglycemia, and the dose of bolus insulin reduced for postmeal hypoglycemia.

title: Long-term amiodarone use can cause thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism). Patients with overt hypothyroidism should continue amiodarone but initiate thyroid replacement therapy.
Sulfonylureas (eg, glyburide) can accumulate in elderly patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and cause hypoglycemia; this effect is
body: Sulfonylureas (eg, glyburide) can accumulate in elderly patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and cause hypoglycemia; this effect is potentiated by trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. Goals for diabetes control should be relaxed in elderly individuals with CKD.

title: Both hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism can raise blood pressure
body: Both hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism can raise blood pressure. Untreated thyroid disease can impair the response to antihypertensive management, but many patients experience normalization of blood pressure when the underlying thyroid disorder is treated. Patients with hypertension warrant screening for thyroid disease in the initial laboratory evaluation.

title: Moderate to severe hypertriglyceridemia-induced pancreatitis requires rapid lowering of serum triglyceride levels
body: Moderate to severe hypertriglyceridemia-induced pancreatitis requires rapid lowering of serum triglyceride levels. If blood glucose is very high (≥500 mg/dL), an insulin infusion can correct triglyceride levels within 3-4 days. However, if glucose is <500 mg/dL or pancreatitis is severe (eg, lactic acidosis, hypocalcemia), therapeutic plasma exchange apheresis should be considered.

title: The first step in evaluation of Cushing syndrome is to confirm the diagnosis with a low-dose dexamethasone suppression test, 24-hour urine
body: The first step in evaluation of Cushing syndrome is to confirm the diagnosis with a low-dose dexamethasone suppression test, 24-hour urine free cortisol assay, or late-night salivary cortisol assay. Patients must have abnormal results on 2 different tests. ACTH-dependent and ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome should then be differentiated with a plasma ACTH level.

title: Most patients with osteoporosis are treated with a bisphosphonate
body: Most patients with osteoporosis are treated with a bisphosphonate. However, these medications are relatively contraindicated in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and creatinine clearance <30-35 mL/min. Denosumab reduces the risk offracture in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis and is appropriate for use in patients with CKD.

title: Gastric bypass surgery is associated with many nutritional deficiencies
body: Gastric bypass surgery is associated with many nutritional deficiencies. Copper deficiency has a clinical presentation similar to B12 deficiency (eg, anemia, leukopenia, and myeloneuropathy). Excessive zinc supplementation can also exacerbate symptoms of copper deficiency.

title: In patients with mild hypertriglyceridemia, the decision to initiate Iipid-Iowering therapy is determined primarily by the overall risk of
body: In patients with mild hypertriglyceridemia, the decision to initiate Iipid-Iowering therapy is determined primarily by the overall risk of cardiovascular events. If medication is needed, statins, which have been shown to prevent cardiovascular events, are preferred over non-statin medications.

title: Central hypothyroidism is characterized by low (or inappropriately normal) TSH and low free T4
body: Central hypothyroidism is characterized by low (or inappropriately normal) TSH and low free T4. Evaluation should include MRI of the pituitary to rule out a mass lesion and testing for additional pituitary hormone deficiencies. The treatment is levothyroxine with the dose adjusted to maintain free T4 in the high-normal range.

title: Routine screening for osteoporosis in men remains controversial
body: Routine screening for osteoporosis in men remains controversial. However, osteoporosis screening and potential treatment should be pursued in men with risk factors (eg, androgen deprivation therapy, chronic corticosteroid use, low-trauma fractures). Osteoporotic skeletal fractures occur in up to 20% of men within 5 years of starting androgen deprivation therapy.

title: Basal insulin is a safe, simple, and effective way to initiate insulin in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus who fail one or more oral
body: Basal insulin is a safe, simple, and effective way to initiate insulin in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus who fail one or more oral agents. Intensive insulin therapy (basal-bolus) is considered for very high A1C with symptomatic hyperglycemia. Insulin Secretagogues are discontinued when intensive insulin therapy is begun, while metformin is usually continued.

title: Total testosterone levels < 300 ng/dL in a blood sample taken between 7 AM and 10 AM in patients with reported clinical features are
body: Total testosterone levels < 300 ng/dL in a blood sample taken between 7 AM and 10 AM in patients with reported clinical features are suggestive of testosterone deficiency. Measurement of free testosterone level is not usually required unless the patient is obese or elderly. Treatment includes transdermal or intramuscular testosterone preparations.

title: Vitamin D deficiency can mask hypercalcemia in primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) and present as a normal to high-normal calcium that
body: Vitamin D deficiency can mask hypercalcemia in primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) and present as a normal to high-normal calcium that increases once vitamin D is repleted. The diagnosis is confirmed with a disproportionately elevated PTH level that is usually higher than the PTH level seen in PHPT without vitamin D deficiency.

title: Latent autoimmune diabetes of adulthood (LADA) is type 1 diabetes mellitus that manifests later in life, usually in thin patients age >35
body: Latent autoimmune diabetes of adulthood (LADA) is type 1 diabetes mellitus that manifests later in life, usually in thin patients age >35 but < 50 with abrupt symptom onset, and a family/personal history of autoimmune disease. These patients have anti-islet cell and glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies, are at increased risk of ketoacidosis, respond poorly to dietary therapy and oral diabetic medications, and usually require insulin earlier.

title: Diagnosis of endogenous Cushing syndrome requires confirmation on at least 2 different screening tests
body: Diagnosis of endogenous Cushing syndrome requires confirmation on at least 2 different screening tests. Options include low-dose overnight dexamethasone suppression test, late-night salivary cortisol, and 24- hour urine free cortisol. Estrogen (eg, oral contraceptive pills) increases cortisol-binding globulin and total cortisol, resulting in a false positive on a dexamethasone suppression test.

title: Painless thyroiditis usually occurs in women > 1 year post pregnancy, but it can occur in non-postpartum women and men
body: Painless thyroiditis usually occurs in women > 1 year post pregnancy, but it can occur in non-postpartum women and men. Patients typically present with 1-2 months of mild hyperthyroid symptoms followed by hypothyroid symptoms and recovery. Patients with mild symptoms usually require no therapy except for thyroid function test monitoring. Beta-blockers are preferred for symptomatic thyrotoxic patients.

title: Most men with end-stage renal disease experience sexual dysfunction (eg, low libido, erectile dysfunction, decreased frequency of
body: Most men with end-stage renal disease experience sexual dysfunction (eg, low libido, erectile dysfunction, decreased frequency of intercourse, infertility). Contributing factors include vascular impairment, peripheral and autonomic neuropathy, gonadal dysfunction, psychological stress, concurrent medications, and medical comorbidities. Most patients respond to phosphodiesterase inhibitors (eg, sildenafil).

title: SGLT2 inhibitors lower blood glucose by decreasing the reabsorption of glucose in the kidney
body: SGLT2 inhibitors lower blood glucose by decreasing the reabsorption of glucose in the kidney. The most common side effects are genital candidiasis, urinary tract infections, and osmotic diuresis leading to hypotension.

title: Progressive insulin deficiency plays a very important role in the pathophysiology of diabetes and is one of the main reasons for failure of
body: Progressive insulin deficiency plays a very important role in the pathophysiology of diabetes and is one of the main reasons for failure of anti-diabetic therapy over time despite good initial response.

title: Hyperthyroidism may present with apathy in older individuals
body: Hyperthyroidism may present with apathy in older individuals. Shortness of breath, weight loss, and atrial fibrillation occur more commonly in older patients. Screening for hyperthyroidism should be done in older individuals presenting with new onset atrial fibrillation.

title: Patients treated with corticosteroids for >3 weeks are likely to develop suppression of the hypothalamic- pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis
body: Patients treated with corticosteroids for >3 weeks are likely to develop suppression of the hypothalamic- pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. Patients with a Cushingoid appearance have a higher likelihood of HPA suppression. HPA axis suppression from corticosteroid use may not resolve for up to 6-12 months after discontinuation of the medication.

title: Thyroid hormone therapy is indicated following thyroidectomy for patients with differentiated thyroid cancer to suppress TSH stimulation of
body: Thyroid hormone therapy is indicated following thyroidectomy for patients with differentiated thyroid cancer to suppress TSH stimulation of residual tumor tissue. However, suppressive doses of levothyroxine can induce a hyperthyroid state and increase the risk Ofsystolic hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and osteoporosis.

title: Prolactinomas in men usually present with visual changes, headaches, and hypogonadism
body: Prolactinomas in men usually present with visual changes, headaches, and hypogonadism. They are typically larger at the time of diagnosis than they are in women (most often due to a delay in diagnosis). Diagnosis is confirmed with a serum prolactin level followed by brain MRL

title: TSH remains suppressed for months after radioactive iodine ablative treatment. Further treatment decisions are based on total T3 and free T4 levels, patient symptoms, and clinical examination.
Primary hypothyroidism is treated with levothyroxine, with the dose adjusted to maintain serum TSH in the normal (or low-normal) range
body: Primary hypothyroidism is treated with levothyroxine, with the dose adjusted to maintain serum TSH in the normal (or low-normal) range. Further dose increases or the addition of liothyronine (T3) are not recommended. Hypothyroid symptoms are nonspecific, and patients with residual symptoms should be evaluated for alternate etiologies.

title: Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis is caused by preceding viral infection
body: Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis is caused by preceding viral infection. Patients usually present with anterior neck pain, a diffusely tender thyroid, and features of thyrotoxicosis. Treatment is supportive with NSAIDs for mild to moderate thyroid pain and glucocorticoids for severe pain. Thionamides and radioactive iodide therapy are not useful in the treatment of subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.

title: The prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus is increased in patients with hypertension, and patients with both hypertension and diabetes are
body: The prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus is increased in patients with hypertension, and patients with both hypertension and diabetes are at increased risk for cardiovascular complications. Patients with hypertension should be screened for diabetes with a fasting glucose level, hemoglobin A1c, or oral glucose tolerance test.

title: Primary adrenal insufficiency (PAI) is usually due to autoimmune adrenalitis and may be seen with other autoimmune endocrine disorders
body: Primary adrenal insufficiency (PAI) is usually due to autoimmune adrenalitis and may be seen with other autoimmune endocrine disorders. Typical findings include fatigue, hypotension, hyponatremia, and low blood glucose. PAI can become acutely worse due to acute stressors, leading to adrenal crisis. Initial evaluation includes 8 AM serum cortisol, plasma ACTH, and ACTH stimulation test. Treatment requires corticosteroid replacement.

title: Orlistat is used for the long-term treatment of obesity
body: Orlistat is used for the long-term treatment of obesity. It inhibits pancreatic lipase to reduce fat absorption and increase fecal fat excretion. Patients with fat intake > 30% of total calories can develop side effects similar to fat malabsorption (eg, flatus, fecal incontinence, oily spotting). A lower fat intake can reduce these symptoms.

title: Radioactive iodine uptake can differentiate between increased synthesis of thyroid hormone and release of preformed hormone in patients
body: Radioactive iodine uptake can differentiate between increased synthesis of thyroid hormone and release of preformed hormone in patients with hyperthyroidism. A concurrent thyroid scan is recommended to identify a toxic nodule or toxic multinodular goiter in hyperthyroid patients with palpable nodules.

title: Thyrotoxicosis is a cause of parathyroid hormone-independent hypercalcemia. It can lead to a negative calcium balance, decreased bone density, and increased risk offracture.
Lifestyle changes (e.g., diet/exercise) resulting in weight loss is the most effective and safest way to prevent the development of type 2
body: Lifestyle changes (e.g., diet/exercise) resulting in weight loss is the most effective and safest way to prevent the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus, especially in patients > age 60. Metformin may be considered for diabetes prevention in younger patients at high risk for future DM.

title: Oral estrogens increase the serum concentration Ofthyroid binding globulin (TBG)
body: Oral estrogens increase the serum concentration Ofthyroid binding globulin (TBG). In normal patients, feedback loops promote increased endogenous production of thyroid hormones to compensate for the increased number of bound thyroid hormone molecules. However, patients with hypothyroidism cannot adequately compensate and an increased dose of levothyroxine is usually necessary.

title: Hyperprolactinemia is common in chronic renal failure due to increased release and decreased clearance of prolactin
body: Hyperprolactinemia is common in chronic renal failure due to increased release and decreased clearance of prolactin. Prolactin levels can be normalized with dopamine agonists, but sexual dysfunction often persists due to additional contributing factors.

title: Patients with hypertension and incidental adrenal masses require evaluation for Cushing’s syndrome, primary hyperaldosteronism
body: Patients with hypertension and incidental adrenal masses require evaluation for Cushing’s syndrome, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, and excess adrenal androgen (in females). Primary hyperaldosteronism can present with hypertension and without spontaneous hypokalemia.

title: Primary hyperaldosteronism (PH) is characterized by hypertension, metabolic alkalosis, and hypokalemia
body: Primary hyperaldosteronism (PH) is characterized by hypertension, metabolic alkalosis, and hypokalemia. Potassium may be normal at baseline, but thiazide or loop diuretics may trigger hypokalemia. An elevated plasma aldosterone concentration to plasma renin activity ratio >20 suggests PH.

title: Subclinical hypothyroidism can be associated with ovulatory dysfunction, which may improve with levothyroxine treatment
body: Subclinical hypothyroidism can be associated with ovulatory dysfunction, which may improve with levothyroxine treatment. Treatment is also considered in patients with positive anti-thyroperoxidase antibodies, goiter, pregnancy, overt symptoms, or cardiovascular risk factors.

title: Central hypothyroidism usually presents with hypothyroid symptoms, low TSH, and low T4 with evidence of other hormone deficiencies
body: Central hypothyroidism usually presents with hypothyroid symptoms, low TSH, and low T4 with evidence of other hormone deficiencies. Patients should undergo neuroimaging and pituitary hormone testing. Glucocorticoid deficiency must be diagnosed and treated in patients with central hypothyroidism before starting levothyroxine therapy. Levothyroxine given to patients with undiagnosed glucocorticoid deficiency can precipitate an adrenal crisis.

title: Osteoporosis in men is often due to secondary causes. Elderly men with hip fractures frequently have hypogonadism and should be screened with an early-morning serum testosterone assay.
Early onset of severe osteoporosis and recurrent fragility fractures require evaluation for secondary causes of osteoporosis.
Initial work-up of patients with chronic pericardial effusion includes a complete blood count, basic metabolic panel, thyroid function
body: Initial work-up of patients with chronic pericardial effusion includes a complete blood count, basic metabolic panel, thyroid function tests, anti-double stranded DNA antibodies, and complement levels.

title: The preferred initial medication for type 2 diabetes mellitus is metformin
body: The preferred initial medication for type 2 diabetes mellitus is metformin. The addition of basal insulin is recommended when a patient requires a significant reduction in hemoglobin A1c (eg, A1c >10%). If glycemic control is still not adequate, options include adding rapid-acting insulin, changing to a premixed insulin formulation, or adding a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonist. Compared with the other options, the addition of a GLP-1 agonist is associated with fewer episodes of hypoglycemia and less weight gain.

title: Osteopenia is defined as a T score of -1.1 to -2.4 and osteoporosis as a T score <-2.5
body: Osteopenia is defined as a T score of -1.1 to -2.4 and osteoporosis as a T score <-2.5. Diagnostic interpretation is based on the lowest T score at the lumbar spine (average bone density at L1-L4) and either hip.

title: Injectable GLP-1 analogues (eg, exenatide, Iiraglutide) are useful in patients with type 2 diabetes who fail metformin monotherapy. They have a low risk of hypoglycemia and induce weight loss.
Clinical features that warrant evaluation for androgen deficiency include decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, testicular atrophy, loss
body: Clinical features that warrant evaluation for androgen deficiency include decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, testicular atrophy, loss of body hair, gynecomastia, hot flashes, and an unexplained decrease in bone density. Nonspecific symptoms (eg, fatigue, weakness, weight changes) alone do not warrant testing in most cases. The initial step is a morning serum testosterone level, and low levels should be confirmed on repeat testing.

title: Risk factors for developing hungry bone syndrome after parathyroidectomy include moderate-to-severe hyperparathyroidism with evidence of
body: Risk factors for developing hungry bone syndrome after parathyroidectomy include moderate-to-severe hyperparathyroidism with evidence of high bone turnover, older age, and renal dysfunction.
