Laboratory findings include low calcium, low phosphorus, low magnesium, and normal (or high) PTH levels.

title: An adrenal incidentaloma is a mass >1 cm in diameter discovered incidentally on radiology studies
body: An adrenal incidentaloma is a mass >1 cm in diameter discovered incidentally on radiology studies. Risk for malignancy can be assessed based on morphological characteristics. Patients should be tested for biochemical evidence OfCushing syndrome (dexamethasone suppression test), pheochromocytoma (plasma or urinary metanephrines), and hyperaldosteronism (plasma aldosterone and plasma renin activity).

title: Thyroid storm is a life-threatening thyrotoxicosis in patients with undiagnosed or incompletely treated hyperthyroidism
body: Thyroid storm is a life-threatening thyrotoxicosis in patients with undiagnosed or incompletely treated hyperthyroidism. Patients can develop tachycardia, hypertension, cardiac arrhythmias, fever, tremor, and altered mentation. Treatment includes beta blockers and a thionamide (eg, propylthiouracil).

title: Hypoglycemia in a nondiabetic patient requires further evaluation if all 3 criteria of Whipple's triad (blood glucose <55 mg/dL
body: Hypoglycemia in a nondiabetic patient requires further evaluation if all 3 criteria of Whipple's triad (blood glucose <55 mg/dL, hypoglycemic symptoms, relief of symptoms with glucose administration) are present. Surreptitious sulfonylurea use can cause hypoglycemia associated with elevated or inappropriately normal insulin and C-peptide levels.

title: Myxedema coma is a life-threatening condition characterized by altered mental status, hypothermia, and nonpitting swelling of the
body: Myxedema coma is a life-threatening condition characterized by altered mental status, hypothermia, and nonpitting swelling of the extremities, face, and tongue. Treatment with intravenous levothyroxine (T4) and liothyronine (T3) should not be delayed while awaiting results Ofthyroid function tests.

title: Pituitary apoplexy commonly presents with acute headache, bitemporal visual field defects, and paresis of the oculomotor nerve (CN III)
body: Pituitary apoplexy commonly presents with acute headache, bitemporal visual field defects, and paresis of the oculomotor nerve (CN III). Most cases are due to hemorrhage into a pituitary adenoma. Pituitary apoplexy is often complicated by acute secondary adrenal insufficiency, which can be life-threatening. Patients with suspected pituitary apoplexy should therefore receive immediate high-dose glucocorticoid therapy.

title: Etiologies of metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia include vomiting, diuretic use, or abnormal renal sodium handling (eg, Gitelman and
body: Etiologies of metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia include vomiting, diuretic use, or abnormal renal sodium handling (eg, Gitelman and Bartter syndromes). Urinary chloride level is typically low in patients with vomiting and high in patients with diuretic use or abnormal renal sodium handling.

title: Patients with diabetic ketoacidosis should receive high-flow intravenous (IV) fluids and IV insulin
body: Patients with diabetic ketoacidosis should receive high-flow intravenous (IV) fluids and IV insulin. Isotonic saline (NS) is preferred initially, with eventual switching to 1/2 NS. Once blood glucose is <200-250 mg/dL, dextrose should be added to the fluids, but IV insulin should be continued. Potassium should also be added to fluids unless serum potassium is elevated (>5.2 mEq/L).

title: Hypomagnesemia is often associated with hypocalcemia and hypokalemia. Persistent hypokalemia despite potassium replacement should prompt a check of serum magnesium.
Hospitalized patients commonly have low T3 due to illness suppressing the conversion of T4 to T3
body: Hospitalized patients commonly have low T3 due to illness suppressing the conversion of T4 to T3. In the setting of low TSH, measuring T3 levels can differentiate between hyperthyroidism (high T3) and euthyroid sick syndrome (low T3). Treating patients with euthyroid sick syndrome is not beneficial, and thyroid function usually normalizes a few weeks after recovery from illness.

title: Hypercalcemia in patients with granulomatous diseases is caused by extra-renal production of 1- hydroxylase, which results in excessive
body: Hypercalcemia in patients with granulomatous diseases is caused by extra-renal production of 1- hydroxylase, which results in excessive conversion of 25-hydroxyvitamin D to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (calcitriol). Glucocorticoids are the treatment of choice in these patients (eg, those with sarcoidosis and lymphoma).

title: Hypercalcemia of malignancy typically presents acutely with severe hypercalcemia (>13 mg∕dL) and significant symptoms, whereas primary
body: Hypercalcemia of malignancy typically presents acutely with severe hypercalcemia (>13 mg∕dL) and significant symptoms, whereas primary hyperparathyroidism typically presents insidiously with mild hypercalcemia (<11 mg∕dL) and minimal symptoms. Most cases of malignancy-associated hypercalcemia are due to parathyroid hormone-related peptide secretion by the tumor.

title: Amiodarone can cause significant thyroid dysfunction due to its high iodine content, direct effects on thyroid follicular cells, and
body: Amiodarone can cause significant thyroid dysfunction due to its high iodine content, direct effects on thyroid follicular cells, and alteration Ofthyroid hormone metabolism. Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis can be caused by increased thyroid hormone synthesis or destruction of thyroid follicles with release of preformed hormone.

title: Stridor after total thyroidectomy is a medical emergency. Evaluation for wound hematoma and the possibility of hypocalcemia and bilateral nerve injury is needed to assure a patent airway.
Most hospitalized patients with diabetes mellitus require insulin to achieve optimal glycemic control
body: Most hospitalized patients with diabetes mellitus require insulin to achieve optimal glycemic control. Basal bolus regimen (consisting of basal, prandial, and correctional insulin forms) is the best option for hospitalized diabetic patients who are allowed to eat their meals.

title: Patients with limited life expectancy are unlikely to live long enough to benefit from the detection of malignancies and are more likely to
body: Patients with limited life expectancy are unlikely to live long enough to benefit from the detection of malignancies and are more likely to experience harm (both physical and psychological) from the diagnosis. Patients with an expected lifespan of <10 years should not be screened for malignancy (eg, breast, colon).

title: Pelvic organ prolapse can be treated conservatively or surgically depending on patient preference, severity of disease, and comorbidities
body: Pelvic organ prolapse can be treated conservatively or surgically depending on patient preference, severity of disease, and comorbidities. Vaginal pessaries and pelvic floor muscle exercises are an effective conservative treatment for most patients.

title: Nucleic acid amplification testing is the most sensitive and specific test for the diagnosis of Chlamydia trachomatis infection
body: Nucleic acid amplification testing is the most sensitive and specific test for the diagnosis of Chlamydia trachomatis infection. Retesting within 3 weeks of treatment is not recommended due to a high rate of false-positive results.

title: Common signs of early pregnancy include fatigue, weight gain, secondary amenorrhea, and uterine enlargement
body: Common signs of early pregnancy include fatigue, weight gain, secondary amenorrhea, and uterine enlargement. A pregnancy test is indicated in all reproductive-age women regardless of sterilization status.

title: Interstitial cystitis causes chronic pelvic pain that increases with bladder filling and is relieved with voiding
body: Interstitial cystitis causes chronic pelvic pain that increases with bladder filling and is relieved with voiding. Urinalysis is typically normal. Treatment includes patient education, avoidance Oftriggers, and oral pharmacotherapy (eg, amitriptyline, pentosan polysulfate sodium).

title: Hirsutism is excess terminal hair growth in androgen-dependent areas (eg, chin, upper lip, upper abdomen, chest, back)
body: Hirsutism is excess terminal hair growth in androgen-dependent areas (eg, chin, upper lip, upper abdomen, chest, back). All women with hirsutism require a serum total testosterone level to evaluate for possible underlying androgen disorders.

title: Plugged milk ducts are localized areas of milk stasis that cause distension of breast tissue, resulting in pain, tender and palpable
body: Plugged milk ducts are localized areas of milk stasis that cause distension of breast tissue, resulting in pain, tender and palpable masses, and no signs of infection in breastfeeding women. Treatment is supportive and includes optimizing breastfeeding.

title: Women age ≥30 with a palpable breast mass and negative breast imaging (eg, mammogram, ultrasound) require further evaluation with a core needle biopsy to exclude malignancy.
Acute cervicitis typically presents with purulent cervical discharge and a friable cervix
body: Acute cervicitis typically presents with purulent cervical discharge and a friable cervix. Management includes nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea as well as empiric treatment with azithromycin plus ceftriaxone.

title: Pituitary prolactinomas (ie, Iactotroph adenomas) present with galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and hyperprolactinemia
body: Pituitary prolactinomas (ie, Iactotroph adenomas) present with galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and hyperprolactinemia. A prolactin level >200 ng/mL usually indicates a prolactinoma. Diagnosis is confirmed via MRI of the head. First-line treatment is with dopamine agonists (eg, Cabergoline, bromocriptine).

title: Vulvovaginal atrophy (genitourinary syndrome of menopause) typically presents with dyspareunia due to vaginal introitus narrowing. Treatment is with water-based lubricants and vaginal estrogen.
Women who have sex with women have risk factors for ovarian cancer (eg, low parity, low contraceptive use); however, despite these risk
body: Women who have sex with women have risk factors for ovarian cancer (eg, low parity, low contraceptive use); however, despite these risk factors, they are still considered to be at average risk. Ovarian cancer screening in low- or average-risk women is not indicated.

title: Tamoxifen, an estrogen antagonist in the breast, is used for adjuvant therapy in some patients with estrogen receptor-positive breast
body: Tamoxifen, an estrogen antagonist in the breast, is used for adjuvant therapy in some patients with estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. Tamoxifen is associated with an increased risk for venous thromboembolism.

title: Nonclassic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) presents with hyperandrogenism and ovulatory dysfunction similar to polycystic ovary
body: Nonclassic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) presents with hyperandrogenism and ovulatory dysfunction similar to polycystic ovary syndrome, and has a later onset than classic CAH. Diagnosis is confirmed by elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels that significantly increase after ACTH administration.

title: Mastalgia is a benign breast condition characterized by bilateral breast pain and tenderness that occurs up to 2 weeks prior to menses and
body: Mastalgia is a benign breast condition characterized by bilateral breast pain and tenderness that occurs up to 2 weeks prior to menses and wanes with the onset of menses. Symptomatic relief can be achieved by wearing a properly fitted bra that provides adequate breast support.

title: Diagnostic criteria for bacterial vaginosis include a thin, gray, malodorous vaginal discharge; a vaginal pH >4.5; an amine odor after the
body: Diagnostic criteria for bacterial vaginosis include a thin, gray, malodorous vaginal discharge; a vaginal pH >4.5; an amine odor after the application of potassium hydroxide (eg, "whiff” test); and clue cells on wet mount microscopy. Treatment is with metronidazole or clindamycin.

title: Polycystic ovary syndrome presents with menstrual irregularities and hyperandrogenism and is diagnosed after excluding other mimicking
body: Polycystic ovary syndrome presents with menstrual irregularities and hyperandrogenism and is diagnosed after excluding other mimicking disorders. Imaging is not required for diagnosis but is recommended in patients with suspected androgen-secreting tumors. Oral contraceptive pills and weight loss are first-line therapies.

title: Estrogen-based menopausal hormone therapy is contraindicated in patients with a history of venous thromboembolism, breast cancer, coronary
body: Estrogen-based menopausal hormone therapy is contraindicated in patients with a history of venous thromboembolism, breast cancer, coronary heart disease, or active liver disease. Nonhormonal treatments include selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, and gabapentin.

title: Paget disease of the breast is characterized by a unilateral, erythematous, intensely pruritic, ulcerative lesion of the nipple-areolar
body: Paget disease of the breast is characterized by a unilateral, erythematous, intensely pruritic, ulcerative lesion of the nipple-areolar complex. Diagnosis is by tissue biopsy. Patients also require diagnostic bilateral mammography, as many have underlying breast malignancy.

title: Primary dysmenorrhea is a common cause of cyclic menstrual pelvic pain
body: Primary dysmenorrhea is a common cause of cyclic menstrual pelvic pain. Diagnosis is clinical; patients with cyclic pelvic pain and a normal pelvic examination require no further evaluation. Treatment is with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and/or combination oral contraceptives.

title: Current cervical cancer screening guidelines are Pap testing alone every 3 years at age 21-65 or Pap plus human papillomavirus cotesting
body: Current cervical cancer screening guidelines are Pap testing alone every 3 years at age 21-65 or Pap plus human papillomavirus cotesting every 5 years at age 30-65. Screening can be discontinued in low-risk women age >65 with prior adequate screening.

title: Postmenopausal bleeding (PMB) requires assessment with either transvaginal ultrasound or endometrial biopsy to rule out endometrial cancer
body: Postmenopausal bleeding (PMB) requires assessment with either transvaginal ultrasound or endometrial biopsy to rule out endometrial cancer. Although vaginal atrophy is the most common cause of PMB, the incidence of endometrial cancer increases with age and should be ruled out.

title: Vulvovaginal candidiasis is a common cause Ofvaginal discharge and pruritus
body: Vulvovaginal candidiasis is a common cause Ofvaginal discharge and pruritus. Diagnosis is confirmed by pseudohyphae and budding yeast on microscopy. Treatment is with a single dose of oral fluconazole or a topical azole.

title: Patients with stress urinary incontinence should be evaluated for modifiable risk factors
body: Patients with stress urinary incontinence should be evaluated for modifiable risk factors. Initial treatment is with behavioral therapy and pelvic floor muscle exercises. Surgical therapy should be reserved for those who fail noninvasive therapy.

title: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea presents in patients with secondary amenorrhea, low FSH, and low estrogen levels secondary to relative
body: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea presents in patients with secondary amenorrhea, low FSH, and low estrogen levels secondary to relative caloric deficiency (eg, excessive exercise, weight loss). First-line treatment is with life-style changes, including decreasing exercise and increasing caloric intake.

title: Short-term (<5 years) hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is recommended for postmenopausal women with moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms
body: Short-term (<5 years) hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is recommended for postmenopausal women with moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms. Combined estrogen/progesterone is the first-line treatment for patients with an intact uterus and no history of breast cancer or cardiovascular disease. HRT is not recommended for prevention of dementia, heart disease, or osteoporosis.

title: Lifestyle modifications and behavioral therapy (eg, pelvic muscle exercises, bladder training) are first-line treatments for urgency
body: Lifestyle modifications and behavioral therapy (eg, pelvic muscle exercises, bladder training) are first-line treatments for urgency incontinence. Keeping a voiding diary, scheduling bladder emptying, and slowly increasing the time between voids can be an effective therapy for urgency incontinence. If first-line treatments fail, pharmacologic therapy (eg, antimuscarinics, beta-3 agonists) is initiated.

title: The treatment goals in polycystic ovary syndrome are improvement in hyperandrogenism symptoms, ovulation induction in women desiring
body: The treatment goals in polycystic ovary syndrome are improvement in hyperandrogenism symptoms, ovulation induction in women desiring pregnancy, and evaluation/treatment of comorbidities. Oral contraceptives are first-line therapy for hirsutism. An anti-androgen (eg, spironolactone) is added if there is an inadequate cosmetic response after 6 months of oral contraceptive therapy.

title: Overflow incontinence presents with continuous leakage of urine secondary to urinary retention caused by underactive detrusor function (eg
body: Overflow incontinence presents with continuous leakage of urine secondary to urinary retention caused by underactive detrusor function (eg, diabetes mellitus) or outflow obstruction (eg, pelvic organ prolapse). Treatment focuses on correcting reversible causes, cholinergic agonists, and intermittent self­ catheterization.

title: Physiologic Ieukorrhea occurs due to elevated estrogen levels associated with combination hormonal contraceptive use
body: Physiologic Ieukorrhea occurs due to elevated estrogen levels associated with combination hormonal contraceptive use. Patients typically have a normal pelvic examination, pH, and microscopy. Physiologic Ieukorrhea does not require treatment.

title: Patients with Pap test results showing atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASCUS) require human papillomavirus (HPV)
body: Patients with Pap test results showing atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASCUS) require human papillomavirus (HPV) co-testing to determine the risk of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or cervical cancer. A negative HPV test indicates no increased risk for malignancy.

title: Recurrent urinary tract infections are defined as >2 infections in 6 months or >3 infections in 1 year
body: Recurrent urinary tract infections are defined as >2 infections in 6 months or >3 infections in 1 year. Postcoital or daily prophylactic antibiotics (eg, fluoroquinolones, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, nitrofurantoin) are recommended in patients with recurrent UTIs. Urologic evaluation is not required in most cases of uncomplicated cystitis/pyelonephritis.

title: Current guidelines recommend initiating routine cervical cancer screening at age 21
body: Current guidelines recommend initiating routine cervical cancer screening at age 21. Recommended screening strategies include Pap tests every 3 years from age 21-65 or Pap plus human papillomavirus tests from age 30-65. Screening can be discontinued in most women who are age >65 or have had a total hysterectomy.

title: The human papillomavirus vaccination series is indicated for women age 11-26 and men age 11-21 to reduce the risk of HPV-associated disease
body: The human papillomavirus vaccination series is indicated for women age 11-26 and men age 11-21 to reduce the risk of HPV-associated disease regardless of HIV status, prior incomplete vaccination, or prior abnormal Pap tests.

title: Primary ovarian insufficiency is loss of ovarian function in women age <40, resulting in amenorrhea and menopausal symptoms (eg, hot
body: Primary ovarian insufficiency is loss of ovarian function in women age <40, resulting in amenorrhea and menopausal symptoms (eg, hot flashes, dyspareunia). Risk factors include autoimmune disease, genetic abnormalities (eg, Turner syndrome, fragile X syndrome), and previous chemoradiation. Laboratory evaluation shows elevated FSH and low estradiol levels.

title: Emergency contraception should be provided as soon as possible in patients who had unprotected intercourse
body: Emergency contraception should be provided as soon as possible in patients who had unprotected intercourse. First-line options include the copper-containing intrauterine device and oral levonorgestrel pill.

title: Condyloma acuminata are due to low-oncogenic-risk human papillomavirus infection
body: Condyloma acuminata are due to low-oncogenic-risk human papillomavirus infection. Lesions appear as multiple nonfriable, fungating lesions over the vulva and perianal region. Diagnosis is made clinically and treatment is typically with topical agents.

title: Overflow incontinence is caused by underactive detrusor function or bladder outlet obstruction
body: Overflow incontinence is caused by underactive detrusor function or bladder outlet obstruction. Anticholinergics (eg, tricyclic antidepressants, antihistamines, antimuscarinics) relax the detrusor muscle, increase bladder capacity, and cause urinary retention. Chronic urinary retention leads to dribbling, incomplete emptying, and a large postvoid residual volume.

title: Patients with a ruptured ectopic pregnancy typically have first-trimester vaginal bleeding, lower abdominal pain, hemodynamic instability
body: Patients with a ruptured ectopic pregnancy typically have first-trimester vaginal bleeding, lower abdominal pain, hemodynamic instability, and a complex adnexal mass. A ruptured ectopic pregnancy is managed with surgery.

title: The etiology of ascites can often be determined by evaluation of the ascitic fluid cell count, serum-to- ascites albumin gradient (SAAG)
body: The etiology of ascites can often be determined by evaluation of the ascitic fluid cell count, serum-to- ascites albumin gradient (SAAG), and fluid total protein. Low levels of inflammatory cells and elevations in the SAAG (1.1 g/dL) and fluid total protein (2.5 g/dL) are consistent with ascites due to heart failure.

title: Patients taking chronic NSAIDs at high or moderate risk for Gl toxicity should be switched to either a selective COX-2 inhibitor or be given a PPI or misoprostol in combination with the NSAID.
Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a progressive autoimmune disease leading to fibrosis and destruction of the intrahepatic bile ducts
body: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a progressive autoimmune disease leading to fibrosis and destruction of the intrahepatic bile ducts, and is usually seen in women age 30-65. Clinical features may include pruritus, fatigue, skin hyperpigmentation, hyperlipidemia, and elevated alkaline phosphatase levels. Antimitochondrial antibodies have high sensitivity and specificity for PBC.

title: The initial evaluation of patients with chronic constipation should include detailed history, physical examination, and basic laboratory
body: The initial evaluation of patients with chronic constipation should include detailed history, physical examination, and basic laboratory testing. Those without alarm features can undergo a therapeutic trial of medication adjustment and/or dietary fiber intake and lifestyle modification. Those with alarm features should undergo further evaluation based on history, including additional laboratory testing (eg, TSH level), abdominal imaging, and colonoscopy.

title: Secondary lactose intolerance can develop after acute infection or inflammation and is characterized by crampy abdominal pain, bloating
body: Secondary lactose intolerance can develop after acute infection or inflammation and is characterized by crampy abdominal pain, bloating, increased flatulence, and diarrhea. Management involves a lactose- restricted diet, enzyme replacement, and vitamin D and calcium supplementation. Once the inciting insult resolves, recovery of lactose tolerance can occur over a period of months.

title: Fecal impaction is common in elderly patients and can lead to stool overflow incontinence
body: Fecal impaction is common in elderly patients and can lead to stool overflow incontinence. Evaluation of fecal incontinence should begin with a perineal inspection and digital rectal examination. Management includes manual disimpaction and a chronic bowel regimen to prevent recurrence.

title: Patients with 1 or 2 small tubular adenomas (< 1 cm) with low-grade dysplasia should undergo repeat colonoscopy in 5 years. Any adenoma > 1 cm requires repeat colonoscopy in 3 years.
Inflammatory bowel disease often presents in early adulthood with abdominal pain, diarrhea (with occult or gross blood), and systemic
body: Inflammatory bowel disease often presents in early adulthood with abdominal pain, diarrhea (with occult or gross blood), and systemic symptoms (eg, weight loss, fever, fatigue). It is associated with a high prevalence of Clostridium difficile colonization/infection. Colonoscopy with biopsy is the diagnostic study of choice for ulcerative colitis, and Ileocolonoscopy should be considered for patients with suspected ileocolonic Crohn disease.

title: Bone loss is common in celiac disease due to malabsorption of vitamin D
body: Bone loss is common in celiac disease due to malabsorption of vitamin D. Manifestations may include osteopenia/osteoporosis or osteomalacia with bone pain, muscle weakness, and impaired ambulation. DXA should be performed at the time of diagnosis of celiac disease. In addition to a gluten-free diet, patients with bone disease should receive calcium and vitamin D supplementation.

title: Typhlitis presents most commonly in patients who become neutropenic after chemotherapy
body: Typhlitis presents most commonly in patients who become neutropenic after chemotherapy. Symptoms include fever, right lower-quadrant abdominal pain, nausea with or without vomiting, and watery or bloody diarrhea. Diagnosis is confirmed with computed tomography, and management involves supportive care, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and bowel rest. Patients who deteriorate clinically may require surgery.

title: Primary biliary cholangitis predominantly affects women age 30-65
body: Primary biliary cholangitis predominantly affects women age 30-65. Patients typically have a cholestatic injury pattern on liver biomarkers and positive anti-mitochondrial antibodies. Up to 50% of patients also develop metabolic bone disease, which may manifest as osteoporosis and/or osteomalacia.

title: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant disorder with multiple hamartomatous gastrointestinal tract polyps, pigmented
body: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant disorder with multiple hamartomatous gastrointestinal tract polyps, pigmented mucocutaneous papules, and increased risk of malignancy (both gastrointestinal and non-gastrointestinal). Increased surveillance for malignancy is recommended and includes colonoscopy starting at age 18, upper endoscopy and small-bowel series starting at age 8, early mammograms, and testicular examination in boys under age 12.

title: Low-carbohydrate diets can produce rapid initial weight loss
body: Low-carbohydrate diets can produce rapid initial weight loss. Compared with low-fat diets, low- carbohydrate diets produce similar long-term weight loss and improvements in blood pressure and fasting blood glucose. Low-carbohydrate diets are associated with increased incidence of unpleasant gastrointestinal effects.

title: One-time screening for hepatitis C is recommended for individuals at increased risk
body: One-time screening for hepatitis C is recommended for individuals at increased risk. Risks include injection or intranasal drug use, blood transfusion before 1992, long-term hemodialysis, being born to a hepatitis C virus-infected mother, incarceration, unregulated tattoos, and percutaneous exposure. Individuals born between 1945 and 1965 should also be tested.

title: For patients with a first-degree relative with colon cancer at age <60, early colorectal cancer screening with colonoscopy is indicated
body: For patients with a first-degree relative with colon cancer at age <60, early colorectal cancer screening with colonoscopy is indicated; screening should begin at age 40 or 10 years prior to the age of diagnosis of colon cancer in the family, whichever comes first.

title: About 40% of patients develop vitamin B12 deficiency after gastric bypass surgery
body: About 40% of patients develop vitamin B12 deficiency after gastric bypass surgery. The resulting peripheral neuropathy from chronic vitamin B12 deficiency may not be reversible. Patients therefore should be maintained on a daily multivitamin and additional supplementation such as vitamin B12 to avoid potential complications. Monitoring of serum B12 and other micronutrients should be done at 3 months, 6 months, and annually after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass.

title: Oropharyngeal dysphagia is commonly seen after a neurologic injury such as a stroke, and is best diagnosed with a modified barium swallow
body: Oropharyngeal dysphagia is commonly seen after a neurologic injury such as a stroke, and is best diagnosed with a modified barium swallow (MBS). Prompt diagnosis is essential to prevent aspiration pneumonia, which carries high morbidity and mortality rates.

title: Patients with systemic sclerosis may develop small intestinal bacterial overgrowth due to reduced peristalsis and intestinal dilation
body: Patients with systemic sclerosis may develop small intestinal bacterial overgrowth due to reduced peristalsis and intestinal dilation. Clinical features include abdominal bloating, discomfort, diarrhea, and malabsorption. Antibiotic therapy can alleviate the symptoms, but recurrent courses may be required.

title: Pseudoachalasia differs from classic achalasia in that it is caused by a tumor at the gastroesophageal junction and not through impairment
body: Pseudoachalasia differs from classic achalasia in that it is caused by a tumor at the gastroesophageal junction and not through impairment of LES relaxation. It should be considered in older patients (> 60 years), those with shorter symptom duration (< 6 months), or acute weight loss. Diagnosis is made by barium swallow followed by endoscopy.

title: Chronic pancreatitis can lead to splenic vein thrombosis. Gastric varices localized to the gastric fundus confirm the diagnosis. Bleeding from these varices can be cured by splenectomy.
Prostate cancer treatment is the most common reason for radiation injury to the rectum
body: Prostate cancer treatment is the most common reason for radiation injury to the rectum. Acute radiation proctitis can occur during or within 6 weeks of radiation therapy. Chronic radiation proctitis occurs 9-12 months after therapy. Diagnosis is made via sigmoidoscopy, which reveals large, continuous areas of mucosal pallor with friability and telangiectasias.

title: Indications for more immediate endoscopy in gastro esophageal reflux disease (GERD) are based on alarm symptoms (i.e., age > 50 years
body: Indications for more immediate endoscopy in gastro esophageal reflux disease (GERD) are based on alarm symptoms (i.e., age > 50 years, dysphagia, weight loss, anemia, hematemesis/melena). In the absence of these alarm symptoms, a simple trial of proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole) is recommended.

title: Proctitis typically presents with tenesmus, purulent discharge, and small-volume stools containing blood
body: Proctitis typically presents with tenesmus, purulent discharge, and small-volume stools containing blood. Sexually transmitted infections should be considered in proctitis patients engaging in anal intercourse; N gonorrhoeae is the most common causative organism.

title: Autoimmune hepatitis is a chronic hepatitis due to autoantibodies against hepatocytes and is more common in women and individuals age > 40
body: Autoimmune hepatitis is a chronic hepatitis due to autoantibodies against hepatocytes and is more common in women and individuals age > 40. Patients may be asymptomatic, be symptomatic (eg, fatigue, abdominal pain, itching, arthralgias), or develop acute liver failure. Diagnosis is confirmed by antibody testing (anti-nuclear antibody, anti-smooth muscle antibody, and/or anti-liver/kidney microsomal antibody), elevated serum aminotransferases, histology, and exclusion of other chronic liver diseases.

title: Empiric fluconazole therapy can be considered in patients with HIV who have typical oral thrush and esophageal symptoms
body: Empiric fluconazole therapy can be considered in patients with HIV who have typical oral thrush and esophageal symptoms. Treatment for Candida esophagitis requires systemic therapy; it should not be treated with topical antifungals.

title: Peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis usually presents with abdominal pain and nausea
body: Peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis usually presents with abdominal pain and nausea. Fever and leukocytosis may not be present. Diagnosis is suggested by peritoneal fluid showing >100 WBCs or > 50% neutrophils (regardless of fluid WBC count), and is confirmed with positive peritoneal fluid cultures.

title: Rectovaginal fistulas should be suspected in Crohn's disease patients complaining of vaginal fecal discharge, increased vaginal gas, or
body: Rectovaginal fistulas should be suspected in Crohn's disease patients complaining of vaginal fecal discharge, increased vaginal gas, or severe malodorous discharge. Initial medical therapy consists of antibiotics for mild symptoms and anti-TNF inhibitors for moderate to severe symptoms. Surgery is usually reserved for patients who fail medical therapy or develop recurrent fistulas.

title: Chronic mesenteric ischemia presents with fear of eating (Sitophobia) and intermittent dull postprandial epigastric pain that resolves
body: Chronic mesenteric ischemia presents with fear of eating (Sitophobia) and intermittent dull postprandial epigastric pain that resolves within 2 hours. Noninvasive imaging (computed tomography scan, magnetic resonance angiography, or duplex ultrasonography) is preferred over angiography for initially diagnosing the high-grade stenoses in multiple mesenteric vessels.

title: Initial Clostridium difficile infection is treated with oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin
body: Initial Clostridium difficile infection is treated with oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin. Intravenous metronidazole should be added to high-dose oral vancomycin in patients with fulminant infection (eg, hypotension, ileus, megacolon). Treatment options for the first recurrence include a prolonged course of oral vancomycin given in a pulsed and tapered regimen or oral fidaxomicin.

title: Patients presenting with peptic ulcer disease and Helicobacter pylori infection from an endemic area should have biopsies of the ulcer to
body: Patients presenting with peptic ulcer disease and Helicobacter pylori infection from an endemic area should have biopsies of the ulcer to rule out malignancy. Endoscopy may be repeated in 6 weeks after therapy if the biopsies were inadequate or the patient has high risk factors for gastric cancer.

title: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients taking anti-TNF therapy should not receive live vaccines, but they should receive the standard
body: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients taking anti-TNF therapy should not receive live vaccines, but they should receive the standard adult immunizations. Intramuscular influenza and pneumococcal vaccines are recommended for IBD patients on anti-TNF therapy.

title: Empiric fluconazole therapy can be considered in patients with HIV who have typical oral thrush and esophageal symptoms
body: Empiric fluconazole therapy can be considered in patients with HIV who have typical oral thrush and esophageal symptoms. However, endoscopy is indicated for those with severe odynophagia and fevers, especially if they do not have thrush.

title: Gilbert’s syndrome usually presents with asymptomatic isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal liver enzymes and negative
body: Gilbert’s syndrome usually presents with asymptomatic isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with normal liver enzymes and negative work-up for hemolysis. Further invasive tests or treatments are not necessary due to the benign nature of the disease.

title: In the absence of alarm features, chronic slow-transit constipation can be treated with dietary fiber and lifestyle changes
body: In the absence of alarm features, chronic slow-transit constipation can be treated with dietary fiber and lifestyle changes. If pharmacologic therapy is indicated, an initial trial of bulk-forming laxatives such as methylcellulose or psyllium is preferred.

title: Primary biliary cholangitis is characterized by pruritus, fatigue, hepatomegaly, and a cholestatic injury pattern on liver function tests
body: Primary biliary cholangitis is characterized by pruritus, fatigue, hepatomegaly, and a cholestatic injury pattern on liver function tests. It predominantly affects women, and antimitochondrial antibodies are a sensitive marker for diagnosis. Treatment with ursodeoxycholic acid slows development of end-stage liver disease and increases survival.

title: Ascites is usually managed with salt restriction (< 2 g∕day), abstinence from alcohol, avoidance of drugs that cause renal
body: Ascites is usually managed with salt restriction (< 2 g∕day), abstinence from alcohol, avoidance of drugs that cause renal vasoconstriction, and oral diuretics (high-dose spironolactone and low-dose furosemide). Refractory ascites is treated with serial therapeutic paracentesis and possible definitive treatment with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic stent-shunt or liver transplant.

title: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease are at increased risk for developing colorectal cancer
body: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease are at increased risk for developing colorectal cancer. Those with ulcerative colitis involving the entire colon or Crohn disease with colonic involvement should have a surveillance colonoscopy 8-10 years after disease diagnosis, and those with ulcerative colitis limited to the left colon should have a colonoscopy 12-15 years after diagnosis. Colonoscopy is then generally repeated every 1-3 years.

title: Patients with jaundice and abdominal pain should be evaluated for gallstones with ultrasound
body: Patients with jaundice and abdominal pain should be evaluated for gallstones with ultrasound. Those who have no evidence of gallstones should undergo CT scan of the abdomen to evaluate for pancreatic pathology, particularly if there are signs (eg, unintentional weight loss) concerning for malignancy. Depending on CT scan findings, further evaluation with endoscopic ultrasound, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, or MR cholangiopancreatography is often required.

title: Patients with Barrett esophagus and high-grade dysplasia require endoscopic eradication therapy (preferred) or esophagectomy.
Patients with small, distal hyperplastic polyps should be considered to have a normal colonoscopy and are at average risk for colorectal
body: Patients with small, distal hyperplastic polyps should be considered to have a normal colonoscopy and are at average risk for colorectal cancer. Patients with hyperplastic polyposis syndrome are at higher risk of colorectal cancer and require increased colonoscopic surveillance.

title: Microscopic colitis presents as chronic watery diarrhea without bleeding
body: Microscopic colitis presents as chronic watery diarrhea without bleeding. Colonoscopy reveals a grossly normal mucosa with mononuclear lymphocytic infiltrates on biopsy. Initial management includes antidiarrheal medications and discontinuation of causative drugs. Budesonide can be added for persistent symptoms.

title: Patients with achalasia are at an increased risk of subsequent development of squamous cell cancer of the esophagus.
Crohn disease is a common cause of atypical anal fissures
body: Crohn disease is a common cause of atypical anal fissures. Patients with atypical features (eg, lateral or anterior location, multiple, painless, very deep, recurrent, nonhealing) or those who do not improve after 8 weeks of optimal therapy should undergo a colonoscopy for evaluation of Crohn disease.

title: Acute hepatitis B viral (HBV) infection may be associated with serum sickness-like syndrome (fever, symmetric polyarthritis, and urticarial
body: Acute hepatitis B viral (HBV) infection may be associated with serum sickness-like syndrome (fever, symmetric polyarthritis, and urticarial skin lesions without mucosal involvement). Diagnosis is confirmed by the presence of hepatitis B surface antigen. The rash and joint symptoms often resolve within 2-3 weeks followed by development of the icteric phase of HBV infection. Treatment is usually supportive.

title: Chronic liver disease associated with neuropsychiatric manifestations suggests Wilson disease, which is caused by a defect in copper
body: Chronic liver disease associated with neuropsychiatric manifestations suggests Wilson disease, which is caused by a defect in copper transport. Kayser-Fleischer rings are characteristic, but their absence on slit lamp examination does not rule out the diagnosis.

title: Common complications of bariatric gastric bypass surgery include stomal stenosis, dumping syndrome and cholelithiasis
body: Common complications of bariatric gastric bypass surgery include stomal stenosis, dumping syndrome and cholelithiasis. Stomal stenosis at the gastro-jejunal anastomosis typically presents with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and early satiety. Dumping syndrome causes abdominal pain, hypotension and reflex tachycardia.

title: Proctalgia fugax usually presents with severe and episodic rectal pain lasting seconds to minutes that is unrelated to bowel movements
body: Proctalgia fugax usually presents with severe and episodic rectal pain lasting seconds to minutes that is unrelated to bowel movements. Patients are usually asymptomatic between episodes. Diagnosis is made after excluding other gastrointestinal causes of anal and rectal pain.

title: Patients newly diagnosed with cirrhosis require esophagogastroduodenoscopy to document varices and assess the risk for variceal hemorrhage
body: Patients newly diagnosed with cirrhosis require esophagogastroduodenoscopy to document varices and assess the risk for variceal hemorrhage. First-line prophylaxis typically consists of nonselective beta blockers.

title: Celiac disease is associated with hyposplenism; therefore, pneumococcal vaccination is recommended at the time of diagnosis, regardless of
body: Celiac disease is associated with hyposplenism; therefore, pneumococcal vaccination is recommended at the time of diagnosis, regardless of patient age. Other common complications of celiac disease include dermatitis herpetiformis and nutritional deficiencies leading to impaired bone metabolism and neuropathy. Strict adherence to a gluten-free diet can minimize or prevent many of these of complications.

title: Current guidelines suggest routine surveillance with ultrasound every 6 months in patients with chronic hepatitis B infection and/or
body: Current guidelines suggest routine surveillance with ultrasound every 6 months in patients with chronic hepatitis B infection and/or cirrhosis. MRI of the liver has better sensitivity and specificity than CT scan or ultrasound in differentiating malignant nodules from the regenerative nodules associated with cirrhosis. Lesions < 1 cm can be managed with ultrasound follow-up in 3 months.

title: Patients with colorectal cancer who have resectable liver metastases should be offered surgery followed by chemotherapy with curative intent.
Dyspepsia most frequently has no detectable underlying cause; however, it may be a sign of serious pathology (eg, malignancy, peptic ulcer
body: Dyspepsia most frequently has no detectable underlying cause; however, it may be a sign of serious pathology (eg, malignancy, peptic ulcer disease). Patients age ≥60 with new-onset dyspepsia should undergo initial evaluation with upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, whereas those age <60 (without compelling indication for endoscopy) should be tested for Helicobacter pylori or receive a trial of acid suppression.

title: Microscopic colitis causes a chronic nonbloody diarrhea and is often triggered by medications (eg, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs)
body: Microscopic colitis causes a chronic nonbloody diarrhea and is often triggered by medications (eg, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) and smoking. Colonoscopy reveals normal-appearing mucosa with mononuclear lymphocytic infiltrates on biopsy. Management includes removal of offending agents, antidiarrheal agents, and budesonide.

title: Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture) is a medical emergency
body: Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture) is a medical emergency. The classic triad Offorceful vomiting, chest pain, and subcutaneous emphysema should alert the physician about its possibility. Chest x-ray may show mediastinal air and the diagnosis can be confirmed with an esophagram. Another important clinical clue is the rapid development of pleural effusion (often within hours), usually on the left side.

title: Patients with dyspepsia who have not used nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, who have no symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux, or who are
body: Patients with dyspepsia who have not used nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, who have no symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux, or who are age <60 should undergo urea breath testing or stool antigen testing to evaluate for Helicobacter pylori infection and determine further therapy.

title: Metaplastic (chronic) atrophic gastritis is an inflammatory condition that leads to metaplasia of the gastric mucosa and its complications
body: Metaplastic (chronic) atrophic gastritis is an inflammatory condition that leads to metaplasia of the gastric mucosa and its complications (eg, pernicious anemia, gastric ulcers, and cancer). Serum gastrin levels can be profoundly elevated due to hypochlorhydria, but gastric pH will be > 5. Management of atrophic gastritis includes treatment of complications and screening of high-risk individuals for malignancy.

title: Impaired gastric emptying usually presents with early satiety, postprandial reflux, nausea, vomiting, and a succussion splash on
body: Impaired gastric emptying usually presents with early satiety, postprandial reflux, nausea, vomiting, and a succussion splash on examination. All patients should first be evaluated for mechanical or mucosal causes with an upper endoscopy.

title: Up to 20% of patients can fail standard initial therapy for Helicobacter pylori infection
body: Up to 20% of patients can fail standard initial therapy for Helicobacter pylori infection. Patients with persistent symptoms should undergo eradication testing (eg, urea breath test, fecal antigen test, or repeat upper endoscopy) and be treated with an alternate regimen (different triple therapy or quadruple therapy) if positive.

title: Pancreatic pseudocyst should be suspected after an attack of resolved acute pancreatitis in patients with persistently elevated lipase
body: Pancreatic pseudocyst should be suspected after an attack of resolved acute pancreatitis in patients with persistently elevated lipase, abdominal fullness, or early satiety. Diagnosis is confirmed via abdominal computed tomography scan. Most pseudocysts resolve without intervention.

title: Enteropathy-associated T cell lymphoma is an aggressive lymphoma commonly seen in patients with celiac disease and poor dietary control
body: Enteropathy-associated T cell lymphoma is an aggressive lymphoma commonly seen in patients with celiac disease and poor dietary control. Patients present with abdominal pain, B symptoms, hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, bowel obstruction/perforation, and/or gastrointestinal bleeding. Diagnosis is confirmed by pathology of resected tumor. Prognosis is poor, and treatment involves combination chemotherapy.

title: Celiac disease may present with extraintestinal manifestations in the absence of classic intestinal symptoms
body: Celiac disease may present with extraintestinal manifestations in the absence of classic intestinal symptoms. It should be considered in any patient with an autoimmune history who develops unexplained iron deficiency anemia or any of the recognized extraintestinal manifestations.

title: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth is a common complication of gastrointestinal bypass surgery
body: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth is a common complication of gastrointestinal bypass surgery. It presents with abdominal distension and discomfort, flatulence, diarrhea, and nutritional deficiencies. Diagnosis is made with a positive hydrogen breath test Orjejunal aspiration and culture with high levels of bacterial colonization.

title: Patients with Schatzki rings maybe asymptomatic or present with dysphagia and/or reflux symptoms
body: Patients with Schatzki rings maybe asymptomatic or present with dysphagia and/or reflux symptoms. Diagnosis is best confirmed with barium esophagram. Treatment includes dilation and acid suppression therapy, especially for patients with recurrent symptoms requiring repeated dilations.

title: Consistent, modest elevations in aminotransferases are most commonly due to hepatic steatosis (either alcohol- or metabolism-related)
body: Consistent, modest elevations in aminotransferases are most commonly due to hepatic steatosis (either alcohol- or metabolism-related), medications, viral hepatitis, or hemochromatosis. Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease is diagnosed by the exclusion of other common liver diseases.

title: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease is a common cause of elevated liver enzymes in patients with metabolic syndrome and minimal or no alcohol
body: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease is a common cause of elevated liver enzymes in patients with metabolic syndrome and minimal or no alcohol history. Laboratory abnormalities include mild to moderate aminotransferase elevation (2-5 times the upper limit of normal), with an aspartate aminotransferase to alanine aminotransferase ratio typically <1. Iron studies are often abnormal, likely due to chronic inflammation.

title: Colonoscopy is indicated after an episode of diverticulitis to rule out malignancy and assess the severity of disease
body: Colonoscopy is indicated after an episode of diverticulitis to rule out malignancy and assess the severity of disease. Recommendations to decrease consumption of nuts and seeds have not altered outcomes. A high- fiber diet may reduce diverticulitis recurrence.

title: Autoimmune hepatitis is characterized by persistently abnormal Iiverfunction studies (eg, transaminitis) and circulating autoantibodies
body: Autoimmune hepatitis is characterized by persistently abnormal Iiverfunction studies (eg, transaminitis) and circulating autoantibodies, including antinuclear antibody (ANA), antismooth muscle antibody (ASMA), anti-liver/kidney microsomal-1 antibody (LKM-1), and anti-liver cytosol-1 antibody (LC-1). Prednisone is the preferred therapy and is usually combined with azathioprine to allow for lower glucocorticoid doses and fewer side effects.

title: Corticosteroids are useful for achieving initial remission in ulcerative colitis but should not be used to maintain remission
body: Corticosteroids are useful for achieving initial remission in ulcerative colitis but should not be used to maintain remission. In mild-to-moderate disease, 5-aminosalycilate drugs are recommended for maintenance therapy. Other therapies, including azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, and anti-tumor necrosis factor agents, are appropriate for moderate-to-severe disease and steroid-dependent ulcerative colitis.

title: Diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotic therapy
body: Diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotic therapy. Management includes checking stool for Clostridium difficile and supportive measures (eg, hydration, discontinuation of antibiotics, altering diet). Polymerase chain reaction tests for C difficile are very sensitive (97%) and specific (93%).

title: Patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease symptoms that are refractory to once-daily proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy should
body: Patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease symptoms that are refractory to once-daily proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy should increase to twice-daily PPI therapy. In the absence of unexplained alarm symptoms, upper endoscopy is not indicated prior to failure of 4-8 weeks of twice-daily PPI therapy.

title: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease is commonly associated with metabolic syndrome (diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and obesity) in
body: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease is commonly associated with metabolic syndrome (diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and obesity) in patients with minimal alcohol history. Patients should be counseled for gradual weight loss and optimal control of diabetes and hyperlipidemia to help prevent or slow the progression of cirrhosis.

title: Cholestyramine is used to treat diarrhea due to bile salt malabsorption from ileal resection.
Factitious diarrhea is usually due to laxative abuse and is a diagnosis of exclusion that requires a high index of suspicion
body: Factitious diarrhea is usually due to laxative abuse and is a diagnosis of exclusion that requires a high index of suspicion. Stool analysis typically shows osmotic diarrhea with osmolality of 250-400 mθsm∕kg. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy is typically normal, but colonoscopy may show melanosis coli related to chronic laxative abuse.

title: Patients with both iron deficiency anemia and positive stool occult test are evaluated with a combination of upper endoscopy and
body: Patients with both iron deficiency anemia and positive stool occult test are evaluated with a combination of upper endoscopy and colonoscopy to avoid missing simultaneous lesions. If both tests are negative, the next step (for occult bleeding) is small bowel evaluation with wireless capsule endoscopy.

title: Poor-quality bowel preparation may result in missing small polyps on surveillance colonoscopy; therefore, most patients should undergo repeat colonoscopy within a year.
Dumping syndrome is a common complication of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery
body: Dumping syndrome is a common complication of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery. Early dumping syndrome is characterized by abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, and hypotension/tachycardia 15-30 minutes after eating. Late dumping syndrome presents with symptoms of hypoglycemia (eg, dizziness/confusion, fatigue, diaphoresis) 2-3 hours after eating.

title: Uncomplicated diverticulitis can be managed with outpatient oral antibiotics, bowel rest with gradual transition to fluid intake, and close
body: Uncomplicated diverticulitis can be managed with outpatient oral antibiotics, bowel rest with gradual transition to fluid intake, and close follow-up. Hospitalization is indicated for patients with high fever or significant leukocytosis, poor oral intake, significant comorbidities, or immunosuppression. Complicated diverticulitis usually requires intravenous antibiotics and possible computed tomography-guided drainage of fluid collections.

title: Topical nitroglycerin improves blood flow to the anal area to promote wound healing and is preferred for acute fissures
body: Topical nitroglycerin improves blood flow to the anal area to promote wound healing and is preferred for acute fissures. Other conservative measures include adequate fluid and fiber intake, sitz baths, and keeping the anal area dry and clean. Botulinum toxin injection into the anal area also results in rapid healing and is recommended for patients refractory to topical nitroglycerin.

title: Ulcerative colitis is strongly associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis, which should be suspected in those with cholestatic liver
body: Ulcerative colitis is strongly associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis, which should be suspected in those with cholestatic liver injury. Diagnosis is made by findings of multifocal Stricturing and dilation of hepatic bile ducts on MR or endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography.

title: Autonomic dysfunction in longstanding diabetes mellitus can lead to gastrointestinal dysmotility
body: Autonomic dysfunction in longstanding diabetes mellitus can lead to gastrointestinal dysmotility. Diabetic diarrhea is characterized by painless, watery diarrhea, fecal incontinence, and/or alternating normal bowel movements and constipation. Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth is a common complication and may contribute to symptoms.

title: Involuntary weight loss in the elderly is often due to difficulties in obtaining and preparing food
body: Involuntary weight loss in the elderly is often due to difficulties in obtaining and preparing food. Other relatively common causes include loss of appetite and interest in food resulting from either depression or medications and the presence of an underlying malignancy.

title: Patients presenting with acute diarrhea associated with steatorrhea should first be evaluated for infectious etiologies
body: Patients presenting with acute diarrhea associated with steatorrhea should first be evaluated for infectious etiologies. Giardia Iamblia (also known as intestinalis or duodenalis) is the most common infectious cause of malabsorption and is diagnosed with stool microscopy or stool immunoassay. Metronidazole is the treatment of choice.

title: Zenker's diverticulum is a pouch formed by pharyngoesophageal wall herniation above the upper esophageal sphincter
body: Zenker's diverticulum is a pouch formed by pharyngoesophageal wall herniation above the upper esophageal sphincter. Patients usually present with months to years of transient oropharyngeal dysphagia, halitosis, gurgling in the throat, food regurgitation, appearance of a neck mass, and weight loss. Barium swallow is preferred for diagnosis. Treatment usually involves surgery or endoscopy in highly skilled centers.

title: Dyspepsia is usually idiopathic but may be due to gastroesophageal reflux disease, nonsteroidal anti­ inflammatory drugs, or peptic ulcer
body: Dyspepsia is usually idiopathic but may be due to gastroesophageal reflux disease, nonsteroidal anti­ inflammatory drugs, or peptic ulcer disease. Asymptomatic gallstones are common and may coexist with dyspepsia but do not require treatment.

title: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) usually presents with chronic abdominal pain with alternating episodes of constipation and diarrhea
body: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) usually presents with chronic abdominal pain with alternating episodes of constipation and diarrhea. Warning signs/symptoms (eg, nocturnal or worsening abdominal pain, weight loss, rectal bleeding, and laboratory abnormalities) do not usually suggest IBS and require prompt investigation to rule out other etiologies. Underlying celiac disease is commonly misdiagnosed as irritable bowel disease.

title: Patients with clinical features suggesting celiac disease should undergo serologic studies (anti­ transglutaminase IgA or anti-endomysial
body: Patients with clinical features suggesting celiac disease should undergo serologic studies (anti­ transglutaminase IgA or anti-endomysial IgA antibodies); IgA levels should be checked in those with negative results. Patients with positive serologies or highly suggestive symptoms should then undergo endoscopy with biopsy to establish a diagnosis. A cutaneous biopsy showing dermatitis herpetiformis is also diagnostic.

title: The incidence of celiac disease is increased in patients with autoimmune hypothyroidism and can lead to undertreatment of hypothyroidism
body: The incidence of celiac disease is increased in patients with autoimmune hypothyroidism and can lead to undertreatment of hypothyroidism due to malabsorption of levothyroxine. Initial testing should include an IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase antibody assay. A gluten-free diet usually restores the absorption of levothyroxine.

title: Chronic proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use can impair intestinal magnesium absorption and cause hypomagnesemia
body: Chronic proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use can impair intestinal magnesium absorption and cause hypomagnesemia. The incidence of hypomagnesemia is significantly higher when PPIs are combined with other drugs (eg, diuretics) associated with hypomagnesemia.

title: Most patients with cholecystitis should undergo early laparoscopic cholecystectomy as it is associated with reduced morbidity/mortality
body: Most patients with cholecystitis should undergo early laparoscopic cholecystectomy as it is associated with reduced morbidity/mortality. Patients who are at high risk for surgery and fail to improve with conservative treatment (fluids, analgesics, empiric antibiotics) can benefit from percutaneous cholecystostomy.

title: Patients with acute gastrointestinal hemorrhage due to peptic ulcer should undergo endoscopic sampling for Helicobacter pylori
body: Patients with acute gastrointestinal hemorrhage due to peptic ulcer should undergo endoscopic sampling for Helicobacter pylori. However, false-negative results can occur due to active gastrointestinal bleeding or certain medications (eg, proton pump inhibitors, bismuth, antibiotics). Therefore, a negative biopsy should be confirmed by a second test (urea breath or stool antigen) after the patient can safely stop the proton pump inhibitor for 1-2 weeks.

title: Arteriovenous malformation can present with significant lower gastrointestinal bleeding and chronic iron deficiency anemia
body: Arteriovenous malformation can present with significant lower gastrointestinal bleeding and chronic iron deficiency anemia. It is found more commonly in elderly patients with end-stage renal disease and aortic stenosis.

title: The diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia depends on a high index of clinical suspicion in patients with known risk factors for
body: The diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia depends on a high index of clinical suspicion in patients with known risk factors for thromboembolic disease (eg, atrial fibrillation, atherosclerosis). CT or MR angiography of the abdomen is typically used for diagnosis in stable patients.

title: Perforation from routine endoscopic procedures is uncommon and typically occurs from mechanical trauma, barotrauma, electrocautery, or
body: Perforation from routine endoscopic procedures is uncommon and typically occurs from mechanical trauma, barotrauma, electrocautery, or therapeutic interventions. Immediate abdominal (upright or lateral decubitus) and upright chest radiographs can confirm a perforation. Patients with high clinical suspicion for perforation and negative x-rays should undergo CT scan with a water-soluble contrast agent, which can detect subtle perforation. ■ >3 End ® Resources

title: Gastrinoma should be suspected in patients with multiple stomach ulcers and thickened gastric folds on endoscopy
body: Gastrinoma should be suspected in patients with multiple stomach ulcers and thickened gastric folds on endoscopy. The diagnosis is strongly suggested by serum gastrin level > 1000 pg/mL and gastric pH < 4.0. Endoscopic ultrasound, somatostatin receptor scintigraphy, and CT or MRI imaging can localize and stage the gastrinoma.

title: Eosinophilic esophagitis typically presents in younger males with history of asthma or allergies that develop intermittent dysphagia
body: Eosinophilic esophagitis typically presents in younger males with history of asthma or allergies that develop intermittent dysphagia despite treatment for GERD. Emergent endoscopy is indicated for patients with acute food impaction associated with difficulty swallowing or hoarse voice. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis and treatment involves steroids and allergen avoidance.

title: Alcoholic hepatitis (AH) usually presents with acute jaundice, fever, anorexia, right upper- quadrant/epigastric pain, and abdominal
body: Alcoholic hepatitis (AH) usually presents with acute jaundice, fever, anorexia, right upper- quadrant/epigastric pain, and abdominal distention due to ascites. Patients should have other causes of acute hepatitis excluded. An aspartate aminotransferase:alanine aminotransferase ratio >2 in an alcoholic patient usually distinguishes AH from other causes.

title: Spontaneous esophageal rupture is due to acute barotrauma from vomiting or retching that leads to a transmural tear
body: Spontaneous esophageal rupture is due to acute barotrauma from vomiting or retching that leads to a transmural tear. Patients classically present with forceful retching followed by severe retrosternal chest and upper abdominal pain. Diagnosis is confirmed with computed tomography or esophagography with gastrografin.

title: The threshold for blood transfusion in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding (without comorbidity) who are hemodynamically stable is
body: The threshold for blood transfusion in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding (without comorbidity) who are hemodynamically stable is hemoglobin of < 7 g/dL. This results in fewer complications, fewer further episodes of bleeding, and decreased mortality.

title: Budd-Chiari syndrome (thrombosis of hepatic veins) should be suspected in young women who present with rapid onset of abdominal pain and
body: Budd-Chiari syndrome (thrombosis of hepatic veins) should be suspected in young women who present with rapid onset of abdominal pain and ascites. Diagnosis is made by ultrasound with Doppler flow, computed tomography scan, or magnetic resonance angiography. Treatment includes anticoagulation, treatment of liver complications, angioplasty, transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunts, or liver transplant.

title: Patients with proximal small-bowel obstruction present with vomiting and less abdominal distention
body: Patients with proximal small-bowel obstruction present with vomiting and less abdominal distention. Common non-pancreatic causes of lipase elevation include renal insufficiency, diabetic ketoacidosis, and intestinal obstruction or ileus.

title: Patients with peptic ulcers and high-risk features on endoscopy (eg, active bleeding, visible vessels, adherent clot) typically require
body: Patients with peptic ulcers and high-risk features on endoscopy (eg, active bleeding, visible vessels, adherent clot) typically require endoscopic therapy. Following endoscopy, they should be kept in the hospital, placed on a clear liquid diet for 2 days, and continued on a high-dose intravenous proton pump inhibitor for 3 days to minimize bleeding risks.

title: Fulminant Clostridium difficile infection is characterized by hypotension, shock, or the presence of ileus or toxic megacolon
body: Fulminant Clostridium difficile infection is characterized by hypotension, shock, or the presence of ileus or toxic megacolon. Patients with fulminant disease should be treated with high-dose oral vancomycin and intravenous metronidazole. Patients with signs of toxic megacolon, impending perforation, or septic shock require immediate surgical evaluation as they may benefit from subtotal colectomy.

title: Treatment of patients with active variceal bleeding includes hemodynamic resuscitation, intravenous octreotide, prophylactic antibiotics
body: Treatment of patients with active variceal bleeding includes hemodynamic resuscitation, intravenous octreotide, prophylactic antibiotics, and endoscopic therapy. Antibiotics are continued for a total of 7 days even if cultures remain negative.

title: Medication-induced esophagitis is due to direct mucosal injury and is frequently noted with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
body: Medication-induced esophagitis is due to direct mucosal injury and is frequently noted with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, tetracyclines, bisphosphonates, iron supplements, and potassium chloride. Discontinuation of the offending medication is usually adequate treatment, but additional evaluation is indicated for patients with severe, atypical, or persistent symptoms.

title: In a case of corrosive ingestion after initial stabilization is achieved, endoscopy should be performed to grade the severity of injury. Steroids are not recommended in such cases.
Ischemic colitis usually presents with abrupt onset of abdominal pain over the affected large bowel, with subsequent hematochezia
body: Ischemic colitis usually presents with abrupt onset of abdominal pain over the affected large bowel, with subsequent hematochezia. CT scan is the preferred initial diagnostic study to rule out extensive bowel injury. Diagnosis is subsequently confirmed with colonoscopy.

title: Mallory-Weiss tear is an upper gastrointestinal mucosal tear due to a sudden increase of intra-abdominal pressure from forceful retching
body: Mallory-Weiss tear is an upper gastrointestinal mucosal tear due to a sudden increase of intra-abdominal pressure from forceful retching. Endoscopy is preferred for diagnosis. Most patients have self-limited (24- 48 hours) bleeding with spontaneous healing of ulcers. Patients with active bleeding usually require endoscopic treatment with epinephrine injection, cautery, or hemoclip application.

title: Hepatopulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a complication of chronic liver disease that is associated with hypoxemia and Intrapulmonary vascular
body: Hepatopulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a complication of chronic liver disease that is associated with hypoxemia and Intrapulmonary vascular dilatations (IPVDs). Patients typically present with symptoms/signs of liver disease, dyspnea, platypnea, and orthodeoxia. Contrast echocardiography is preferred to diagnose IPVDs and confirm likely HPS.

title: Early enteral feeding is associated with a decreased incidence of stress ulcers in critically ill patients
body: Early enteral feeding is associated with a decreased incidence of stress ulcers in critically ill patients. Recommended agents for prophylaxis in high-risk individuals include an oral proton pump inhibitor or intravenous H2 receptor blocker depending on the patient’s ability to receive oral medications.

title: Scurvy (vitamin C deficiency) is commonly associated with gingival hypertrophy, bleeding gums, and petechiae
body: Scurvy (vitamin C deficiency) is commonly associated with gingival hypertrophy, bleeding gums, and petechiae. A low ascorbic acid level is diagnostic; treatment with oral or injectable vitamin C rapidly improves symptoms.

title: Patients presenting with markedly elevated hepatic aminotransferases should raise suspicion for acetaminophen toxicity. N-acetylcysteine is the antidote of choice.
Stress ulcer prophylaxis may be beneficial in high-risk critically ill patients but should be discontinued once the patient leaves the
body: Stress ulcer prophylaxis may be beneficial in high-risk critically ill patients but should be discontinued once the patient leaves the intensive care unit and no longer has an indication. Unnecessary use of proton pump inhibitors may be associated with adverse affects (eg, nosocomial pneumonia, Clostridium difficile infection) and higher costs.

title: Incidental gallstones are a common finding in patients with abdominal pain but do not require treatment if they are not the cause of the
body: Incidental gallstones are a common finding in patients with abdominal pain but do not require treatment if they are not the cause of the symptoms. Patients with incidental gallstones who present with atypical features (lack of biliary colic) should be evaluated for other causes of pain.

title: Initial management of opioid-induced constipation typically includes increasing fluid/fiber intake and physical activity in addition to
body: Initial management of opioid-induced constipation typically includes increasing fluid/fiber intake and physical activity in addition to therapy with daily senna-docusate or an osmotic laxative (eg, polyethylene glycol, lactulose). Refractory constipation may respond to treatment with methylnaltrexone, a peripherally acting opioid antagonist.

title: Ogilvie syndrome presents with marked colonic dilation without evidence of obstruction and frequently occurs in elderly males
body: Ogilvie syndrome presents with marked colonic dilation without evidence of obstruction and frequently occurs in elderly males. Therapy is usually supportive with treatment of possible underlying causes; neostigmine is indicated in patients who fail conservative therapy. Those who fail neostigmine or have contraindications may require colonoscopic or surgical decompression.

title: Severe ulcerative colitis flare is characterized by >6 bloody bowel movements per day, tachycardia, anemia, fever, severe cramps, weight
body: Severe ulcerative colitis flare is characterized by >6 bloody bowel movements per day, tachycardia, anemia, fever, severe cramps, weight loss, and elevated inflammatory markers. Treatment includes systemic glucocorticoids and high-dose 5-aminosalicylic acid compounds. Treatment should not be withheld while awaiting test results due to the risk of developing toxic megacolon.

title: Intrahepatic cholestasis is suspected in patients with a cholestatic pattern of liver injury and absence of biliary obstruction on
body: Intrahepatic cholestasis is suspected in patients with a cholestatic pattern of liver injury and absence of biliary obstruction on abdominal ultrasound. Drug toxicity is an important cause of intrahepatic cholestasis and often occurs with antibiotic use. Removal of the offending agent will lead to recovery in most patients.

title: Infected necrosis should be suspected in patients with necrotizing pancreatitis who do not improve or who deteriorate clinically after a
body: Infected necrosis should be suspected in patients with necrotizing pancreatitis who do not improve or who deteriorate clinically after a week of hospitalization. These patients can either be treated with empiric antibiotics (eg, carbapenem) or first undergo CT-guided aspiration to direct antimicrobial therapy. Percutaneous/open surgical debridement may be necessary in patients who fail to respond to antibiotics.

title: History, physical examination, laboratory tests, and imaging studies should be aimed towards finding a precipitating cause in patients with
body: History, physical examination, laboratory tests, and imaging studies should be aimed towards finding a precipitating cause in patients with hepatic encephalopathy. If no obvious cause is evident from this work­ up, patients with ascites should undergo a diagnostic paracentesis to rule out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

title: Neoadjuvant concurrent chemoradiotherapy is the standard of care in locally advanced (T3∕T4) rectal cancer
body: Neoadjuvant concurrent chemoradiotherapy is the standard of care in locally advanced (T3∕T4) rectal cancer. Neoadjuvant therapy causes significant down-staging of the primary tumor before resection and is associated with higher rates of sphincter preservation and local control.

title: Feeding tubes have not been demonstrated to provide adequate nutrition, prevent pressure ulcers or aspiration pneumonia, afford comfort
body: Feeding tubes have not been demonstrated to provide adequate nutrition, prevent pressure ulcers or aspiration pneumonia, afford comfort, improve functional status, or prolong life in patients with advanced dementia.

title: Early endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography is indicated in patients with gallstone pancreatitis and evidence of common bile duct
body: Early endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography is indicated in patients with gallstone pancreatitis and evidence of common bile duct obstruction or acute cholangitis. Cholecystectomy should be performed after recovery to reduce the risk of recurrence in these patients.

title: Acute onset of left upper-quadrant pain raises the possibility of splenic infarction in patients with sickle cell trait (Hb AS); diagnosis
body: Acute onset of left upper-quadrant pain raises the possibility of splenic infarction in patients with sickle cell trait (Hb AS); diagnosis is through hemoglobin electrophoresis. Treatment of splenic infarction is supportive.

title: Sigmoid volvulus is formed by twisting of a segment of the intestine, often leading to bowel obstruction and gangrene if untreated
body: Sigmoid volvulus is formed by twisting of a segment of the intestine, often leading to bowel obstruction and gangrene if untreated. Sigmoid volvulus is more common in elderly patients who are institutionalized or affected by neurologic or psychiatric conditions. Uncomplicated sigmoid volvulus is treated with sigmoidoscopy. Surgery is reserved for recurrent or complicated cases.

title: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia suggest the possibility of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP)
body: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia suggest the possibility of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). It is rare to see the full classic pentad. The idiopathic form of TTP is due to an antibody directed against a von Willebrand factor-cleaving protease (ADAMTS13) and is a medical emergency requiring prompt treatment with plasma exchange to replace the protease and prevent end­ organ damage. Measurement of low ADAMTS13 activity is not required to make the diagnosis.

title: Superior pulmonary sulcus (Pancoast) tumors arise in the apical pleuropulmonary groove and typically present with shoulder pain (most
body: Superior pulmonary sulcus (Pancoast) tumors arise in the apical pleuropulmonary groove and typically present with shoulder pain (most common), Horner syndrome, and/or C8-T2 neurological findings (eg, paresthesias in the fourth and fifth digits). Chest x-ray is usually the first diagnostic step; additional chest imaging (eg, CT scan, MRI) and core needle biopsy are then typically required.

title: Pseudothrombocytopenia occurs due to ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-Induced platelet clumping and should be suspected in
body: Pseudothrombocytopenia occurs due to ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA)-Induced platelet clumping and should be suspected in asymptomatic patients with low platelet counts. A repeat platelet count using an anticoagulant other than EDTA that shows normal platelets confirms the diagnosis.

title: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia typically presents with absolute lymphocytosis (>5,000∕mnv) in an asymptomatic older patient
body: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia typically presents with absolute lymphocytosis (>5,000∕mnv) in an asymptomatic older patient. Physical examination often reveals Iymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and/or hepatomegaly. Diagnosis is confirmed with peripheral blood smear and peripheral blood flow cytometry. Lymph node and bone marrow biopsies are not required. ■ I

title: Supratherapeutic INR <5 without significant bleeding can be managed by holding warfarin
body: Supratherapeutic INR <5 without significant bleeding can be managed by holding warfarin. INR 5-9 is managed similarly if no bleeding is present; those with increased bleeding risk may also be treated with low-dose oral vitamin K. INR >9 requires temporary warfarin cessation and high-dose oral vitamin K.
