Life­ threatening or serious bleeding with any INR requires holding warfarin and immediate INR reversal (eg, intravenous vitamin K, fresh frozen plasma).

title: Essential thrombocythemia is a clonal myeloproliferative disorder characterized by platelet counts >450,000∕mm
body: Essential thrombocythemia is a clonal myeloproliferative disorder characterized by platelet counts >450,000∕mm . Patients may be asymptomatic or have vasomotor symptoms, thrombosis, and/or hemorrhage. Approximately 20% of patients develop acquired von Willebrand disease, which may limit the ability to use aspirin in treatment.

title: Anemia of chronic disease (ACD) is usually due to a systemic illness that alters iron metabolism or decreases erythropoiesis
body: Anemia of chronic disease (ACD) is usually due to a systemic illness that alters iron metabolism or decreases erythropoiesis. Clinically difficult cases can be distinguished from IDA through bone marrow analysis which shows increased iron staining in the macrophages, but decreased staining in the erythrocyte precursors.

title: Hairy cell leukemia (HCL) is a rare, mature B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder that typically causes splenomegaly and pancytopenia
body: Hairy cell leukemia (HCL) is a rare, mature B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder that typically causes splenomegaly and pancytopenia. HCL is usually suspected when a peripheral blood smear shows tumor cells that are 1-2 times the size of normal lymphocytes with "hairy" projections. Confirmation is made with peripheral blood flow cytometry and trephine bone marrow biopsy with immunohistochemical stains.

title: Renal cell cancer can be asymptomatic or present with abdominal pain, abdominal mass, and hematuria
body: Renal cell cancer can be asymptomatic or present with abdominal pain, abdominal mass, and hematuria. Advanced renal cell cancer can be associated with a variety of paraneoplastic symptoms including hypercalcemia, erythrocytosis, and weight loss.

title: The BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations account for the majority of the hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome
body: The BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations account for the majority of the hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome. Women with BRCA1 or 2 should be offered risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy when childbearing is complete or at age 35-40.

title: Prolonged aPTT or PT can be evaluated by using mixing studies
body: Prolonged aPTT or PT can be evaluated by using mixing studies. Factor deficiency will result in a normal clotting test after plasma mixing, while an inhibitor will cause persistent prolongation of the aPTT or PT.

title: In patients who received chest radiation, annual screening mammograms are recommended starting 8-10 years after radiation therapy. Annual TSH testing is also recommended in these patients.
Individuals exposed to chemotherapeutic agents are at risk for developing myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), mixed
body: Individuals exposed to chemotherapeutic agents are at risk for developing myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), mixed myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasms (MDS/MPN), and acute myeloid leukemias (AML).

title: Small cell lung cancer is very responsive to systemic platinum-based chemotherapy (eg, etoposide plus cisplatin)
body: Small cell lung cancer is very responsive to systemic platinum-based chemotherapy (eg, etoposide plus cisplatin). Patients with localized disease (limited to the ipsilateral hemithorax) also typically receive concurrent thoracic radiation. Those with extensive disease (metastatic, contralateral lymph nodes, malignant pericardial/pleural effusion) initially receive systemic chemotherapy alone.

title: Patients with isolated thrombocytopenia should undergo thorough evaluation to rule out secondary causes (e.g., drugs and infections), which
body: Patients with isolated thrombocytopenia should undergo thorough evaluation to rule out secondary causes (e.g., drugs and infections), which includes HIV testing and possible hepatitis C testing. Patients with negative results on both of these studies are presumed to have ITP

title: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) is a common disorder (seen in an aging population) that does not require specific
body: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) is a common disorder (seen in an aging population) that does not require specific treatment but merits close clinical monitoring. It is stratified according to the risk of disease progression. Higher-risk MGUS patients should undergo a baseline bone marrow biopsy to document <10% clonal plasma cells.

title: Patients with brain metastases from most cancer types can safely receive anticoagulation with low- molecular-weight heparin without an
body: Patients with brain metastases from most cancer types can safely receive anticoagulation with low- molecular-weight heparin without an increased risk of intracerebral hemorrhage. Brain metastases from melanoma, choriocarcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, or renal cell carcinoma are associated with a greater risk of intracerebral hemorrhage; these individuals require a nuanced assessment of the risks and benefits of anticoagulation prior to initiation of therapy.

title: Polycythemia is defined as a hemoglobin level >16 g/dL in women and >16.5 g/dL in men and is typically categorized into primary and
body: Polycythemia is defined as a hemoglobin level >16 g/dL in women and >16.5 g/dL in men and is typically categorized into primary and secondary causes. Primary polycythemia is erythropoietin (EPO)- independe∩t and is usually associated with low EPO levels; polycythemia vera is the most common cause and is usually diagnosed by JAK2 mutation testing and bone marrow biopsy. Secondary polycythemia is usually EPO-dependent and marked by high EPO levels; hypoxia is the most common cause and is typically diagnosed by oxygen saturation testing at rest, after exercise, and during sleep.

title: Myelofibrosis is characterized by bone marrow fibrosis, massive splenomegaly, normocytic anemia, and circulating immature myeloid cells
body: Myelofibrosis is characterized by bone marrow fibrosis, massive splenomegaly, normocytic anemia, and circulating immature myeloid cells, erythroblasts, and teardrop cells. Bone marrow aspirate usually results in a dry tap, and diagnosis requires bone marrow biopsy to confirm fibrosis and exclude other causes of marrow involvement.

title: The 3-step pain relief ladder process begins with nonopioid drugs
body: The 3-step pain relief ladder process begins with nonopioid drugs. Patients who have insufficient pain control should be started on a weak opioid. If the weak opioid is unable to control the pain, it should be switched to a strong opioid (eg, morphine). However, patients with severe pain require initial therapy with a short-acting, strong opioid.

title: Systemic lupus erythematosus patients may present with warm agglutinin autoimmune hemolytic anemia
body: Systemic lupus erythematosus patients may present with warm agglutinin autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Diagnosis is established with positive direct Coombs' test with IgG. Corticosteroids are the first-line therapy. Refractory disease requires splenectomy.

title: Differentiation of breast cancer into subtypes is important to guide further therapy
body: Differentiation of breast cancer into subtypes is important to guide further therapy. Triple-negative breast cancer accounts for 20% of all breast cancers. Radiation therapy after chemotherapy is indicated in the adjuvant treatment of breast cancer.

title: Myelofibrosis and acute myeloid leukemia/myelodysplastic syndrome are the major long-term complications of polycythemia vera (PV)
body: Myelofibrosis and acute myeloid leukemia/myelodysplastic syndrome are the major long-term complications of polycythemia vera (PV). Patients with post-PV myelofibrosis present with anemia, decreased need for phlebotomy, worsening splenomegaly, and constitutional symptoms. Diagnosis is made by bone marrow biopsy.

title: Erythromelalgia usually presents with recurrent episodic warmth, redness, and burning in the extremities symmetrically
body: Erythromelalgia usually presents with recurrent episodic warmth, redness, and burning in the extremities symmetrically. Secondary erythromelalgia usually indicates an underlying myeloproliferative disorder. Treatment is directed towards the underlying disorder in secondary erythromelalgia, and aspirin may relieve symptoms in most patients.

title: Carcinoid tumors are rare neuroendocrine tumors that cause episodic flushing, diarrhea, bronchospasm, and cardiac lesions
body: Carcinoid tumors are rare neuroendocrine tumors that cause episodic flushing, diarrhea, bronchospasm, and cardiac lesions. Elevated 24-hour urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid can confirm the diagnosis in most patients. Abdominal imaging (eg, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging) and OctreoScan can stage and localize tumor. Treatment involves somatostatin analogs (eg, octreotide) and surgery or chemoembolization for liver metastases.

title: Patients with chronic kidney disease and anemia should first be evaluated for iron deficiency and then treated with erythropoietin to
body: Patients with chronic kidney disease and anemia should first be evaluated for iron deficiency and then treated with erythropoietin to achieve a goal hemoglobin level of 10-11 g/dL. Higher levels of hemoglobin may be associated with increased morbidity and mortality.

title: Patients who received intracranial irradiation (e.g., childhood ALL) are at an increased risk Ofdeveloping brain tumors (primarily meningiomas) after a prolonged latency period.
The 2 most common causes of spherocytosis are autoimmune hemolytic anemia and hereditary spherocytosis (HS)
body: The 2 most common causes of spherocytosis are autoimmune hemolytic anemia and hereditary spherocytosis (HS). The direct antiglobulin test (Coombs) is negative in HS patients. The diagnosis of HS is confirmed with the eosin-5-maleimide binding (flow cytometry) or acidified glycerol lysis tests. Treatment of HS includes red blood cell transfusion for symptomatic anemia, folic acid supplementation, and splenectomy for severe cases.

title: Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) should be suspected in patients who have ≥1 cytopenias with no clear alternate (eg, medications, B-∣2
body: Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) should be suspected in patients who have ≥1 cytopenias with no clear alternate (eg, medications, B-∣2 deficiency) cause. Diagnostic evaluation requires peripheral blood smear and bone marrow aspirate/biopsy to assess for dysplastic cytologic features consistent with MDS.

title: Thyroglobulin is secreted by most differentiated thyroid cancers and is a useful marker of recurrent or persistent cancer following
body: Thyroglobulin is secreted by most differentiated thyroid cancers and is a useful marker of recurrent or persistent cancer following thyroidectomy and radioactive iodine ablation. Elevated thyroglobulin requires further testing with neck ultrasound and diagnostic radioiodine scan.

title: Cancer-related anemia is common and can be due to a myriad of causes
body: Cancer-related anemia is common and can be due to a myriad of causes. Treatment should be considered for patients with hemoglobin levels <10 mg/dL who are symptomatic (eg, exertional fatigue, orthostasis, dyspnea, sustained tachycardia, chest pain). Asymptomatic patients do not usually require treatment and can be monitored with serial hemoglobins.

title: Biopsy should be performed if an abnormal node has not resolved after four weeks, there are findings suggesting malignancy, or generalized
body: Biopsy should be performed if an abnormal node has not resolved after four weeks, there are findings suggesting malignancy, or generalized Iymphadenopathy of uncertain etiology is present. An excisional biopsy of an intact node is preferred. Ideally, the largest, most suspicious, and most accessible node is selected; but if no single node predominates, the choices in descending order in regards to diagnostic yield are supraclavicular, cervical, axillary, and inguinal.

title: Absolute basophilia and eosinophilia in the peripheral blood are very suspicious for underlying myeloproliferative disorders, especially
body: Absolute basophilia and eosinophilia in the peripheral blood are very suspicious for underlying myeloproliferative disorders, especially CML. Nearly 90-95% of patients with CML have the Philadelphia translocation. The resulting BCR-ABL fusion protein can be detected in the peripheral blood to confirm the diagnosis.

title: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) may present in phases (chronic stable, accelerated, or blast phase) with nonspecific systemic symptoms
body: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) may present in phases (chronic stable, accelerated, or blast phase) with nonspecific systemic symptoms, leukocytosis, anemia, and thrombocytosis. Diagnosis is confirmed by identifying the Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABLI fusion gene, or BCR-ABLI fusion mRNA. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., imatinib) are first line agents for the treatment of CML.

title: Patients with sickle cell disease are at high risk for ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke
body: Patients with sickle cell disease are at high risk for ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Exchange transfusion is recommended for acute stroke; scheduled simple transfusions are recommended to prevent recurrent strokes.

title: Xerostomia occurs in approximately 80% of patients who receive radiotherapy for head and neck cancers
body: Xerostomia occurs in approximately 80% of patients who receive radiotherapy for head and neck cancers. Treatment includes supportive measures (eg, saline rinses, mouth lubricants) and pharmacotherapy with parasympathomimetic agents (eg, cevimeline) to stimulate salivary flow.

title: Celiac disease is a relatively common cause of iron deficiency anemia due to decreased intestinal iron absorption
body: Celiac disease is a relatively common cause of iron deficiency anemia due to decreased intestinal iron absorption. The most sensitive and specific serologic test to diagnose celiac disease is anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies.

title: Small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors (eg, imatinib, sorafenib, and sunitinib) are associated with skin reactions such as hand-foot
body: Small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors (eg, imatinib, sorafenib, and sunitinib) are associated with skin reactions such as hand-foot skin reaction (HFSR). Patients with HFSR present with focal, tender lesions that appear as blisters or hyperkeratosis in areas of friction or trauma. Treatment is supportive and discontinuation of tyrosine kinase inhibitor is not usually necessary.

title: Increased cure rates and long-term survival for cancer patients make quality-of-life issues such as fertility preservation important
body: Increased cure rates and long-term survival for cancer patients make quality-of-life issues such as fertility preservation important. Referral to a reproductive endocrinologist must be made as early as possible after diagnosis to avoid treatment delays.

title: Lymphadenopathy can be observed for 3-4 weeks in patients with no signs or symptoms of malignancy; those with persistent Iymphadenopathy
body: Lymphadenopathy can be observed for 3-4 weeks in patients with no signs or symptoms of malignancy; those with persistent Iymphadenopathy require excisional lymph node biopsy to evaluate for cancer. Indolent lymphomas often present with months Ofwaxing and waning painless, localized Iymphadenopathy without other manifestations.

title: Elderly patients with poor performance status who present with advanced NSCLC typically do not respond well to aggressive therapy
body: Elderly patients with poor performance status who present with advanced NSCLC typically do not respond well to aggressive therapy. Early palliative care with hospice referral may help prolong life and enhance quality of life.

title: Symptomatic cobalamin deficiency can be present in the absence of macrocytic anemia and a reduction of serum cobalamin below the lower
body: Symptomatic cobalamin deficiency can be present in the absence of macrocytic anemia and a reduction of serum cobalamin below the lower limit of normal. In this setting, an elevated serum methylmalonic acid is an important adjunctive test to confirm a diagnosis of cobalamin deficiency.

title: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) diagnosis requires >5000 B lymphocytes∕mιτr in the peripheral blood and flow cytometry confirmation of
body: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) diagnosis requires >5000 B lymphocytes∕mιτr in the peripheral blood and flow cytometry confirmation of circulating B lymphocyte Clonality. CLL is usually an indolent disease, and asymptomatic patients do not need treatment.

title: Acute graft-versus-host disease occurs within 100 days of hematopoietic stem cell transplant; chronic graft- versus-host disease can occur
body: Acute graft-versus-host disease occurs within 100 days of hematopoietic stem cell transplant; chronic graft- versus-host disease can occur at any time. The skin, liver, and gastrointestinal tract are most commonly affected. Treatment includes steroids for both acute and chronic disease.

title: Approximately 25% of men on testosterone therapy develop polycythemia (hemoglobin >16.5 g∕dL)
body: Approximately 25% of men on testosterone therapy develop polycythemia (hemoglobin >16.5 g∕dL). Polycythemia can be associated with venous thromboembolism and cardiovascular complications. Therefore, patients require hematocrit monitoring; if levels exceed 54%, testosterone should be reduced or discontinued. ■ I>3 End ® Resources Suspend

title: Testing for G6PD deficiency during an acute hemolytic episode may produce a false negative result as the older and more deficient
body: Testing for G6PD deficiency during an acute hemolytic episode may produce a false negative result as the older and more deficient erythrocytes are destroyed and replaced by reticulocytes that commonly have normal G6PD levels. If a false negative is suspected, it is recommended to recheck the G6PD level 2 to 3 months after the hemolytic episode.

title: Alpha- and beta-thalassemia trait usually presents with microcytic and hypochromic anemia often confused with iron deficiency anemia
body: Alpha- and beta-thalassemia trait usually presents with microcytic and hypochromic anemia often confused with iron deficiency anemia. However, thalassemia trait usually has normal (or increased) iron and ferritin stores with mild anemia and normal red cell distribution width. Hemoglobin electrophoresis helps distinguish among the various forms of thalassemia.

title: In patients with advanced cancer, physicians' predictions (based on prior clinical experience), clinical symptoms, and performance status
body: In patients with advanced cancer, physicians' predictions (based on prior clinical experience), clinical symptoms, and performance status are the 3 most important factors for predicting survival time. Performance status is the most important of these. The strongest clinical symptoms associated with short survival time are weight loss, xerostomia, dysphagia, dyspnea, anorexia, and cognitive impairment.

title: Tamoxifen is associated with an elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE)
body: Tamoxifen is associated with an elevated risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Patients who take tamoxifen for primary prevention of breast cancer should discontinue the medication prior to any surgery associated with a moderate or high risk of VTE (eg, hip arthroplasty). ■ I÷0 End © Resources Suspend

title: Doxorubicin and other anthracyclines cause cardiotoxicity related to the cumulative dose of chemotherapy
body: Doxorubicin and other anthracyclines cause cardiotoxicity related to the cumulative dose of chemotherapy. Other risk factors for developing cardiotoxicity include exposure at an early age, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, concurrent use of other cardiotoxic agents, chest irradiation, and bone marrow transplantation.

title: Sexual dysfunction is the most common long-term adverse effect of external beam radiation for prostate cancer
body: Sexual dysfunction is the most common long-term adverse effect of external beam radiation for prostate cancer. The risk depends on the radiation technique and radiation field. The risk increases further if androgen deprivation therapy is added to the radiation treatment.

title: Type 1 von Willebrand disease (VWD) is a quantitative disorder of von Willebrand factor (VWF) and can range from mild to severe disease
body: Type 1 von Willebrand disease (VWD) is a quantitative disorder of von Willebrand factor (VWF) and can range from mild to severe disease. VWF concentrates are used perioperatively in severe VWD to decrease bleeding risk in both major and minor surgeries. Levels should be checked during this period to ensure adequate factor replacement.

title: In patients with a transient, very high thrombotic-risk condition (eg, venous thromboembolism within 3 months), elective high-bleeding-risk
body: In patients with a transient, very high thrombotic-risk condition (eg, venous thromboembolism within 3 months), elective high-bleeding-risk surgeries/procedures should be postponed until the thrombotic risk becomes more acceptable.

title: Patients presenting with recurrent acute abdominal pain combined with dark urine and hyponatremia should be evaluated for acute
body: Patients presenting with recurrent acute abdominal pain combined with dark urine and hyponatremia should be evaluated for acute intermittent porphyria. The diagnostic test is an elevated urinary porphobilinogen (PBG) during an acute attack. Treatment involves glucose loading and intravenous hemin.

title: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) is presumed when the patient’s history (e.g., drug exposure), physical examination, complete blood
body: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) is presumed when the patient’s history (e.g., drug exposure), physical examination, complete blood count, and peripheral blood smear examination do not suggest other etiologies for isolated thrombocytopenia. Bone marrow aspiration is indicated in patients > age 60 to rule out myelodysplastic syndromes. Patients with mild to moderate asymptomatic thrombocytopenia (> 30,000 cells∕μL) should not be treated, since the majority of these patients will have a stable and benign course.

title: The risk of developing vitamin B12 deficiency is increased in patients treated with metformin
body: The risk of developing vitamin B12 deficiency is increased in patients treated with metformin. The risk increases with older patients, higher metformin doses, and longer durations of treatment. Metformin is thought to impair the terminal ileal absorption of vitamin B 2 by inhibiting calcium-dependent binding of the intrinsic fact0r-B^∣2 complex to its receptor.

title: Superficial vein thrombophlebitis has similar risk factors to deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and presents with tenderness, pain, induration
body: Superficial vein thrombophlebitis has similar risk factors to deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and presents with tenderness, pain, induration, and/or erythema along the superficial vein with possible palpable nodular cord. Ultrasound is indicated to rule out DVT in patients with superficial vein thrombosis > 5 cm, anatomic proximity of thrombus to the deep venous system (< 5 cm), and medical risk factors.

title: Multiple myeloma is usually diagnosed by serum electrophoresis showing an M-spike and urine electrophoresis with immunofixation showing
body: Multiple myeloma is usually diagnosed by serum electrophoresis showing an M-spike and urine electrophoresis with immunofixation showing light/heavy chains. Urine studies can be replaced by serum free light chain assay for screening purposes. Patients with negative serum and urine studies are labelled as having non-secretory myeloma.

title: Warm agglutinin autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) is a common complication of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and is characterized by a
body: Warm agglutinin autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) is a common complication of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and is characterized by a positive direct antiglobulin (Coombs’) test and spherocytes on peripheral smear. Treatment involves steroids followed by splenectomy in refractory patients. Patients with severe hemolysis and symptomatic anemia require packed RBC transfusion.

title: Patients with a high pretest probability of deep venous thrombosis (DVT) should undergo compressive ultrasonography for diagnosis
body: Patients with a high pretest probability of deep venous thrombosis (DVT) should undergo compressive ultrasonography for diagnosis. False negatives occur in 3% of high probability cases; patients who have negative initial testing, continue to be symptomatic, have no clear alternate diagnosis, and have an elevated d-dimer should be retested with whole leg compressive ultrasound within 24 hours.

title: Acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease is characterized by pulmonary infiltrates associated with fever, pain, hypoxemia, and pulmonary
body: Acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease is characterized by pulmonary infiltrates associated with fever, pain, hypoxemia, and pulmonary crackles. Management includes supplemental oxygen, intravenous hydration, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and pain medication. Mild cases may be managed without transfusion. Moderate cases require conventional red cell transfusion, and exchange transfusion is recommended in severe cases.

title: Leukostasis is an oncologic emergency associated with extremely high white blood cell counts
body: Leukostasis is an oncologic emergency associated with extremely high white blood cell counts. Induction chemotherapy is the preferred treatment. When chemotherapy must be postponed, Ieukapheresis (for symptomatic patients) and/or hydroxyurea can be used for temporary rapid Cytoreduction.

title: Aplastic crisis may cause acute worsening anemia in sickle cell disease patients and is usually due to a bone marrow infection causing
body: Aplastic crisis may cause acute worsening anemia in sickle cell disease patients and is usually due to a bone marrow infection causing decreased erythropoiesis. Parvovirus B-19 is the most common cause and treatment is supportive (eg, transfusions, rest, analgesics, hydration, and oxygenation).

title: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia often presents with constitutional symptoms, oozing from mucosal sites, and manifestations related to
body: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia often presents with constitutional symptoms, oozing from mucosal sites, and manifestations related to neoplastic infiltration of hematopoietic tissue (eg, hepatosplenomegaly, Iymphadenopathy, cytopenias) or high levels of IgM (eg, cryoglobulinemia, peripheral neuropathy, hyperviscosity syndrome). Diagnosis is made with serum protein electrophoresis and bone marrow biopsy. ■ ÷0 End ® Resources

title: Priapism is a serious complication associated with sickle cell disease and defined as an erection lasting >2- 4 hours
body: Priapism is a serious complication associated with sickle cell disease and defined as an erection lasting >2- 4 hours. Blood aspiration from the corpus cavernosum, followed by saline irrigation and use of adrenergic agonists (eg, epinephrine), is first-line therapy. If priapism still persists, surgical shunting may be required.

title: Patients who develop thrombocytopenia after initiation of heparin products should be evaluated for heparin- induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
body: Patients who develop thrombocytopenia after initiation of heparin products should be evaluated for heparin- induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) type 2 with a 4 Ts score. Patients with low (<3) scores are unlikely to have HIT type 2 and can continue heparin therapy without additional testing or change in treatment. ■ I>3 End @ Resources Suspend

title: Low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) is more effective than vitamin K antagonists (e.g., warfarin) in reducing the risk of recurrent venous
body: Low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) is more effective than vitamin K antagonists (e.g., warfarin) in reducing the risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism in cancer patients. However, LMWH is not associated with improved survival in these patients.

title: Malignant pleural effusions are exudative by Light criteria and usually lymphocyte-predominant
body: Malignant pleural effusions are exudative by Light criteria and usually lymphocyte-predominant. Pleural fluid cytology has low sensitivity for malignancy in the setting of high pH (≥7.3). When fluid analysis fails to confirm the etiology of pleural effusion, CT scan of the chest with pleural phase contrast enhancement provides guidance for diagnostic tissue biopsy.

title: Metastatic cancer patients with bone metastases are susceptible to skeletal-related events (SREs) (eg, fracture, skeletal instability/loss
body: Metastatic cancer patients with bone metastases are susceptible to skeletal-related events (SREs) (eg, fracture, skeletal instability/loss, spinal cord compression). Denosumab and the intravenous bisphosphonates, zoledronic acid and pamidronate, have been shown to prevent SREs and decrease morbidity. Denosumab does not require renal dose adjustments.

title: Incentive spirometry has been shown to reduce the likelihood of developing acute chest syndrome and should be encouraged in all patients
body: Incentive spirometry has been shown to reduce the likelihood of developing acute chest syndrome and should be encouraged in all patients presenting with sickle cell pain crisis. Similarly, hydroxyurea should be started in all patients with a history of acute chest syndrome or risk of developing it (eg, HbSS).

title: Von Willebrand disease is a common bleeding disorder that can present with mucocutaneous bleeding (eg, epistaxis, heavy menses) and normal
body: Von Willebrand disease is a common bleeding disorder that can present with mucocutaneous bleeding (eg, epistaxis, heavy menses) and normal platelet counts and coagulation studies. Diagnosis requires plasma von Willebrand factor antigen and activity assays. Treatment is with desmopressin (DDAVP), which causes release of von Willebrand factor and factor Vlll from endothelial cells.

title: Patients with solitary brain metastasis benefit from surgery or stereotactic radiation followed by whole-brain radiation.
Pancreatic cancer patients commonly present with biliary obstruction. Endoscopic stent placement is preferred to relieve biliary obstruction and prevent cholangitis.
Dabigatran is a direct thrombin inhibitor used for anticoagulation
body: Dabigatran is a direct thrombin inhibitor used for anticoagulation. Patients on this medication who require urgent or emergency procedures should undergo thrombin time testing. Those with normal thrombin times are not anticoagulated and can proceed with surgery. If thrombin time is elevated, administration of the dabigatran antidote idarucizumab should be considered.

title: Vitamin K deficiency causes a coagulopathy with a prolonged prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time (PT » PTT)
body: Vitamin K deficiency causes a coagulopathy with a prolonged prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time (PT » PTT). Vitamin K deficiency initially lowers factor Vll levels, and may later affect II, IX and X. Liver parenchymal disease lowers factor V and Vll levels. Factor Vlll levels are decreased in disseminated intravascular coagulation but significantly increased or normal in liver failure.

title: Most asymptomatic patients should not receive a red blood cell transfusion if their hemoglobin is >7-8 g/dL
body: Most asymptomatic patients should not receive a red blood cell transfusion if their hemoglobin is >7-8 g/dL. This includes postoperative surgical patients and those with stable cardiovascular disease. Patients with symptoms (eg, myocardial ischemia or orthostatic hypotension/tachycardia unresponsive to fluids) may benefit from blood transfusion to maintain a hemoglobin >10 g/dL.

title: Early ambulation following deep venous thrombosis is associated with fewer complications compared to prolonged bed rest
body: Early ambulation following deep venous thrombosis is associated with fewer complications compared to prolonged bed rest. It is reasonable to start mobilization once therapeutic levels of anticoagulation have been reached.

title: Patients at high risk for tumor lysis syndrome from chemotherapy should be treated with aggressive hydration (to maintain a urine output of
body: Patients at high risk for tumor lysis syndrome from chemotherapy should be treated with aggressive hydration (to maintain a urine output of >80-100 mL/hr), rasburicase, and careful clinical and biochemical monitoring.

title: Pregnancy can cause thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) due to either the formation of autoantibodies or the emergence of a
body: Pregnancy can cause thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) due to either the formation of autoantibodies or the emergence of a previously undiagnosed hereditary case. Patients can be minimally symptomatic or critically ill, but laboratory evaluation typically shows severe thrombocytopenia and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia. Unlike disseminated intravascular coagulation, TTP is usually associated with normal coagulation studies.

title: Polycythemia vera is a myeloproliferative disorder due to clonal red blood cell proliferation that is erythropoietin (EPO)-Independent
body: Polycythemia vera is a myeloproliferative disorder due to clonal red blood cell proliferation that is erythropoietin (EPO)-Independent. Most patients have low EPO levels and positive JAK2 mutation testing. Patients at low risk for thrombosis (eg, age <60, no prior thrombosis) are treated with serial phlebotomy, low-dose aspirin, and symptom control. Those at greater thrombus risk or with active thrombus also require myelosuppression.

title: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) should be suspected in patients treated (or recently treated) with heparin who develop unexplained
body: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) should be suspected in patients treated (or recently treated) with heparin who develop unexplained thrombocytopenia (or a > 50% decrease in platelet count from baseline) or newly diagnosed thrombosis (venous or arterial). Once HIT is suspected, all forms of heparin must be stopped immediately, laboratory testing for HIT should be obtained, and alternate anticoagulants (eg, direct thrombin inhibitors) should be started even if thrombosis has not occurred.

title: Patients who are immunodeficient or those receiving blood products from a family donor or HLA-matched platelets should receive irradiated
body: Patients who are immunodeficient or those receiving blood products from a family donor or HLA-matched platelets should receive irradiated blood products to prevent transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease. Patients with HIV do not appear to be at risk for this condition and can receive nonirradiated blood. ■ I÷0 End © Resources Suspend

title: Type 1 heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is a non-immune-mediated thrombocytopenia due to an immediate (within 48 hours) reaction to heparin
body: Type 1 heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is a non-immune-mediated thrombocytopenia due to an immediate (within 48 hours) reaction to heparin therapy. Platelet counts rarely drop to <100,000∕mm0 and usually recover spontaneously regardless of heparin continuation or discontinuation.

title: Delayed-onset, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is an immune-mediated condition that usually arises 5- 19 days after heparin cessation
body: Delayed-onset, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is an immune-mediated condition that usually arises 5- 19 days after heparin cessation. Most patients present in the outpatient setting with thrombocytopenia and arterial or venous thrombus. HIT antibody testing is required for confirmation, but empiric treatment with a nonheparin anticoagulation (eg, direct thrombin inhibitor) should be initiated with urgency to prevent life­ threatening complications.

title: Solid organ transplant patients are more susceptible to nosocomial infections within a month of surgery due to prolonged hospitalization
body: Solid organ transplant patients are more susceptible to nosocomial infections within a month of surgery due to prolonged hospitalization, mechanical ventilation, immunosuppression, and exposure to multiple catheters or devices. Common organisms causing nosocomial pneumonia in transplant patients include vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, Candida, and Pseudomonas.

title: Dengue fever is a common cause of fever in travelers returning from an endemic area (eg, Caribbean, parts of Asia, and South America)
body: Dengue fever is a common cause of fever in travelers returning from an endemic area (eg, Caribbean, parts of Asia, and South America). Patients typically develop fever, retro-orbital pain/headache, a characteristic macular rash, and bleeding complications. Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia are common laboratory abnormalities.

title: Patients with suspected bacterial meningitis who have a positive cerebrospinal fluid Gram stain should have empiric therapy narrowed to
body: Patients with suspected bacterial meningitis who have a positive cerebrospinal fluid Gram stain should have empiric therapy narrowed to target the likely organism. Patients with gram-positive bacilli are likely to have Listeria monocytogenes meningoencephalitis; first-line treatment consists of ampicillin or penicillin G with or without a synergistic aminoglycoside. ÷3 End © Resources Il Suspend

title: Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus cereus enterotoxins are common causes of vomiting-predominant, foodborne illness
body: Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus cereus enterotoxins are common causes of vomiting-predominant, foodborne illness. Symptoms tend to arise rapidly, usually within 1-6 hours of ingestion. Abdominal cramps and vomiting are the primary features, but fever or diarrhea can occasionally occur.

title: Patients with history of splenectomy are susceptible to severe infections from encapsulated bacteria (eg, N meningitidis)
body: Patients with history of splenectomy are susceptible to severe infections from encapsulated bacteria (eg, N meningitidis). Meningococcemia may present with fever, myalgias, purpura fulminans, meningitis, DIC, and shock (with or without adrenal insufficiency). Treatment includes third-generation cephalosporins (eg, ceftriaxone or cefotaxime) and vancomycin. Close respiratory contacts of affected individuals require prophylaxis with rifampin, ciprofloxacin, or ceftriaxone.

title: Patients with hospital-acquired meningitis should be empirically treated with an antipseudomonal cephalosporin and vancomycin
body: Patients with hospital-acquired meningitis should be empirically treated with an antipseudomonal cephalosporin and vancomycin. Cefepime, ceftazidime, and meropenem are all highly effective against gram-negative organisms (e.g., Pseudomonas) and have good CNS penetration.

title: Regardless of vaccination status, healthcare workers (with close proximity and prolonged duration or exposure to respiratory secretions)
body: Regardless of vaccination status, healthcare workers (with close proximity and prolonged duration or exposure to respiratory secretions) and close contacts of infected patients with meningococcal disease should receive antibiotic chemoprophylaxis, ideally within the first 24 hours of patient diagnosis. Recommended regimens include rifampin, ciprofloxacin, or ceftriaxone.

title: Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis usually presents in HIV patients with headache, fever, stiff neck, and possible altered mental status with
body: Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis usually presents in HIV patients with headache, fever, stiff neck, and possible altered mental status with neurological deficits. Treatment involves prompt antifungal therapy in 3 phases (induction, consolidation, and maintenance). Patients often require serial lumbar punctures to reduce the increased intracranial pressure frequently seen with the infection.

title: The manifestations of Lyme disease are typically categorized into 3 progressive stages
body: The manifestations of Lyme disease are typically categorized into 3 progressive stages. Early localized infection is marked by a viral-like syndrome and erythema migrans. Weeks or months later, patients can develop signs of early disseminated disease such as arthralgias, carditis (eg, atrioventricular block), and nervous system abnormalities (eg, facial nerve palsy, meningitis). Late Lyme disease is typically associated with intermittent or persistent arthritis in >1 large joints (particularly the knee).

title: Secondary bacterial pneumonia is typically characterized by a transient improvement of influenza symptoms followed by worsened fever and
body: Secondary bacterial pneumonia is typically characterized by a transient improvement of influenza symptoms followed by worsened fever and lower respiratory tract illness. Most cases are caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, but methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is also a frequent culprit, particularly in young, previously healthy patients. Empiric treatment should include coverage for community-acquired pneumonia (eg, ceftriaxone and azithromycin) and for MRSA (eg, vancomycin).

title: Mycobacterium avium complex infection occurs in HIV-infected patients with CD4 < 50 cells/mm
body: Mycobacterium avium complex infection occurs in HIV-infected patients with CD4 < 50 cells/mm . Disseminated disease presents with fever, night sweats, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. Hepatosplenomegaly and abdominal Iymphadenopathy are common. Diagnosis is made via blood cultures, and treatment includes clarithromycin and ethambutol.

title: Vibrio vulnificus is found in shellfish and can cause potentially fatal infections in patients with chronic liver disease and cirrhosis
body: Vibrio vulnificus is found in shellfish and can cause potentially fatal infections in patients with chronic liver disease and cirrhosis. Suspected patients should be treated promptly with antibiotics and ICU monitoring. High risk groups (i.e., hepatitis, hemochromatosis, cirrhosis) should avoid consumption or contact with raw shellfish.

title: Human granulocytic anaplasmosis (HGA), a tick-borne illness, should be suspected in patients from endemic areas who develop flulike
body: Human granulocytic anaplasmosis (HGA), a tick-borne illness, should be suspected in patients from endemic areas who develop flulike symptoms with leukopenia and/or thrombocytopenia. Coinfection with Lyme disease occurs in up to 15% of cases (both are transmitted by the Ixodes scapularis tick) and should be suspected when patients also have a rash with central clearing. Diagnosis can be made with buffy coat or peripheral blood smear examination (intraleukocytic morulae); empiric treatment with doxycycline should be initiated while awaiting testing results.

title: Lyme carditis can be asymptomatic or present with palpitations, lightheadedness, syncope, dyspnea, or chest pain
body: Lyme carditis can be asymptomatic or present with palpitations, lightheadedness, syncope, dyspnea, or chest pain. Atrioventricular conduction block is the most common cardiac presentation and can progress to complete heart block. Hospital admission with IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone preferred) is recommended for symptomatic patients and those with second- or third-degree AV block or first-degree AV block with PR interval > 300 msec.

title: Echocardiography should be performed in all patients with Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia regardless of the presence of clinical signs suggestive of endocarditis.
Hospitalized patients with neutropenic fever should generally receive monotherapy with an anti- pseudomonal beta-lactam (eg
body: Hospitalized patients with neutropenic fever should generally receive monotherapy with an anti- pseudomonal beta-lactam (eg, piperacillin-tazobactam) or a carbapenem. The routine addition of a second agent (eg, vancomycin) targeting gram-positive pathogens is not recommended.

title: Measles infections tend to begin with fever, malaise, and anorexia followed by the "3 Cs" of cough, conjunctivitis, and coryza
body: Measles infections tend to begin with fever, malaise, and anorexia followed by the "3 Cs" of cough, conjunctivitis, and coryza. Koplik spots (white lesions on an erythematous base) then form on mucous membranes, followed by the characteristic exanthem (maculopapular rash that spreads in a cephalocaudal and centrifugal manner). Measles is highly infectious and transmitted by droplet nuclei, so airborne isolation is required for ≥4 days after rash onset.

title: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is a tick-borne rickettsial illness that causes nonspecific symptoms followed by a maculopapular rash 3-5 days
body: Rocky Mountain spotted fever is a tick-borne rickettsial illness that causes nonspecific symptoms followed by a maculopapular rash 3-5 days later. The rash typically starts on the ankles and wrists and spreads centrally to the trunk and peripherally to the palms and soles. Empiric therapy with doxycycline should be started as soon as possible to decrease morbidity and mortality.

title: Neurocysticercosis is an important cause of seizure in individuals from endemic areas (eg, Central and South America, sub-Saharan Africa)
body: Neurocysticercosis is an important cause of seizure in individuals from endemic areas (eg, Central and South America, sub-Saharan Africa), including Hispanic immigrants. Neuroimaging (eg, CT or MRI) may reveal viable cysts (5-20 mm round, hypodense lesions without enhancement), enhancement/edema as cysts degenerate, and calcified granulomas in the cortex or brainstem.

title: Nocardia is commonly seen in immunocompromised patients and typically involves the lung, brain, and skin
body: Nocardia is commonly seen in immunocompromised patients and typically involves the lung, brain, and skin. Diagnosis is made clinically and confirmed with culture isolating acid-fast, filamentous Gram-positive rods. Treatment involves TMP-SMX, imipenem, amikacin, or third-generation cephalosporins.

title: Legionella pneumonia usually presents with fever, relative bradycardia, possible neurologic and Gl symptoms, and potential unilobar chest
body: Legionella pneumonia usually presents with fever, relative bradycardia, possible neurologic and Gl symptoms, and potential unilobar chest x-ray infiltrate progressing to consolidation. Suspected patients with Legionella pneumonia should have both a urinary antigen test and a Legionella culture from a respiratory sample to confirm diagnosis. Treatment consists of respiratory fluoroquinolones (e.g., Ievofloxacin) or “newer” macrolides (e.g., azithromycin) while awaiting results.

title: Cough, fever, arthritis, and erythema nodosum after recent travel to the southwestern United States is consistent with coccidioidomycosis
body: Cough, fever, arthritis, and erythema nodosum after recent travel to the southwestern United States is consistent with coccidioidomycosis. Patients receiving tumor necrosis factor-alpha inhibitors are at increased risk for opportunistic infections, including fungal pathogens.

title: In patients with AIDS, ring-enhancing central nervous system lesions with mass effect and edema are suggestive of primary central nervous
body: In patients with AIDS, ring-enhancing central nervous system lesions with mass effect and edema are suggestive of primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCL) or toxoplasma encephalitis. Imaging features suggestive of PCL are solitary lesions, lesions > 4 cm, and those involving the corpus callosum, periventricular, or periependymal areas. Toxoplasma encephalitis should be suspected in patients with multiple ring-enhancing lesions and a predilection for the basal ganglia.

title: Clostridium septicum usually presents with bacteremia followed by spontaneous gas gangrene in an extremity without a history of trauma
body: Clostridium septicum usually presents with bacteremia followed by spontaneous gas gangrene in an extremity without a history of trauma. Since the bacteria originates in the Gl tract and is associated with Gl pathology (e.g., colon cancer), all patients with C. septicum bacteremia should undergo a colonoscopy.

title: Injection drug users are at increased risk for infective endocarditis (IE) involving the right-sided heart valves
body: Injection drug users are at increased risk for infective endocarditis (IE) involving the right-sided heart valves. Staphylococcus aureus is the most common organism. Patients often present due to septic pulmonary emboli (eg, multiple bilateral cavitary lesions). Cardiac examination is usually normal (eg, no heart murmurs).

title: Patients with potential meningococcal meningitis require at least 24 hours of droplet precautions after the initiation of antibiotics in
body: Patients with potential meningococcal meningitis require at least 24 hours of droplet precautions after the initiation of antibiotics in order to prevent transmission to individuals in close contact. Droplet precautions include the use of a surgical mask when an individual is within 6 feet of the source patients. ___________________________

title: Consider acute schistosomiasis (Katayama fever) among patients presenting with fever and eosinophilia after return from an endemic area
body: Consider acute schistosomiasis (Katayama fever) among patients presenting with fever and eosinophilia after return from an endemic area, including sub-Saharan Africa. Corticosteroids and supportive care are indicated in the acute setting followed by antiparasitic treatment after acute symptoms resolve.

title: Patients with suspected acute bacterial meningitis require urgent empiric treatment with ceftriaxone and vancomycin
body: Patients with suspected acute bacterial meningitis require urgent empiric treatment with ceftriaxone and vancomycin. Ampicillin should be added for those age >50 to empirically cover for Listeria monocytogenes. All patients should also receive adjunctive dexamethasone to reduce risk of neurologic sequelae and death from potential pneumococcal meningitis.

title: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus is a serious, vision-threatening complication of latent varicella zoster virus infection. Treatment consists of intravenous acyclovir and urgent ophthalmologic evaluation.
Clostridium difficile infection usually presents with multiple episodes of watery diarrhea after recent antibiotic use
body: Clostridium difficile infection usually presents with multiple episodes of watery diarrhea after recent antibiotic use. Diagnosis is confirmed by stool studies, and treatment involves oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin. Patients refractory to treatment may need further investigation with sigmoidoscopy or colonoscopy. ■ >3 End ® Resources

title: Malaria should be considered in a traveler returning from an endemic area who has acute febrile illness, anemia, splenomegaly, and jaundice
body: Malaria should be considered in a traveler returning from an endemic area who has acute febrile illness, anemia, splenomegaly, and jaundice. Persons who have received inadequate prophylaxis are at risk. Identification of the parasite on peripheral blood smear can establish the diagnosis.

title: Patients with suspected infective endocarditis require blood cultures (3 sets) and echocardiography to estimate its likelihood using the modified Duke criteria.
Prophylactic antibiotics are warranted following a cat bite with deep injury
body: Prophylactic antibiotics are warranted following a cat bite with deep injury. Antibiotic coverage should include an agent that treats Pasturella multocida. Amoxicillin/clavulanate is preferred as first-line therapy, and doxycycline/metronidazole is used in patients with penicillin allergy. Many physicians give the first dose intravenously followed by oral medications for 3-5 days.

title: Transesophageal echocardiogram is highly sensitive for the diagnosis of infective endocarditis and its complications; it should be obtained
body: Transesophageal echocardiogram is highly sensitive for the diagnosis of infective endocarditis and its complications; it should be obtained early in patients with suspected complications or sudden clinical deterioration.

title: For patients with meningococcal infection, droplet precautions should be in effect for the first 24 hours of antimicrobial therapy and
body: For patients with meningococcal infection, droplet precautions should be in effect for the first 24 hours of antimicrobial therapy and involve wearing a facemask if within 6-10 feet of the patient. Rifampin, ciprofloxacin, and ceftriaxone are recommended antibiotic chemoprophylaxis drugs for persons at risk.

title: Yersinia pestis infection causes the highly lethal bubonic plague and presents with swollen and painful lymph nodules and sudden onset of
body: Yersinia pestis infection causes the highly lethal bubonic plague and presents with swollen and painful lymph nodules and sudden onset of high-grade fever. Suspected patients should be treated rapidly with tetracyclines or streptomycin. Post-exposure prophylaxis with doxycycline is recommended for contact with known cases.

title: Nearly 90% of patients with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) will have lactic acid dehydrogenase levels >50 U/L above baseline; a
body: Nearly 90% of patients with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP) will have lactic acid dehydrogenase levels >50 U/L above baseline; a level >450 U/L is predictive of PCP rather than another pulmonary process. The most commonly described radiographic appearance in PCP is diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Spontaneous pneumothorax develops in approximately 5% of patients.

title: Chikungunya virus disease should be considered in patients who develop fevers and severe polyarthralgias shortly after travel to an endemic area.
Fusariosis can occur in severely immunocompromised patients
body: Fusariosis can occur in severely immunocompromised patients. Inoculation commonly occurs when breaks in the skin are exposed to tap water or soil. Patients can present with refractory fever, skin lesions, and pulmonary disease. Diagnosis is suggested by skin biopsy (> 50% of patients) and/or positive blood cultures (-40% of patients) that usually grow a mold. Treatment is with amphotericin B +/- voriconazole with varying efficacy.

title: Septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein should be suspected in patients with a recent history of pharyngitis who develop neck
body: Septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein should be suspected in patients with a recent history of pharyngitis who develop neck pain, neck swelling, persistent fever despite antibiotic therapy, and cavitary lung lesions. Infection is usually due to the anaerobic organism Fusobacterium necrophorum. Treatment involves 4 weeks of antibiotics with anaerobic coverage.

title: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome (TSS) must be considered in patients with abrupt onset of fever, hypotension, and diffuse erythroderma
body: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome (TSS) must be considered in patients with abrupt onset of fever, hypotension, and diffuse erythroderma. Most cases occur in the setting of menstrual tampons, nasal packing, or surgical/postpartum wound infections. Treatment involves supportive care, removing the foreign material (or surgery), and broad-spectrum antistaphylococcal antibiotics (eg, clindamycin and vancomycin).

title: Patients with suspected acute bacterial meningitis require early treatment with empiric antibiotics and dexamethasone to limit neurologic
body: Patients with suspected acute bacterial meningitis require early treatment with empiric antibiotics and dexamethasone to limit neurologic sequelae and death. Those who need a head CT scan (eg, altered mental state, focal neurologic deficit, immunocompromised state, new-onset seizure, papilledema, history of central nervous system disease) prior to lumbar puncture should first receive blood cultures, antibiotics, and dexamethasone. Patients who do not require a head CT scan should receive blood cultures and lumbar puncture prior to treatment.

title: Patients with a history of Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) should have careful antibiotic stewardship
body: Patients with a history of Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) should have careful antibiotic stewardship. Fluoroquinolones, clindamycin, and broad-spectrum penicillins/cephalosporins are associated with high rates of CDAD; therefore, alternate antibiotics with a lower risk of CDAD should be used when possible.

title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) typically presents with fever, purulent secretions, and hypoxia in ventilated patients 48-72 hours
body: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) typically presents with fever, purulent secretions, and hypoxia in ventilated patients 48-72 hours after intubation. Common organisms include MRSA, MSSA, and gram­ negative organisms (e.g., Pseudomonas). Vancomycin and Iinezolid are appropriate first-line agents for treating MRSA pneumonia.

title: Candidemia is a common hospital-acquired infection and usually occurs in the setting of a central venous catheter, total parenteral
body: Candidemia is a common hospital-acquired infection and usually occurs in the setting of a central venous catheter, total parenteral nutrition, and/or an immunocompromised state (eg, neutropenia). The cornerstone of treatment is catheter removal and empiric antifungal therapy with an echinocandin (eg, caspofungin). Candida in blood cultures should never be considered a contaminant.

title: Although extended spectrum beta-lactamase-producing organisms may show in vitro susceptibility to penicillins with beta-lactamase
body: Although extended spectrum beta-lactamase-producing organisms may show in vitro susceptibility to penicillins with beta-lactamase inhibitors, cephalosporins, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, and aztreonam, treatment with these agents is likely to result in high failure rates. Carbapenems (eg, imipenem, meropenem, doripenem, and ertapenem) are the only recommended treatment option for these organisms.

title: Listeriosis usually occurs due to the ingestion of contaminated food
body: Listeriosis usually occurs due to the ingestion of contaminated food. Healthy individuals are at risk for self­ limited febrile gastroenteritis, but those with immunosuppression or advanced age can also develop invasive disease (eg, bacteremia, sepsis, pneumonia, meningitis). Ampicillin is the first-line treatment for invasive infection.

title: Urinary incontinence is not an indication for indwelling catheters. When not required, indwelling catheters should be removed promptly to avoid the risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infection.
Asymptomatic candiduria is common in patients with chronic urinary catheters and usually requires catheter removal/exchange
body: Asymptomatic candiduria is common in patients with chronic urinary catheters and usually requires catheter removal/exchange. Systemic antifungal therapy is not recommended for asymptomatic candiduria in a normal host. Persistent candiduria after catheter exchange/removal usually requires imaging to evaluate for perinephric abscess, fungus ball, or hydronephrosis.

title: Pyrimethamine (in conjunction with sulfadiazine) is the preferred treatment for toxoplasmosis in HIV patients
body: Pyrimethamine (in conjunction with sulfadiazine) is the preferred treatment for toxoplasmosis in HIV patients. Pyrimethamine causes bone marrow suppression and leucovorin should be used in conjunction to decrease the risk of hematologic complications.

title: Prevention of catheter-related infections includes maximal sterile barrier precautions with insertion, Chlorhexidine skin disinfection, and
body: Prevention of catheter-related infections includes maximal sterile barrier precautions with insertion, Chlorhexidine skin disinfection, and the use of antibiotic-impregnated catheters. Femoral insertion site, routine replacement of central catheters, and prophylactic antibiotics are not recommended.

title: Patients with hot tub/spa exposure are at risk for Mycobacterium avium complex infection and can present with hypersensitivity pneumonitis
body: Patients with hot tub/spa exposure are at risk for Mycobacterium avium complex infection and can present with hypersensitivity pneumonitis ("hot tub lung"). Manifestations are often acute and resemble an influenza infection. Most cases are self-limited and resolve with supportive care; a short course of prednisone can be used if symptoms do not resolve.

title: Rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis is an uncommon but devastating infection in diabetic patients with poor glucose control and frequent
body: Rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis is an uncommon but devastating infection in diabetic patients with poor glucose control and frequent episodes of ketoacidosis. Diagnosis is made by histology and culture revealing irregular branching hyphae without septations. Surgical intervention combined with IV amphotericin B is needed to achieve cure.

title: Tinea corporis is a dermatophyte infection that begins as a pruritic and scaly patch or plaque with erythema in a circular or oval pattern
body: Tinea corporis is a dermatophyte infection that begins as a pruritic and scaly patch or plaque with erythema in a circular or oval pattern. The rash has irregular margins that develop central clearing and expand into an annular (ring-like) shape. Mild-to-moderate disease usually responds to 2-4 weeks of topical antifungals. Oral agents are reserved for severe or widespread disease, immunocompromised patients, and failure with topical therapy.

title: Early findings of necrotizing fasciitis include erythema spreading across muscle fascia, swelling, and exquisite tenderness out of
body: Early findings of necrotizing fasciitis include erythema spreading across muscle fascia, swelling, and exquisite tenderness out of proportion to its appearance. Infection spreads rapidly and the patient appears ill. Tender areas become anesthetic, and examination shows skin discoloration, crepitus, and hemorrhagic blisters. Early aggressive surgical debridement of necrotic tissue is of utmost importance to prevent local necrosis and systemic toxicity.

title: Catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) usually requires systemic antibiotics and catheter removal in patients with suppurative
body: Catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) usually requires systemic antibiotics and catheter removal in patients with suppurative thrombophlebitis, endocarditis, sepsis, or persistent bacteremia. Catheter removal is usually indicated In CRBSI due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, or fungi.

title: Typhoid fever usually presents in patients with recent travel to an endemic region with fever, bacteremia, and relative bradycardia
body: Typhoid fever usually presents in patients with recent travel to an endemic region with fever, bacteremia, and relative bradycardia. Patients later develop abdominal pain and a macular rash. Bone marrow culture is the most sensitive method for isolating the causative organism.

title: Adult otitis media is a clinical diagnosis based on the history of ear pain and conductive hearing loss as well as Otoscopic findings of
body: Adult otitis media is a clinical diagnosis based on the history of ear pain and conductive hearing loss as well as Otoscopic findings of erythema, opacification, bulging, or air-fluid level of the tympanic membrane. Although amoxicillin is first-line antibiotic therapy, amoxicillin-clavulanate is a better choice if otitis media is unresolved in 48-72 hours.

title: Cervicofacial actinomycosis most commonly presents in the mandibular region as a slowly growing, non- tender mass with characteristic
body: Cervicofacial actinomycosis most commonly presents in the mandibular region as a slowly growing, non- tender mass with characteristic sulfur granules. The infection can extend through tissue planes and form abscesses, fistulas, and draining sinus tracts. Diagnosis is confirmed by culture, and penicillin for 6-12 months is the preferred therapy.

title: The Centor criteria (tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical Iymphadenopathy, fever by history, and absence of cough) are widely used
body: The Centor criteria (tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical Iymphadenopathy, fever by history, and absence of cough) are widely used to determine the likelihood of group A streptococcal pharyngitis. Patients with >2 criteria should have a rapid streptococcal antigen test and receive therapy with oral penicillin or amoxicillin if test results are positive.

title: Herpes simplex virus transmission can occur with asymptomatic viral shedding and during prodromal phases and active lesions
body: Herpes simplex virus transmission can occur with asymptomatic viral shedding and during prodromal phases and active lesions. The most effective strategy for reducing transmission is daily suppressive therapy.

title: Norovirus is the most common cause of epidemic gastroenteritis in adults and children. Vomiting is more prominent. Outbreaks commonly occur in restaurant, travel, and health care settings.
Ehrlichial infection is commonly caused by Ehrlichia Chaffeensis (human monocytic ehrlichiosis [HME]) and Anaplasma phagocytophilum (human
body: Ehrlichial infection is commonly caused by Ehrlichia Chaffeensis (human monocytic ehrlichiosis [HME]) and Anaplasma phagocytophilum (human granulocytic anaplasmosis [HGA]). Ehrlichiosis presents with severe and prolonged fever, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia. Rash without central clearing is infrequent in HME and very rare in HGA. Doxycycline is the preferred treatment.

title: A patient exposed within 90 days of diagnosis of primary, secondary, or early latent syphilis in a sex partner should receive treatment
body: A patient exposed within 90 days of diagnosis of primary, secondary, or early latent syphilis in a sex partner should receive treatment (even if the patient is seronegative for syphilis). A patient exposed >90 days after diagnosis of primary, secondary, or early latent syphilis in a sex partner should undergo serologic testing and also receive treatment if results are not immediately available or follow-up is uncertain.

title: Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) is commonly found in the environment and can present similarly to M tuberculosis
body: Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) is commonly found in the environment and can present similarly to M tuberculosis. Patients with underlying lung disease (eg, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) are particularly predisposed to developing MAC and require at least 2 positive sputum cultures to confirm the diagnosis. Treatment with macrolides, ethambutol, and rifamycins is usually started after diagnostic confirmation.

title: The diagnosis of babesiosis can be established based on identification of organisms on a thin blood smear (intraerythrocytic ring forms
body: The diagnosis of babesiosis can be established based on identification of organisms on a thin blood smear (intraerythrocytic ring forms with Maltese cross tetrads). Patients with a history of splenectomy are at risk for severe illness.

title: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) disease commonly occurs in the first few months after solid organ transplantation
body: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) disease commonly occurs in the first few months after solid organ transplantation. Infection is defined as CMV viral isolation, and disease is defined as clinical symptoms (eg, mononucleosis­ like syndrome) with organ involvement (eg, hepatitis, colitis, and pneumonitis). Treatment involves immunosuppression reduction and antiviral therapy (eg, ganciclovir) for more severe disease.

title: Leptospirosis should be considered in patients with epidemiologic exposure to Leptospira (e.g., rodent urine) who present with an acute
body: Leptospirosis should be considered in patients with epidemiologic exposure to Leptospira (e.g., rodent urine) who present with an acute febrile illness. Conjunctival suffusion is a common and specific finding. Appropriate treatment is with doxycycline or penicillin.

title: Antiviral treatment (eg, Oseltamivir) is recommended for patients with <48 hours of influenza-like symptoms
body: Antiviral treatment (eg, Oseltamivir) is recommended for patients with <48 hours of influenza-like symptoms. Those who require hospitalization, have severe or progressive illness, or are at high risk of complications should also receive antiviral therapy regardless of symptom duration. Negative rapid influenza antigen testing or a history of influenza vaccination does not rule out influenza infection.

title: Penicillin is the drug of choice to treat neurosyphilis, which can present with a variety of syndromes
body: Penicillin is the drug of choice to treat neurosyphilis, which can present with a variety of syndromes. Patients with a history of penicillin allergy should undergo desensitization in a monitored inpatient setting.

title: Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction should be considered in patients with an acute febrile illness following treatment for syphilis
body: Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction should be considered in patients with an acute febrile illness following treatment for syphilis. Treatment is supportive and may include nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or acetaminophen.

title: Chronic schistosomiasis most commonly occurs in patients who live in endemic areas or have frequent exposure to contaminated fresh water
body: Chronic schistosomiasis most commonly occurs in patients who live in endemic areas or have frequent exposure to contaminated fresh water. Symptoms of genitourinary schistosomiasis include dysuria, urinary frequency, bladder outlet obstruction, and terminal hematuria.

title: In HIV-negative patients treated for syphilis, repeat nontreponemal testing should be performed at 6 and 12 months to document response
body: In HIV-negative patients treated for syphilis, repeat nontreponemal testing should be performed at 6 and 12 months to document response. A serofast response should be considered in patients who have a 4-fold decrease in titers but a persistently positive, low-level titer despite treatment.

title: Strongyloidiasis should be suspected in patients presenting with peripheral eosinophilia, Gl and pulmonary complaints, and exposure to an
body: Strongyloidiasis should be suspected in patients presenting with peripheral eosinophilia, Gl and pulmonary complaints, and exposure to an endemic area. Invasive Strongyloides infection can lead to multiorgan dysfunction and septic shock. Diagnosis includes at least 2 stool samples (often negative), ELISA test for IgG antibody, and/or duodenal aspirate/biopsy. Treatment involves ivermectin or albendazole.

title: Asymptomatic patients with tick bites from endemic Lyme disease areas do not require serologic testing
body: Asymptomatic patients with tick bites from endemic Lyme disease areas do not require serologic testing. Prophylaxis is recommended in patients who live in endemic areas and have deer tick attachments 36 hours. Prophylaxis should be initiated within 72 hours of tick removal. Patients with erythema migrans do not need serologic testing, but they should be treated with doxycycline, cefuroxime, or amoxicillin.

title: The chancre of primary syphilis typically develops at the inoculation site (eg, external genitalia, posterior pharynx, anus, vagina).
Postexposure prophylaxis for hepatitis A is indicated as soon as possible in all unvaccinated household contacts including adults < age 40
body: Postexposure prophylaxis for hepatitis A is indicated as soon as possible in all unvaccinated household contacts including adults < age 40 and children > age 12 months. The hepatitis A virus vaccine is preferred over immune globulin in these patients; however, immune globulin is recommended in children < 12 months and immunocompromised individuals.

title: Patients with pyelonephritis who have continued fever, Iumboabdominal pain, and systemic symptoms require evaluation for obstructive
body: Patients with pyelonephritis who have continued fever, Iumboabdominal pain, and systemic symptoms require evaluation for obstructive uropathy or development of a suppurative urinary tract process (eg, renal or perinephric abscess).

title: Post-Lyme disease syndrome usually presents with myalgias, arthralgias, headaches, and cognitive complaints weeks to months after initial
body: Post-Lyme disease syndrome usually presents with myalgias, arthralgias, headaches, and cognitive complaints weeks to months after initial successful treatment. Antibiotics are not indicated for these symptoms, and spontaneous resolution is seen within 6 months of initial treatment.

title: Inflammatory diarrhea usually originates in the large bowel and presents with small-volume, frequent diarrhea; possible febrile prodrome
body: Inflammatory diarrhea usually originates in the large bowel and presents with small-volume, frequent diarrhea; possible febrile prodrome; and possible blood or mucus in the stool. Noninflammatory diarrhea originates in the small bowel and usually presents with large-volume, watery diarrhea. Organisms with preformed toxins typically cause sudden-onset nausea and vomiting 1-6 hours after ingestion without significant diarrhea.

title: Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex (MAC) is commonly found in the environment and can contaminate or colonize sputum
body: Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex (MAC) is commonly found in the environment and can contaminate or colonize sputum. The diagnosis of pulmonary MAC infection requires the presence of clinical criteria in addition to microbiological confirmation, with at least 2 positive sputum cultures. Once diagnosis is confirmed, patients are treated with combination therapy of clarithromycin, ethambutol, and rifampin.

title: Genital ulcers are most commonly due to herpes simplex virus (HSV) or syphilis
body: Genital ulcers are most commonly due to herpes simplex virus (HSV) or syphilis. Syphilis usually causes a single ulcer. Painful genital ulcers are more likely due to HSV or chancroid. Medical history and physical examination are not completely accurate, and all patients should be tested for both HSV and syphilis. Further testing for other pathogens is based on these initial results and the response to therapy.

title: Cutaneous larva migrans is the most common skin lesion in travelers to tropical endemic regions
body: Cutaneous larva migrans is the most common skin lesion in travelers to tropical endemic regions. It is due to hookworm larval (usually Ancylostoma braziliense) penetration of the skin with migration and a subsequent serpiginous reddish-brown lesion. Treatment involves ivermectin (preferred) or albendazole for symptom relief and to reduce the risk of bacterial superinfection.

title: A tuberculin skin test reaction of ≥5 mm is considered positive in a patient with recent exposure to an individual with active pulmonary
body: A tuberculin skin test reaction of ≥5 mm is considered positive in a patient with recent exposure to an individual with active pulmonary tuberculosis. Daily isoniazid for 9 months is a common treatment for latent tuberculosis infection; pyridoxine is generally added to prevent isoniazid-induced peripheral neuropathy in patients who are pregnant, those who have other conditions associated with neuropathy (eg, diabetes, uremia, alcoholism, HIV), and individuals with seizure disorder.

title: For patients with pneumonia who are at risk for Pseudomonas or other resistant pathogens, empiric antibiotic therapy should include an
body: For patients with pneumonia who are at risk for Pseudomonas or other resistant pathogens, empiric antibiotic therapy should include an antipseudomonal penicillin/cephalosporin or a carbapenem. In patients with risk factors for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, either vancomycin or Iinezolid should be added. Daptomycin should not be used for pneumonia treatment due to its lack of activity in the lung.

title: Prophylaxis for Pneumocystis pneumonia is recommended for patients with AIDS who have CD4 counts <200∕mm0
body: Prophylaxis for Pneumocystis pneumonia is recommended for patients with AIDS who have CD4 counts <200∕mm0. Prophylaxis can be safely discontinued in patients on antiretroviral therapy who have CD4 counts >200∕mπv for >3 months.

title: AIDS-related lymphomas are common in patients with advanced HIV, a low CD4 count (<100∕μL), high HIV viral load, and a prior diagnosis of
body: AIDS-related lymphomas are common in patients with advanced HIV, a low CD4 count (<100∕μL), high HIV viral load, and a prior diagnosis of AIDS. Patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) tend to present with B symptoms, extranodal disease, and involvement of unusual locations. Diffuse large-cell NHL and Burkitt lymphoma are the most common AIDS-related lymphomas.

title: Prostheticjoint infection should be considered in patients with increasing pain after joint replacement
body: Prostheticjoint infection should be considered in patients with increasing pain after joint replacement. Arthrocentesis establishes the diagnosis. Treatment involves surgical debridement (or removal in delayed or late-onset cases) followed by a prolonged course of intravenous antibiotics.

title: PPD/TST assesses for latent TB and a positive reaction is based on induration (rather than erythema) and patient risk factors
body: PPD/TST assesses for latent TB and a positive reaction is based on induration (rather than erythema) and patient risk factors. A positive test requires chest x-ray to rule out active infection. Patients with a negative chest x-ray should be treated with an appropriate regimen in addition to laboratory monitoring.

title: Chagas disease is the leading cause of dilated cardiomyopathy in Central and South America
body: Chagas disease is the leading cause of dilated cardiomyopathy in Central and South America. It is caused by Trypanosoma cruzi infection and is characterized by myocarditis progressing to dilated cardiomyopathy, nonspecific electrocardiogram abnormalities including right bundle branch block and left anterior fascicular block, and development of left ventricular apical aneurysms.

title: In patients with advanced HIV, trimethoprim-sulfaraethoxazole is the preferred first-line treatment for prevention of pneumocystis (CD4
body: In patients with advanced HIV, trimethoprim-sulfaraethoxazole is the preferred first-line treatment for prevention of pneumocystis (CD4 count <200∕mrrr) and toxoplasma (CD4 count <100∕mm0 and positive IgG). Azithromycin is used for Mycobacterium avium complex prophylaxis when CD4 count is <50∕mm . Routine fungal prophylaxis is not generally required, but patients who live in Histoplasma-endem'∖c regions often receive preventive treatment when CD4 counts are <150∕mnv.

title: HIV may present in its acute phase as a flu-like illness and as a cause of persistent sore throat
body: HIV may present in its acute phase as a flu-like illness and as a cause of persistent sore throat. When a rash is present, HIV enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay testing is sensitive with a lower rate of false negatives.

title: Patients with HIV who have low CD4 counts (usually <100∕mm0) and high pretreatment HIV RNA levels are at greatest risk for immune
