body: Patients with HIV who have low CD4 counts (usually <100∕mm0) and high pretreatment HIV RNA levels are at greatest risk for immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome, which is characterized by paradoxical worsening of a preexisting chronic infection or unmasking of an unrecognized infection within weeks or a few months of antiretroviral initiation. Treatment is generally focused on the underlying infection; antiretroviral therapy (ART) can usually be continued without interruption. However, patients with severe or life-threatening complications may require the temporary cessation of ART and/or the addition of corticosteroids.

title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) with a once-daily 2-drug antiretroviral regimen (tenofovir plus emtricitabine) can reduce the risk of
body: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) with a once-daily 2-drug antiretroviral regimen (tenofovir plus emtricitabine) can reduce the risk of acquiring HIV by >90%. PrEP is generally offered to those at substantial risk of new HIV infection due to sexual behaviors (eg, HIV-positive partner, inconsistent/no condom use) or injection drug use. To qualify, patients must have negative fourth-generation HIV testing, no manifestations of acute HIV, normal renal function, and documented hepatitis B infection/vaccination status. ■ ÷0 End ® Resources

title: Acute rheumatic fever is characterized by fever, migratory arthritis, subcutaneous nodules, carditis/valvular heart disease, and elevated
body: Acute rheumatic fever is characterized by fever, migratory arthritis, subcutaneous nodules, carditis/valvular heart disease, and elevated inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein). It is diagnosed clinically based on the Jones criteria in conjunction with confirmation of group A Streptococcal infection.

title: Antiviral therapy is recommended for patients at high risk for influenza complications, particularly within the first 48 hours after
body: Antiviral therapy is recommended for patients at high risk for influenza complications, particularly within the first 48 hours after symptom onset. In the absence of suspected resistance, Oseltamivir is the treatment of choice for patients with suspected influenza infection with underlying pulmonary disease.

title: Identification of cases of influenza within a long-term care facility should prompt early institution of prophylactic antiviral therapy to
body: Identification of cases of influenza within a long-term care facility should prompt early institution of prophylactic antiviral therapy to all residents (even those previously vaccinated) during the outbreak.

title: Babesiosis usually presents as a flu-like illness with hemolytic anemia in susceptible patients (eg, asplenic, age >50, immunocompromised)
body: Babesiosis usually presents as a flu-like illness with hemolytic anemia in susceptible patients (eg, asplenic, age >50, immunocompromised) who travel to tickborne endemic areas. Transfusion-associated babesiosis is also becoming increasingly common. Treatment for mild babesiosis includes azithromycin plus atovaquone (preferred) or oral clindamycin plus quinine. Severe disease requires hospitalization with intravenous clindamycin plus quinine.

title: Histoplasmosis can present as an asymptomatic pulmonary nodule in patients living in endogenous areas (the Ohio and Mississippi River
body: Histoplasmosis can present as an asymptomatic pulmonary nodule in patients living in endogenous areas (the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys). These patients do not require antifungal therapy if they are not immunocompromised.

title: Serology in acute hepatitis B virus infection typically demonstrates hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis B e antigen, IgM
body: Serology in acute hepatitis B virus infection typically demonstrates hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis B e antigen, IgM hepatitis B core antibody, and elevated viral DNA. Most adult patients will improve clinically and clear the infection with only supportive care and do not require antiviral therapy. A small minority will develop chronic infection evidenced by persistence of HBsAg for >6 months.

title: The foundation of treatment for skin abscess is incision and drainage
body: The foundation of treatment for skin abscess is incision and drainage. Empiric antibiotic therapy is generally added for those with an abscess ≥2 cm, extensive surrounding cellulitis, systemic signs of infection, neutropenia, multiple abscesses, extremes of age, or lack of response to incision and drainage.

title: All patients with candidemia should undergo a dilated retina ophthalmologic examination to evaluate for endogenous endophthalmitis.
Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis occurs in severely immunocompromised patients
body: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis occurs in severely immunocompromised patients. Diagnosis is made by chest computed tomography scan (nodules with or without cavitations surrounded by ground-glass infiltrates), culture, histopathology, or enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for galactomannan antigen. Voriconazole is the preferred treatment.

title: Asymptomatic patients with late syphilis or syphilis of unknown duration (>1 year) who are HIV-negative should be treated with benzathine penicillin weekly for 3 weeks.
Considertuberculosis (TB) co-infection in patients with HIV infection and appropriate epidemiological risk factors regardless of CD4 cell
body: Considertuberculosis (TB) co-infection in patients with HIV infection and appropriate epidemiological risk factors regardless of CD4 cell count. All patients with HIV infection should undergo testing for latent TB infection.

title: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) can present with anal pruritus and spreads easily through autoinfection or contaminated linens
body: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) can present with anal pruritus and spreads easily through autoinfection or contaminated linens. Diagnosis is confirmed by microscopic analysis of perianally-placed clear cellophane tape. Albendazole is the preferred treatment along with preventative measures.

title: Acute HIV infection should be considered in patients who have an acute viral illness and risk factors for HIV infection
body: Acute HIV infection should be considered in patients who have an acute viral illness and risk factors for HIV infection. Diagnosis is made by HIV-RNA polymerase chain reaction testing as HIV antibody testing may be negative. Treatment with combination antiretroviral therapy is recommended.

title: Tabes dorsalis most commonly presents with sensory ataxia and lancinating pains, and cardiovascular syphilis most commonly presents with
body: Tabes dorsalis most commonly presents with sensory ataxia and lancinating pains, and cardiovascular syphilis most commonly presents with asymptomatic aortic insufficiency or resultant left heart failure. In both, treponemal assays remain almost 100% sensitive.

title: For close contacts of a patient with tuberculosis, a tuberculin skin test (TST) reaction of ≥5 mm induration is considered positive and
body: For close contacts of a patient with tuberculosis, a tuberculin skin test (TST) reaction of ≥5 mm induration is considered positive and warrants further evaluation (chest x-ray, symptom review). However, the TST can take up to 8-12 weeks to become positive. Therefore, individuals in close contact with an infected person who have a negative initial TST should have the test repeated 8-12 weeks after exposure. ___________________________

title: Fluoroquinolones, azithromycin, and rifaximin are appropriate treatment choices for travelers’ diarrhea
body: Fluoroquinolones, azithromycin, and rifaximin are appropriate treatment choices for travelers’ diarrhea. Patients can be given a prescription prior to travel to the endemic region and told to self-medicate at onset of moderate to severe diarrhea. Antimotility agents may be used in conjunction with antibiotics, but not in severe diarrhea.

title: Bronchiectasis results when damage occurs to the bronchial walls, setting up a cycle Offuture infections and further airway damage
body: Bronchiectasis results when damage occurs to the bronchial walls, setting up a cycle Offuture infections and further airway damage. The most common symptoms are daily productive cough, mucopurulent sputum, dyspnea, fatigue, and hemoptysis. Diagnosis is confirmed with CT scan.

title: Secondary syphilis can produce a wide variety of manifestations including diffuse maculopapular rash (most characteristic), systemic
body: Secondary syphilis can produce a wide variety of manifestations including diffuse maculopapular rash (most characteristic), systemic symptoms (eg, fever, malaise, headache, anorexia, diffuse Iymphadenopathy), and diffuse organ involvement (eg, mild hepatitis, uveitis). Diagnosis is confirmed with serologic testing using nontreponemal (eg, rapid plasma reagin, VDRL) and treponemal (eg, FTA-ABS) assays.

title: The initial lesion of Iymphocutaneous sporotrichosis is a reddish nodule that later ulcerates and appears at the site of a thorn prick or
body: The initial lesion of Iymphocutaneous sporotrichosis is a reddish nodule that later ulcerates and appears at the site of a thorn prick or other skin injury. From the site of inoculation, the fungus spreads along the lymphatics forming additional subcutaneous nodules and ulcers. Definitive diagnosis is made by culture, and itraconazole is the drug of choice for treatment.

title: Osteomyelitis should be suspected in patients presenting with an ulcer > 2 cm , duration > 2 weeks, visualized bone, and elevated ESR
body: Osteomyelitis should be suspected in patients presenting with an ulcer > 2 cm , duration > 2 weeks, visualized bone, and elevated ESR. Plain films may not show periosteal elevation and cortical erosion for 10-14 days. MRI is the most accurate imaging modality for diagnosis of osteomyelitis, especially in diabetics. However, bone biopsy is recommended in most situations to guide antimicrobial therapy.

title: Recurrent cellulitis can occur in up to 30% of patients after an initial episode and is usually due to lymphatic stasis or skin barrier
body: Recurrent cellulitis can occur in up to 30% of patients after an initial episode and is usually due to lymphatic stasis or skin barrier breakdown. Tinea pedis can cause skin breakdown between the toes and is a potential site for bacterial entry in this small area often overlooked by clinicians. Treatment of underlying tinea pedis can decrease the incidence of recurrent episodes of ipsilateral cellulitis.

title: The risk of Borrelia burgdorferi transmission increases in the first 48-72 hours after tick attachment and usually does not require
body: The risk of Borrelia burgdorferi transmission increases in the first 48-72 hours after tick attachment and usually does not require treatment in asymptomatic patients. Antibiotic prophylaxis with doxycycline 200 mg in a single dose is recommended for patients meeting all 5 criteria (eg, > 36 hours of engorged tick attachment in an endemic area).

title: Patients with symptomatic recurrent herpes Iabialis should be treated with oral antiviral therapy (acyclovir, famciclovir, or valacyclovir)
body: Patients with symptomatic recurrent herpes Iabialis should be treated with oral antiviral therapy (acyclovir, famciclovir, or valacyclovir) at symptom onset (eg, pain, burning, tingling, or pruritus). Chronic suppressive therapy (daily acyclovir or valacyclovir) is recommended for patients with > 4 episodes a year, painful or disfiguring lesions without a prodrome, or herpes simplex virus recurrences with complications (eg, aseptic meningitis).

title: Asymmetric migratory joint pain and pustular lesions are characteristic Ofdisseminated gonococcal infection
body: Asymmetric migratory joint pain and pustular lesions are characteristic Ofdisseminated gonococcal infection. Diagnosis involves blood cultures, synovial fluid analysis (if purulent arthritis is present), and mucosal (eg, pharyngeal, rectal, urethral, or cervical) cultures. Treatment is ceftriaxone for 7-14 days and concomitant treatment of chlamydia with azithromycin or doxycycline.

title: Chemoprophylaxis regimens for malaria depend on Plasmodium species (eg, P falciparum versus P vivax or P ovale) and resistance (mostly chloroquine) patterns.
Herpes zoster causes a dermatomal vesicular skin rash and acute pain
body: Herpes zoster causes a dermatomal vesicular skin rash and acute pain. Antiviral medications are indicated when patients present within 72 hours of rash onset (or new lesions are still forming). Pain control for acute neuritis generally necessitates nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, acetaminophen, or weak opioids (eg, codeine, tramadol). Patients who have continued pain >4 months after rash onset (postherpetic neuralgia) may benefit from tricyclic antidepressants, gabapentin, or pregabalin.

title: Patients with recurrent dengue fever are at high risk for developing dengue hemorrhagic fever due to a heightened secondary immune response
body: Patients with recurrent dengue fever are at high risk for developing dengue hemorrhagic fever due to a heightened secondary immune response. Mosquito control by use of repellant (eg, DEET) and limited exposure of skin are the only effective methods to prevent contraction of the dengue virus.

title: The most common complications of tattoos are local skin infections from staphylococcal species and hypersensitivity reactions from metals
body: The most common complications of tattoos are local skin infections from staphylococcal species and hypersensitivity reactions from metals in the ink. Disseminated infections and nontuberculous mycobacterial infections are less common.

title: Disseminated blastomycoses commonly involves bone, skin, and the genitourinary tract
body: Disseminated blastomycoses commonly involves bone, skin, and the genitourinary tract. Disseminated histoplasmosis is associated with involvement of the reticuloendothelial system (lymphadenopathy, pancytopenia, and hepatosplenomegaly). Disseminated nocardiosis often causes brain abscesses. *Blasto blasts bones, balls (epididymo-orchitis), and skin.

title: Testosterone replacement therapy should be considered only in men with clinically significant androgen deficiency (eg, low libido, erectile
body: Testosterone replacement therapy should be considered only in men with clinically significant androgen deficiency (eg, low libido, erectile dysfunction, loss of body hair, gynecomastia, decreased bone density, testicular atrophy) and an unequivocally low morning serum testosterone level confirmed on repeat testing. Careful pretreatment evaluation is recommended to identify patients with a favorable risk:benefit ratio.

title: Phosphodiesterase inhibitors (eg, sildenafil) are contraindicated for treating erectile dysfunction in patients taking nitrates for angina
body: Phosphodiesterase inhibitors (eg, sildenafil) are contraindicated for treating erectile dysfunction in patients taking nitrates for angina due to the risks of hypotension and syncope. Treatment options for these patients include intraurethral alprostadil and vacuum assist devices.

title: Epididymitis usually presents with acute scrotal pain, exquisite testicular tenderness, and an intact cremasteric reflex
body: Epididymitis usually presents with acute scrotal pain, exquisite testicular tenderness, and an intact cremasteric reflex. Diagnosis is usually made clinically, but Doppler ultrasound can be used in equivocal cases to document increased flow to the affected epididymis. Treatment usually consists of testicular elevation, NSAIDs, and antibiotics with close follow-up.

title: Testicular cancers are usually hypoechoic on ultrasound
body: Testicular cancers are usually hypoechoic on ultrasound. Pure seminomas do not cause alpha-fetoprotein elevation. Testicular cancer spreads into the retroperitoneum and imaging of the abdomen is an important part of staging. Testicular biopsy is contraindicated. Radical orchiectomy is required for confirming the diagnosis, histologic classification, and local tumor control, even in patients with metastasis.

title: Varicoceles are due to tortuous dilation of the pampiniform plexus surrounding the spermatic cord
body: Varicoceles are due to tortuous dilation of the pampiniform plexus surrounding the spermatic cord. Asymptomatic patients do not require treatment; those with scrotal discomfort usually improve with analgesics (eg, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) and/or scrotal support.

title: Bladder storage symptoms such as frequency and nocturia are common side effects of diuretic therapy, which should be discontinued prior to further testing or treatment of benign prostatic hyperplasia.
Chronic prostatitis is characterized by recurrent or persistent lower urinary tract symptoms, prostatic tenderness, and repeated
body: Chronic prostatitis is characterized by recurrent or persistent lower urinary tract symptoms, prostatic tenderness, and repeated identification of the same organism on urine culture. A prolonged (4-6 weeks) course Ofantibiotics is recommended, and fluoroquinolones (eg, ciprofloxacin) are preferred for most patients.

title: Patients with epididymitis refractory to therapy require investigation (eg, scrotal ultrasound) for emergent etiologies (eg, torsion) or complications (eg, abscess, infarction).
Patients with cerebellar hemorrhage typically present acutely with severe headache, nausea/vomiting, vertigo, unsteadiness, and mental
body: Patients with cerebellar hemorrhage typically present acutely with severe headache, nausea/vomiting, vertigo, unsteadiness, and mental status changes. Space occupying lesions (e.g., hemorrhage) in the small posterior fossa can quickly obliterate the fourth ventricle to cause obstructive hydrocephalus, increased intracranial pressure, and Cushing's reflex (hypertension, bradycardia, and Cheyne-Stokes breathing).

title: Valproic acid can lead to elevated serum ammonia levels resulting in encephalopathy
body: Valproic acid can lead to elevated serum ammonia levels resulting in encephalopathy. Patients presenting with encephalopathy on valproic acid should have their serum ammonia and valproate levels checked. Treatment includes discontinuing the drug and starting lactulose. L-carnitine can also be considered.

title: Acute exacerbations of prior neurologic deficits may occur in conjunction with acute infection or metabolic derangement and can sometimes
body: Acute exacerbations of prior neurologic deficits may occur in conjunction with acute infection or metabolic derangement and can sometimes be difficult to distinguish from a new ischemic event. Diffusion-weighted brain MRI can be considered if uncertainty exists or if diagnostic confirmation is required.

title: Temperature management, consisting of avoidance of fever and maintenance of body temperature ≤36 C (96.8 F) for 24-48 hours, has been shown
body: Temperature management, consisting of avoidance of fever and maintenance of body temperature ≤36 C (96.8 F) for 24-48 hours, has been shown to reduce mortality and improve neurologic recovery following sudden cardiac arrest.

title: Diabetic amyotrophy usually presents with acute and asymmetric focal lower extremity pain associated with weakness, muscle atrophy
body: Diabetic amyotrophy usually presents with acute and asymmetric focal lower extremity pain associated with weakness, muscle atrophy, areflexia, autonomic dysfunction, and unintentional weight loss. Patients frequently have coexisting diabetic symmetrical polyneuropathy. Treatment is mainly symptomatic and includes physical and occupational therapy, medication for pain control, and strict glycemic control. Many patients make partial functional recovery.

title: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a condition with broad clinical symptoms
body: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a condition with broad clinical symptoms. It presents with acute to subacute onset of severe headache (thunderclap), hemiparesis, seizures, altered mentation, and visual impairment. A brain MRI commonly shows evidence Ofsymmetrical hyperintense T2∕FLAIR signal abnormalities predominantly in the subcortical white matter of posterior parieto-occipital lobes suggestive of vasogenic edema. Hypertensive crisis is one of the many causes of PRES, which is believed to be the result of impaired cerebral autoregulation.

title: Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis typically presents with the subacute onset of headache and multifocal neurologic deficits in patients with
body: Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis typically presents with the subacute onset of headache and multifocal neurologic deficits in patients with metastatic breast cancer, lung cancer, or melanoma. Diagnosis can be made with gadolinium-enhanced MRI of the brain and spinal cord. Lumbar puncture increases diagnostic accuracy but is generally performed after MRI to avoid the risk of cerebral herniation and potential for radiographic artifact.

title: Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) is due to thiamine deficiency and can occur in patients with chronic alcohol use or chronic malnutrition (eg
body: Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) is due to thiamine deficiency and can occur in patients with chronic alcohol use or chronic malnutrition (eg, anorexia nervosa, hyperemesis gravidarum, post-gastric bypass surgery). Iatrogenic WE can be prevented by administering intravenous thiamine before or concurrently with dextrose.

title: Serotonin syndrome is caused by excess serotonergic activity, most commonly due to drug-drug interactions or use of multiple serotonergic
body: Serotonin syndrome is caused by excess serotonergic activity, most commonly due to drug-drug interactions or use of multiple serotonergic medications. It consists of mental status changes, autonomic dysregulation, and neuromuscular hyperactivity. Initial management includes benzodiazepines and supportive measures.

title: Thrombolytic therapy is indicated for acute ischemic stroke in patients who are seen within 4.5 hours of symptom onset
body: Thrombolytic therapy is indicated for acute ischemic stroke in patients who are seen within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. Mechanical thrombectomy is indicated for those with a large artery occlusion in the anterior circulation and should be performed within 24 hours of when the patient last had normal function. Aspirin therapy reduces the risk of recurrent ischemic strokes and is recommended within 24-48 hours of the first onset; however, it should be withheld for 24 hours in patients who undergo thrombolysis.

title: Elderly patients presenting with mental status changes and focal seizures should be empirically treated with acyclovir for possible herpes
body: Elderly patients presenting with mental status changes and focal seizures should be empirically treated with acyclovir for possible herpes simplex virus (HSV) encephalitis until proven otherwise. Diagnosis is confirmed by HSV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of the cerebrospinal fluid.

title: Optic neuritis typically presents with acute monocular vision loss over a period of hours to days, eye pain, central scotoma, and color
body: Optic neuritis typically presents with acute monocular vision loss over a period of hours to days, eye pain, central scotoma, and color vision loss out of proportion to loss of visual acuity. It is frequently associated with multiple sclerosis. Intravenous methylprednisolone is the preferred treatment as oral glucocorticoids are associated with increased risk of recurrent optic neuritis.

title: Patients presenting with new-onset headache with focal neurologic deficits in the setting of cerebral metastatic disease should be started
body: Patients presenting with new-onset headache with focal neurologic deficits in the setting of cerebral metastatic disease should be started on intravenous steroids (e.g., methylprednisolone or dexamethasone) to reduce vasogenic edema and mass effect.

title: The only laboratory test that is absolutely required prior to thrombolytic therapy in patients with ischemic stroke is a blood glucose concentration.
Guillain-Barre syndrome is an ascending weakness that develops approximately a week following a respiratory Orgastrointestinal infection
body: Guillain-Barre syndrome is an ascending weakness that develops approximately a week following a respiratory Orgastrointestinal infection and has been strongly associated with Campylobacter jejuni infection. About one-third of patients have no history of antecedent illness. An increased cerebrospinal protein with normal white blood cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation) suggests the diagnosis but may not be present for up to a week after symptom onset.

title: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis consists of serologies (acetylcholine receptor and muscle-specific tyrosine kinase receptor antibodies) and
body: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis consists of serologies (acetylcholine receptor and muscle-specific tyrosine kinase receptor antibodies) and nerve conduction studies in a stepwise manner. Thyroid-stimulating hormone and chest computed tomography (to look for thymoma) should be ordered in all patients diagnosed with myasthenia gravis.

title: Early carotid revascularization (within 1-2 weeks) with carotid artery endarterectomy is recommended for patients with symptomatic
body: Early carotid revascularization (within 1-2 weeks) with carotid artery endarterectomy is recommended for patients with symptomatic high-grade carotid stenosis who have transient ischemic attack or stroke; very early revascularization (<48 hours) should be avoided in these patients.

title: Features of cerebellar stroke include persistent vertigo, limb ataxia, falling/nystagmus to the side of the lesion, inability to ambulate
body: Features of cerebellar stroke include persistent vertigo, limb ataxia, falling/nystagmus to the side of the lesion, inability to ambulate, and symptoms persisting >72 hours. It is common in patients with advanced age and other cardiovascular risk factors. MRI and MR angiography are the preferred diagnostic studies.

title: Acute dystonic reactions can be caused by antidopaminergic agents (eg, metoclopramide)
body: Acute dystonic reactions can be caused by antidopaminergic agents (eg, metoclopramide). Treatment involves discontinuation of the drug and administration Ofanticholinergic agents (eg, benztropine, trihexyphenidyl) or agents with both anticholinergic and antihistamine effects (eg, diphenhydramine).

title: West-Nile virus is a mosquito-borne disease that mainly occurs during the summer months, especially when the weather is humid
body: West-Nile virus is a mosquito-borne disease that mainly occurs during the summer months, especially when the weather is humid. Encephalitis associated with acute asymmetric flaccid paralysis or extrapyramidal symptoms is highly suggestive of West-Nile virus infection. The diagnosis is confirmed with positive serum or CSF IgM titer for West Nile virus. Treatment is mainly supportive.

title: Vertigo is classified as peripheral or central
body: Vertigo is classified as peripheral or central. Peripheral vertigo usually presents with more dizziness and is due to benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, Meniere's disease, vestibular neuronitis, or labyrinthitis. Central vertigo presents with more gait disturbances and is due to stroke, multiple sclerosis, migraine, or CNS tumor. MRI of the brain should be done to evaluate patients with central vertigo for acute causes such as stroke.

title: Convulsive syncope can be mistaken for seizure, but features such as post-ictal state, tongue biting, head/eye turning to one side, and
body: Convulsive syncope can be mistaken for seizure, but features such as post-ictal state, tongue biting, head/eye turning to one side, and hypersalivation are typically absent. The evaluation of syncope should begin with a careful history, physical examination (including orthostatic vital signs), and an electrocardiogram.

title: Migraine with brainstem aura is a subset of migraine characterized by vertigo, dysarthria, ataxia, and diplopia
body: Migraine with brainstem aura is a subset of migraine characterized by vertigo, dysarthria, ataxia, and diplopia. Because the symptoms can mimic posterior circulatory defects, vascular lesions should be ruled out with MRI and MR angiography. ■ I■a End © Resources

title: Patients with neoplastic epidural spinal cord compression and severe neurologic symptoms can benefit from intravenous corticosteroids (eg
body: Patients with neoplastic epidural spinal cord compression and severe neurologic symptoms can benefit from intravenous corticosteroids (eg, dexamethasone). Definitive management with spinal surgery (eg, tumor resection, spine stabilization) is indicated emergently in patients with an unstable spine, limited disease burden, and favorable prognosis to increase the likelihood of regaining mobility.

title: The respiratory status of patients with myasthenic crisis should be monitored using serial measurements of vital capacity (VC) and maximal
body: The respiratory status of patients with myasthenic crisis should be monitored using serial measurements of vital capacity (VC) and maximal inspiratory force (MIF). Patients should be electively intubated when VC <20 mL/kg or MIF >-30 cm H2O (eg, 0 to -30). Treatment includes plasmapheresis or intravenous immunoglobulin, along with high-dose steroids.

title: Mononeuritis multiplex is a painful, asymmetrical, sensory and motor peripheral neuropathy
body: Mononeuritis multiplex is a painful, asymmetrical, sensory and motor peripheral neuropathy. It affects 2 or more nerves in different parts of the body and is most common in patients with vasculitides, connective tissue diseases, or systemic disorders such as diabetes mellitus.

title: In patients with acute ischemic stroke, aspirin and anticoagulation (for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis) should not be started within
body: In patients with acute ischemic stroke, aspirin and anticoagulation (for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis) should not be started within 24 hours of initiating tissue plasminogen activator and should generally be preceded by neuroimaging to rule out intracranial hemorrhage.

title: Cluster headache typically presents with multiple short attacks of severe unilateral periorbital, supraorbital, or temporal pain associated
body: Cluster headache typically presents with multiple short attacks of severe unilateral periorbital, supraorbital, or temporal pain associated with restlessness and ipsilateral autonomic symptoms (eg, ptosis, miosis, lacrimation, conjunctival injection, rhinorrhea/nasal congestion). Acute therapy usually involves oxygen and/or sumatriptan. Verapamil is the preferred agent for chronic preventive therapy.

title: Ischemic stroke is classified as embolic or thrombotic
body: Ischemic stroke is classified as embolic or thrombotic. Embolic strokes usually have abrupt onset of focal neurologic findings with maximal symptoms at onset. Thrombotic strokes usually present as fluctuating symptoms with periodic improvement and stuttering progression.

title: Acute lumbo-sacral radiculopathy is characterized by low back pain associated with radiating pain and/or numbness along a dermatomal
body: Acute lumbo-sacral radiculopathy is characterized by low back pain associated with radiating pain and/or numbness along a dermatomal distribution (most commonly L5 and S1). Activity modification and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for pain are effective in up to 90% of patients. Magnetic resonance imaging is reserved for patients with acute neurological deficits (i.e., weakness, problems walking, or bowel/bladder difficulties), suspicion for infection or malignancy, or failure to improve with initial management.

title: Brainstem (ie, midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata) strokes should be considered in patients with acute cranial nerve (CN) deficits and
body: Brainstem (ie, midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata) strokes should be considered in patients with acute cranial nerve (CN) deficits and crossed signs (contralateral hemiparesis or hemisensory loss). CN III dysfunction with contralateral hemiplegia suggests a stroke at the level of the midbrain.

title: A single focal seizure due to a structural brain lesion has a high risk of recurrence and requires treatment with an antiepileptic drug.
Clinical features of giant cell arteritis include systemic symptoms, headaches, jaw claudication, and amaurosis fugax
body: Clinical features of giant cell arteritis include systemic symptoms, headaches, jaw claudication, and amaurosis fugax. Inflammatory markers (eg, erythrocyte sedimentation rate) are usually elevated. Temporal artery biopsy is the preferred confirmatory test, but patients should be started on immediate high- dose glucocorticoids to prevent vision loss while awaiting biopsy results.

title: Within the first 24 hours of intravenous tPA treatment, the patient's blood pressure should be maintained < 180/105 mm Hg
body: Within the first 24 hours of intravenous tPA treatment, the patient's blood pressure should be maintained < 180/105 mm Hg. Early enteral feeding, anticoagulants, and anti-platelet agents should be avoided for the first 24 hours until repeat CT head imaging shows no hemorrhagic conversion.

title: Non-pupil-sparing third nerve palsies are most concerning for aneurysmal compression; MR or CT angiography should be performed immediately
body: Non-pupil-sparing third nerve palsies are most concerning for aneurysmal compression; MR or CT angiography should be performed immediately. Pupil-sparing third nerve palsies are most commonly caused by microvascular ischemia associated with diabetes mellitus. I÷3 End © Resources Il Suspend

title: ICA dissection typically occurs after head or neck trauma with acute neurologic deficits, headache that may radiate to the neck, and
body: ICA dissection typically occurs after head or neck trauma with acute neurologic deficits, headache that may radiate to the neck, and possible Horner syndrome. MRA/CTA of the neck is preferred to diagnose vascular dissection (ICA or vertebral), which typically has a flame-shaped, tapered appearance. Prompt recognition and treatment can decrease the risk of stroke, neurologic disability, and death.

title: Brain death can be suggested by clinical criteria (e.g., coma, absent cranial nerve reflexes and motor responses, CT/MRI brain imaging
body: Brain death can be suggested by clinical criteria (e.g., coma, absent cranial nerve reflexes and motor responses, CT/MRI brain imaging consistent with a devastating CNS event, etc.). Two clinical brain death examinations and apnea testing are recommended and considered appropriate for brain death diagnosis. Every attempt should be made to remove all confounding variables that can interfere with obtaining a reliable clinical examination and bedside apnea test.

title: Elderly people with silent brain infarcts have an increased risk of developing dementia than those without such lesions.
In patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage, rebleeding is the major cause of death within the first 24 hours of presentation. Vasospasm usually does not occur until day 3.
Intracranial aneurysms occur in up to 20% of individuals with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
body: Intracranial aneurysms occur in up to 20% of individuals with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. However, routine screening for aneurysms is controversial. If chosen, screening is best performed with time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography, which does not require gadolinium contrast and can be done at any glomerular filtration rate level. Computed tomography angiography is an alternate screening method.

title: In patients with hemorrhagic stroke, intermittent pneumatic compression started within 72 hours of the acute event is effective in
body: In patients with hemorrhagic stroke, intermittent pneumatic compression started within 72 hours of the acute event is effective in preventing deep-vein thrombosis (DVT). Pharmacologic DVT prophylaxis may be considered 1-4 days following stroke in immobile patients as long as repeat imaging rules out further bleeding.

title: Initial management of delirium is aimed at treatment of reversible causes, patient orientation, and environmental modification
body: Initial management of delirium is aimed at treatment of reversible causes, patient orientation, and environmental modification. A cautious trial of antipsychotics is reserved for patients who fail conservative measures and pose a significant risk of harm to themselves or others. Restraints are a last resort and can worsen agitation.

title: Treatment for patients with myasthenic crisis includes plasma exchange or intravenous immunoglobulin due to their rapid onset of action and
body: Treatment for patients with myasthenic crisis includes plasma exchange or intravenous immunoglobulin due to their rapid onset of action and peak effect. High-dose glucocorticoids are used to maintain symptom control, but onset is delayed; glucocorticoids alone are not recommended as they are associated with a transient worsening of symptoms. Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (eg, pyridostigmine) should be stopped temporarily during mechanical ventilation to minimize oral secretions.

title: Patients with recent (within 24-48 hours) transient ischemic attack (TIA) and risk factors (eg, multiple recurrent TIAs, atrial
body: Patients with recent (within 24-48 hours) transient ischemic attack (TIA) and risk factors (eg, multiple recurrent TIAs, atrial fibrillation, symptom duration > 1 hour, symptomatic internal carotid artery stenosis > 50%, hypercoagulable disorders, or high ABCDz score) have higher risk of stroke within the next 48 hours. They should be hospitalized for further investigation and prevention.

title: Medication-overuse headache (MOH) can present in the setting of a primary chronic headache disorder
body: Medication-overuse headache (MOH) can present in the setting of a primary chronic headache disorder. It needs to be addressed separately from the chronic headache disorder by the discontinuation of the offending analgesic agent and the introduction of a short oral steroid taper.

title: Essential tremor is the most common action tremor and occurs more commonly with advancing age
body: Essential tremor is the most common action tremor and occurs more commonly with advancing age. It usually involves the hands and arms and worsens at the end of goal-directed movements. Treatment usually includes propranolol or primidone.

title: Essential tremor is an autosomal dominant tremor induced by action or posture
body: Essential tremor is an autosomal dominant tremor induced by action or posture. It tends to affect the upper extremities but can also occur in the head, voice, chin, and legs. Treatment involves the use of beta blockers (eg, propranolol) or primidone.

title: Parkinson disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by bradykinesia, cogwheel rigidity, and resting tremor
body: Parkinson disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by bradykinesia, cogwheel rigidity, and resting tremor. Carbidopa/levodopa is the most effective medication for treatment of motor symptoms; however, in mild to moderate disease and patients age <65, dopamine agonists are generally preferred as they are associated with fewer motor fluctuations.

title: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy usually presents with progressive muscle weakness, distal sensory loss, and
body: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy usually presents with progressive muscle weakness, distal sensory loss, and diminished or absent reflexes developing over >8 weeks. Diagnosis is confirmed with electrodiagnostic studies demonstrating peripheral nerve demyelination. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis will show albuminocytologic dissociation in the vast majority of cases.

title: Phenytoin toxicity presents with horizontal nystagmus, ataxia, slurred speech, and mental status changes
body: Phenytoin toxicity presents with horizontal nystagmus, ataxia, slurred speech, and mental status changes. Causes include dosage increase, drug-drug interactions causing altered metabolism, hepatic or renal disease, or decreased serum albumin. Treatment includes discontinuation of the drug and supportive care.

title: Athletes with concussion should be removed from play until their symptoms have resolved, and they can subsequently benefit from a graduated return to play protocol.
Non-motor symptoms, such as rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder, excessive daytime somnolence, mood disturbance, anosmia, and
body: Non-motor symptoms, such as rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder, excessive daytime somnolence, mood disturbance, anosmia, and constipation, can be suggestive of early Parkinson disease and manifest before the onset of motor symptoms.

title: Restless legs syndrome is a movement disorder characterized by a sensation of lower extremity discomfort and an urge to move the legs that
body: Restless legs syndrome is a movement disorder characterized by a sensation of lower extremity discomfort and an urge to move the legs that is relieved with movement. It is commonly associated with iron deficiency. Patients with a ferritin level <75 μg∕L or other evidence of iron deficiency should receive iron supplementation, which may alleviate symptoms.

title: Amyloid angiopathy is the second most common cause of intracerebral hemorrhage, especially in patients age >75. The location of the hemorrhage is typically lobar. The risk of recurrence is high.
Phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE-5) inhibitors prevent the breakdown of cyclic guanosine monophosphate in the corpus cavernosum
body: Phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE-5) inhibitors prevent the breakdown of cyclic guanosine monophosphate in the corpus cavernosum. However, PDE-5 inhibitors also interact with phosphodiesterase-6 in the retina and can result in dose-dependent, temporary visual side effects such as bluish tinting, blurry vision, and photophobia.

title: Morton’s neuroma (interdigital nerve compression) results from painful enlargement of the plantar digital nerve between the metatarsal
body: Morton’s neuroma (interdigital nerve compression) results from painful enlargement of the plantar digital nerve between the metatarsal heads. Patients complain of burning pain and numbness usually between the 3rα and 4τn metatarsals. Treatment is conservative.

title: Brachial plexopathy can occur in patients with a history of cancer and radiation therapy
body: Brachial plexopathy can occur in patients with a history of cancer and radiation therapy. Cancer-induced brachial plexopathy usually presents with more severe pain at symptom onset, involves the lower plexus, and is associated with Horner’s syndrome.

title: Many dizzy elderly patients may not have a cardiac or central nervous system etiology
body: Many dizzy elderly patients may not have a cardiac or central nervous system etiology. Other factors causing dizziness include decreased vision, medications, peripheral neuropathy, deconditioning, and abnormal peripheral Vestibularfunction (most common). Comprehensive balance training exercises may be beneficial in these patients.

title: Sensory disturbances (eg, impaired vision) are a common cause of falls in the elderly
body: Sensory disturbances (eg, impaired vision) are a common cause of falls in the elderly. Visual acuity should be part of the initial fall prevention assessment. Additional assessment for fall risk in elderly patients includes postural vital signs, balance and gait testing, and home hazard evaluation.

title: Carotid endarterectomy is indicated in symptomatic patients with high-grade carotid artery stenosis (70%-99%)
body: Carotid endarterectomy is indicated in symptomatic patients with high-grade carotid artery stenosis (70%-99%). Regardless of severity, patients with symptomatic carotid stenosis should receive medical therapy, including statin and antiplatelet therapy, and maintain blood pressure <130/80 mm Hg to control atherosclerotic risk factors.

title: Multiple sclerosis is characterized by central nervous system deficits disseminated in time and space
body: Multiple sclerosis is characterized by central nervous system deficits disseminated in time and space. T2- weighted MRI typically shows multifocal ovoid white matter lesions in the periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, or spinal cord areas. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis can support the diagnosis in atypical cases and usually shows Oligoclonal IgG bands and elevated IgG index.

title: Extrapyramidal symptoms such as dystonia in patients with Parkinson disease are the result of insufficient dopamine in the central nervous
body: Extrapyramidal symptoms such as dystonia in patients with Parkinson disease are the result of insufficient dopamine in the central nervous system. Patients on immediate-release carbidopa/levodopa may need longer-acting carbidopa/levodopa at night to maintain steady levels of dopamine and to avoid unwanted extrapyramidal symptoms.

title: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension presents with headaches, visual symptoms, tinnitus, and diplopia
body: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension presents with headaches, visual symptoms, tinnitus, and diplopia. Diagnosis involves ocular examination, neuroimaging (magnetic resonance imaging and magnetic resonance venography), and lumbar puncture demonstrating elevated opening pressure (> 250 mm H2O). If unrecognized, patients are at risk of vision loss. Initial treatment involves discontinuation of the offending medications and weight loss plus acetazolamide in idiopathic cases.

title: Thymoma is the most common cause of an anterior mediastinal mass
body: Thymoma is the most common cause of an anterior mediastinal mass. It often occurs concomitantly with myasthenia gravis (MG). Thymectomy is suggested for patients < age 60 with generalized MG. Other anterior mediastinal masses include teratoma, lymphoma, and thyroid tumors.

title: Individuals with very mild dementia or those who are highly educated with dementia can have normal mini­ mental state examination scores.
Diabetic neuropathy is the most common cause of peripheral neuropathy in adults and may be associated with prediabetes
body: Diabetic neuropathy is the most common cause of peripheral neuropathy in adults and may be associated with prediabetes. Early signs can include impaired sensation (eg, pain/temperature, vibration/proprioception) involving the feet and diminished ankle reflexes. Motor weakness may occur in advanced cases.

title: Dopaminergic agonists (ropinirole, pramipexole) are the mainstays Oftreatment for restless leg syndrome.
The classic triad of normal-pressure hydrocephalus is cognitive dysfunction, gait difficulty, and urinary incontinence
body: The classic triad of normal-pressure hydrocephalus is cognitive dysfunction, gait difficulty, and urinary incontinence. Diagnosis is usually confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging showing enlarged ventricles and symptomatic improvement after removal of 30-50 mL of cerebrospinal fluid via lumbar puncture. Treatment involves ventriculoperitoneal shunting.

title: Guillain-Barre syndrome usually presents after recent infectious illness with ascending symmetrical weakness, loss of reflexes, and no
body: Guillain-Barre syndrome usually presents after recent infectious illness with ascending symmetrical weakness, loss of reflexes, and no significant sensory loss. Diagnosis is made clinically with neurophysiology studies as well as lumbar puncture showing high protein with normal WBC count (90% patients). Treatment is supportive and can be accelerated by plasmapheresis or IVIG.

title: Carpal tunnel syndrome is primarily a clinical diagnosis
body: Carpal tunnel syndrome is primarily a clinical diagnosis. Electrodiagnostic studies are usually performed during atypical presentations, to evaluate disease severity, and prior to considering surgery. Mild-to- moderate cases can be treated conservatively (eg, wrist splinting, injectable corticosteroids).

title: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) is characterized by chronic pulsatile headaches, often associated with
body: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) is characterized by chronic pulsatile headaches, often associated with "whooshing" tinnitus. The headaches are worsened by lying flat. Funduscopy should be performed to evaluate for the presence of papilledema, which suggests elevated intracranial pressure. If neuroimaging is negative, the diagnosis can be confirmed by measuring opening pressure on lumbar puncture.

title: Cervical Spondylotic myelopathy is a relatively common and potentially treatable cause of progressive disability in older adults
body: Cervical Spondylotic myelopathy is a relatively common and potentially treatable cause of progressive disability in older adults. This condition often presents with upper motor neuron signs in the lower extremities and lower motor neuron signs in the upper extremities. MRI is the diagnostic study of choice.

title: Peroneal neuropathy is usually due to an injury of the nerve at the fibular head and typically presents with foot drop and paresthesias of
body: Peroneal neuropathy is usually due to an injury of the nerve at the fibular head and typically presents with foot drop and paresthesias of the dorsum of the foot. Patients usually have normal reflexes and foot inversion, which can help differentiate peroneal neuropathy from other causes of neuropathy in the lower extremity.

title: Acute onset Ofweakness and sensory loss below a segmental spinal level, paresthesias, and bowel/bladder/sphincter dysfunction suggest
body: Acute onset Ofweakness and sensory loss below a segmental spinal level, paresthesias, and bowel/bladder/sphincter dysfunction suggest transverse myelitis. Magnetic resonance imaging with contrast shows enhancing cord segments with surrounding edema. Treatment is mainly supportive and can include intravenous corticosteroids.

title: Parkinson-plus syndromes (eg, multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy, Corticobasal degeneration) can generally be
body: Parkinson-plus syndromes (eg, multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy, Corticobasal degeneration) can generally be distinguished from idiopathic Parkinson disease by the rapid onset of symptoms, symmetric neurologic findings, absence of tremor, early autonomic dysfunction, and poor response to Ievodopa. The hallmark features of multiple system atrophy include akinetic-rigid parkinsonism, autonomic failure, and cerebellar ataxia.

title: Acetaminophen is the preferred medication for migraines during pregnancy due to its low risk of adverse events
body: Acetaminophen is the preferred medication for migraines during pregnancy due to its low risk of adverse events. Other options in patients not responding to acetaminophen include nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (2nd trimester), opioids, and antiemetics.

title: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is characterized by impaired cognition with preserved functioning and independence of activities of daily
body: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is characterized by impaired cognition with preserved functioning and independence of activities of daily living. Patients with the amnestic MCI subtype are at increased risk for developing dementia.

title: Bell's palsy is an acute peripheral facial nerve palsy likely due to herpes simplex virus activation
body: Bell's palsy is an acute peripheral facial nerve palsy likely due to herpes simplex virus activation. Prednisone given early after symptom onset speeds recovery and enhances outcome. Addition of Valacyclovir may help patients with severe facial palsy.

title: A single unprovoked seizure requires investigation with laboratory studies, MRI of the brain, and EEG to rule out underlying organic
body: A single unprovoked seizure requires investigation with laboratory studies, MRI of the brain, and EEG to rule out underlying organic disease and estimate future seizure risk. Abnormal studies indicate a high risk of recurrence and usually require antiepileptics.

title: Acute neuritis associated with herpes zoster is treated with traditional oral analgesics
body: Acute neuritis associated with herpes zoster is treated with traditional oral analgesics. Post-herpetic neuralgia (pain that persists months after resolution of the rash) is treated with tricyclic antidepressants, gabapentin, or pregabalin. Antiviral therapy is recommended only for patients who present within 72 hours of initial herpes zoster symptoms.

title: There is no pharmacotherapy with established efficacy for mild cognitive impairment
body: There is no pharmacotherapy with established efficacy for mild cognitive impairment. Higher levels of physical exercise, cognitive activities, active social interactions, and control of cardiovascular risk factors appear to be associated with a decrease in the rate of decline in cognitive impairment in patients at risk for dementia.

title: Anticonvulsant hypersensitivity syndrome is a rare but serious disorder that usually occurs within 2 months of initiating anticonvulsant
body: Anticonvulsant hypersensitivity syndrome is a rare but serious disorder that usually occurs within 2 months of initiating anticonvulsant therapy. Clinical manifestations include fever, rash, pharyngitis, Iymphadenopathy, facial edema, and systemic organ involvement (eg, hepatitis, nephritis). Management includes discontinuation of the offending drug and systemic glucocorticoids.

title: Brain abscess is usually characterized by single or multiple ring-enhancing lesions at the grey-white matter junction with significant
body: Brain abscess is usually characterized by single or multiple ring-enhancing lesions at the grey-white matter junction with significant vasogenic edema or mass effect. Toxoplasmosis usually causes multiple ring­ enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia and frontal/parietal regions and almost always occurs in those with HIV who have CD4 counts <100∕mnrr and positive toxoplasma IgG serology. Primary central nervous system lymphoma usually occurs in the subcortical white matter and is most common in those with HIV who have CD4 counts <50∕mm0.

title: Nonpharmacologic therapies (eg, environmental, behavioral) are first-line interventions in dementia patients with behavioral disturbances
body: Nonpharmacologic therapies (eg, environmental, behavioral) are first-line interventions in dementia patients with behavioral disturbances. Antipsychotics are not consistently effective and should be reserved for patients who do not respond to nonpharmacological interventions or when agitated behavior poses a safety risk to the patient or caregivers.

title: Complete occlusion of the carotid artery in an asymptomatic patient typically indicates adequate collateral blood flow; therefore, the risks of carotid intervention outweigh the benefits.
Foot drop is usually due to common peroneal nerve injury or L5 lumbosacral radiculopathy
body: Foot drop is usually due to common peroneal nerve injury or L5 lumbosacral radiculopathy. Common peroneal nerve compression causes painless weakness of foot dorsiflexion, eversion, and toe extension; L5 radiculopathy usually causes back pain with more extensive weakness involving foot dorsiflexion, eversion and inversion; toe extension; and leg abduction. MRI in lumbosacral radiculopathy can show nerve root compression.

title: Carpal tunnel syndrome usually affects the dominant hand and is due to compression of the median nerve by the flexor retinaculum
body: Carpal tunnel syndrome usually affects the dominant hand and is due to compression of the median nerve by the flexor retinaculum. Mild to moderate symptoms are treated with conservative therapy (e.g., wrist splint, steroid injections). Surgical decompression is reserved for patients with severe symptoms (or evidence of axonal injury on EMG) or mild to moderate symptoms refractory to conservative therapy.

title: Dopamine receptor antagonists (eg, typical or atypical antipsychotics, antiemetics) may cause secondary parkinsonism
body: Dopamine receptor antagonists (eg, typical or atypical antipsychotics, antiemetics) may cause secondary parkinsonism. Most cases resolve after discontinuation of the offending agent. Patients that require continued antipsychotic therapy should be switched to a low-risk agent (eg, quetiapine, clozapine).

title: Natalizumab is a recombinant monoclonal antibody against alpha-4 integrins that is a second-line agent for relapsing-remitting multiple
body: Natalizumab is a recombinant monoclonal antibody against alpha-4 integrins that is a second-line agent for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. However, the drug has been associated with development of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, and all patients should have JC virus antibody testing prior to starting natalizumab.

title: Vestibular schwannoma originates from the Schwann cells surrounding the vestibulocochlear nerve and is the most common tumor causing
body: Vestibular schwannoma originates from the Schwann cells surrounding the vestibulocochlear nerve and is the most common tumor causing sensorineural hearing loss. Patients typically present with chronic ipsilateral tinnitus, ipsilateral sensorineural hearing loss, vertigo, nausea/vomiting, and problems with balance.

title: Clinically isolated syndrome is defined as the first episode of central nervous system dysfunction caused by demyelination; it may progress
body: Clinically isolated syndrome is defined as the first episode of central nervous system dysfunction caused by demyelination; it may progress to multiple sclerosis (MS). All such patients should undergo a brain MRI to evaluate for demyelinating plaques and assess MS risk stratification. Patients with abnormal MRI findings may receive disease-modifying therapy.

title: Meralgia paresthetica is due to lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) compression and presents with pure sensory symptoms (e.g., numbness
body: Meralgia paresthetica is due to lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) compression and presents with pure sensory symptoms (e.g., numbness, paresthesias, and dysesthesias) in the anterolateral thigh. Risk factors include wearing tight pants or belts, pregnancy, obesity, and diabetes. The diagnosis is made clinically. Patients should be reassured that this is not a serious condition, and they usually respond to conservative treatment.

title: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (i.e., pseudotumor cerebri) presents with a chronic, holocranial, and pulsatile headache worsened by
body: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (i.e., pseudotumor cerebri) presents with a chronic, holocranial, and pulsatile headache worsened by lying flat and ameliorated by sitting up. The diagnosis requires normal imaging and elevated cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure (>250 mm H2O). The optic nerves are frequently affected; therefore, dedicated visual field testing and funduscopy need to be performed to rule out impending visual loss.

title: Subdural hematoma should be suspected in an elderly patient presenting with new confusion, personality changes, headache, or lethargy in
body: Subdural hematoma should be suspected in an elderly patient presenting with new confusion, personality changes, headache, or lethargy in the setting of possible head trauma. Diagnosis is suggested by the presence of a crescent-shaped extra-axial lesion on head CT scan.

title: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that causes destruction of the upper and lower motor neurons in
body: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that causes destruction of the upper and lower motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord. Asymmetric limb weakness (eg, hand weakness and foot drop) is the most common presenting symptom. Sensory symptoms are absent. Median survival time is approximately 5 years from the time of diagnosis, and respiratory failure is the most common cause of death.

title: Diagnostic evaluation of peripheral neuropathy should be considered in patients when the etiology of neuropathy is unclear or in the
body: Diagnostic evaluation of peripheral neuropathy should be considered in patients when the etiology of neuropathy is unclear or in the setting of severe or rapidly developing symptoms. The initial workup may include laboratory studies such as blood glucose, vitamin B^∣2, TSH, antinuclear antibody, rapid plasma reagin, hemoglobin A1c, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, complete blood count, and serum protein electrophoresis.

title: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis consists of serologies (anti-acetylcholine receptor and anti-muscle-specific kinase antibodies) and nerve
body: Diagnosis of myasthenia gravis consists of serologies (anti-acetylcholine receptor and anti-muscle-specific kinase antibodies) and nerve conduction studies in a stepwise manner. Pyridostigmine (acetylcholinesterase inhibitor) is the first-line treatment. TSH and CT scan or MRI of the chest (to look for a thymoma) should be ordered in all patients diagnosed with this condition.

title: Polypharmacy often leads to adverse consequences in an aging patient
body: Polypharmacy often leads to adverse consequences in an aging patient. Drugs with anti-cholinergic effects (i.e., memory impairment, hallucinations, confusion, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention) can be especially troublesome in the geriatric population and should be avoided.

title: Paroxysmal hemicrania presents as episodic or chronic unilateral throbbing head pain (usually lasting 2-30 minutes) associated with
body: Paroxysmal hemicrania presents as episodic or chronic unilateral throbbing head pain (usually lasting 2-30 minutes) associated with autonomic symptoms. Improvement with indomethacin confirms the diagnosis. Main features differentiating paroxysmal hemicranias from cluster headaches are the higher frequency and shorter duration of attacks and the response to indomethacin.

title: Traumatic brain injury of any severity can lead (a few hours or days later) to post-concussive syndrome, which is clinically described by
body: Traumatic brain injury of any severity can lead (a few hours or days later) to post-concussive syndrome, which is clinically described by the following constellation of symptoms: Headache, confusion, amnesia, difficulty concentrating or multitasking, vertigo, mood alteration, sleep disturbance, and anxiety. The majority of patients usually improve within weeks to months with symptomatic treatment.

title: Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration typically presents with the subacute onset of cerebellar symptoms and often precedes the diagnosis
body: Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration typically presents with the subacute onset of cerebellar symptoms and often precedes the diagnosis of malignancy (eg, lung, gynecologic, breast) by years. Paraneoplastic antibodies (eg, anti-Yo, anti-Hu, anti-Ri) can help confirm the diagnosis.

title: The diagnosis of dementia with Lewy bodies requires the presence of dementia plus ≥2 core clinical features: Cognitive fluctuations, visual
body: The diagnosis of dementia with Lewy bodies requires the presence of dementia plus ≥2 core clinical features: Cognitive fluctuations, visual hallucinations, REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), and/or parkinsonism. Pharmacologic management includes cholinesterase inhibitors, melatonin for RBD, low- dose, second-generation antipsychotics (eg, quetiapine) for psychosis, and Carbidopa-Ievodopa for parkinsonism.

title: Preventive therapies should be used for patients with migraines >4 times a month, lasting >12 hours, or causing significant impairment
body: Preventive therapies should be used for patients with migraines >4 times a month, lasting >12 hours, or causing significant impairment. Common options include beta blockers, antidepressants, and anticonvulsants. Beta blockers should be avoided in asthmatic patients due to the risk of bronchospasm.

title: Retinal detachment most commonly presents as a posterior vitreous detachment with floaters, flashing lights, and occasional vision loss
body: Retinal detachment most commonly presents as a posterior vitreous detachment with floaters, flashing lights, and occasional vision loss. Patients with retinal detachment and vision loss require urgent referral to an ophthalmologist.

title: Allergic conjunctivitis is characterized by bilateral conjunctival redness, discharge, and itching
body: Allergic conjunctivitis is characterized by bilateral conjunctival redness, discharge, and itching. It is often associated with other allergic symptoms and atopic conditions (eg, asthma, eczema). Treatment options include topical antihistamines/decongestants, mast cell stabilizers, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.

title: Age-related macular degeneration is characterized by progressive, painless central vision loss in patients age >50. Ocular findings include drusen, with or without hypervascularity and hemorrhages.
A red eye associated with significant pain, visual loss, vomiting, headache, and abnormal pupil reactivity in an older individual is
body: A red eye associated with significant pain, visual loss, vomiting, headache, and abnormal pupil reactivity in an older individual is diagnostic of acute angle-closure glaucoma. Immediate referral to ophthalmology is required for treatment in order to prevent irreversible optic nerve damage.

title: Viral conjunctivitis is characterized by acute conjunctival erythema, discomfort, and watery or mucoid discharge
body: Viral conjunctivitis is characterized by acute conjunctival erythema, discomfort, and watery or mucoid discharge. Most cases are caused by adenovirus and may be associated with upper respiratory symptoms. Viral conjunctivitis is a self-limited condition; moist compresses and topical antihistamines and decongestants can reduce the symptoms.

title: Bacterial keratitis is the most common infectious complication of contact lens use
body: Bacterial keratitis is the most common infectious complication of contact lens use. Symptoms include pain, eyelid swelling, photophobia, and conjunctival injection. Empirictreatmentwith broad-spectrum topical antibiotics is advised.

title: Episcleritis is characterized by acute inflammation of the white of the eye, without involvement of the uveal tract
body: Episcleritis is characterized by acute inflammation of the white of the eye, without involvement of the uveal tract. Episcleritis causes mild irritation or a foreign-body sensation without significant pain, visual impairment, or photophobia and is usually self-limited and idiopathic. Treatment is primarily with topical lubricants.

title: Nuclear cataract is typically slowly progressive, bilateral, and asymmetric
body: Nuclear cataract is typically slowly progressive, bilateral, and asymmetric. Patients frequently experience a worsening of distance vision (myopic shift) initially, which may occur before opacification becomes evident.

title: Anterior uveitis is characterized by a unilateral painful, red eye and photophobia
body: Anterior uveitis is characterized by a unilateral painful, red eye and photophobia. Diagnosis is confirmed by identifying leukocytic exudate in the anterior chamber. Noninfectious etiologies are treated with topical corticosteroids.

title: Corneal abrasion typically presents with eye pain and a foreign body sensation resulting in difficultly keeping the eye open
body: Corneal abrasion typically presents with eye pain and a foreign body sensation resulting in difficultly keeping the eye open. Urgent ophthalmology referral is indicated for penetrating trauma, corneal infiltrate/opacity, foreign bodies that cannot be easily removed, or a significant decrease in vision. Antibiotic ointment is the first-line therapy.

title: Dry macular degeneration typically presents in older adults with progressive vision loss in one or both eyes and Subretinal drusen deposits
body: Dry macular degeneration typically presents in older adults with progressive vision loss in one or both eyes and Subretinal drusen deposits with pigment abnormalities on funduscopy. Smoking cessation and daily antioxidant vitamins with zinc can reduce the risk of disease progression.

title: Linezolid-induced optic neuropathy usually occurs after long-term use (> 4 weeks)
body: Linezolid-induced optic neuropathy usually occurs after long-term use (> 4 weeks). Patients should receive periodic eye and neurological examinations to document early findings and discontinue the drug if present.

title: Central retinal artery occlusion presents with acute, painless, severe vision loss in one eye and relative afferent pupillary defect
body: Central retinal artery occlusion presents with acute, painless, severe vision loss in one eye and relative afferent pupillary defect. Funduscopy shows diffuse ischemic retinal whitening and cherry red macula. Treatment includes urgent ophthalmology consultation and measures to lower intraocular pressure (eg, ocular massage, anterior chamber paracentesis, intravenous acetazolamide or mannitol).

title: Frostbite is a severe and localized cold-induced injury
body: Frostbite is a severe and localized cold-induced injury. It is best treated with rapid rewarming with water temperatures of 37-39 C (98.6-102.2 F). After rewarming, the affected areas are usually air dried and covered with nonadherent gauze. Daily hydrotherapy with subsequent dressing changes and elevation of the affected area aid the healing of superficial frostbite.

title: Herbal supplements are used frequently by the general population
body: Herbal supplements are used frequently by the general population. Many such supplements (eg, ginkgo biloba, ginseng, and saw palmetto) increase risk of bleeding and should be discontinued 14 days prior to surgical procedures.

title: Management of classic (nonexertional) heat stroke includes cooling methods (eg, evaporative cooling), circulatory support (with intravenous
body: Management of classic (nonexertional) heat stroke includes cooling methods (eg, evaporative cooling), circulatory support (with intravenous fluid boluses), airway management, and treatment of complications. Antipyretics and dantrolene are not useful in the management of heat stroke.

title: Lithium toxicity should be managed initially by stabilizing the airway and circulation and aggressive saline infusion to ensure significant
body: Lithium toxicity should be managed initially by stabilizing the airway and circulation and aggressive saline infusion to ensure significant lithium clearance. Hemodialysis is indicated for serum lithium levels > 4 mEq/L (4 mmol∕L) OR levels > 2.5 mEq/L PLUS either signs of significant lithium toxicity or inability to excrete lithium.

title: Symptoms of opioid withdrawal generally begin within 1-2 days after abrupt opioid cessation in patients with sustained use (ie, ≥3 weeks)
body: Symptoms of opioid withdrawal generally begin within 1-2 days after abrupt opioid cessation in patients with sustained use (ie, ≥3 weeks). Clinical features include gastrointestinal symptoms (eg, persistent nausea/vomiting), rhinorrhea or lacrimation, diaphoresis, arthralgias, myalgias, mydriasis, and cardiac symptoms (eg, tachycardia).

title: MDMA (3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine) is a stimulant used commonly at parties with overdose presenting as serotonin syndrome, severe
body: MDMA (3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine) is a stimulant used commonly at parties with overdose presenting as serotonin syndrome, severe hyperthermia, and hyponatremia. MDMA overdose can lead to seizures, coagulopathy, and renal and hepatic failure.

title: Pyelonephritis in pregnancy is associated with maternal (eg, acute respiratory distress syndrome) and obstetrical (eg, preterm labor)
body: Pyelonephritis in pregnancy is associated with maternal (eg, acute respiratory distress syndrome) and obstetrical (eg, preterm labor) complications. Management is with inpatient intravenous antibiotics that are administered until patients are afebrile for 24 to 48 hours.

title: Preeclampsia, defined as new-onset hypertension and proteinuria, can present from 20 weeks gestation to 6 weeks postpartum and can be
body: Preeclampsia, defined as new-onset hypertension and proteinuria, can present from 20 weeks gestation to 6 weeks postpartum and can be complicated by pulmonary edema. Treatment includes blood pressure control and seizure prophylaxis (ie, magnesium sulfate).

title: Pregnant women with HIV should be initiated on combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) as soon as possible, independent of HIV RNA viral
body: Pregnant women with HIV should be initiated on combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) as soon as possible, independent of HIV RNA viral load or CD4 count. Early initiation of ART, intrapartum zidovudine (AZT) administration, cesarean delivery, and postexposure ART prophylaxis for the infant decrease the risk of neonatal HIV transmission. Women who achieve optimal viral load reduction (≤1,000 copies/mL) may deliver vaginally without AZT

title: All patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) should be screened for antiphospholipid syndrome as antiphospholipid antibodies are
body: All patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) should be screened for antiphospholipid syndrome as antiphospholipid antibodies are associated with an increased risk for poor maternal and fetal outcomes. Hydroxychloroquine is safe for use during pregnancy and improves pregnancy outcomes in patients with SLE. Anti-SSA/Ro and Anti-SSB/La antibodies are associated with neonatal lupus and congenital heart block.

title: Gastroesophageal reflux disease is common during pregnancy
body: Gastroesophageal reflux disease is common during pregnancy. Initial treatment includes lifestyle modification and antacids; more severe cases are treated with histamine-2 receptor antagonists or proton pump inhibitors.

title: The first-line anticoagulant for pregnant patients with venous thromboembolism is subcutaneous low- molecular-weight heparin. Anticoagulation is continued until at least 6 weeks postpartum.
Hyperglycemia during pregnancy is associated with adverse fetal outcomes
body: Hyperglycemia during pregnancy is associated with adverse fetal outcomes. First-line therapy for glycemic control in patients with gestational diabetes mellitus is dietary modification; if that fails, insulin is the preferred treatment.

title: Pregnant patients with hypothyroidism should increase their levothyroxine dose at the time pregnancy is first detected
body: Pregnant patients with hypothyroidism should increase their levothyroxine dose at the time pregnancy is first detected. TSH should then be checked every 4 weeks and the dose adjusted to trimester-specific norms.

title: Patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) are at increased risk of developing GDM in future pregnancies. Therefore, first-trimester glucose screening is recommended in subsequent pregnancies.
Patients should receive the tetanus toxoid-reduced diphtheria toxoid-acellular pertussis (Tdap) during each pregnancy regardless of prior
body: Patients should receive the tetanus toxoid-reduced diphtheria toxoid-acellular pertussis (Tdap) during each pregnancy regardless of prior vaccination history. Vaccination in the third trimester is preferred as it provides passive immunity to the infant.

title: Pregnant patients with hyperthyroidism are maintained at a mildly hyperthyroid state to avoid fetal hypothyroidism
body: Pregnant patients with hyperthyroidism are maintained at a mildly hyperthyroid state to avoid fetal hypothyroidism. Propylthiouracil is preferred for moderate to severe hyperthyroidism during the first trimester; because propylthiouracil can cause hepatotoxicity, methimazole is preferred during the second and third trimesters. Radioactive iodine is contraindicated during pregnancy.

title: Gestational thrombocytopenia is the most common cause of thrombocytopenia in pregnancy and usually arises late in gestation (often at
body: Gestational thrombocytopenia is the most common cause of thrombocytopenia in pregnancy and usually arises late in gestation (often at delivery). Platelet counts are typically 100,000-150,000/mm , so patients do not have bruising, bleeding, or physical examination abnormalities. The condition is benign and self­ limited and requires no additional testing/treatment. ■ I■a End © Resources

title: Physiologic changes during pregnancy can lead to laboratory values that fall outside of normal reference ranges
body: Physiologic changes during pregnancy can lead to laboratory values that fall outside of normal reference ranges. Moderate elevations in alkaline phosphatase and asymptomatic cholelithiasis are common and do not require intervention. In addition, patients with a single episode of uncomplicated biliary colic typically require only supportive care.

title: All pregnant patients should be screened for anemia, and physiologic changes in hemoglobin can be observed without further evaluation or treatment; baseline levels return 6-8 weeks postpartum.
Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy presents in the second and third trimesters with pruritus and elevated bile acids and is associated
body: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy presents in the second and third trimesters with pruritus and elevated bile acids and is associated with an increased risk of fetal demise. Management includes administration of ursodeoxycholic acid to lower bile acid levels and delivery at 37 weeks gestation.

title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome presents with mental status changes, fever, muscle rigidity, and autonomic instability after starting
body: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome presents with mental status changes, fever, muscle rigidity, and autonomic instability after starting antipsychotics or withdrawing dopamine agonists. Treatment includes withdrawal of a neuroleptic agent or reinstitution of a dopamine agonist, as well as supportive care.

title: Factitious disorder involves the intentional falsification of symptoms for the purpose of assuming the sick role
body: Factitious disorder involves the intentional falsification of symptoms for the purpose of assuming the sick role. It should be suspected in patients with inconsistencies in their history, examination, and laboratory tests and poor response to standard treatments.

title: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a first-line treatment for major depression with psychotic features, and is appropriate for patients
body: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a first-line treatment for major depression with psychotic features, and is appropriate for patients with severe depression who require rapid intervention (eg, not eating/drinking, severe suicidality). Evidence demonstrates that ECT is highly effective and safe for geriatric patients.

title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is characterized by mental status change, muscle rigidity, high fever, and autonomic instability
body: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is characterized by mental status change, muscle rigidity, high fever, and autonomic instability. Management involves prompt discontinuation of the causative agent and aggressive supportive measures.

title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is a life-threatening, idiosyncratic drug reaction to dopamine antagonists
