body: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is a life-threatening, idiosyncratic drug reaction to dopamine antagonists. It typically occurs within days of antipsychotic initiation or dose escalation and presents with high fever, generalized muscle rigidity, autonomic instability, and mental status change.

title: Lithium interacts with several medications (eg, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs, and diuretics) that increase serum lithium levels by
body: Lithium interacts with several medications (eg, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs, and diuretics) that increase serum lithium levels by decreasing GFR or increasing diuresis. The elderly are at increased risk for lithium toxicity due to reduced GFR and volume of distribution. Treatment includes IV hydration, gastric lavage, and/or hemodialysis in cases of large ingestion.

title: Second-generation antipsychotics are associated with metabolic side effects, and patients should be routinely monitored for weight gain
body: Second-generation antipsychotics are associated with metabolic side effects, and patients should be routinely monitored for weight gain, hyperglycemia, and dyslipidemia. Olanzapine and clozapine are associated with the greatest risk.

title: Clozapine treatment can result in the development of life-threatening neutropeŋja and agranulocytosis
body: Clozapine treatment can result in the development of life-threatening neutropeŋja and agranulocytosis. Clozapine should be held if the absolute neutrophil count falls below 1,000∕mm0 and discontinued indefinitely at levels below 500∕mιτr.

title: Tricyclic antidepressant overdose manifests with respiratory depression, hypotension, tachycardia, sedation, seizures, coma, and death
body: Tricyclic antidepressant overdose manifests with respiratory depression, hypotension, tachycardia, sedation, seizures, coma, and death. A wide complex tachycardia or a QRS duration of >100 msec is an indication for intravenous sodium bicarbonate even in the absence of acidosis as it predicts a higher risk of arrhythmia, which may be fatal.

title: Serotonin syndrome presents with mental status changes, autonomic hyperactivity, and neuromuscular abnormalities after exposure to
body: Serotonin syndrome presents with mental status changes, autonomic hyperactivity, and neuromuscular abnormalities after exposure to serotonergic agents. Clonus is an important clinical finding. Treatment involves removing the offending drug, benzodiazepines for agitation, and supportive care. Cyproheptadine is the preferred antidote if supportive measures are unsuccessful.

title: Depression in terminally ill patients is undertreated
body: Depression in terminally ill patients is undertreated. Due to their rapid onset of action, psychostimulants should be considered for treating depressed palliative care patients with a life expectancy of days to weeks.

title: Capacity to consent to or refuse treatment requires the ability to express a choice, understand the relevant medical information
body: Capacity to consent to or refuse treatment requires the ability to express a choice, understand the relevant medical information, appreciate the consequences Oftreatment options, and offer a rationale for the decision. Patients with decision-making capacity have the right to refuse medical treatment. Physicians must adhere to these decisions regardless of what they believe to be the best choice.

title: Strategies to reduce overprescribing of opioid medications include using non-opioid medications for mild pain and prescribing limited
body: Strategies to reduce overprescribing of opioid medications include using non-opioid medications for mild pain and prescribing limited quantities of opioid medications for moderate to severe pain. For most patients with moderate postoperative pain, a short-term (3-5 days) prescription of an opioid analgesic is appropriate.

title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors are first-line pharmacotherapy for social anxiety
body: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors are first-line pharmacotherapy for social anxiety disorder. Benzodiazepines can be considered for poor responders without a history of substance use. Beta blockers can be used as needed for rarely occurring performance situations.

title: Bulimia nervosa should be suspected in otherwise healthy patients who present with bilateral parotid gland enlargement and mild electrolyte
body: Bulimia nervosa should be suspected in otherwise healthy patients who present with bilateral parotid gland enlargement and mild electrolyte abnormalities. Other suspicious findings include oropharyngeal ulcers, erosion of dental enamel, and scars and calluses on the back of the hand.

title: The second-generation antipsychotic quetiapine is a first-line treatment for bipolar depression
body: The second-generation antipsychotic quetiapine is a first-line treatment for bipolar depression. Antidepressant monotherapy should be avoided in patients with bipolar I disorder due to the risk of switching to mania or inducing rapid cycling.

title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors are first-line medications for treatment of panic
body: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors are first-line medications for treatment of panic disorder. Benzodiazepines can provide immediate relief and are appropriate for patients experiencing acute and distressing symptoms while waiting for the antidepressant to take effect.

title: The long-term treatment Ofanorexia nervosa includes psychotherapy and nutritional rehabilitation
body: The long-term treatment Ofanorexia nervosa includes psychotherapy and nutritional rehabilitation. However, a patient with unstable vital signs, BMI <15 kg/m , or serious medical complication of malnutrition (eg, syncope, electrolyte disturbance, seizures, cardiac failure, dysrhythmias) must be hospitalized to prevent mortality from organ failure.

title: Patients who are nonresponders to an adequate trial of their initial antidepressant should generally be switched to a different
body: Patients who are nonresponders to an adequate trial of their initial antidepressant should generally be switched to a different antidepressant. Partial responders may benefit from augmentation with a second agent.

title: Older men have the highest risk of suicide and should be screened carefully for depression
body: Older men have the highest risk of suicide and should be screened carefully for depression. Physicians must perform a careful assessment of risk and protective factors and use clinical judgment to identify those at high risk who require psychiatric hospitalization.

title: The diagnosis of depression in patients with advanced cancer should rely primarily on nonsomatic symptoms such as loss of interest and
body: The diagnosis of depression in patients with advanced cancer should rely primarily on nonsomatic symptoms such as loss of interest and pleasure, worthlessness, excessive guilt, and suicidality. Patients with cancer should be evaluated periodically for symptoms of depression as treatment can improve quality of life for both patients and families.

title: Patients with delusional disorder, somatic type, typically seek care from primary care providers and dermatologists rather than
body: Patients with delusional disorder, somatic type, typically seek care from primary care providers and dermatologists rather than psychiatrists. The disorder is characterized by fixed delusions that something is wrong with their body; patients' functioning is otherwise intact with no other prominent symptoms of psychosis.

title: Treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder consists of serotonergic medications and/or cognitive- behavioral therapy
body: Treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder consists of serotonergic medications and/or cognitive- behavioral therapy. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are first-line treatment due to their favorable side effect profile. Higher doses and trials of at least 6 weeks are often necessary for response.

title: Post-traumatic stress disorder is characterized by at least 1 month of symptoms in response to a life­ threatening event and includes
body: Post-traumatic stress disorder is characterized by at least 1 month of symptoms in response to a life­ threatening event and includes intrusive thoughts, nightmares, or flashbacks about the trauma; avoidance of reminders of the event; hyperarousal; dissociative symptoms; and sleep disturbance.

title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are often associated with sexual dysfunction
body: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are often associated with sexual dysfunction. Treatment options include lowering the dose, switching to another antidepressant (eg, bupropion, mirtazapine), or augmenting with either bupropion or a phosphodiesterase inhibitor.

title: Alcoholism is often unrecognized in the elderly and is frequently accompanied by changes in sleep, poor oral intake, and decreased
body: Alcoholism is often unrecognized in the elderly and is frequently accompanied by changes in sleep, poor oral intake, and decreased attention to self-care. Unexplained accidents, elevated mean corpuscular volume, and elevated liver function studies should prompt consideration of alcohol use disorder.

title: Antipsychotic medications are equally efficacious but have different side effect profiles
body: Antipsychotic medications are equally efficacious but have different side effect profiles. The second- generation antipsychotic (SGA) medications cause fewer extrapyramidal side effects than first-generation antipsychotics but may be associated with weight gain and metabolic syndrome. Among the SGAs, aripiprazole has a lower potential to cause weight gain and metabolic effects and is a preferred drug for minimizing these issues.

title: Major depressive disorder in older patients can present with reversible cognitive changes rather than depressed mood
body: Major depressive disorder in older patients can present with reversible cognitive changes rather than depressed mood. Older patients with new-onset cognitive impairment should routinely be assessed for depression.

title: Schizophrenia is characterized by >2 of the following: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, and negative
body: Schizophrenia is characterized by >2 of the following: Delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, and negative symptoms for >6 months. Negative symptoms, which can be difficult to differentiate from depression, are a core feature of the illness.

title: Manic episodes are characterized by elevated or irritable mood, hyperactivity, grandiosity, distractibility, hypertalkativeness, and
body: Manic episodes are characterized by elevated or irritable mood, hyperactivity, grandiosity, distractibility, hypertalkativeness, and decreased need for sleep. An episodic, as opposed to chronic, course is helpful in differentiating bipolar disorder from adult attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder.

title: Chronic fatigue syndrome is characterized by a relatively sudden onset of intense fatigue that is worse on exertion, is not relieved by
body: Chronic fatigue syndrome is characterized by a relatively sudden onset of intense fatigue that is worse on exertion, is not relieved by rest, and represents a marked deterioration from a previous level Offunctioning. Sleep and cognition are commonly affected. Treatment includes cognitive-behavioral therapy and graded exercise therapy.

title: Patients with depression can be mistakenly labeled as treatment-resistant if they fail to receive an adequate antidepressant trial
body: Patients with depression can be mistakenly labeled as treatment-resistant if they fail to receive an adequate antidepressant trial. Antidepressants should be continued for at least 6 weeks at a therapeutic dosage before considering medication augmentation or switching.

title: Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) is the first-line treatment for chronic insomnia. Patients with continued severe insomnia can be treated with a combination of CBT and short-term pharmacotherapy.
Bipolar disorder is frequently misdiagnosed
body: Bipolar disorder is frequently misdiagnosed. Physicians must be alert to signs of mania or hypomania and consider bipolar disorder in the differential diagnosis of patients with hyperactivity and decreased sleep.

title: The cognitive impairment that may accompany major depressive disorder in the elderly is reversible and generally improves with treatment of
body: The cognitive impairment that may accompany major depressive disorder in the elderly is reversible and generally improves with treatment of the depression; selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are first-line pharmacotherapy.

title: Generalized anxiety disorder is characterized by excessive, uncontrollable worry about multiple issues lasting >6 months. It commonly presents with insomnia and anxiety-related somatic symptoms.
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, particularly fluoxetine, have been shown to be effective in reducing bingeing and purging in patients with bulimia nervosa.
Abrupt discontinuation of short half-life antidepressants such as paroxetine or venlafaxine can result in an antidepressant discontinuation
body: Abrupt discontinuation of short half-life antidepressants such as paroxetine or venlafaxine can result in an antidepressant discontinuation syndrome. Treatment consists of restarting the medication and gradually tapering or substituting an equivalent dose of long-acting fluoxetine.

title: Prior to initiating antidepressants, physicians should carefully screen patients with depression for past hypomanic and manic episodes to
body: Prior to initiating antidepressants, physicians should carefully screen patients with depression for past hypomanic and manic episodes to rule out bipolar disorder. Antidepressant monotherapy should be avoided in patients with bipolar disorder.

title: Transient global amnesia is characterized by a transient episode of impairment in anterograde memory
body: Transient global amnesia is characterized by a transient episode of impairment in anterograde memory. Patients are disoriented to place or time, but self-awareness and motor and social skills are preserved. The differential diagnoses include toxic/metabolic encephalopathy, stroke, and seizures, which must be ruled out.

title: Loneliness is an independent risk factor for functional disability and increased mortality in the elderly that is modifiable with social
body: Loneliness is an independent risk factor for functional disability and increased mortality in the elderly that is modifiable with social interventions. Physicians should routinely inquire about loneliness at health care visits and recommend interventions that decrease social isolation.

title: Maintenance antidepressant pharmacotherapy (1-3 years) is indicated for patients with recurrent episodes
body: Maintenance antidepressant pharmacotherapy (1-3 years) is indicated for patients with recurrent episodes. Patients with ≥3 lifetime depressive episodes, severe episodes (eg, suicide attempts), or episodes lasting ≥2 years can be maintained on treatment indefinitely.

title: Varenicline is the most effective intervention for smoking cessation, and the small increased risk of cardiovascular events is outweighed
body: Varenicline is the most effective intervention for smoking cessation, and the small increased risk of cardiovascular events is outweighed by the risks of continued smoking for most patients. Bupropion is a good option for patients who are concerned about post-cessation weight gain, but it is contraindicated in those with seizure or eating disorders.

title: Depression is a common and treatable cause of sleep disturbance and fatigue. All patients presenting with these symptoms should undergo depression screening.
Somatic symptom disorder is optimally managed through regularly scheduled visits with the same physician, who can minimize unnecessary
body: Somatic symptom disorder is optimally managed through regularly scheduled visits with the same physician, who can minimize unnecessary diagnostic testing, inappropriate interventions, and specialist referrals. Antidepressants and cognitive-behavioral therapy have also been shown to be beneficial.

title: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by excessive preoccupation with weight and recurrent episodes of binge eating and compensatory behaviors
body: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by excessive preoccupation with weight and recurrent episodes of binge eating and compensatory behaviors that include self-induced vomiting, laxative abuse, fasting, and excessive exercise. Patients are normal to overweight in contrast to the low weight seen in those with anorexia nervosa.

title: Alcohol withdrawal syndrome may present with tremors, insomnia, restlessness, gastrointestinal upset, headache, diaphoresis, tachycardia
body: Alcohol withdrawal syndrome may present with tremors, insomnia, restlessness, gastrointestinal upset, headache, diaphoresis, tachycardia, and hypertension, as well as generalized seizures and delirium tremens. In the emergency setting, lorazepam is the preferred agent for treatment of the emerging withdrawal syndrome.

title: Management of chronic fatigue syndrome includes excluding other medical and psychiatric causes of fatigue followed by referral for cognitive-behavioral therapy and graded exercise therapy.
In milder forms of autism spectrum disorder, delayed diagnosis into adulthood is common
body: In milder forms of autism spectrum disorder, delayed diagnosis into adulthood is common. Characteristic features of the disorder include impaired social communication and reciprocal social interactions, restricted interests, and behavioral rigidity.

title: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often persists into adulthood
body: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often persists into adulthood. Compared to children, adults with ADHD are less overtly hyperactive but experience chronic problems with distractibility, disorganization, and impulsivity that cause significant social and occupational impairment.

title: Caregiver distress can result in poor physical health and sleep and mood disturbances, as well as early nursing home placement for
body: Caregiver distress can result in poor physical health and sleep and mood disturbances, as well as early nursing home placement for relatives with dementia. Support services (eg, respite care, support groups and programs) can help reduce caregiver burden.

title: Depressed patients with an inadequate response to a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor should have their dose increased within the
body: Depressed patients with an inadequate response to a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor should have their dose increased within the therapeutic range. Switching to an alternate antidepressant or augmenting with another class of antidepressant can be considered for patients who fail to respond to a maximally tolerated dose.

title: Varenicline is an effective treatment for smoking cessation
body: Varenicline is an effective treatment for smoking cessation. Despite initial concerns about adverse neuropsychiatric symptoms, varenicline does not appear to increase the risk of suicide or depression in patients with past psychiatric symptoms. Although adverse cardiovascular events (eg, myocardial ischemia, arrhythmia) are possible, the risks are thought to be less than those from continued smoking.

title: The initial behavioral approaches to insomnia consist of sleep hygiene and stimulus control therapy
body: The initial behavioral approaches to insomnia consist of sleep hygiene and stimulus control therapy. With stimulus control, patients learn to reassociate the bedroom environment with restful sleep by using the bedroom only for sleep or sexual activity and going to bed only when sleepy.

title: Mirtazapine is a first-line antidepressant choice for depressed elderly patients with insomnia, anxiety, and weight loss.
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors combined with trauma-focused cognitive-behavioral
body: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors combined with trauma-focused cognitive-behavioral therapy are the first-line treatment for patients with post-traumatic stress disorder.

title: Drug side effect profiles and specific depressive symptoms can help guide initial antidepressant medication selection
body: Drug side effect profiles and specific depressive symptoms can help guide initial antidepressant medication selection. Bupropion, a norepinephrine dopamine reuptake inhibitor, is a first-line treatment for major depressive disorder that is associated with less weight gain and fewer sexual side effects compared with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

title: Erectile dysfunction can be due to multiple etiologies, including vascular, neurologic, hormonal, and psychological abnormalities
body: Erectile dysfunction can be due to multiple etiologies, including vascular, neurologic, hormonal, and psychological abnormalities. Psychogenic causes should be suspected if erectile dysfunction has a sudden onset and the patient is able to have early morning and nocturnal erections during REM sleep.

title: Initial evaluation of patients with chronic insomnia requires a detailed sleep history to clarify sleep patterns and identify contributing
body: Initial evaluation of patients with chronic insomnia requires a detailed sleep history to clarify sleep patterns and identify contributing factors (eg, substances, psychosocial stressors, environmental issues). A 2-week sleep diary is a useful assessment tool that can help confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment interventions.

title: Jet lag usually occurs after crossing several time zones with sleep disturbances, daytime fatigue, reduced performance, malaise, and
body: Jet lag usually occurs after crossing several time zones with sleep disturbances, daytime fatigue, reduced performance, malaise, and gastrointestinal symptoms (eg, constipation). Behavioral modifications and melatonin are effective initial treatments with few side effects.

title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors are first-line medications for generalized anxiety
body: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors are first-line medications for generalized anxiety disorder. Benzodiazepines are used as second-line therapy and should be limited to nondepressed patients without a history of substance abuse who fail to respond to or cannot tolerate antidepressants.

title: Acute stress disorder (ASD) develops within 4 weeks of a traumatic event and is characterized by intrusive re-experiencing of the traumatic
body: Acute stress disorder (ASD) develops within 4 weeks of a traumatic event and is characterized by intrusive re-experiencing of the traumatic event, hyperarousal, and avoidance behaviors. Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the first-line treatment for ASD and decreases the risk of development of post-traumatic stress disorder.

title: A single-item screening that asks patients how many times in the past year they have had 5 (4 for women) or more drinks in a day is an
body: A single-item screening that asks patients how many times in the past year they have had 5 (4 for women) or more drinks in a day is an effective tool to identify unhealthy alcohol use prior to asking further questions. The AUDIT-C is another widely validated instrument for assessment of alcohol use.

title: Akathisia is a common extrapyramidal symptom caused by antipsychotic medication and is characterized by inner restlessness, difficulty
body: Akathisia is a common extrapyramidal symptom caused by antipsychotic medication and is characterized by inner restlessness, difficulty sitting still, and an urge to move. It may be mistaken for psychotic agitation. Management includes antipsychotic dose reduction if feasible and treatment with beta blockers or benzodiazepines.

title: First-line treatment for anorexia nervosa consists of nutritional rehabilitation and psychotherapy
body: First-line treatment for anorexia nervosa consists of nutritional rehabilitation and psychotherapy. Adjunctive pharmacotherapy is indicated for treatment-resistant patients who do not respond to psychological interventions.

title: All veterans, especially those reporting new-onset insomnia, anxiety, and substance use, should be screened for post-traumatic stress disorder.
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are first-line treatment for pregnant patients with moderate to severe major depression or those
body: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are first-line treatment for pregnant patients with moderate to severe major depression or those who do not respond to psychotherapy alone. Physicians should discuss the risks and benefits of antidepressant treatment and untreated depression with patients to facilitate their decision-making.

title: Sexual dysfunction is a common side effect of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)
body: Sexual dysfunction is a common side effect of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs). In SSRI responders, augmentation with a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor (eg, sildenafil) or bupropion can be beneficial. SSRI nonresponders are best managed by switching to a non-SSRI antidepressant (eg, bupropion, mirtazapine) for lower rates of treatment-related sexual dysfunction.

title: Pharmacotherapy is appropriate for patients with moderate to severe alcohol use disorder
body: Pharmacotherapy is appropriate for patients with moderate to severe alcohol use disorder. Naltrexone is a first-line treatment that decreases cravings and heavy drinking; it can be initiated in patients who are still drinking provided they do not take opioids and have no significant liver disease.

title: Psychotherapy, particularly dialectical behavioral therapy, is the first-line treatment for borderline personality disorder.
Tardive dyskinesia (TD) is a movement disorder due to prolonged exposure to dopamine receptor blockers (eg, antipsychotics, metoclopramide)
body: Tardive dyskinesia (TD) is a movement disorder due to prolonged exposure to dopamine receptor blockers (eg, antipsychotics, metoclopramide). Metoclopramide should be discontinued if TD develops. In cases of antipsychotic-induced TD when discontinuation is not feasible, options include switching to a second- generation antipsychotic or adding valbenazine.

title: Postpartum patients with sleep disturbance and fatigue should be carefully assessed for other depressive symptoms (eg, anhedonia, appetite
body: Postpartum patients with sleep disturbance and fatigue should be carefully assessed for other depressive symptoms (eg, anhedonia, appetite disturbance, impaired concentration, feelings of worthlessness, suicidal ideation). Postpartum depression negatively impacts both maternal and infant well-being and should be treated with psychotherapy and/or antidepressants.

title: Patients with a first episode of major depressive disorder should continue antidepressants for an additional 6 months following acute
body: Patients with a first episode of major depressive disorder should continue antidepressants for an additional 6 months following acute response to reduce the risk of relapse. Maintenance treatment (1-3 years or indefinitely) should be considered for patients with recurrent, severe/chronic episodes.

title: Patients should be routinely screened for intimate partner violence. The presence of chronic somatic symptoms and poorly explained injuries should raise particular concern.
The mainstay Oftreatment for anorexia nervosa is nutritional rehabilitation plus psychotherapy. In treatment-resistant cases, olanzapine can be used as an adjunct to help accelerate weight gain.
Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (eg, duloxetine) possess analgesic properties that make them a preferred choice in patients
body: Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (eg, duloxetine) possess analgesic properties that make them a preferred choice in patients with comorbid depression and chronic pain, including painful diabetic neuropathy.

title: First-line treatment of somatic symptom disorder consists of regularly scheduled follow-up visits together with psychotherapy and/or
body: First-line treatment of somatic symptom disorder consists of regularly scheduled follow-up visits together with psychotherapy and/or antidepressants. Among psychotherapies, cognitive-behavioral therapy has the best evidence.

title: Panic disorder involves recurrent, unexpected anxiety attacks characterized by abrupt onset, short duration, and prominent physical
body: Panic disorder involves recurrent, unexpected anxiety attacks characterized by abrupt onset, short duration, and prominent physical symptoms. Diagnosis requires ruling out medical and substance-induced causes as well as other psychiatric disorders that can include infrequent, Situationally triggered panic attacks.

title: Elderly white men have the highest rate of completed suicide
body: Elderly white men have the highest rate of completed suicide. Risk factors include loss of a spouse, feeling depressed or hopeless, and physical illness. There should be a low threshold for suicide screening in this population and emergency psychiatric follow-up if necessary.

title: Tension pneumothorax should be suspected in a patient with hemodynamic instability and iatrogenic risk factors for pneumothorax (eg
body: Tension pneumothorax should be suspected in a patient with hemodynamic instability and iatrogenic risk factors for pneumothorax (eg, central-line placement). Urgent decompression of the pleural space with needle thoracostomy or chest tube placement is required.

title: Massive hemoptysis is a life-threatening emergency caused most frequently by bronchiectasis, aspergilloma, necrotizing pneumonia, and
body: Massive hemoptysis is a life-threatening emergency caused most frequently by bronchiectasis, aspergilloma, necrotizing pneumonia, and, rarely, bronchogenic carcinoma. Initial management includes airway protection and resuscitation. Rigid bronchoscopy is the procedure of choice, if a skilled physician is readily available.

title: Light's criteria can distinguish between transudative and exudative pleural effusion
body: Light's criteria can distinguish between transudative and exudative pleural effusion. However, a transudative effusion related to congestive heart failure may meet criteria for an exudative effusion after diuresis. Further differentiation may be necessary with either serum-effusion albumin gradient or serum­ effusion protein difference.

title: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis typically occurs in the setting of a severely immunocompromised state
body: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis typically occurs in the setting of a severely immunocompromised state. Patients commonly have fever, pleuritic chest pain, and hemoptysis; imaging often reveals nodular disease with ground-glass opacities or cavitary lesions with air fluid levels. Diagnosis is usually made with sputum fungal stain and culture and serum fungal biomarkers (eg, galactomannan, beta-D-glucan). A positive serum galactomannan assay has a specificity >75%.

title: Unexplained or prolonged chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation may be due to pneumonia, heart failure, or pulmonary embolism
body: Unexplained or prolonged chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation may be due to pneumonia, heart failure, or pulmonary embolism (PE). A high index of clinical suspicion with modified Wells criteria can help in recognizing PE and determining its probability. CT pulmonary angiogram is the imaging modality of choice in those with a high clinical probability.

title: Fat embolization syndrome (FES) occurs as a complication of long-bone fractures and presents with the classic triad of respiratory
body: Fat embolization syndrome (FES) occurs as a complication of long-bone fractures and presents with the classic triad of respiratory distress, neurologic abnormalities, and a petechial rash 24-72 hours after the traumatic insult. Prevention of FES includes early immobilization Offractures and operative correction. Treatment is supportive.

title: Right endobronchial intubation is a frequent complication of endotracheal (ET) tube placement
body: Right endobronchial intubation is a frequent complication of endotracheal (ET) tube placement. If endobronchial intubation is suspected based on physical examination (asymmetric breath sounds and chest rise) and failure of oxygenation, the ET tube should be retracted and then a chest x-ray or ultrasound should be performed to confirm proper placement.

title: Churg-Strauss syndrome can mimic other systemic vasculitis syndromes (e.g., granulomatosis with polyangiitis) with common features such as
body: Churg-Strauss syndrome can mimic other systemic vasculitis syndromes (e.g., granulomatosis with polyangiitis) with common features such as renal involvement (glomerulonephritis), mononeuritis multiplex, and upper airway disease (e.g., sinus, ear, nose, and throat involvement). It is associated with asthma and severe peripheral eosinophilia, which is usually not seen in other vasculitis syndromes.

title: Patients hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia should be started on intravenous antibiotics
body: Patients hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia should be started on intravenous antibiotics. A switch to oral therapy may be considered when the patient is improving clinically, Inemodynamically stable, and able to take oral medications (functioning Gl tract). Seven days of oral therapy is clinically as effective as longer courses of oral therapy or 7 days of intravenous therapy. Bacteremia may help identify the pathogen and direct therapy, but it does not affect the duration of oral therapy

title: Lung abscess occurs in individuals with a predisposition to aspiration
body: Lung abscess occurs in individuals with a predisposition to aspiration. It typically has an indolent presentation with fever, night sweats, weight loss, and cough with foul-smelling sputum. Chest x-ray generally reveals a cavitary lesion with an associated air-fluid level. First-line treatment is ampicillin- sulbactam or a carbapenem.

title: In the setting of high pretest probability for acute pulmonary embolism, a low-probability or intermediate­ probability
body: In the setting of high pretest probability for acute pulmonary embolism, a low-probability or intermediate­ probability ventilation-perfusion scan result is nondiagnostic. In patients with elevated bleeding risk, additional testing (eg, lower-extremity ultrasound) is indicated following such a result to further aid the risk/benefit analysis of long-term anticoagulation.

title: Intraosseous cannulation can provide rapid intravascular access in patients with severe shock and cardiopulmonary arrest when intravenous access cannot be readily obtained.
Thoracentesis should be performed on suspected parapneumonic pleural effusions in the setting of pneumonia
body: Thoracentesis should be performed on suspected parapneumonic pleural effusions in the setting of pneumonia. Parapneumonic effusions range from uncomplicated to empyema based on pleural fluid analysis. Uncomplicated effusions typically resolve with antibiotic therapy for pneumonia, while complicated effusions and empyema require chest tube drainage and antibiotics. Surgery is reserved for individuals who fail to respond to drainage and antibiotics.

title: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease usually presents with the classic triad of nasal polyposis, asthma, and aspirin (or NSAID)
body: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease usually presents with the classic triad of nasal polyposis, asthma, and aspirin (or NSAID) sensitivity. The reaction is not an IgE-mediated allergic response but is likely a shift in the arachidonic acid metabolic pathway causing excessive leukotriene production. These patients should be treated with leukotriene antagonists and optimal asthma management.

title: Initial treatment of moderate hypothermia includes supportive care, active and passive external rewarming, and warmed intravenous fluids to maintain blood pressure and circulation.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patients have a chronic respiratory acidosis with an increased baseline pCO2
body: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patients have a chronic respiratory acidosis with an increased baseline pCO2. If present for more than 4-5 days, the kidney will retain 4 mEq/L of bicarbonate for each 10 mm Hg increase in pCO2. COPD exacerbation causes a significant drop in the serum pH with a slight increase in serum bicarbonate. Deviations from this "rule of thumb" suggest the presence of an additional acid-base disorder.

title: Inhaled short-acting beta-2 selective adrenergic agonists and systemic corticosteroids are the mainstay for emergency department treatment
body: Inhaled short-acting beta-2 selective adrenergic agonists and systemic corticosteroids are the mainstay for emergency department treatment of an acute asthma attack. Patients should be discharged with a prescription for a short course of oral steroids and an inhaled corticosteroid to prevent recurrent asthma attacks following discontinuation of oral steroids.

title: Pleurisy is inflammation of the lung pleura, which can cause severe pain with movement (eg, deep breathing, coughing)
body: Pleurisy is inflammation of the lung pleura, which can cause severe pain with movement (eg, deep breathing, coughing). Viral pleuritis is a common cause and may present with or without an initial viral prodrome. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (eg, indomethacin) effectively treat the pain and pleural inflammation.

title: Anaphylaxis can present with relatively mild manifestations but progress to life-threatening disease
body: Anaphylaxis can present with relatively mild manifestations but progress to life-threatening disease. Skin findings, respiratory compromise, hypotension, or gastrointestinal symptoms after exposure to an allergen suggest anaphylaxis. Intramuscular epinephrine is recommended for all patients with features of anaphylaxis.

title: Severity of illness scores, such as the CURB-65 criteria, help determine the initial site of care for patients with community-acquired
body: Severity of illness scores, such as the CURB-65 criteria, help determine the initial site of care for patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). In patients without comorbid conditions, a macrolide or doxycycline is sufficient for outpatient CAP therapy. The presence of comorbid conditions (eg, diabetes) or other risk factors for drug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae or a history of antimicrobials within the past 3 months requires the use of a respiratory fluoroquinolone or a β-lactam with activity against S pneumoniae plus a macrolide.

title: Methemoglobinemia should be suspected when there is cyanosis with a normal arterial PaO2, “dark chocolate” blood that does not change color
body: Methemoglobinemia should be suspected when there is cyanosis with a normal arterial PaO2, “dark chocolate” blood that does not change color on oxygenation, or the presence of a saturation gap. The most common offending agent(s) are local anesthetics. Symptomatic patients or those with a methemoglobin level >20% require prompt administration of methylene blue. Those in shock may also require blood transfusion or exchange transfusion.

title: Early enteral nutrition is an important aspect of care for critically ill patients but should be withheld in those who are severely hemodynamically unstable with decreased intravascular volume.
Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with hypoxemia (PaO2∕FiO2 <300 mm Hg) and bilateral alveolar infiltrates
body: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with hypoxemia (PaO2∕FiO2 <300 mm Hg) and bilateral alveolar infiltrates. Ventilation with low tidal volumes (6 mL/kg of ideal body weight) improves mortality. Objective assessment (eg, echocardiography) is needed to definitively exclude hydrostatic pulmonary edema in patients without ARDS risk factors.

title: Patients with acute lung injury and adequate perfusion should receive conservative fluid management that targets a CVP of < 4 mm Hg or a
body: Patients with acute lung injury and adequate perfusion should receive conservative fluid management that targets a CVP of < 4 mm Hg or a pulmonary artery occlusion pressure of < 8 mm Hg. Although this target is difficult to achieve, conservative fluid management results in improved oxygenation index and more ventilator-free days.

title: Hyperglycemia in critically ill ICU patients is associated with poor outcomes
body: Hyperglycemia in critically ill ICU patients is associated with poor outcomes. Glucose levels of 140-180 mg/dL are currently recommended to avoid extremes of hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia, and are only achievable with insulin infusions and frequent glucose checks.

title: Patients with moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations should undergo a trial of noninvasive
body: Patients with moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations should undergo a trial of noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation (NPPV). However, patients with any NPPV contraindication or who cannot tolerate or fail to respond to NPPV within 2 hours should be intubated and undergo invasive mechanical ventilation.

title: Noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation in cardiogenic pulmonary edema patients enhances oxygenation via improvements in respiratory
body: Noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation in cardiogenic pulmonary edema patients enhances oxygenation via improvements in respiratory Qdead space ventilation, ↑tidal volume, ↑alveolar∕minute ventilation) and cardiac indices Qpreload, jafterload).

title: The 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine is recommended for all adults age >65 followed by the 23- valent pneumococcal polysaccharide
body: The 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine is recommended for all adults age >65 followed by the 23- valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine at least 12 months later. Administration of pneumococcal and inactivated influenza vaccinations to individuals age >65 with chronic illness improves survival and reduces the occurrence of infectious and vascular events.

title: Management of moderate to severe exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease includes standard therapy (eg, inhaled β-agonists
body: Management of moderate to severe exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease includes standard therapy (eg, inhaled β-agonists, inhaled anticholinergics, steroids, and possibly antibiotics) and a trial of noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation unless contraindicated.

title: Extubating to noninvasive ventilation may decrease recurrent respiratory failure, invasive ventilation time, and mortality in patients with
body: Extubating to noninvasive ventilation may decrease recurrent respiratory failure, invasive ventilation time, and mortality in patients with underlying lung disease (eg, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and compensated hypercapnia who are recovering from acute respiratory failure.

title: Auto-positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) is caused by air remaining in the lungs due to incomplete expiration in mechanically
body: Auto-positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) is caused by air remaining in the lungs due to incomplete expiration in mechanically ventilated patients. Strategies for correcting auto-PEEP include reducing minute ventilation, increasing expiratory time, and giving medications to treat airway obstruction.

title: Critical illness myopathy (CIM) should be considered in any critically ill patient who develops generalized weakness or difficulty weaning
body: Critical illness myopathy (CIM) should be considered in any critically ill patient who develops generalized weakness or difficulty weaning from the ventilator. The strongest risk factor for CIM is the use of intravenous glucocorticoids. Therapy involves avoidance of glucocorticoids and rehabilitation, and prognosis is generally favorable.

title: Growth of Candida from respiratory secretions rarely indicates invasive candidiasis and should not be treated with antifungal therapy.
Risk for central line-associated bloodstream infections increases the longer a catheter remains in place
body: Risk for central line-associated bloodstream infections increases the longer a catheter remains in place. Critically ill patients should be assessed daily for the need for continued central venous access.

title: Important causes Ofdistress (e.g., pain, respiratory insufficiency) in intubated patients must be identified and treated prior to the
body: Important causes Ofdistress (e.g., pain, respiratory insufficiency) in intubated patients must be identified and treated prior to the administration of sedatives. Pain should be suspected in critically ill patients if pain- related behaviors (e.g., grimacing, agitation, writhing) or signs of sympathetic activation (e.g., tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypertension) are present. Postoperative hypertension can often be due to inadequate pain control or failure to restart home antihypertensive agents.

title: A sudden rise in end-tidal CO2 is the earliest indicator of return of spontaneous circulation in patients in cardiac arrest undergoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation. ■ >3 End ® Resources
Protocolized sedation refers to the use of a sedation algorithm or daily sedation interruption. It has been shown to reduce duration of mechanical ventilation and length of intensive care unit stay.
Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI) should be considered in patients with acute onset dyspnea, hypoxemia, and pulmonary
body: Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI) should be considered in patients with acute onset dyspnea, hypoxemia, and pulmonary infiltrates that occur during or within 6 hours after transfusion of any plasma containing blood product. Treatment involves mainly supportive care, stopping the transfusion, and vasopressor support for hypotension. The blood bank should be notified and the blood donor investigated to prevent future incidents in other recipients.

title: Patients in septic shock who do not respond to fluid resuscitation require vasopressors to improve their poor systemic vascular resistance
body: Patients in septic shock who do not respond to fluid resuscitation require vasopressors to improve their poor systemic vascular resistance. Norepinephrine is the preferred vasopressor agent for septic shock.

title: The incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) can be decreased with Semirecumbent positioning, oral antiseptics, and avoiding
body: The incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) can be decreased with Semirecumbent positioning, oral antiseptics, and avoiding proton pump inhibitors and histamine receptor-blocking agents. Routine antibiotic prophylaxis for VAP is not recommended due to development of drug-resistant organisms.

title: Increasing PEEP improves oxygenation by recruiting flooded and collapsed alveoli, and is first-line therapy in ARDS patients with severe hypoxemia.
Free-flowing effusions ≤10 mm usually resolve with antibiotic therapy alone
body: Free-flowing effusions ≤10 mm usually resolve with antibiotic therapy alone. Larger effusions should be imaged with ultrasound and/or CT Effusions without high-risk features (Ioculation, >⅓ hemithorax, pleural thickening) should undergo diagnostic thoracentesis. Effusions with high-risk features or pH <7.2, glucose <60 mg/dL, or positive Gram stain/culture should be drained.

title: The rapid shallow breathing index is calculated using the respiratory rate divided by the tidal volume in liters and is a predictor of successful extubation if < 105.
Proper positioning of the endotracheal tube can be confirmed by auscultation, observation, and insertion depth. A chest radiograph is required to confirm placement.
Peak and plateau pressures are derived from the ventilator according to the different clinical states of the airway, lung, and chest wall
body: Peak and plateau pressures are derived from the ventilator according to the different clinical states of the airway, lung, and chest wall. Peak pressures, also known as dynamic pressures, measure the resistance to flow of air delivered from the ventilator and the amount of pressure needed to inflate the lung. Plateau pressures are static lung pressures, measured during an inspiratory hold, that give an estimate of lung compliance.

title: A massive pulmonary embolism (PE) usually presents with acute dyspnea and hypotension, with systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a drop in
body: A massive pulmonary embolism (PE) usually presents with acute dyspnea and hypotension, with systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a drop in systolic blood pressure of >40 mm Hg from baseline for > 15 minutes. Critically ill and hemodynamically unstable patients should first have a bedside TTE to look for RV dysfunction, with immediate thrombolytics given for positive results.

title: Mechanical ventilation in assist control mode is usually initiated with a respiratory rate of 14-18 breaths per minute, tidal volume of
body: Mechanical ventilation in assist control mode is usually initiated with a respiratory rate of 14-18 breaths per minute, tidal volume of 8-10 mL/kg of ideal body weight, the lowest possible FiO2 to meet respiratory goals, and PEEP of 5 cm H2O. Chest x-ray is performed to confirm endotracheal tube placement and an ABG is done to monitor for acid base disturbances. Ventilator settings can be adjusted to correct acid base disturbances.

title: Patients in respiratory failure after extubation should be reintubated immediately. Patients with COPD may benefit from a trial of noninvasive ventilation.
Patients with cirrhosis can have chronic respiratory alkalosis due to increased minute ventilation
body: Patients with cirrhosis can have chronic respiratory alkalosis due to increased minute ventilation. The cause is unknown but may be the result of the hormonal effects of increased progesterone and estrogen or possibly due to hepatopulmonary syndrome in some patients.

title: The intermittent use of noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation in patients with chronic respiratory failure from chest wall disease has
body: The intermittent use of noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation in patients with chronic respiratory failure from chest wall disease has been shown to improve dyspnea, sleep disturbances, and mortality. It also may partially reverse cor pulmonale.

title: Unilateral diaphragmatic paralysis occurs rarely due to phrenic nerve injury after cardiac surgery
body: Unilateral diaphragmatic paralysis occurs rarely due to phrenic nerve injury after cardiac surgery. Patients may present with dyspnea at rest or with exertion and supine hypoxemia. Spirometry shows a drop in forced vital capacity in the supine position, and chest x-ray reveals elevated hemidiaphragm. Diagnosis is confirmed via the "sniff test" using fluoroscopy.

title: Patients with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease may be considered for hospice care when they have disabling dyspnea at rest, progression to end-stage disease, hypoxemia, or hypercapnia.
Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is associated with pulmonary hypertension and interstitial lung disease
body: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is associated with pulmonary hypertension and interstitial lung disease. Restrictive lung diseases such as SSc-associated pulmonary fibrosis show reduced FEV1, FVC, TLC, and DLCO with a normal FEV1∕FVC ratio.

title: Kyphoscoliosis causes a progressive decline in chest wall compliance, resulting in a restrictive defect
body: Kyphoscoliosis causes a progressive decline in chest wall compliance, resulting in a restrictive defect. The respiratory rate increases to compensate for low tidal volume ventilation. Younger patients may undergo surgical correction. Supportive therapy includes pulmonary rehabilitation and noninvasive positive pressure ventilation.

title: Ventilator-induced lung injury is a major cause of mortality and morbidity in acute respiratory distress syndrome
body: Ventilator-induced lung injury is a major cause of mortality and morbidity in acute respiratory distress syndrome. Injury can be avoided by using low tidal volume ventilation (4-6 mL/kg of ideal body weight) and maintaining a plateau pressure of ≤30 cm H2O. The resulting hypercapnia is permissible as long as pH is ≥7.20 and the patient lacks contraindications.

title: Rapid eye movement (REM) behavior disorder (RBD) is a sleep disorder characterized by loss of REM atonia, which precipitates the acting out
body: Rapid eye movement (REM) behavior disorder (RBD) is a sleep disorder characterized by loss of REM atonia, which precipitates the acting out of dreams during sleep. RBD is highly associated with the later development of neurodegenerative disease, particularly Parkinson disease and dementia with Lewy bodies.

title: Snoring indicates upper airway resistance, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) should be investigated in patients with obesity, OSA risk
body: Snoring indicates upper airway resistance, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) should be investigated in patients with obesity, OSA risk factors, and mission-critical occupations. Suspected OSA patients should have full-night, attended polysomnography (PSG) to confirm diagnosis and assess disease severity. Initial treatment includes behavior modification and a positive airway pressure device.

title: Chronic eosinophilic pneumonia is characterized by respiratory symptoms, eosinophilia (peripherally and > 25% on bronchoalveolar lavage)
body: Chronic eosinophilic pneumonia is characterized by respiratory symptoms, eosinophilia (peripherally and > 25% on bronchoalveolar lavage), and peripheral pulmonary infiltrates on chest imaging. Unlike acute eosinophilic pneumonia, onset of symptoms is gradual and respiratory failure is rare. Both types of eosinophilic pneumonias respond dramatically to glucocorticoids.

title: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome is defined as daytime hypercapnia and hypoxemia (PaCO2 > 45 mm Hg and PaO2 < 70 mm Hg) in an obese patient
body: Obesity hypoventilation syndrome is defined as daytime hypercapnia and hypoxemia (PaCO2 > 45 mm Hg and PaO2 < 70 mm Hg) in an obese patient (BMI > 30 kg∕ιτr) in the absence of any other cause of hypoventilation. Arterial blood gas analysis identifies alveolar hypoventilation and should be obtained in any patient with morbid obesity and unexplained hypoxemia or signs and symptoms of cor pulmonale.

title: Alpha-1 antitrypsin levels should be tested in all patients with new-onset obstructive pulmonary disease, but early-onset emphysema (age
body: Alpha-1 antitrypsin levels should be tested in all patients with new-onset obstructive pulmonary disease, but early-onset emphysema (age ≤45 years), emphysema with minimal smoking history, or unexplained liver disease are particularly suggestive. Deficiency typically results in early-onset, basilar emphysema, liver disease, and, occasionally, panniculitis.

title: Obstructive sleep apnea is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity, including cardiac arrhythmias
body: Obstructive sleep apnea is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity, including cardiac arrhythmias. Treatment with continuous positive airway pressure helps to improve symptoms and cardiovascular complications.

title: Patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and pulse oximetry >95% on room air can travel by air without the need for
body: Patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and pulse oximetry >95% on room air can travel by air without the need for additional testing or in-flight oxygen supplementation. Further testing is required for patients with pulse oximetry (SpO2) of 92%-95% and risk factors (eg, forced expiratory volume in 1 second <50%, moderate to severe pulmonary hypertension). The preferred method is hypoxia altitude simulation test. Supplemental oxygen is recommended during flights for patients with resting SpO2 <92%.

title: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is a hypersensitivity reaction to Aspergillus that occurs in the airways of patients with asthma
body: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is a hypersensitivity reaction to Aspergillus that occurs in the airways of patients with asthma and cystic fibrosis. It presents with worsening asthma symptoms, fevers, fleeting infiltrates, pleuritic chest pain, and peripheral eosinophilia. The first step in diagnosis is Aspergillus skin testing. If left untreated, the disorder can result in bronchiectasis with a poor prognosis.

title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), formerly known as Wegener granulomatosis, is characterized by the triad of upper airway disease
body: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), formerly known as Wegener granulomatosis, is characterized by the triad of upper airway disease, lower respiratory tract disease, and glomerulonephritis. The entire triad may not be present initially. Lung involvement can lead to lung nodules, pulmonary cavitations, infiltrates, or pleural effusion detected on chest x-ray.

title: Restrictive pattern PFTs Occurwith interstitial lung disease, conditions that cause restriction of the chest wall, and neuromuscular
body: Restrictive pattern PFTs Occurwith interstitial lung disease, conditions that cause restriction of the chest wall, and neuromuscular disorders. Obesity with hypoventilation typically presents with a low FEV1 and a normal FEV1∕FVC ratio.

title: Pulmonary hypertension may present with nonspecific symptoms such as dyspnea, lethargy, or fatigue
body: Pulmonary hypertension may present with nonspecific symptoms such as dyspnea, lethargy, or fatigue. Pulmonary function tests in primary pulmonary hypertension are usually normal or mildly abnormal with decreased diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide.

title: V/Q scanning is superior to CT pulmonary angiogram in diagnosing chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH)
body: V/Q scanning is superior to CT pulmonary angiogram in diagnosing chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). All patients should receive lifelong anticoagulation with a target INR of 2.0 to 3.0 and an early referral for surgical thromboendarterectomy.

title: Asthma can lead to adverse outcomes in pregnancy unless it is effectively managed
body: Asthma can lead to adverse outcomes in pregnancy unless it is effectively managed. Although there are risks to giving medication during pregnancy, these risks are outweighed by the danger of uncontrolled asthma.

title: Improper use of inhaled devices decreases drug delivery, patient adherence to treatment regimen, and drug effectiveness, leading to
body: Improper use of inhaled devices decreases drug delivery, patient adherence to treatment regimen, and drug effectiveness, leading to uncontrolled asthma and multiple emergency department visits. Improper use is an often overlooked cause of asthma therapy failure.

title: Patients receiving thoracic or neck irradiation are at risk for acute radiation pneumonitis, which usually presents with
body: Patients receiving thoracic or neck irradiation are at risk for acute radiation pneumonitis, which usually presents with antibiotic-nonresponsive pneumonia 4-12 weeks after radiation exposure. Treatment for acute disease includes prednisone for 2 weeks followed by a gradual taper over 3-12 weeks.

title: Paradoxical vocal fold motion describes partial airway obstruction due to abnormal closure of the true vocal cords during inspiration
body: Paradoxical vocal fold motion describes partial airway obstruction due to abnormal closure of the true vocal cords during inspiration. Diagnosis is confirmed by flow-volume loop showing variable extrathoracic airway obstruction and laryngoscopy revealing inspiratory adduction of the vocal cords. Treatment involves supportive care during acute episodes and speech therapy/counseling for long-term care.

title: Reactive airway dysfunction syndrome is a nonimmune asthma-like illness that occurs after a single high- level exposure to a pulmonary
body: Reactive airway dysfunction syndrome is a nonimmune asthma-like illness that occurs after a single high- level exposure to a pulmonary irritant. Pulmonary function testing may show obstruction, and methacholine challenge testing can establish the diagnosis.

title: Fixed upper airway obstruction limits airflow in both inhalation and exhalation
body: Fixed upper airway obstruction limits airflow in both inhalation and exhalation. Extrathoracic dynamic obstruction causes blunting of the flow-volume loop during inhalation (airway "tugged in"). Intrathoracic dynamic obstruction limits airflow during exhalation (compression from increased intrathoracic pressure).

title: Patients with high resolution chest CT findings suggestive of bronchiectasis should undergo functional assessment with pulmonary function
body: Patients with high resolution chest CT findings suggestive of bronchiectasis should undergo functional assessment with pulmonary function testing and identification of potentially reversible causes. Initial diagnostic evaluation includes a complete blood count with differential, immunoglobulin quantitation (i.e., IgA, IgG, and IgM), and sputum culture and smear (bacteria, fungi, and mycobacteria).

title: Wheezing is most commonly due to obstructive lung diseases such as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
body: Wheezing is most commonly due to obstructive lung diseases such as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. However, there are other causes of wheezing, and spirometry is recommended in stable patients to confirm the diagnosis prior to initiation of therapy.

title: A short course of systemic corticosteroids is indicated for patients with moderate to severe asthma exacerbation or mild exacerbation
body: A short course of systemic corticosteroids is indicated for patients with moderate to severe asthma exacerbation or mild exacerbation unresponsive to bronchodilator therapy; it reduces the rates of short­ term relapse and hospitalization, as well as the need for beta agonist use. Prednisone 40-60 mg daily for 5-7 days is the recommended treatment regimen.

title: Mild-to-moderate pulmonary hypertension (PH) is commonly associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and confers a worse
body: Mild-to-moderate pulmonary hypertension (PH) is commonly associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and confers a worse prognosis. Specific pulmonary vasoactive medications have not been proven to relieve PH associated with COPD, and treatment should focus on corticosteroids, bronchodilators, and supplemental oxygen.

title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is characterized by progressive dyspnea, hypoxemia, and cough
body: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is characterized by progressive dyspnea, hypoxemia, and cough. Examination findings may include dry pulmonary crackles and digital clubbing. High-resolution CT scan may show honeycombing, cystic changes, and traction bronchiectasis. If CT is not diagnostic, lung biopsy may be needed.

title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease categorization usually guides optimal therapy
body: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease categorization usually guides optimal therapy. Patients with category B-D disease should undergo pulmonary rehabilitation to improve symptoms, exercise capacity, and quality of life.

title: Based on the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) guidelines, disease is categorized based on symptom burden and
body: Based on the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) guidelines, disease is categorized based on symptom burden and risk of exacerbation to determine appropriate management. Patients with GOLD category B disease (moderate-severe symptoms and <1 exacerbation a year) should be on a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (eg, tiotropium), in addition to an as-needed short-acting beta agonist (eg, albuterol).

title: Silicosis is usually due to occupational exposure and may present with chronic cough and dyspnea on exertion
body: Silicosis is usually due to occupational exposure and may present with chronic cough and dyspnea on exertion. Chest imaging reveals multiple micronodules, predominately in the upper lung fields. Silicosis is associated with an increased incidence of lung cancer and active tuberculosis, which should be screened for and appropriately treated at the time of diagnosis.

title: Irreversible airflow limitation in a chronic smoker with progressive dyspnea and chronic cough suggests chronic obstructive pulmonary
body: Irreversible airflow limitation in a chronic smoker with progressive dyspnea and chronic cough suggests chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide signifies emphysema.

title: Most patients with a first-time, provoked venous thromboembolism should be treated with 3 months of anticoagulation
body: Most patients with a first-time, provoked venous thromboembolism should be treated with 3 months of anticoagulation. Finite extension of the treatment period (eg, for a total of 6-12 months) is appropriate if the provoking factor is temporarily persistent (eg, prolonged immobility following leg surgery).

title: The diagnosis of sarcoidosis requires compatible clinical and radiologic manifestations, exclusion of other diseases with similar
body: The diagnosis of sarcoidosis requires compatible clinical and radiologic manifestations, exclusion of other diseases with similar presentation, and histopathologic evidence of noncaseating granulomas. Endobronchial ultrasound with nodal aspiration is the preferred initial method of mediastinal lymph node sampling in patients with suspected sarcoidosis.

title: The degree of reversibility of airway obstruction in response to bronchodilators best distinguishes asthma from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Presence of bronchial breath sounds, increased tactile fremitus, egophony or bronchophony, and dullness to percussion are suggestive of
body: Presence of bronchial breath sounds, increased tactile fremitus, egophony or bronchophony, and dullness to percussion are suggestive of lobar pneumonia. Although wheezing is most often associated with asthma, it can be present in other disorders such as congestive heart failure and infection.

title: Anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody disease (Goodpasture syndrome) commonly presents with progressive glomerulonephritis, renal
body: Anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody disease (Goodpasture syndrome) commonly presents with progressive glomerulonephritis, renal failure, and pulmonary hemorrhage. Systemic symptoms (eg, fever, weight loss, arthralgias, fatigue) are absent; their presence should raise suspicion for vasculitis.

title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is the most common type of interstitial lung disease
body: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is the most common type of interstitial lung disease. It typically presents with nonproductive cough and progressive shortness of breath, and may lead to pulmonary hypertension and right-sided heart failure. High-resolution chest CT scan is the preferred test for diagnosis.

title: Adding a long-acting β-agonist (LABA) is superior to doubling the inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) dose for improving asthma control and
body: Adding a long-acting β-agonist (LABA) is superior to doubling the inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) dose for improving asthma control and quality of life in patients with persistent asthma not effectively controlled with ICS alone.

title: Acute bronchitis is usually viral in origin and does not require antibiotics
body: Acute bronchitis is usually viral in origin and does not require antibiotics. Many patients develop a persistent cough due to bronchospasm with transient airway obstruction. Inhaled beta-2 adrenergic agonists can relieve the obstruction and provide symptomatic relief in those with significant symptoms.

title: Pleural effusion is a common manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis. The effusion is typically an exudate with a low pH, very low glucose level, and very high LDH level.
Outpatient therapy is an important management option for patients with deep vein thrombosis and should be considered for those who are
body: Outpatient therapy is an important management option for patients with deep vein thrombosis and should be considered for those who are hemodynamically stable with a low risk of bleeding, normal renal function, and stable social environment.

title: Repeated thoracentesis can detect up to 90% of malignant cells in high-risk patients
body: Repeated thoracentesis can detect up to 90% of malignant cells in high-risk patients. If there is still a suspicion of malignancy despite repeated negative thoracentesis, thoracoscopy should be performed.

title: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in pregnancy is associated with gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and preeclampsia
body: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in pregnancy is associated with gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and preeclampsia. Presenting symptoms of OSA are similar to those in nonpregnant patients (eg, snoring, excessive fatigue, daytime somnolence), and patients with such symptoms should be evaluated with overnight polysomnography.

title: A chylothorax is a rare effusion with a classic milky-white appearance that is caused by traumatic or non- traumatic thoracic duct
body: A chylothorax is a rare effusion with a classic milky-white appearance that is caused by traumatic or non- traumatic thoracic duct obstruction. Bulky Iymphadenopathy from lymphoma is an important etiology.

title: New-onset cough, especially when accompanied by weight loss, should raise suspicion for lung malignancy in patients with a significant
body: New-onset cough, especially when accompanied by weight loss, should raise suspicion for lung malignancy in patients with a significant smoking history. Such patients are best evaluated with CT scan of the chest (preferably with intravenous contrast) as x-ray cannot rule out lung malignancy in patients with a relatively high pretest probability of disease.

title: Adult cystic fibrosis (CF) patients usually present with chronic respiratory tract infections, unexplained upper lobe bronchiectasis
body: Adult cystic fibrosis (CF) patients usually present with chronic respiratory tract infections, unexplained upper lobe bronchiectasis, congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens, and/or pancreatitis. Nearly 7% of CF patients are diagnosed after 18 years of age, and sweat chloride test helps confirm CF in suspected patients. Patients with suspected CF and negative or equivocal tests should undergo further testing with DNA analysis and/or nasal potential difference measurement.

title: Solitary pulmonary nodules <0.6 cm are unlikely to be malignant, whereas those >0.8 cm require additional management or surveillance
body: Solitary pulmonary nodules <0.6 cm are unlikely to be malignant, whereas those >0.8 cm require additional management or surveillance. Nodules that are intermediate or high probability for malignancy (ie, ≥5% probability) based on clinical factors (eg, nodule size, patient age, smoking history) should be biopsied or surgically excised.

title: Pulmonary artery hypertension affects the small pulmonary arteries and capillaries
body: Pulmonary artery hypertension affects the small pulmonary arteries and capillaries. The resulting ventilation perfusion mismatch leads to a reduced diffusing capacity of carbon monoxide. Spirometry usually remains unaffected.

title: Asplenic patients are at increased risk of infection from encapsulated organisms and overwhelming infection
body: Asplenic patients are at increased risk of infection from encapsulated organisms and overwhelming infection. Any febrile illness in an asplenic patient should prompt aggressive antibiotic therapy and urgent diagnostic evaluation.

title: The management of obesity hypoventilation syndrome includes weight reduction, nocturnal positive­ pressure ventilation, and avoidance of
body: The management of obesity hypoventilation syndrome includes weight reduction, nocturnal positive­ pressure ventilation, and avoidance of sedative medications. Patients should be encouraged to lose weight, but positive-pressure ventilation should not be delayed while they attempt to do so.

title: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (extrinsic allergic alveolitis) is a form of interstitial lung disease that develops after allergen inhalation
body: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (extrinsic allergic alveolitis) is a form of interstitial lung disease that develops after allergen inhalation. It should be suspected in patients who have symptom onset due to specific antigen exposure and resolution of symptoms on cessation of exposure. Chest CT reveals ground-glass opacities. Diagnosis is confirmed with bronchoalveolar lavage and lung biopsy.

title: Narcolepsy is characterized by excessive daytime somnolence, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and low cerebrospinal fluid hypocretin-1 levels
body: Narcolepsy is characterized by excessive daytime somnolence, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and low cerebrospinal fluid hypocretin-1 levels. The diagnosis is confirmed with a multiple sleep latency test. First- line treatment for daytime somnolence is modafinil.

title: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is an immunologic pulmonary disorder caused by hypersensitivity to Aspergillus fumigatus
body: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is an immunologic pulmonary disorder caused by hypersensitivity to Aspergillus fumigatus. It often occurs in patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis. Patients present with recurrent episodes of low-grade fever, wheezing, bronchial hyperreactivity, productive cough, and hemoptysis. Diagnosis is made with a positive skin prick test followed by findings of elevated IgE and positive Aspergillus antibodies.

title: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) improve symptoms, lung function, and quality of life
body: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) improve symptoms, lung function, and quality of life. ICS also reduce frequency of exacerbations in patients with COPD with an FEV^ < 60% of predicted value. They should be used in conjunction with long-acting beta agonists. Major side effects are dysphonia, skin bruising, oral candidiasis, and slightly increased risk of pneumonia.

title: Drug therapy for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation includes glucocorticoids, bronchodilators, and antibiotics
body: Drug therapy for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation includes glucocorticoids, bronchodilators, and antibiotics. Antibiotics have proven benefit in severe COPD exacerbation, especially for patients requiring intensive care unit admission, but they are less likely to be of benefit for mild exacerbation.

title: Pulmonary rehabilitation is a multidisciplinary approach involving lower- and upper-extremity exercises to improve endurance/conditioning
body: Pulmonary rehabilitation is a multidisciplinary approach involving lower- and upper-extremity exercises to improve endurance/conditioning, breathing retraining to decrease breathing frequency, disease education/therapy, and psychosocial support. Pulmonary rehabilitation may improve exercise tolerance and health-related quality of life to decrease the number of hospitalizations or days in the hospital.

title: Long-term home oxygen therapy (LTOT) improves quality of life and prolongs survival in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
body: Long-term home oxygen therapy (LTOT) improves quality of life and prolongs survival in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and significant chronic hypoxemia. LTOT is indicated in those with resting PaO2 ≤55 mm Hg or oxygen saturation ≤88%, and in those with resting PaO2 ≤59 mm Hg or oxygen saturation ≤89% and comorbid cor pulmonale (right-sided heart failure) or erythrocytosis.

title: Dyspnea is a distressing symptom of end-stage chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and often remains undertreated
body: Dyspnea is a distressing symptom of end-stage chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and often remains undertreated. Opiates can blunt the uncomfortable sensation of dyspnea in patients with advanced lung disease. The concerns of potential respiratory depression with opiate use seem unwarranted.

title: Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction is a transient form of airway hyper-responsiveness that occurs during or after strenuous activity in
body: Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction is a transient form of airway hyper-responsiveness that occurs during or after strenuous activity in asthmatic and some nonasthmatic athletes. Primary treatment is a short­ acting beta-2 agonist administered 5-15 minutes prior to exercise. If symptoms persist, leukotriene receptor antagonists or inhaled corticosteroids (in case of poor asthma control) can be added to improve control.

title: Sarcoidosis may present in symptomatic patients with pulmonary symptoms, an abnormal chest x-ray, and erythema nodosum
body: Sarcoidosis may present in symptomatic patients with pulmonary symptoms, an abnormal chest x-ray, and erythema nodosum. Staging of pulmonary sarcoidosis is based on chest radiograph appearance. Stage III and IV patients do not have the classic bilateral hilar adenopathy. Diagnosis of sarcoidosis requires suggestive clinical and radiographic findings, exclusion Ofsimilarly presenting conditions, and tissue biopsy showing noncaseating granulomas.

title: Decompensated left ventricular diastolic dysfunction is a common cause of secondary pulmonary hypertension
body: Decompensated left ventricular diastolic dysfunction is a common cause of secondary pulmonary hypertension. Patients demonstrate normal left ventricular ejection fraction on echocardiogram, as well as elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure >25 mm Hg and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure >15 mm Hg on right heart catheterization. Diuresis to euvolemia is the most appropriate initial management.

title: OSA should be suspected in high-risk patients who complain of snoring or excessive daytime sleepiness
body: OSA should be suspected in high-risk patients who complain of snoring or excessive daytime sleepiness. Polysomnography is the preferred test to diagnose OSA and non-surgical therapy (weight loss and CPAP) is the mainstay of treatment.

title: Patients with high-risk characteristics, such as age >50 and smoking history (particularly in men), should be considered for a follow-up
body: Patients with high-risk characteristics, such as age >50 and smoking history (particularly in men), should be considered for a follow-up chest x-ray 7-12 weeks after pneumonia therapy to document pneumonia resolution and exclude underlying disease (eg, malignancy).

title: Most solitary pulmonary nodules are benign, infectious granulomas or hamartomas
