body: Most solitary pulmonary nodules are benign, infectious granulomas or hamartomas. Solid lesions that are stable on serial imaging over 2-3 years do not need further follow-up. In the absence of previous imaging, low-risk lesions and intermediate-risk lesions between 0.5-0.7 cm should be followed with serial CT imaging.

title: Benign asbestos-related pleural effusions are often exudative and bloody, with pleural fluid eosinophilia (>10% nucleated cells, frequently
body: Benign asbestos-related pleural effusions are often exudative and bloody, with pleural fluid eosinophilia (>10% nucleated cells, frequently >50%). They may be asymptomatic or cause pleuritic pain and dyspnea and are considered a marker for future development of asbestos-related pleural disease.

title: In patients with asthma, normal physiologic changes during sleep can lead to nocturnal asthma symptoms
body: In patients with asthma, normal physiologic changes during sleep can lead to nocturnal asthma symptoms. Comorbid illnesses (eg, gastroesophageal reflux disease, obstructive sleep apnea, upper airway cough syndrome) can mimic or contribute to nocturnal asthma symptoms and should also be considered. Uncontrolled asthma symptoms (eg, frequent nocturnal awakenings) should be treated with a step-up in asthma therapy.

title: Sniffing toluene-containing solvents can result in renal tubular acidosis with marked hypokalemia and hypophosphatemia. The resultant electrolyte disturbances can produce life-threatening weakness.
Patients with isopropyl alcohol ingestion have altered mental status, elevated osmolar gap, normal anion gap, and ketonuria/ketonemia. Treatment is mainly supportive.
Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) causes more serious side effects in HIV patients, particularly in hospitalized patients
body: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) causes more serious side effects in HIV patients, particularly in hospitalized patients. Hyperkalemia is the most common side effect, especially when given in high doses.

title: Hyponatremia is commonly seen after endurance athletic events and is due to ingestion of large amounts of hypotonic fluids during the event
body: Hyponatremia is commonly seen after endurance athletic events and is due to ingestion of large amounts of hypotonic fluids during the event. Hyponatremia is usually asymptomatic, but severe levels can result in nausea, vomiting, headache, disorientation, and seizures.

title: Patients with stones ≥10 mm, those with complicated nephrolithiasis (eg, acute kidney injury, sepsis, complete ureteral obstruction
body: Patients with stones ≥10 mm, those with complicated nephrolithiasis (eg, acute kidney injury, sepsis, complete ureteral obstruction, uncontrolled pain), and those whose stones do not pass within 4-6 weeks should be evaluated by a urologist for stone removal. ■ I>3 End ® Resources Suspend

title: Muscle crush injury results in significant extracellular fluid sequestration within the damaged tissue, decreased renal perfusion
body: Muscle crush injury results in significant extracellular fluid sequestration within the damaged tissue, decreased renal perfusion, myoglobin release, rhabdomyolysis, and acute kidney injury. Initial management involves aggressive fluid repletion with normal saline.

title: Almost all patients with a serum potassium > 8 mEq/L have EKG changes
body: Almost all patients with a serum potassium > 8 mEq/L have EKG changes. Significant hyperkalemia in the absence of EKG changes should suggest the possibility of pseudohyperkalemia. The presence of significant leukocytosis or thrombocytosis is associated with spurious hyperkalemia, and the patient should have a redraw of arterial blood with care to prevent hemolysis (i.e. no tourniquet or shaking, stored on ice, and promptly analyzed).

title: Chronic partial bilateral urinary obstruction can result in normal or slightly increased urine volume, while complete bilateral obstruction
body: Chronic partial bilateral urinary obstruction can result in normal or slightly increased urine volume, while complete bilateral obstruction causes anuria. Relief of the obstruction leads to post-obstructive diuresis (500-1000 cc/hr) that can be worsened by trying to match volume repletion with urine output. Treatment usually involves volume repletion at a significantly lower rate than urine volume loss.

title: Both methanol and ethylene glycol toxicities are associated with an increased anion gap metabolic acidosis and an elevated osmolar gap
body: Both methanol and ethylene glycol toxicities are associated with an increased anion gap metabolic acidosis and an elevated osmolar gap. Methanol is toxic to the retina and ethylene glycol is toxic to the kidney. Isopropyl alcohol toxicity is associated with an elevated osmolar gap, but NOT an increased anion gap metabolic acidosis.

title: Positive blood on urine dipstick in the absence of red blood cells on microscopic urinalysis suggests myoglobinuria due to rhabdomyolysis
body: Positive blood on urine dipstick in the absence of red blood cells on microscopic urinalysis suggests myoglobinuria due to rhabdomyolysis. Acute kidney injury typically occurs due to acute tubular necrosis; however, the fractional excretion of sodium is often low despite the mechanism of intrinsic renal injury. Elevated serum creatine kinase (often >10,000 U∕L) confirms the diagnosis.

title: The initial management of severe hypercalcemia (>13 mg/dL) includes saline hydration to promote urinary calcium excretion and calcitonin to
body: The initial management of severe hypercalcemia (>13 mg/dL) includes saline hydration to promote urinary calcium excretion and calcitonin to decrease bone resorption. Bisphosphonates require 2-4 days to affect serum calcium levels but should be given concurrently to provide a sustained calcium-lowering effect.

title: Intravenous acyclovir is relatively insoluble in urine and can precipitate within the renal tubules, leading to urinary obstruction and
body: Intravenous acyclovir is relatively insoluble in urine and can precipitate within the renal tubules, leading to urinary obstruction and acute kidney injury. Normal saline infusion during acyclovir administration with a goal urine output of 75 mL/hr is recommended to prevent crystal formation.

title: Acute urinary retention is an important cause of delirium in the elderly, although these patients often do not develop abdominal discomfort
body: Acute urinary retention is an important cause of delirium in the elderly, although these patients often do not develop abdominal discomfort or specific urinary symptoms. Rapid resolution of symptoms typically occurs after bladder decompression.

title: All patients who present with nephrolithiasis should undergo at least a basic workup, including imaging (eg, noncontrast CT scan), serum
body: All patients who present with nephrolithiasis should undergo at least a basic workup, including imaging (eg, noncontrast CT scan), serum chemistry, urinalysis, and stone analysis. Hyperparathyroidism is the most common cause of hypercalcemia in patients with nephrolithiasis.

title: This patient with advanced-stage chronic kidney disease (CKD) has a bleeding disorder that may be related to his renal failure
body: This patient with advanced-stage chronic kidney disease (CKD) has a bleeding disorder that may be related to his renal failure. The bleeding tendency in CKD is multifactorial, but likely results from defects in platelet and von Willebrand factor interaction when forming a hemostatic platelet plug. The degree of uremia does not correlate with bleeding risk, and coagulation studies (PT∕PTT) and platelet counts may both be normal. The bleeding time, however, is often prolonged.

title: In the presence of a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis, a negative urinary anion gap suggests a gastrointestinal cause of the acidosis.
Combined respiratory alkalosis and increased anion gap metabolic acidosis suggest the presence of salicylate intoxication
body: Combined respiratory alkalosis and increased anion gap metabolic acidosis suggest the presence of salicylate intoxication. Other clinical and laboratory features include decreased hearing, tinnitus, and very low serum uric acid. Treatment is supportive and involves alkalization of the urine with intravenous bicarbonate to promote renal excretion. Dialysis is reserved for more serious cases.

title: Intra-abdominal hypertension and abdominal compartment syndrome often follow aggressive volume expansion in patients with trauma, septic
body: Intra-abdominal hypertension and abdominal compartment syndrome often follow aggressive volume expansion in patients with trauma, septic shock, or other conditions. Abdominal compartment syndrome can cause multi-organ failure, including acute kidney injury. Measurement of hydrostatic pressure within the bladder is preferred to assess intra-abdominal pressure. Most patients require surgical decompression.

title: Milk-alkali syndrome is characterized by parathyroid hormone-independent hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, and metabolic alkalosis
body: Milk-alkali syndrome is characterized by parathyroid hormone-independent hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, and metabolic alkalosis. It is usually caused by excessive ingestion of calcium carbonate. The risk is increased in patients taking medications that decrease glomerular filtration. Treatment includes isotonic saline infusion and furosemide.

title: By decreasing creatinine secretion, both trimethoprim and cimetidine can result in an increased serum creatinine without decreasing the glomerular filtration rate.
Ultrasound findings of multiple renal cysts may suggest autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, which is associated with several
body: Ultrasound findings of multiple renal cysts may suggest autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, which is associated with several extra-renal manifestations (e.g., hepatic cysts and intracerebral aneurysms).

title: Several pharmacologic agents are associated with non-anion gap metabolic acidosis
body: Several pharmacologic agents are associated with non-anion gap metabolic acidosis. Acetazolamide inhibits carbonic anhydrase and typically causes bicarbonate diuresis with a non-anion gap metabolic acidosis.

title: Acute kidney injury after implementation of a new drug (especially antibiotics) should raise suspicion for acute interstitial nephritis
body: Acute kidney injury after implementation of a new drug (especially antibiotics) should raise suspicion for acute interstitial nephritis. Symptom onset is variable and generally occurs weeks to months after primary exposure; however, symptoms develop more rapidly (days) after second exposure. The presence of white blood cell casts, urine eosinophils, hematuria, and pyuria are suggestive but not required for diagnosis.

title: Hepatorenal syndrome presents with renal dysfunction and bland urine sediment in patients with advanced liver disease and portal
body: Hepatorenal syndrome presents with renal dysfunction and bland urine sediment in patients with advanced liver disease and portal hypertension. A 48-hour trial of diuretic cessation and volume expansion with albumin is required for the diagnosis.

title: The presence of a mixed acid-base disorder is suggested by clinical history and when there is a lesser or greater degree of compensation
body: The presence of a mixed acid-base disorder is suggested by clinical history and when there is a lesser or greater degree of compensation than what typically occurs in response to the primary acid-base disorder.

title: Acute interstitial nephritis is characterized by acute renal failure with concurrent fever, rash, and eosinophilia, with sterile pyuria
body: Acute interstitial nephritis is characterized by acute renal failure with concurrent fever, rash, and eosinophilia, with sterile pyuria, hematuria, and white blood cell casts on urinalysis. Common causes include antibiotics, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and proton pump inhibitors.

title: Recurrent urinary tract infections in patients with alkaline urine should raise the possibility of a struvite stone
body: Recurrent urinary tract infections in patients with alkaline urine should raise the possibility of a struvite stone. Antibiotics alone do not remove the source of the infection; elimination of the stone is required.

title: Acute interstitial nephritis is a common cause of renal dysfunction and is frequently caused by proton pump inhibitors, antibiotics, and
body: Acute interstitial nephritis is a common cause of renal dysfunction and is frequently caused by proton pump inhibitors, antibiotics, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Characteristic presentation can include fever, rash, and eosinophilia; urinalysis often shows pyuria, hematuria, and white blood cell casts. Offending medications should be stopped immediately. ■ >3 End ® Resources ISuspend

title: Prostatic nodules found on digital rectal examination should be promptly evaluated by transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) guided prostatic biopsy, regardless of the PSA level.
The estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) data provided by the hospital laboratory is valid only under stable clinical conditions
body: The estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) data provided by the hospital laboratory is valid only under stable clinical conditions. The commonly used formulas appear less accurate for individuals with a normal GFR.

title: Primary hyperparathyroidism is the most common cause of hypercalcemia
body: Primary hyperparathyroidism is the most common cause of hypercalcemia. Serum calcium in hydrochlorothiazide-induced hypercalcemia is typically high normal or modestly elevated. The majority of hydrochlorothiazide-treated patients with overt hypercalcemia have underlying primary hyperparathyroidism.

title: The presence Ofsignificant proteinuria and dysmorphic red blood cells on urinalysis suggests a glomerular cause of hematuria
body: The presence Ofsignificant proteinuria and dysmorphic red blood cells on urinalysis suggests a glomerular cause of hematuria. IgA nephropathy is characterized by recurrent episodes of gross hematuria (glomerulonephritis), typically following an upper respiratory infection. Factors associated with an adverse prognosis include elevated blood pressure, Iowerthan normal estimated glomerular filtration rate, and significant proteinuria.

title: The relationship between serum creatinine concentration and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is non-linear; every time the GFR halves, the
body: The relationship between serum creatinine concentration and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is non-linear; every time the GFR halves, the serum creatinine doubles. When the GFR is normal, relatively large decreases in GFR result in only small increases in serum creatinine. Conversely, when the GFR is significantly decreased, small decrements in GFR produce relatively large changes in serum creatinine.

title: Recurrent urolithiasis commonly occurs in gastric bypass patients due to hyperoxaluria and hypocitraturia. Treatment involves a low oxalate diet and exogenous citrate supplementation.
Lithium can be associated with nephrogenic Dl in up to 20-40% of patients
body: Lithium can be associated with nephrogenic Dl in up to 20-40% of patients. Symptomatic patients should discontinue lithium. Patients who cannot stop lithium may be treated with salt restriction and a trial of diuretics (i.e., amiloride or thiazides) with careful monitoring of renal function and serum lithium levels.

title: Uric acid stones are often radiolucent but may be seen on ultrasound or CT scan
body: Uric acid stones are often radiolucent but may be seen on ultrasound or CT scan. They are highly soluble in alkaline urine; alkalinization of the urine to pH 6.0-6.5 with oral potassium citrate is the treatment of choice. Allopurinol can be added if there are recurrent symptoms despite initial measures, especially if hyperuricosuria or hyperuricemia occurs.

title: Mixed cryoglobulinemia is commonly associated with hepatitis C and can cause glomerulonephritis
body: Mixed cryoglobulinemia is commonly associated with hepatitis C and can cause glomerulonephritis. Treatment includes eradicating hepatitis C and immunosuppression and/or plasmapheresis for cryoglobulinemia.

title: Hemolytic-uremic syndrome is associated with a prodromal diarrheal illness, usually caused by a shiga toxin-producing enterohemorrhagic E
body: Hemolytic-uremic syndrome is associated with a prodromal diarrheal illness, usually caused by a shiga toxin-producing enterohemorrhagic E. coli leading to microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury. The diagnosis is made clinically and can be evaluated with peripheral blood smear to look for Schistocytes as well as serologic testing for enterohemorrhagic E. coli.

title: Polyuria and polydipsia can be due either to a solute diuresis (usually uncontrolled diabetes mellitus with glycosuria) or a water diuresis
body: Polyuria and polydipsia can be due either to a solute diuresis (usually uncontrolled diabetes mellitus with glycosuria) or a water diuresis. Water diuresis can be due to impaired ADH secretion (central DI), impaired action of ADH on the kidney (nephrogenic DI), or excess fluid intake. The response to controlled/observed water deprivation differentiates among these possibilities.

title: Nephrotic syndrome, particularly membranous nephropathy, is associated with a high frequency of thromboembolic events, predominately deep
body: Nephrotic syndrome, particularly membranous nephropathy, is associated with a high frequency of thromboembolic events, predominately deep venous and renal venous thrombosis. Renal venous thrombosis is often asymptomatic; pulmonary embolism may be the presenting sign.

title: Calcimimetics such as Cinacalcet decrease the frequency of fractures and the rate of parathyroidectomy in patients with chronic kidney
body: Calcimimetics such as Cinacalcet decrease the frequency of fractures and the rate of parathyroidectomy in patients with chronic kidney disease who have hyperphosphatemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism. Calcimimetics also reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease in older patients (age >65). Major side effects are hypocalcemia and gastrointestinal disturbances.

title: In patients with hematuria, the passage of blood clots in the urine indicates a non-glomerular source of urinary tract bleeding. Thus, evaluation should proceed accordingly.
Amyloidosis (primary [AL] or secondary [AA]) is a common cause of nephrotic syndrome in patients age >60
body: Amyloidosis (primary [AL] or secondary [AA]) is a common cause of nephrotic syndrome in patients age >60. Other common manifestations include restrictive cardiomyopathy with heart failure. Treatment is largely supportive.

title: Orthostatic proteinuria is a benign condition commonly seen in children and young adults (2-5%)
body: Orthostatic proteinuria is a benign condition commonly seen in children and young adults (2-5%). It is generally less than 1 g∕day, but may surpass 3 g/day in select patients. The diagnosis can be established by finding a difference in quantitative proteinuria estimated by spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratio obtained upon arising (little, if any, proteinuria) and at the end of the day before recumbency (significant proteinuria).

title: Hyperphosphatemia is the inciting event for chronic kidney disease-related mineral bone disease (osteitis fibrosa, osteomalacia, adynamic
body: Hyperphosphatemia is the inciting event for chronic kidney disease-related mineral bone disease (osteitis fibrosa, osteomalacia, adynamic bone disease). Calcium-containing phosphate binders are preferred in hypocalcemic and normocalcemic patients. Non-calcium-containing binders are used in patients with hypercalcemia, low parathyroid hormone levels, vascular calcification, or suspected adynamic bone disease. Drug trade names: Sevelamer- RenaGeI, Renvela Lanthanum - Fosrenol Calcium acetate - PhosLo

title: Decompensated heart failure can worsen symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Volume overload should be treated with increased diuretic doses before adjustments are made to the BPH regimen.
Henoch-Schonlein purpura is a systemic vasculitis characterized by IgA-immune complex deposition in small vessels and the renal mesangium
body: Henoch-Schonlein purpura is a systemic vasculitis characterized by IgA-immune complex deposition in small vessels and the renal mesangium. It is most common in children but can present in adults and should be suspected in patients with some combination of palpable purpura, abdominal pain, arthritis, and renal dysfunction. ■ I>3 End ® Resources Suspend

title: Urge incontinence in the setting of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) often responds to alpha-adrenergic blockers
body: Urge incontinence in the setting of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) often responds to alpha-adrenergic blockers. Antimuscarinic agents can be added for patients with persistent symptoms, but postvoid residual volume should be measured before initiating these medications in men with BPH.

title: Explosive-onset nephrotic syndrome characterized by heavy proteinuria and profound hypoalbuminemia and that occurs shortly following an
body: Explosive-onset nephrotic syndrome characterized by heavy proteinuria and profound hypoalbuminemia and that occurs shortly following an upper respiratory infection is typical for minimal change disease. Because the clinical phenotype does not accurately predict renal histopathology, most adults with non­ diabetic nephrotic syndrome should undergo renal biopsy to confirm diagnosis and guide therapy.

title: Calcium oxalate stones are the most common cause of nephrolithiasis
body: Calcium oxalate stones are the most common cause of nephrolithiasis. To reduce the risk of recurrent nephrolithiasis, patients should increase intake of fluids, dietary calcium, and fruits and vegetables, and decrease intake of sodium and animal protein. ■ >3 End ® Resources

title: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin Il receptor blockers are first-line medications for the management of diabetic
body: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin Il receptor blockers are first-line medications for the management of diabetic nephropathy due to their renal protective effects. Both therapies are associated with a rise in serum creatinine of up to 30%-35% from baseline; this is acceptable and should not cause discontinuation of therapy.

title: Atheroembolic disease usually presents with acute kidney injury after arteriography involving the aorta, and is associated with livedo reticularis and a cyanotic or gangrenous toe.
For patients with mild benign prostatic hyperplasia, simple behavioral modifications (eg, shifting fluid intake to earlier in the day
body: For patients with mild benign prostatic hyperplasia, simple behavioral modifications (eg, shifting fluid intake to earlier in the day, decreasing caffeine and alcohol intake, double voiding) may be adequate. Patients with more severe symptoms or obstructive complications (eg, bladder infections, bladder stones, renal impairment) warrant more aggressive management.

title: Thiazide diuretics can lead to hyponatremia (more commonly than loop diuretics), especially in frail and elderly women with a low body mass
body: Thiazide diuretics can lead to hyponatremia (more commonly than loop diuretics), especially in frail and elderly women with a low body mass index. Patients with nonspecific symptoms after starting thiazide diuretics should have laboratory evaluation of their electrolytes. Treatment consists of stopping the diuretic and fluid repletion in symptomatic patients.

title: NSAIDs are commonly associated with elevations in blood pressure and can also affect the efficacy of anti­ hypertensive agents
body: NSAIDs are commonly associated with elevations in blood pressure and can also affect the efficacy of anti­ hypertensive agents. A trial of discontinuation of the NSAID should be considered in patients with Suboptimal blood pressure control.

title: Hypercalciuria is a common risk factor for the formation of calcium-containing kidney stones
body: Hypercalciuria is a common risk factor for the formation of calcium-containing kidney stones. Several dietary factors (as shown in below table) can have a favorable impact in reducing the incidence of calcium stones. Restrict Increase Sodium Calcium Animal protein Citrate Fluids; fruits & vegetables

title: Patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis should first be treated with medical therapy (eg, a diuretic and either ACE inhibitor or
body: Patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis should first be treated with medical therapy (eg, a diuretic and either ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker) as it is as efficacious as angioplasty or surgery. Patients who fail optimal medical therapy (eg, progressive renal insufficiency) or those with recurrent flash pulmonary edema or heart failure should be considered for angioplasty.

title: Crystal-induced acute kidney injury occurs when poorly soluble drugs precipitate in the renal tubules
body: Crystal-induced acute kidney injury occurs when poorly soluble drugs precipitate in the renal tubules. Sulfadiazine is insoluble at a pH of ≤5.5; prevention and treatment include hydration and alkalinization of the urine to a pH of >7.15 to increase solubility. ■ I>3 End ® Resources Suspend

title: Management of acute prostatitis involves obtaining a urine culture followed by empiric treatment with fluoroquinolones or oral
body: Management of acute prostatitis involves obtaining a urine culture followed by empiric treatment with fluoroquinolones or oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Prostate massage is not recommended. If bladder drainage is required, the suprapubic route should be used.

title: Advancing age, male sex, Caucasian ethnicity, cigarette smoking, exposure to selected chemicals, chronic bladder inflammation, and a family
body: Advancing age, male sex, Caucasian ethnicity, cigarette smoking, exposure to selected chemicals, chronic bladder inflammation, and a family history of cancer are risk factors for bladder cancer. Hematuria in a patient with risk factors should promote a timely evaluation for cancer with imaging, urine cytology, and cystoscopy.

title: Urinary incontinence is a common complication after radical prostatectomy for localized prostate cancer and is usually due to a damaged
body: Urinary incontinence is a common complication after radical prostatectomy for localized prostate cancer and is usually due to a damaged urinary sphincter. Pelvic floor exercises with biofeedback can significantly accelerate recovery and decrease the incidence of postprostatectomy stress incontinence.

title: Iron deficiency is the most common cause of erythropoietin resistance in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD)
body: Iron deficiency is the most common cause of erythropoietin resistance in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD). All patients with ESRD receiving erythropoietin-stimulating agents should be treated with intravenous iron, regardless of results of iron studies unless ferritin >500 ng/mL.

title: Diabetics with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) treated with either a living related or cadaveric donor kidney transplant (compared to
body: Diabetics with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) treated with either a living related or cadaveric donor kidney transplant (compared to dialysis) have better survival, quality of life, and rehabilitation. Infections are the most common cause of death in the early post-transplant period.

title: Patients with a normal digital rectal examination (DRE) and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) < 3 ng/mL may be followed routinely
body: Patients with a normal digital rectal examination (DRE) and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) < 3 ng/mL may be followed routinely. Men with PSA > 7 ng/mL or abnormal DRE should be referred to a urologist for possible biopsy.

title: BK polyoma virus presents in renal transplant recipients most commonly after rejection and significant immunosuppression
body: BK polyoma virus presents in renal transplant recipients most commonly after rejection and significant immunosuppression. Patients typically develop tubulointerstitial nephritis with rising creatinine and the presence of intranuclear inclusions in urine cells. Definitive diagnosis requires renal biopsy plus positive immunohistochemistry tests using antibodies directed specifically against the BK virus.

title: Suspect cystinuria in patients with large branched calculi or a first stone occurring at an early age (childhood or adolescence)
body: Suspect cystinuria in patients with large branched calculi or a first stone occurring at an early age (childhood or adolescence). Hexagonal (benzene ring) crystals are seen in 25% of the patients on initial urinalysis. Increased fluid intake, alkalinization of the urine (with potassium citrate or bicarbonate), and chelating agents (in some cases) can prevent further cystine stone formation.

title: In patients with hypertension and proteinuric chronic kidney disease, diuretics can correct edema and increase the effectiveness of other
body: In patients with hypertension and proteinuric chronic kidney disease, diuretics can correct edema and increase the effectiveness of other antihypertensive medications. Loop diuretics are more effective than thiazide diuretics in patients with creatinine clearance <30 mL/min/1.73 m .

title: Patients with chronic kidney disease are at risk for contrast-induced nephropathy
body: Patients with chronic kidney disease are at risk for contrast-induced nephropathy. Preventive measures include avoidance of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, periprocedural infusion of normal saline, and use of the smallest possible volume of contrast media.

title: Diabetic nephropathy typically presents with bland urinalysis and albuminuria; however, hematuria and red blood cell casts may occur
body: Diabetic nephropathy typically presents with bland urinalysis and albuminuria; however, hematuria and red blood cell casts may occur. Progression is slow (years); therefore, nondiabetic glomerular diseases should be considered in patients with rapidly progressive disease, unexpected reductions in glomerular filtration rates (>30%) after ACE inhibitor initiation, active urinary sediment, or symptoms of other systemic diseases. ■ I÷0 End © Resources Suspend

title: A subset of patients with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis develop scleroderma renal crisis, characterized by acute kidney injury (no
body: A subset of patients with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis develop scleroderma renal crisis, characterized by acute kidney injury (no active urinary sediment), accelerated hypertension, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia. Treatment involves prompt initiation of an angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor (even in patients with advanced renal dysfunction).

title: Tuberous sclerosis complex is being recognized more frequently in adults
body: Tuberous sclerosis complex is being recognized more frequently in adults. Patients who present with > 1 renal angiomyolipoma or pulmonary Iymphangioleiomyomatosis in women should undergo a thorough dermatologic examination and brain imaging to screen for tuberous sclerosis. Management usually involves seizure control and surveillance for CNS, pulmonary, and renal manifestations.

title: Postoperative hyponatremia usually occurs due to surgical stress-related release of vasopressin, use of nonelectrolyte solutions for
body: Postoperative hyponatremia usually occurs due to surgical stress-related release of vasopressin, use of nonelectrolyte solutions for irrigation, or infusion of hypotonic solutions. Acute, symptomatic hyponatremia should be emergently treated with hypertonic saline.

title: Women age > 65 should undergo screening for voiding problems with a thorough history and physical examination
body: Women age > 65 should undergo screening for voiding problems with a thorough history and physical examination. Incontinence related to potentially reversible conditions (transient incontinence) can be due to etiologies such as stool impaction, medications, urinary tract infection, mobility issues, lifestyle, and atrophic vaginitis.

title: Intermittent hypokalemia with metabolic alkalosis in the absence of vomiting suggests a diagnosis of either surreptitious purging or
body: Intermittent hypokalemia with metabolic alkalosis in the absence of vomiting suggests a diagnosis of either surreptitious purging or diuretic use. A variable urinary chloride favors diuretic abuse and can be confirmed with a urinary screen for diuretics.

title: The risk/benefit of renal replacement therapy should be assessed in older patients and may not be indicated for selected individuals with
body: The risk/benefit of renal replacement therapy should be assessed in older patients and may not be indicated for selected individuals with significant co-morbidity, especially in nursing home residents.

title: Hematuria and impaired ability to maximally concentrate the urine are two renal abnormalities encountered in patients with sickle cell
body: Hematuria and impaired ability to maximally concentrate the urine are two renal abnormalities encountered in patients with sickle cell trait. A hemoglobin electrophoresis can confirm the diagnosis. A rare complication of sickle trait is the development of renal medullary carcinoma, a highly malignant cancer that is seen almost exclusively in young patients with sickle cell trait.

title: Hypernatremia is usually due to hypotonic fluid loss combined with defects in either cognition/thirst or ability to access water
body: Hypernatremia is usually due to hypotonic fluid loss combined with defects in either cognition/thirst or ability to access water. Free water repletion (5% dextrose) is the preferred treatment in euvolemic patients. However, in patients with hypovolemic hypernatremia, correction of effective circulating volume deficit with isotonic fluids should be done before the replacement of water deficit. Sodium should be corrected at a rate of 0.5 mEq/dL/hr and should not exceed 12 mEq/dL/24 hours, since too rapid a correction results in cerebral edema.

title: Refeeding or giving dextrose-containing fluids to nutritionally depleted individuals (e.g., alcoholics) can lead to severe hypophosphatemia and resultant multi-organ dysfunction.
Tacrolimus and cyclosporine are Calcineurin inhibitors that antagonize interleukin-2 and other cytokines to decrease T cell activity
body: Tacrolimus and cyclosporine are Calcineurin inhibitors that antagonize interleukin-2 and other cytokines to decrease T cell activity. Because both drugs are extensively metabolized by hepatic cytochrome P450, compounds that interact with cytochrome P450 can increase or decrease drug levels. Patients can develop nephrotoxicity (most common), hypertension, neurotoxicity, and metabolic abnormalities.

title: Calcineurin inhibitors (eg, cyclosporine, tacrolimus) can cause nephrotoxicity that presents with declining glomerular filtration rates and
body: Calcineurin inhibitors (eg, cyclosporine, tacrolimus) can cause nephrotoxicity that presents with declining glomerular filtration rates and metabolic abnormalities. Toxicity is dose-dependent; drugs metabolized by cytochrome P450 3A4 can increase toxicity.

title: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is the most characteristic renal lesion seen in African- Americans with HIV
body: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is the most characteristic renal lesion seen in African- Americans with HIV. FSGS in HIV-infected individuals is associated with large echogenic kidneys on ultrasound, few red or white blood cells on urinalysis, heavy proteinuria, and hypoalbuminemia. Surprisingly, hypertension is not seen despite the high incidence of hypertension seen in African Americans.

title: Hematuria is uncommon in patients on dual antiplatelet therapy or anticoagulants
body: Hematuria is uncommon in patients on dual antiplatelet therapy or anticoagulants. Patients with risk factors for malignancy should be evaluated with CT urography followed by cystoscopy to rule out genitourinary tract abnormalities.

title: A simple renal cyst is the most common renal lesion and is usually seen in adults age >50
body: A simple renal cyst is the most common renal lesion and is usually seen in adults age >50. A simple cyst is round with thin, smooth walls; is anechoic; reveals posterior wall enhancement on ultrasound; and does not enhance with intravenous contrast on CT scan/MRI. Simple cysts are benign and do not require follow-up imaging unless symptomatic (eg, hemorrhage, infection, pain).

title: Arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred vascular access modality for chronic hemodialysis
body: Arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred vascular access modality for chronic hemodialysis. However, maturation of a fistula takes up to 3 months. Therefore, if hemodialysis is anticipated, preemptive placement of an AV fistula is recommended, typically when the glomerular filtration rate is 15-20 mL/min/1.73 m . ■ >3 End ® Resources ISuspend

title: Daily protein excretion (> 1 g∕day) has a more detrimental effect on kidney function than initial glomerular filtration rate or the primary
body: Daily protein excretion (> 1 g∕day) has a more detrimental effect on kidney function than initial glomerular filtration rate or the primary cause of renal dysfunction. Angiotension-converting enzyme inhibitors decrease proteinuria, slow the rate of progression to renal failure in most patients, and are recommended for both primary and secondary focal segmental glomerular sclerosis.

title: Multiple myeloma commonly presents with acute kidney injury, most commonly due to cast nephropathy
body: Multiple myeloma commonly presents with acute kidney injury, most commonly due to cast nephropathy. A discrepancy between the amounts of proteinuria detected by dipstick and by quantitative methods suggests non-albumin proteinuria and the presence of light chains, which are directly toxic to renal tubules or can combine with Tamm-HorsfaII proteins to form casts.

title: Retroperitoneal fibrosis typically presents with nonspecific pain in the low back, flank, or abdomen
body: Retroperitoneal fibrosis typically presents with nonspecific pain in the low back, flank, or abdomen. Patients usually have progressively worsening periaortic fibrosis that leads to kidney injury, ureteral obstruction without ureteral dilation, and possible IVC obstruction with edema and DVT. Treatment involves steroids, relieving the obstruction, and treating the underlying cause.

title: Felty's syndrome is a triad of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, neutropenia, and splenomegaly. It is seen in patients with advanced rheumatoid arthritis (usually > 10 years).
Tarsal tunnel syndrome presents with pain and paresthesias in the sole of the foot, distal foot, or toes. Examination can show a positive TineΓs sign and/or sensory loss.
Patients with ankylosing spondylitis have limited chest wall expansion that, if severe enough, can lead to hypoventilation and respiratory
body: Patients with ankylosing spondylitis have limited chest wall expansion that, if severe enough, can lead to hypoventilation and respiratory failure. Treatment of respiratory impairment includes pulmonary rehabilitation and noninvasive positive pressure ventilation.

title: Pseudogout causes an acute inflammatory arthritis, most commonly in the knees
body: Pseudogout causes an acute inflammatory arthritis, most commonly in the knees. Parathyroidectomy can precipitate a pseudogout attack due to an abrupt drop in serum calcium levels, which triggers shedding of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystals into the synovial fluid.

title: Common manifestations of ankylosing spondylitis include enthesitis, inflammatory back pain, and uveitis
body: Common manifestations of ankylosing spondylitis include enthesitis, inflammatory back pain, and uveitis. Examination shows decreases in chest expansion, cervical extension, and Iumbarflexion. An anteroposterior x-ray of the pelvis can confirm the diagnosis, and HLA-B27 is usually positive. Initial treatment includes nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and range-of-motion exercises.

title: Prompt diagnosis Ofgranulomatosis with polyangiitis can be life- and kidney-sparing
body: Prompt diagnosis Ofgranulomatosis with polyangiitis can be life- and kidney-sparing. Although positive anti-neutrophilic cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) support the diagnosis, both false-positive and false­ negative ANCA results do occur. Tissue biopsy is typically obtained at the site of active disease to make a definitive diagnosis (eg, skin, kidney, lung).

title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) presents classically with sinus disease, pulmonary disease, renal disease, and systemic symptoms
body: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) presents classically with sinus disease, pulmonary disease, renal disease, and systemic symptoms. The c-ANCA pattern and anti-PR3 antibodies are most commonly associated with GPA. Diagnosis is confirmed by tissue biopsy showing vasculitis.

title: Primary Raynaud's phenomenon (RP) usually occurs in women < age 30 with no systemic symptoms, no thumb involvement, normal ANA and ESR
body: Primary Raynaud's phenomenon (RP) usually occurs in women < age 30 with no systemic symptoms, no thumb involvement, normal ANA and ESR tests, and normal nailfold Capillaroscopy. Secondary RP is usually seen in men > age 40 with signs of tissue ischemia or ulceration, abnormal laboratory findings and nailfold Capillaroscopy tests, and/or presence of systemic symptoms.

title: Pes anserinus pain syndrome presents with point tenderness along the medial knee
body: Pes anserinus pain syndrome presents with point tenderness along the medial knee. Acute therapy includes restricting activity, placing a pillow between the knees at night, applying ice, and possibly using nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Patients who are refractory to conservative measures may benefit from a glucocorticoid injection.

title: Diabetic neuropathic arthropathy or "Charcot joint" can present acutely with foot or ankle erythema, warmth, and swelling in a diabetic
body: Diabetic neuropathic arthropathy or "Charcot joint" can present acutely with foot or ankle erythema, warmth, and swelling in a diabetic patient, similar to inflammatory or septic arthritis. Joint aspiration and imaging can assist in confirming the diagnosis. Treatment includes casting and avoiding weight bearing. Anti-resorption therapy with bisphosphonates is also useful in some patients.

title: Low back pain that persists with red flags for systemic illness warrants immediate evaluation rather than conservative therapy
body: Low back pain that persists with red flags for systemic illness warrants immediate evaluation rather than conservative therapy. A recent urinary tract infection associated with back pain is concerning for vertebral osteomyelitis, and MRI is the most sensitive test for diagnosis.

title: Adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder syndrome) is due to the lack of glenohumeral joint distensibility leading to > 50% reduction of both
body: Adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder syndrome) is due to the lack of glenohumeral joint distensibility leading to > 50% reduction of both passive and active range of motion. Range of motion exercises to strengthen the glenohumeral joint are preferred for acute treatment. Refractory patients may be treated with steroid joint injections after 6-8 weeks.

title: Acute gout is usually treated with NSAIDs as first-line therapy and colchicine as second-line therapy
body: Acute gout is usually treated with NSAIDs as first-line therapy and colchicine as second-line therapy. Allopurinol is usually given for prophylaxis along with colchicine to patients with recurrent gout, tophaceous gout, nephrolithiasis, radiographic evidence of gouty arthritis, or urinary uric acid excretion >1100 mg∕day. Patients who develop a gouty attack while taking allopurinol should not undergo dose adjustments or drug discontinuation until 3-4 weeks after the acute inflammation subsides.

title: Patellofemoral syndrome (PFPS) is a clinical diagnosis characterized by knee pain that worsens with squatting, moving up and down stairs
body: Patellofemoral syndrome (PFPS) is a clinical diagnosis characterized by knee pain that worsens with squatting, moving up and down stairs, and rest. Examination shows mild crepitus and tenderness on direct compression of the patella during knee extension. Supervised physical therapy is the primary treatment for PFPS.

title: Patients with recurrent genital and oral ulcers combined with skin or ocular lesions likely have Behget disease and require further evaluation.
Management of chronic back pain should emphasize nonpharmacologic measures
body: Management of chronic back pain should emphasize nonpharmacologic measures. A multidisciplinary rehabilitation program, including physical therapy, occupational therapy, and cognitive-behavioral therapy, has been shown to improve pain and functional status better than a single-modality approach.

title: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy usually involves distal parts of the extremities and is characterized by abnormal proliferation of the skin
body: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy usually involves distal parts of the extremities and is characterized by abnormal proliferation of the skin and osseous tissue. It presents with clubbing of the fingers and synovitis of knees, ankles, and fingers. The most common cause is an intrathoracic neoplasm.

title: Adults with parvovirus B19 infection usually present with a flu-like illness 5-10 days after exposure followed by acute, symmetrical
body: Adults with parvovirus B19 infection usually present with a flu-like illness 5-10 days after exposure followed by acute, symmetrical arthralgias/arthritis (e.g., hands/wrists) that can resemble rheumatoid arthritis. Immunocompromised patients and those with preexisting hematological disease can develop more serious complications (e.g., transient aplastic anemia). Diagnosis is confirmed with parvovirus B19 IgM antibodies.

title: Metatarsal shaft stress fracture is usually due to repetitive weight-bearing activities (eg, running, dancing, jumping) and causes
body: Metatarsal shaft stress fracture is usually due to repetitive weight-bearing activities (eg, running, dancing, jumping) and causes gradually worsening pain. Examination usually shows focal metatarsal tenderness or pain with axial loading of the metatarsal.

title: Individuals with dermatomyositis and polymyositis have an increased risk of malignancy compared to the general population
body: Individuals with dermatomyositis and polymyositis have an increased risk of malignancy compared to the general population. Age-appropriate screening (eg, mammogram and colonoscopy) should be performed in these patients, and additional testing may be needed based on history and clinical symptoms.

title: Patients with osteoarthritis typically complain of morning stiffness and groin pain
body: Patients with osteoarthritis typically complain of morning stiffness and groin pain. The pain may radiate towards the knee, but does not extend beyond it. Rest tends to ameliorate the pain, but lying on either side would not affect the pain. Pain is often aggravated by movement (intemal/external rotation) rather than by direct pressure, as in trochanteric bursitis.

title: Polymyalgia rheumatica manifests as shoulder and/or hip girdle achiness along with at least 30 minutes of morning stiffness, and is seen in
body: Polymyalgia rheumatica manifests as shoulder and/or hip girdle achiness along with at least 30 minutes of morning stiffness, and is seen in patients over the age of 50. The majority of patients (80%) have an elevated ESR, but elevated C-reactive protein can be helpful in the diagnosis for patients with a normal ESR. Diagnosis is confirmed with a dramatic response to low-dose prednisone.

title: Lumbar spinal stenosis produces lower extremity symptoms exacerbated by walking downhill and relieved with rest and bending forward; these
body: Lumbar spinal stenosis produces lower extremity symptoms exacerbated by walking downhill and relieved with rest and bending forward; these symptoms are known as pseudoclaudication and may be Similarto vascular claudication. MRI of the lumbar spine is the preferred diagnostic test.

title: Sjogren syndrome (SS) is characterized by lymphocytic inflammation of the lacrimal and salivary glands, which leads to chronic dry eyes and
body: Sjogren syndrome (SS) is characterized by lymphocytic inflammation of the lacrimal and salivary glands, which leads to chronic dry eyes and dry mouth. Approximately 25% of patients have extraglandular manifestations in the skin, lungs, nervous system, heart, and/or kidneys (eg, chronic interstitial nephritis). Diagnosis usually requires anti-SSA and anti-SSB antibody testing and/or lower lip salivary gland biopsy.

title: Methotrexate is the most common first-line treatment for rheumatoid arthritis (RA)
body: Methotrexate is the most common first-line treatment for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Patients with RA who experience worsening disease while taking methotrexate are usually started on TNF antagonists. All patients should have screening for tuberculosis and hepatitis B and C prior to initiating TNF antagonists.

title: Avascular necrosis (AVN) is characterized by groin pain on weight bearing, limited internal rotation and range of motion, and negative
body: Avascular necrosis (AVN) is characterized by groin pain on weight bearing, limited internal rotation and range of motion, and negative inflammatory markers. Chronic steroid/alcohol use, sickle cell disease, and systemic lupus erythematosus are the most common risk factors. The pathognomonic sign of late-stage AVN on x-ray is the crescent sign, but MRI remains the most sensitive modality for diagnosis.

title: Disequilibrium is a nonspecific sense of weakness or imbalance with ambulation
body: Disequilibrium is a nonspecific sense of weakness or imbalance with ambulation. It is common in elderly patients with multiple comorbid conditions. Contributing factors may include cerebellar dysfunction, cervical spondylosis, Parkinsonism, peripheral neuropathy, medication side effects, arthritis, muscle weakness, and visual impairment. Management usually requires a multidisciplinary program including regular exercise, physical therapy, and occupational therapy.

title: Complex regional pain syndrome commonly presents after an injury with throbbing pain, paresthesias, skin temperature changes, and local
body: Complex regional pain syndrome commonly presents after an injury with throbbing pain, paresthesias, skin temperature changes, and local edema. Diagnosis is suggested clinically by symptoms and abrupt symptom relief with a local anesthetic block.

title: Popliteal cysts usually present in patients with underlying knee disease and can be asymptomatic
body: Popliteal cysts usually present in patients with underlying knee disease and can be asymptomatic. Patients with symptomatic cysts may have posterior knee fullness, pain, and/or stiffness increased by activity. Popliteal cysts may also dissect or rupture, resulting in calf pain that mimics thrombophlebitis.

title: Trochanteric bursitis usually presents with lateral hip pain that can radiate into the buttock or toward the knee
body: Trochanteric bursitis usually presents with lateral hip pain that can radiate into the buttock or toward the knee. Examination typically reveals point tenderness over the midpoint of the greater trochanter. Treatment involves local heat, muscle strengthening exercises, conservative measures, and NSAIDs. Persistent symptoms require further evaluation and corticosteroid injection.

title: Recurrent polyarticular gout can lead to tophaceous gout. Allopurinol is the preferred treatment.
Fibromyalgia commonly presents in young to middle-aged women with widespread pain, fatigue, and cognitive/mood disturbances. Regular exercise and good sleep hygiene are the foundation of management.
Psoriatic arthritis can present prior to the manifestation of skin disease in up to 30% of patients
body: Psoriatic arthritis can present prior to the manifestation of skin disease in up to 30% of patients. DIP arthritis and arthritis mutilans are considered the most specific patterns for psoriatic arthritis. Hand x-rays can reveal lysis of the terminal phalanges, joint destruction, and a "pencil-in-cup" appearance.

title: The combination of Raynaud’s phenomenon, acid reflux disease, and skin findings is highly suggestive of systemic sclerosis
body: The combination of Raynaud’s phenomenon, acid reflux disease, and skin findings is highly suggestive of systemic sclerosis. Laboratory tests that can help confirm the diagnosis include antitopoisomerase (SCL- 70), anticentromere (ACA), and anti-RNA polymerase III. ■ ÷EJ End ® Resources

title: Initial medication options for osteoarthritis include acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
body: Initial medication options for osteoarthritis include acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). However, systemic NSAIDs are associated with increased risk of complications in patients age ≥65 and in those with hypertension, heart disease, chronic kidney disease, or a history of gastrointestinal hemorrhage. For these patients, a topical NSAID (eg, diclofenac) may be equally effective and is associated with less systemic toxicity.

title: Determination of the presence and degree of frailty is helpful in assessing the likelihood of adverse post­ operative outcomes in older patients.
Primary Raynaud’s phenomenon is an increased vascular response to cold temperature or emotional stress
body: Primary Raynaud’s phenomenon is an increased vascular response to cold temperature or emotional stress. It usually presents in women < age 30 with symmetrical episodic attacks without evidence of peripheral vascular disease, tissue injury, or abnormal nailfold capillary examination. Treatment primarily involves avoiding aggravating factors and calcium channel blockers (eg, nifedipine, amlodipine) in resistant cases.

title: Patients with giant cell arteritis can present with nonspecific symptoms (i.e.1 fever, fatigue, and weight loss), but jaw claudication is
body: Patients with giant cell arteritis can present with nonspecific symptoms (i.e.1 fever, fatigue, and weight loss), but jaw claudication is the most specific symptom. Temporal artery biopsy confirms the diagnosis, and prompt treatment with glucocorticoids should be initiated. All patients should undergo osteoporosis screening when starting steroids and yearly chest x-rays (up to ten years) to identify patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms.

title: Polymyalgia rheumatica causes proximal muscle aching and stiffness in elderly patients and responds rapidly to low-dose prednisone.
Fibromyalgia causes fatigue, widespread pain, and cognitive/mood disturbances without other physical or laboratory abnormalities
body: Fibromyalgia causes fatigue, widespread pain, and cognitive/mood disturbances without other physical or laboratory abnormalities. Tricyclic antidepressants are an effective initial therapy. Pregabalin, duloxetine, and milnacipran can be effective for patients not responding to tricyclic antidepressants.

title: Dermatomyositis typically presents with proximal and symmetrical muscle weakness and characteristic skin findings (eg, Gottron’s papules
body: Dermatomyositis typically presents with proximal and symmetrical muscle weakness and characteristic skin findings (eg, Gottron’s papules, heliotrope rash). Diagnosis is suggested by clinical findings and can be confirmed with laboratory testing, EMG, and skin/muscle biopsy. Treatment involves glucocorticoids and evaluation for possible associated malignancy.

title: Over half of all patients with systemic lupus erythematosus will develop renal disease during their lifetime
body: Over half of all patients with systemic lupus erythematosus will develop renal disease during their lifetime. A renal biopsy should be performed when any new evidence of kidney involvement, including proteinuria, elevated creatinine, or active urine sediment, is present.

title: de Quervain's tenosynovitis is due to thickening and stenosis of the synovial sheath from chronic overuse of the wrist or hand, trauma, or
body: de Quervain's tenosynovitis is due to thickening and stenosis of the synovial sheath from chronic overuse of the wrist or hand, trauma, or repetitive activity. Patients usually present with pain at the radial side of the wrist and positive Finkelstein's maneuver. Acute treatment involves activity modification, thumb splints, and anti-inflammatory agents.

title: Patients with osteoporosis who have progressive bone loss while on bisphosphonate therapy should be evaluated for conditions that can
body: Patients with osteoporosis who have progressive bone loss while on bisphosphonate therapy should be evaluated for conditions that can contribute to bone loss and should be considered for a change in treatment regimen. Teriparatide is a recombinant parathyroid hormone analog that can increase bone density and reduce fracture risk in patients with severe osteoporosis or who fail first-line treatment.

title: Advanced RA can cause pain due to mechanical stress from joint destruction instead of inflammatory disease activity
body: Advanced RA can cause pain due to mechanical stress from joint destruction instead of inflammatory disease activity. Surgery (eg, total joint replacement, soft-tissue release, and joint fusion) is indicated in RA patients with joint destruction causing intractable pain, severe functional disability, or impending tendon rupture.

title: Mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) is an overlap syndrome with features of systemic sclerosis, SLE1 and polymyositis
body: Mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD) is an overlap syndrome with features of systemic sclerosis, SLE1 and polymyositis. Diagnosis requires anti-RNP antibodies and the presence of swollen hands, myositis, synovitis, or Raynaud’s phenomenon. Treatment is usually glucocorticoids. Pulmonary hypertension is the most common complication leading to increased mortality in MCTD.

title: Rotator cuff tear usually presents with shoulder pain when reaching overhead as well as with weakness during abduction and external
body: Rotator cuff tear usually presents with shoulder pain when reaching overhead as well as with weakness during abduction and external rotation. Best results are obtained if surgical repair is performed within 6 weeks of the inciting injury.

title: Septic arthritis occurs more commonly in patients with comorbidities (e.g., diabetes, HIV) or conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis
body: Septic arthritis occurs more commonly in patients with comorbidities (e.g., diabetes, HIV) or conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, severe osteoarthritis, or prosthetic joints. Patients typically present with monoarthritis with restricted motion and synovial fluid showing an elevated WBC count with positive Gram stain (although it can be negative in 20-30% of cases). Treatment involves IV antibiotics and joint drainage.

title: Osteoarthritis of the hip presents with hip pain, limited range of motion, and x-rays showing joint space narrowing
body: Osteoarthritis of the hip presents with hip pain, limited range of motion, and x-rays showing joint space narrowing. Acetaminophen is usually the first-line therapy for noninflammatory OA, followed by NSAIDS and intraarticular steroid injections. Patients with persistent pain or severe impairment typically require early surgical therapy with total hip replacement.

title: Cervical myelopathy usually presents in patients with rheumatoid arthritis with C1-C2 subluxation due to ligament destruction and bony
body: Cervical myelopathy usually presents in patients with rheumatoid arthritis with C1-C2 subluxation due to ligament destruction and bony erosions. Patients present with multiple neurological findings (e.g., increased reflexes, muscle weakness, etc.) that requires prompt cervical MRI (preferred) to establish the diagnosis. Surgery is required in most cases for spinal stabilization.

title: Positive anti-CCP antibodies with high titers predict radiographic progression and poorer functional outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis
body: Positive anti-CCP antibodies with high titers predict radiographic progression and poorer functional outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis. Patients with anti-CCP antibodies may benefit from more aggressive disease-modifying antirheumatic drug therapy compared to other patients.

title: The combination of erythema nodosum, bilateral ankle arthritis, and bilateral hilar adenopathy has a high specificity for Lofgren's
body: The combination of erythema nodosum, bilateral ankle arthritis, and bilateral hilar adenopathy has a high specificity for Lofgren's syndrome (a variant of sarcoidosis). The syndrome is usually self-limited and has an excellent short- and long-term prognosis. Although no controlled trials are available, NSAIDs usually offer symptomatic relief and corticosteroids are generally not required.

title: Acetaminophen is preferred for osteoarthritis in patients with kidney disease or at risk of peptic ulcer disease
body: Acetaminophen is preferred for osteoarthritis in patients with kidney disease or at risk of peptic ulcer disease. COX-2-specific NSAIDs are equally nephrotoxic and offer no advantage over traditional NSAIDs in patients with renal impairment.

title: Symptomatic vertebral compression fractures are managed acutely by NSAIDS, acetaminophen, and sometimes opioids
body: Symptomatic vertebral compression fractures are managed acutely by NSAIDS, acetaminophen, and sometimes opioids. When this therapy fails, intranasal calcitonin for 2-4 weeks can provide symptomatic improvement.

title: Behgefs disease is characterized by recurrent oral (> 3 times in 1 year) and genital ulcers, ocular and skin lesions, and positive pathergy
body: Behgefs disease is characterized by recurrent oral (> 3 times in 1 year) and genital ulcers, ocular and skin lesions, and positive pathergy test. Some patients present very early with superficial or deep vein thrombosis. Diagnosis is made clinically, and treatment consists of colchicine, glucocorticoids, or immunosuppressive agents.

title: Hemochromatosis is a metabolic disorder often associated with secondary osteoarthritis
body: Hemochromatosis is a metabolic disorder often associated with secondary osteoarthritis. Patients usually have pain in the hands (especially the second and third MCP joints), hips, knees, and shoulders. Typical radiographic findings include chondrocalcinosis and hook-like osteophytes on the metacarpal heads. Elevated serum transferrin saturation correlates with the presence of joint disease.

title: NSAIDs are the preferred agents for acute gout, but steroids (intra-articular or systemic) are safer and preferred in patients with CKD
body: NSAIDs are the preferred agents for acute gout, but steroids (intra-articular or systemic) are safer and preferred in patients with CKD. Colchicine is not recommended in patients with chronic kidney disease. Allopurinol and febuxostat should not be used for acute attacks, but they are both helpful in the prevention of future attacks.

title: Common toxicities of methotrexate include fever, stomatitis, macular rash, gastrointestinal disturbances, and hematologic abnormalities
body: Common toxicities of methotrexate include fever, stomatitis, macular rash, gastrointestinal disturbances, and hematologic abnormalities (megaloblastic anemia). Stomatitis and megaloblastic anemia can be prevented by folic acid supplementation.

title: Paget disease of bone can be asymptomatic or present with bone pain
body: Paget disease of bone can be asymptomatic or present with bone pain. Diagnosis is confirmed by radiographic abnormalities and elevated bone alkaline phosphatase. Bone scan can delineate the extent of disease and guide treatment. Bisphosphonates are the preferred treatment.

title: Septic olecranon bursitis is characterized by acute erythema, warmth, and swelling, and is usually due to infection by skin flora
body: Septic olecranon bursitis is characterized by acute erythema, warmth, and swelling, and is usually due to infection by skin flora. Bursal fluid analysis can confirm the diagnosis. Treatment includes drainage of infected fluid and systemic antibiotics.

title: Men age >50 and postmenopausal women expected to receive corticosteroids at >7.5 mg/day for >3 months are candidates for osteoporosis
body: Men age >50 and postmenopausal women expected to receive corticosteroids at >7.5 mg/day for >3 months are candidates for osteoporosis prevention therapy. Bisphosphonates are preferred in most patients.

title: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a long-term (> 6 years) complication of Sjogren's syndrome
body: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a long-term (> 6 years) complication of Sjogren's syndrome. Risk factors include anti-Ro/SSA or anti-La/SSB antibody positivity, rheumatoid factor positivity, cryoglobulinemia, hypocomplementemia, and lymphocytopenia.

title: Iliotibial band syndrome is a common cause of lateral knee and thigh pain and is especially common in inexperienced runners
body: Iliotibial band syndrome is a common cause of lateral knee and thigh pain and is especially common in inexperienced runners. The diagnosis is primarily clinical with lateral knee pain reproduced on palpation, especially with flexion and extension of the knee. The foundation of management is stretching and strengthening exercises for lower-extremity muscles and temporary reduction in exercise regimen.

title: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus resembles systemic lupus erythematosus, but is less likely to cause central nervous system or renal
body: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus resembles systemic lupus erythematosus, but is less likely to cause central nervous system or renal disease, hematologic abnormalities, or low complement levels. Common triggers include hydralazine, procainamide, anti-tumor necrosis factor agents, and minocycline. Discontinuation of the inciting drug usually leads to resolution.

title: Vertebral osteomyelitis presents with progressively worsening back pain over weeks or months and is often due to hematogenous seeding by
body: Vertebral osteomyelitis presents with progressively worsening back pain over weeks or months and is often due to hematogenous seeding by organisms from distant sites (eg, genitourinary tract). The erythrocyte sedimentation rate is usually elevated, and blood cultures and MRI of the spine are indicated in the initial evaluation.

title: Basic calcium phosphate (BCP) deposition disease of the shoulder - Milwaukee shoulder - is characterized by aggressive destruction of the
body: Basic calcium phosphate (BCP) deposition disease of the shoulder - Milwaukee shoulder - is characterized by aggressive destruction of the glenohumeral joint and rotator cuff. It often presents with a large hemorrhagic effusion, but BCP crystals may not be visible on conventional joint fluid microscopy.

title: NSAIDs are the first-line therapy for all symptomatic ankylosing spondylitis patients, unless contraindicated
body: NSAIDs are the first-line therapy for all symptomatic ankylosing spondylitis patients, unless contraindicated. These patients can also benefit from supervised physical therapy (eg, postural training, range-of-motion stretching), smoking cessation, and other pain relief measures such as local heat or cold packs. The addition of a tumor necrosis factor inhibitor is the next step for persistent pain.

title: The diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is based primarily on clinical features with some support from laboratory and radiologic testing
body: The diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is based primarily on clinical features with some support from laboratory and radiologic testing. Although rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic Citrullinated peptide (anti- CCP) are typically positive in RA, many patients have "seronegative” RA (negative rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP), especially early in the disease. These patients generally have a somewhat less aggressive course.

title: Many patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) will have rheumatoid factor-negative ("seronegative") RA and may have rapid relief of symptoms
body: Many patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) will have rheumatoid factor-negative ("seronegative") RA and may have rapid relief of symptoms with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or glucocorticoids. However, they should be initiated promptly on disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs to prevent long-term joint damage and functional impairment.

title: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis should be started on disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs as soon as possible
body: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis should be started on disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs as soon as possible. Hydroxychloroquine and sulfasalazine are options for mild disease, and methotrexate is commonly the initial drug of choice for moderate and severe disease.

title: Patients with CREST syndrome are more likely to develop pulmonary hypertension (often without interstitial fibrosis) and less likely to
body: Patients with CREST syndrome are more likely to develop pulmonary hypertension (often without interstitial fibrosis) and less likely to develop the renal and cardiac disease seen in the diffuse cutaneous form of systemic sclerosis.

title: Chronic accumulation of colchicine, often seen in patients with chronic kidney disease, can result in significant neuromyopathy
body: Chronic accumulation of colchicine, often seen in patients with chronic kidney disease, can result in significant neuromyopathy. The cytoplasmic vacuolization seen on muscle biopsy is characteristic. This condition resolves on discontinuation of colchicine.

title: Ethanol increases serum uric acid levels. Patients with gout should limit alcohol intake to one or fewer beverages per day to reduce the risk of gout attacks.
Criteria effective for distinguishing giant cell arteritis from other vasculitides include age >50, localized new- onset headache
body: Criteria effective for distinguishing giant cell arteritis from other vasculitides include age >50, localized new- onset headache, erythrocyte sedimentation rate >50 mm∕h, and temporal artery tenderness. Diagnosis is confirmed with temporal artery biopsy, but treatment with glucocorticoids should be initiated immediately.

title: Acute crystal arthritis, such as gout or pseudogout, often occurs in patients hospitalized with for acute illness
body: Acute crystal arthritis, such as gout or pseudogout, often occurs in patients hospitalized with for acute illness. The diagnosis of pseudogout is suggested by chondrocalcinosis on x-ray and synovial fluid showing rhomboid shaped, positively birefringent crystals under polarized light microscopy.

title: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) usually presents with chronic low back pain in patients < age 40 (men>>women)
body: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) usually presents with chronic low back pain in patients < age 40 (men>>women). Extraarticular manifestations of AS include anterior uveitis, aortic regurgitation (due to aortitis or valve dysfunction), decreased chest expansion, and osteopenia.

title: Adult-onset Still's disease is characterized by recurrent high fever, polyarticular arthritis, evanescent macular rash, leukocytosis, and
body: Adult-onset Still's disease is characterized by recurrent high fever, polyarticular arthritis, evanescent macular rash, leukocytosis, and elevated serum ferritin levels. Other nonspecific clinical features such as arthritis, sore throat, Iymphadenopathy, and elevated liver markers may be seen.

title: If the clinical suspicion is high for giant cell arteritis (GCA) but temporal artery biopsy is negative, a contralateral biopsy should be
body: If the clinical suspicion is high for giant cell arteritis (GCA) but temporal artery biopsy is negative, a contralateral biopsy should be considered. In a patient with typical features of GCA, treatment should be continued despite a negative biopsy unless a more likely diagnosis has been found. Addition of aspirin to the steroid regimen is recommended to reduce the risk of long-term vascular complications in GCA (eg, transient ischemic attack, stroke).

title: Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia is usually associated with hepatitis C and may present with palpable purpura, arthralgias
body: Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia is usually associated with hepatitis C and may present with palpable purpura, arthralgias, membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, low serum complement, cutaneous vasculitis, and neuropathy. The vasculitis may cause skin necrosis and gangrene in some patients. Treatment of hepatitis C may reduce cryoglobulins and improve skin symptoms.

title: Medial meniscal injuries typically present with pain, locking, and swelling. Ligament testing for instability is negative, but joint line tenderness is often present.
Dermatitis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus can be managed with sun protection and topical glucocorticoids in most mild cases
body: Dermatitis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus can be managed with sun protection and topical glucocorticoids in most mild cases. Antimalarial drugs such as hydroxychloroquine are used in moderate cases. Immunosuppressive drugs are considered for severe and refractory cases.

title: Metatarsal shaft stress fracture is due to repetitive weight-bearing activities, especially following an abrupt increase in activity
body: Metatarsal shaft stress fracture is due to repetitive weight-bearing activities, especially following an abrupt increase in activity. Patients with the female athlete triad (decreased energy availability, menstrual dysfunction, decreased bone density) are at risk for stress fractures and require screening for an underlying eating disorder.

title: Psoriasis can be a presenting feature of HIV infection
body: Psoriasis can be a presenting feature of HIV infection. Psoriatic arthritis is more aggressive when associated with HIV infection and can include palmoplantar involvement and nail disease. Treatment involves methotrexate, sulfasalazine, or TNF inhibitors in some cases.

title: Cutaneous small vessel vasculitis is a skin-isolated leukocytoclastic vasculitis that usually occurs 7-10 days after drug exposure (eg
body: Cutaneous small vessel vasculitis is a skin-isolated leukocytoclastic vasculitis that usually occurs 7-10 days after drug exposure (eg, penicillin) or infection (eg, hepatitis B or C, HIV). Common findings include palpable purpura and a petechial rash. Systemic organ involvement should prompt evaluation for an alternate diagnosis. Spontaneous resolution typically occurs within days or weeks after the offending drug is discontinued (or the infection is treated).

title: Serologic factors for erosive rheumatoid arthritis can predict the need aggressive therapy to prevent irreversible injury
body: Serologic factors for erosive rheumatoid arthritis can predict the need aggressive therapy to prevent irreversible injury. Factors such as anti-citrullinated peptide antibodies and/or joint erosions seen on x-ray are associated with poor prognosis and more aggressive disease.

title: Plantar fasciitis usually presents with heel pain that is most intense on the first step upon arising
body: Plantar fasciitis usually presents with heel pain that is most intense on the first step upon arising. Examination shows local point tenderness with dorsiflexion of the toes. The condition usually resolves with conservative measures such as plantar stretching exercises and short-term NSAID use.

title: The Ottawa ankle rules can identify patients with ankle sprains who may have an associated fracture that will require imaging
body: The Ottawa ankle rules can identify patients with ankle sprains who may have an associated fracture that will require imaging. The rules take into consideration the location of pain, specific areas of bony tenderness, and ability to bear weight.

title: The appropriate age to begin osteoporosis screening is 65
body: The appropriate age to begin osteoporosis screening is 65. However, most guidelines recommend that testing should begin earlier if the patient has 1 or more risk factors for osteoporosis. Bone mineral density testing with dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry is the most widely used technique.

title: Pseudogout is characterized by acute inflammatory arthritis associated with chondrocalcinosis
body: Pseudogout is characterized by acute inflammatory arthritis associated with chondrocalcinosis. The knee is the most commonly affected joint. Pseudogout is most common in the elderly; onset in a young patient should prompt testing for secondary causes, such as hemochromatosis.

title: Younger patients who present with stroke (or venous thromboembolism), thrombocytopenia, and prolonged PTT should be tested for
body: Younger patients who present with stroke (or venous thromboembolism), thrombocytopenia, and prolonged PTT should be tested for antiphospholipid antibody syndrome. An MRI of the brain should be obtained for risk stratification before initiating anticoagulation.

title: Henoch-Schonlein purpura typically presents with lower extremity palpable purpura, nonspecific abdominal symptoms, renal disease, and
body: Henoch-Schonlein purpura typically presents with lower extremity palpable purpura, nonspecific abdominal symptoms, renal disease, and arthritis/arthralgias. The diagnosis is suggested clinically, but tissue biopsy (e.g., skin, kidney) is the most sensitive and specific test to confirm the diagnosis.

title: Reactive arthritis usually presents after a gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection with asymmetric oligoarthritis and enthesitis
body: Reactive arthritis usually presents after a gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection with asymmetric oligoarthritis and enthesitis, conjunctivitis, or oral ulcers. Diagnosis is suspected clinically and NSAIDs are the preferred first-line therapy. Antibiotics help neither the arthritis nor, if present, underlying gastroenteritis, but they may be beneficial for active chlamydial genitourinary infection.

title: Dermatomyositis can cause weakness of the oropharyngeal and striated muscles in the upper third of the esophagus
body: Dermatomyositis can cause weakness of the oropharyngeal and striated muscles in the upper third of the esophagus. This may lead to dysphagia for both solids and liquids and aspiration with recurrent pneumonia.

title: Polyarteritis nodosa is a small- and medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis negative for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody
body: Polyarteritis nodosa is a small- and medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis negative for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody. It usually involves the mesenteric and renal vessels but spares the pulmonary arteries. Patients can present with systemic symptoms and multiorgan involvement. Tissue biopsy confirms the diagnosis. If there is no obvious site for biopsy, diagnosis can be suggested by imaging studies showing renal, hepatic, or mesenteric microaneurysms of blood vessels.
