title: Acute gout is common in hospitalized patients and can be triggered by infection, surgery, trauma, dehydration, medications, and impaired
body: Acute gout is common in hospitalized patients and can be triggered by infection, surgery, trauma, dehydration, medications, and impaired renal function. Loop diuretics can cause acutely elevated serum uric acid levels and trigger a flare of gout.

title: Injury to the common peroneal nerve causes loss of sensation at the lateral leg and foot
body: Injury to the common peroneal nerve causes loss of sensation at the lateral leg and foot. Motor findings include foot drop and a steppage gait. Risk factors include prolonged hospitalization, trauma, and leg casting. Initial treatment for foot drop due to common peroneal nerve injury includes physical therapy and an ankle foot orthotic.

title: Physicians practicing in the intensive care unit must engage patients and families and provide an accurate picture of the disease process
body: Physicians practicing in the intensive care unit must engage patients and families and provide an accurate picture of the disease process and prospects for recovery. In cases of severe illness and a high likelihood of death, patients and families should be made aware of palliative care treatment options that prioritize comfort and quality of life.

title: At the start of a family meeting, family members should be asked how much they know about the patient's condition
body: At the start of a family meeting, family members should be asked how much they know about the patient's condition. The SPIKES mnemonic is a useful model for framing the family meeting discussion and breaking bad news.

title: Alert fatigue occurs when health care personnel are bombarded by numerous automated alerts and warnings of low clinical consequence and
body: Alert fatigue occurs when health care personnel are bombarded by numerous automated alerts and warnings of low clinical consequence and become conditioned to ignore all alerts, including those with high clinical significance.

title: Physicians have an ethical responsibility to report an impaired colleague to the appropriate state regulatory body (ie, a physician health program or state medical board).
Near-miss events should be reported to the hospital administration as analysis can assist in the identification and correction of errors that jeopardize patient safety.
Confidentiality is a basic legal and ethical principle of medical care. Permission should be obtained prior to disclosing information to other parties, including family members.
Objective clinical judgment can be unconsciously clouded by financial incentives
body: Objective clinical judgment can be unconsciously clouded by financial incentives. Any actual or apparent financial conflict of interest must be disclosed and patients given the opportunity to seek care in independent facilities.

title: Physicians may feel pressured to provide informal or undocumented care to colleagues and should be aware of the ethical implications
body: Physicians may feel pressured to provide informal or undocumented care to colleagues and should be aware of the ethical implications. Referral to an independent clinician who can perform a comprehensive assessment is in the patient's best interest.

title: Health literacy is the ability to comprehend and apply information regarding health conditions
body: Health literacy is the ability to comprehend and apply information regarding health conditions. Impaired health literacy can lead to adverse outcomes, including more frequent hospitalizations and increased morbidity/mortality. Patients taking numerous medications often benefit from regular medication review.

title: Unexplained traumatic injuries, signs of neglect (eg, pressure ulcers), and abrupt changes in financial status or ability to pay are red
body: Unexplained traumatic injuries, signs of neglect (eg, pressure ulcers), and abrupt changes in financial status or ability to pay are red flags for elder abuse. When elder abuse is suspected, adult protective services should be contacted immediately.

title: Assessing driving competence is difficult
body: Assessing driving competence is difficult. Driving history is an important evaluative tool along with the careful evaluation of medical conditions and physical examination. If there is doubt regarding driving competence, evaluation with a directly observed on-road test may be indicated (if available).

title: Family members should be used as medical interpreters only in urgent situations
body: Family members should be used as medical interpreters only in urgent situations. Otherwise, trained medical interpreters should be used for all aspects of the clinician-patient interaction (eg, interview, explanation of diagnosis, consent, treatment planning).

title: Hospice services should be offered to surrogate decision makers for patients with advanced dementia
body: Hospice services should be offered to surrogate decision makers for patients with advanced dementia. Criteria for enrollment include dependence on others for all activities of daily living, lack of verbal communication, and inability to ambulate, in addition to a medical condition such as aspiration pneumonia or eating problems in the past year.

title: Patients have rights to privacy, and their personal health information is protected by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability
body: Patients have rights to privacy, and their personal health information is protected by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). In research studies, de-identifying patients by assigning a unique study number helps ensure confidentiality.
